q3jukr6: A resident wears a fentanyl patch. Which thing noticed during the bath should be mentioned to the nurse because it can raise the amount of drug absorbed?
A heating pad has been left on over the patch site
The patch has been in place for about two days
The patch is on the upper back rather than the chest
The resident showered with warm water this morning
Heat increases blood flow and the rate drug crosses the skin, so a heating pad over a fentanyl patch can cause a dangerous rise in absorption. Normal bathing and a 72 hour wear time are expected.
qgdh9pp: A CNA finds a used fentanyl patch on the bed linen. Why does the CNA handle it with gloves rather than bare fingers?
A used patch still holds drug that absorbs through skin
A used patch is sharp and can cut the fingers
A used patch grows bacteria once it leaves the skin
A used patch loses its backing and leaks drug into the air
A patch is built as a drug reservoir and a good deal of fentanyl remains when it comes off, so skin contact can dose the person handling it. The nurse witnesses disposal.
qbbsdov: A resident has chest pain and asks the CNA to hand over the nitroglycerin bottle on the nightstand. The CNA should:
Stay and call the nurse right away
Hand over the bottle since it belongs to them
Place a tablet under the resident's tongue
Tell the resident to rest and come back later
Chest pain is an emergency. The CNA stays with the resident and gets the nurse, who handles the medicine.
qmbd2: After a resident gets nitroglycerin, the CNA should watch for:
Dizziness, headache, or low blood pressure
Itchy eyes and a runny nose
A rise in blood sugar after the resident eats
Nitroglycerin can drop blood pressure and cause headache and dizziness, so help prevent falls.
q1j3wtsl: Isosorbide mononitrate is taken daily to:
Prevent blood clots after surgery on the hip
Long-acting nitrates like isosorbide help prevent angina episodes.
q1xkli0c: After an albuterol treatment, a resident says his heart is racing and his hands are shaky. The CNA should:
Give the resident another puff to calm him
Tell him to stop using the inhaler for good
Ignore it since it will pass on its own
A fast heart rate and shakiness are common albuterol side effects. Report them to the nurse.
q1oxwjwe: A resident with COPD uses tiotropium every morning and also has an albuterol inhaler. He is more short of breath than usual. What is true about the tiotropium?
It is a daily maintenance inhaler, not a rescue inhaler
It should be given a second time whenever breathing worsens
It works within a minute or two of being inhaled
It replaces the albuterol inhaler once started

Tiotropium is a long-acting bronchodilator taken once a day to prevent symptoms; albuterol is the rescue inhaler that works in minutes. Knowing which is which tells the nurse what the resident needs now.
q9zwg7j: A resident uses a steroid inhaler (fluticasone). Afterward, the resident should usually:
Drink milk to coat the throat
Rinsing after inhaled steroids helps prevent thrush (a yeast infection of the mouth).
q1d4z6qp: Which is the most important oxygen safety rule?
No smoking or open flames near oxygen
Store tanks lying loose on the floor
Use petroleum jelly on the nose for dryness
Turn the flow up whenever the resident is short of breath
Oxygen feeds fire. No smoking, candles, or flames near oxygen, and secure tanks upright.
q1ygz1zr: A resident on 2 liters of oxygen by nasal cannula is more short of breath. Which observation should the CNA report along with the breathlessness?
The tubing is kinked under the wheel of the recliner
The resident wears the cannula with the prongs curved down
The concentrator has been running since early this morning
The head of the bed is raised about 30 degrees
A kink stops flow no matter what the flowmeter reads, and checking the delivery path is within the CNA role. Prongs curve down by design, and a raised head of the bed helps rather than hurts.
qqsoujx: A resident's family member lights a candle in a room where oxygen is in use. The CNA should:
Ask them to put it out right away and explain why
Move the candle to the other side of the bed
Let it burn since the oxygen tank is closed
Turn off the oxygen so the candle is safe
Open flames near oxygen can cause a fire. The candle must be put out.
q1bksl4p: Where should a portable oxygen tank be kept?
Secured upright in a holder or cart
Lying on the floor under the bed
Next to the space heater to keep it warm
Leaning against the wall by the door
Tanks should be secured so they cannot fall and be damaged.
q1kutb12: A resident on donepezil has nausea, diarrhea, and a slow pulse. The CNA should:
Report these signs to the nurse
Stop all of the resident's meals for the day
Give the resident extra fiber and fluids
Encourage the resident to walk around more
Donepezil can cause stomach upset and a slow heart rate. These signs should be reported.
qkz620w: Infections caused by fungus on the skin
Memantine is given for moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease.
qjpwh4w: A resident with Parkinson's disease is very shaky and stiff late in the afternoon. The CNA should:
Report the change to the nurse
Give the resident's next dose early
Tie the resident's hands to stop shaking
Tell the resident to try harder to move
Symptoms can return when the medicine wears off. The nurse needs to know so timing can be reviewed.
q1a8iruk: A resident on carbidopa-levodopa gets dizzy when standing. The CNA should:
Have the resident stand up slowly
Have the resident jump up quickly
Keep the resident in bed all day
Walk the resident without a gait belt
This medicine can cause low blood pressure when standing. The resident should rise slowly, and fall precautions should be used.
qsg0iyg: A resident on sertraline says she wants to end her life. The CNA should:
Stay with her and tell the nurse right away
Promise to keep it a secret
Tell her to cheer up and leave the room
Wait to report it at the end of the shift
Any talk of suicide must be reported immediately. The CNA should not leave the resident alone.
qpvrke6: A resident recently started an antidepressant (escitalopram). The CNA should report:
New confusion, falls, or mood changes
That the resident ate all of lunch
That the resident watched TV today
That the resident wants to call a friend
Changes in mood, behavior, or new confusion should be reported, especially when a medicine is new.
q1qcrlz: Mirtazapine may be given to an older resident for depression. A common side effect is:
Very fast breathing and a high fever
Mirtazapine often causes drowsiness and weight gain, so watch for falls.
q1yqtye1: A resident takes trazodone at bedtime for sleep. The CNA should:
Use fall precautions if the resident gets up at night
Wake the resident every hour to check alertness
Walk the resident alone with no gait belt
Raise all bed rails without an order
Trazodone can cause drowsiness and dizziness, raising the fall risk at night.
q496h7m: An 84 year old resident was started on lorazepam yesterday. Which change should the CNA describe to the nurse first?
Unsteady walking with two near falls today
Sleeping about an hour longer this morning
Asking for help to the bathroom at night
Feeling less worried than she did last week
New unsteadiness is the finding that predicts a hip fracture, and benzodiazepine effects are stronger and last longer in older adults. Sleeping a little longer and less anxiety are expected effects.
qwl1w1r: A resident who takes alprazolam is drowsy at breakfast and keeps nodding off with food in her mouth. Which risk should the CNA act on first?
Choking and aspiration while she is being fed
Dry mouth from the medicine at breakfast
Losing weight from a poor appetite over several weeks
Spilling hot coffee on her lap at the table
A sedated resident cannot protect her airway, so aspiration is the immediate danger. Feeding stops and she is positioned upright while the nurse is told about the sedation.
qf8ztgk: A resident takes zolpidem at bedtime. Which observation from the night shift is most important for the CNA to pass on?
Walking in the hall at 2 a.m. with no memory of it
Fell asleep about 20 minutes after taking the pill
Slept through the night without getting up
Woke once to use the bathroom and went back to sleep

Zolpidem can cause complex sleep behaviors such as walking or eating with no recall, which carry a real injury risk and are a reason the drug is reconsidered. Falling asleep in about 20 minutes is the expected effect.
q1x4bgut: Temazepam is a sleeping pill. Because of this medicine, the CNA should:
Keep the call light within reach at night
Leave the bed in the highest position
Turn off the night light to help sleep
Put the walker in the closet overnight
Sleeping pills raise fall risk. Keep the bed low, the call light close, and the path lit.
q1ltsg4e: Quetiapine (Seroquel) is an antipsychotic. The CNA should watch for:
Increased energy and fast weight loss
Bleeding gums when brushing the teeth
Coughing up thick, yellow mucus each morning
Quetiapine causes sedation and low blood pressure on standing, increasing fall risk.
qioz5uy: A resident on haloperidol has new stiffness, shuffling, and lip smacking. The CNA should:
Report the movements to the nurse
Tell the resident to stop making faces
Ignore it since it is part of dementia
Massage the muscles until they loosen
Antipsychotics can cause movement side effects. These must be reported.
q1o2tsou: Antipsychotics such as risperidone should never be used in a nursing home to:
Keep a resident quiet for staff convenience
Treat a diagnosed mental illness as ordered
Help with hallucinations that frighten the resident
Treat symptoms that put the resident or others at risk
Using medicines to control behavior for staff convenience is a chemical restraint and is not allowed.
q16j41wk: Gabapentin is often used for nerve pain. A common side effect is:
A dry cough and a sore throat that lasts for weeks
Gabapentin can cause dizziness and drowsiness, raising fall risk in older adults.
q1hf7klb: A resident on tamsulosin gets dizzy getting out of bed. The CNA should:
Have him sit on the edge of the bed first
Help him stand up as fast as possible
Tell him to skip his next dose
Leave him alone to walk to the bathroom
Tamsulosin can cause low blood pressure on standing. The resident should dangle first and rise slowly.
qgscl8b: Oxybutynin is used for an overactive bladder. A CNA might notice:
Frequent loose stools and a large appetite
Oxybutynin is anticholinergic and often causes dry mouth, constipation, and confusion in older adults.
qh0fb3x: A resident on prednisone should be watched for:
Lower blood sugar and weight loss
Steroids raise blood sugar, weaken the immune system, and can thin the skin.
q3bc32c: A resident started on cephalexin today has a new red, itchy rash on the chest. The CNA should:
Report the rash to the nurse right away
Apply lotion and check again tomorrow
Tell the resident to stop the antibiotic
Cover the rash so others do not see it
A new rash after starting an antibiotic may be an allergic reaction and must be reported.
qbqsu10: A resident on nitrofurantoin has dark brown urine. The CNA should:
Throw away the urine without recording it
Give cranberry juice and not report
Nitrofurantoin can darken urine, but any color change should be reported so the nurse can check.
qas6kid: A resident on amoxicillin suddenly has hives, wheezing, and a swollen face. The CNA should:
Give the resident cold water to drink
Help the resident walk to the shower
Wait to see if it goes away on its own
These are signs of a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis), which is an emergency.
q1nudvxd: A resident on ciprofloxacin complains of new pain in the back of the ankle. The CNA should:
Report the ankle pain to the nurse
Have the resident walk on it more
Rub the area hard with a lotion
Wait to report it until the antibiotic is done
This antibiotic can rarely damage tendons. New tendon pain should be reported.
q1jwwsm1: A resident on clindamycin has had several watery, foul smelling stools. Which action by the CNA matters most for keeping it from spreading?
Washing hands with soap and water after each contact
Using the alcohol hand rub between each resident contact
Wearing a surgical mask while in the room
Changing gloves only when they look soiled
C. difficile forms spores that alcohol does not kill, so physical removal by washing with soap and running water is what stops transmission. The organism is not spread through the air.
q1lyligq: After caring for a resident with C. diff, the CNA should clean hands with:
Alcohol rubs do not kill C. diff spores. Washing with soap and water removes them.
qeo8crb: Bacterial infections of the bladder and kidney
Nystatin is an antifungal used for thrush and yeast infections of the skin.
qjvo2lw: The nurse has just given a resident nystatin oral suspension for thrush. What should the CNA do next?
Hold food and fluids for about 30 minutes afterward
Offer a large glass of water to rinse it down
Give mouth care with mouthwash right after
Serve the meal tray while the mouth is still wet with it
Nystatin works by touching the fungus directly, so it is swished and held in the mouth and food and drink are kept back for about 30 minutes to keep from washing it away.
qigdoq1: A resident takes alendronate (Fosamax). The CNA should help the resident:
Stay upright for 30 minutes after the pill
Lie flat right after taking the pill
Eat breakfast right before the pill
Lie on the left side for an hour after the dose
Alendronate can irritate the esophagus. Staying upright helps it go down and reduces irritation.
q14cybqi: Infections that cause a high fever
Alendronate helps strengthen bones and lowers fracture risk.
qwoa33f: Calcium carbonate (Tums) may be given for bones or heartburn. A common side effect is:
A dry, hacking cough at night
Calcium carbonate often causes constipation, so bowel movements should be tracked.
q16jr0d5: A resident on ferrous sulfate (iron) has dark green-black stools. The CNA should:
Report the stool color to the nurse
Give extra laxatives from the supply room
Tell the resident iron pills cause no change
Iron often turns stools dark, but black stools can also mean bleeding. The CNA reports it so the nurse can decide.
qkjqaqn: Ferrous sulfate is given to treat:
Bladder spasms that cause leaking urine
Iron tablets help the body make red blood cells.
q2e36tu: Infections of the skin after surgery
Allopurinol lowers uric acid levels to prevent gout flares.
qal0jkl: Meloxicam is an anti-inflammatory pain medicine. The CNA should report:
That the resident walked to the dining room with help
Anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) can cause stomach bleeding, so pain or black stools should be reported.
qypl7n6: High blood pressure with headache and blurred vision
Clopidogrel keeps platelets from sticking, so watch for bruising and bleeding.
qxgb1yo: A CNA finds a tablet on the floor by a resident's bed. Besides handing it to the nurse, what information is most useful to give?
Which resident's room it was in and when it was found
That the tablet is white and oval in shape
That the floor had been mopped earlier in the same shift
That the resident says she took all her pills
The nurse needs to know whose dose may have been missed and roughly when, so the right medication record can be checked. Appearance alone does not identify a tablet reliably.
q1xodjpc: A CNA finds several pills tucked inside a resident's pillowcase. Which detail is most important for the nurse to hear?
Pills from more than one medication pass are present
That the pillowcase had been changed the day before that
The resident has a private room on the unit
The resident takes her pills with applesauce
Pills from several passes means doses have been missed repeatedly, which changes what the nurse checks: a blood pressure that has drifted up, a missed anticoagulant, a skipped antibiotic course.
q8mdlv1: A resident refuses her morning pills. Which part of the refusal is most important for the CNA to pass along?
Which pills she refused and the reason she gave
That she refused at about the usual time
That she has refused once before earlier this month
That she was polite about refusing them

Residents may refuse, and the nurse needs to know which drug was missed and why: a skipped levothyroxine matters differently from a skipped stool softener, and nausea or trouble swallowing can be fixed.
q13ajb2v: In most states, giving residents their medicines is the job of the:
Licensed nurse or certified medication aide
CNA on duty in the room
CNAs do not give medicines unless they are certified as medication aides under state rules.
qb713fm: A nurse asks the CNA to give a resident their pills while the nurse is busy. The CNA is not a medication aide. The CNA should:
Politely refuse and explain it is outside the CNA role
Give the pills since the nurse asked
Give only the vitamins and leave the rest
Ask the resident whether they want to take them now
Giving medicines is outside the CNA scope of practice unless the CNA is certified to do so.
q1iu940s: A CNA finds a full pill cup on a resident's overbed table an hour after the medication pass. Why does the nurse need to know?
The dose is recorded as given but was not taken
The pills will have gone bad sitting in the open air
The cup should have been returned to the cart
The resident may want them later in the day
Medications are charted when they are handed over, so an untouched cup means the record and reality no longer match. The nurse has to find out which drugs were missed before the next dose is due.
q1wf78a1: A CNA should never crush a resident's pills because:
CNAs do not handle medicines, and some pills must not be crushed
It makes the medicine work too slowly
Crushing is only allowed for vitamins and herbal supplements
Crushing is medication administration, and long-acting or coated pills can become unsafe if crushed.
q23ml69: Which sign of an allergic reaction should the CNA report to the nurse right away?
Hives, swelling, and trouble breathing can mean a dangerous allergic reaction.
q1jcp5ls: A resident is on fall precautions because of a new blood pressure medicine. The CNA should:
Keep the bed low and help the resident stand slowly
Leave the walker out of reach so they stay in bed
Turn off all the lights at night
Use restraints so the resident cannot get up alone
Medicines that lower blood pressure can cause dizziness. Fall precautions keep the resident safe.
qxycskk: A CNA notices a new side effect after a resident's medicine changes. The CNA should:
Report it to the nurse and document as directed
Tell the resident to stop taking the medicine
Look up the drug and change the dose
Wait a week to see if it goes away
The CNA observes and reports. The nurse and prescriber decide what to do.
q1n4zyhf: A nurse delegates several tasks to a CNA. Which one is within the CNA role?
Recording a blood pressure before an antihypertensive dose
Judging whether that blood pressure is safe for the next dose
Deciding to hold the dose when the reading is low
Teaching the resident why the dose was held today
CNAs measure, observe, record and report. Interpreting the reading, holding a dose and teaching about medication are nursing judgment; the CNA's number is what the nurse acts on.
q11fp4ht: A resident on several medicines is suddenly confused this afternoon after being clear at breakfast. Which quick check is within the CNA role and most useful to the nurse?
A set of vital signs and a delegated blood glucose
A review of the medication record for new drugs
A judgment about whether this is dementia worsening
A call to the family to ask about her usual behavior
An abrupt change over hours is delirium rather than dementia, and low blood sugar, fever and low oxygen are the fast reversible causes. Reading the record and judging the cause belong to the nurse.
qopo56y: The best way for a CNA to help prevent constipation in a resident on pain medicine is to:
Offer fluids and high-fiber foods as allowed
Limit fluids so the resident does not need the bathroom
Keep the resident in bed as much as possible
Give a laxative from the cart every morning
Fluids, fiber, and activity help prevent opioid constipation. The CNA does not give laxatives.
q1mxy7hw: Before and after helping with any care, including care near medicines, the CNA should:
Put on a gown and face shield
Count the pills in the medicine cart
Hand hygiene is the most important way to prevent the spread of infection.
q6bfcbp: A resident takes several medicines that can cause dizziness. Before walking, the CNA should first have the resident:
Sit on the edge of the bed for a moment
Stand up as fast as possible
Drink a cup of strong coffee
Lie flat for 10 minutes with the legs raised
Dangling before standing lets blood pressure adjust and helps prevent falls.
qtl0x6x: A resident's daughter asks the CNA what her mother's new pill is for. The CNA should:
Refer the question to the nurse
Guess based on the pill's color
Read the chart aloud in the hallway
Tell her it is none of her business
Questions about medicines are answered by the nurse. The CNA also protects the resident's privacy.
q4elj1m: A resident who just got a new medicine has trouble breathing and a swollen throat. The CNA's first action is to:
Call for help and stay with the resident
Leave to find the medicine label
Give the resident water to swallow
Write down the time and continue rounds
Possible anaphylaxis is an emergency. The CNA should call for help and stay with the resident.
q1rd0c35: A resident receiving medicines through a feeding tube should be positioned:
With the head of the bed raised
With the feet higher than the head
Raising the head of the bed helps prevent aspiration during and after tube feeding.
qm6634b: A resident coughs and chokes on her pills every morning. Which observation would be most useful for the nurse deciding on a safer plan?
She coughs on thin liquids but not on pureed food
She prefers to take her pills just before breakfast
She takes seven tablets at the morning pass
She drinks from a cup rather than a straw

Coughing on thin liquids and not on thicker textures points to the kind of swallowing problem a speech evaluation can confirm, and it tells the nurse whether a liquid form or thickened liquids would help.
qg3ptzl: A resident refuses the bedtime snack ordered to prevent low blood sugar overnight. What should the CNA record and report?
The refusal, the time, and what she did eat
That the snack was offered as the order states
That the resident said she was not hungry
That the snack was left at the bedside
The nurse uses the time and the actual intake to judge the risk of a low glucose during the night, which may mean a glucose check or a change in the evening insulin.
qwv38yt: A client is due for both digoxin and metoprolol, and the apical pulse is 56. Which statement about the hold parameters is correct?
Both drugs are commonly held below 60 beats per minute
Digoxin is held below 60 beats per minute and metoprolol below 40
Metoprolol is held below 60 and digoxin below 50
Neither drug has a heart rate hold parameter
Both a cardiac glycoside and a beta blocker slow conduction through the AV node, so a rate under 60 is the usual threshold for holding either drug and reporting. A rate of 56 crosses it for both.
qhzya7k: A client taking digoxin reports nausea, poor appetite, and seeing yellow-green halos around lights. The nurse recognizes these as:
Expected effects that will fade in a week
Signs of an allergic reaction to digoxin
Symptoms of low blood glucose from digoxin
GI upset and visual changes such as yellow-green halos are classic early signs of digoxin toxicity; hold the dose and report the findings.
qv4bcq2: Which lab result places a client taking digoxin at greatest risk for toxicity?
Hypokalemia increases the risk of digoxin toxicity and dysrhythmias.
qf0ilq1: A client with heart failure and atrial fibrillation has taken digoxin for a week. Which finding best shows the drug is doing its job?
A resting rate of 78 and easier breathing when flat
A blood pressure that fell from 140/88 to 118/74
A weight that has gone up two pounds since admission
A potassium that rose from 3.4 to 4.0 mEq/L
Digoxin slows conduction through the AV node and improves contractility, so the rate comes down and heart failure symptoms ease. It is not a blood pressure drug and does not change potassium.
q1fogno6: A client with severe digoxin toxicity and a dangerous dysrhythmia is expected to receive which antidote?
Digoxin immune Fab binds digoxin and reverses life-threatening toxicity.
q37vyu1: The nurse sees an order for potassium chloride 20 mEq IV push. The nurse should:
Question the order, because potassium is never given IV push
Give it slowly over 2 minutes through the existing IV line
Dilute it in 10 mL of saline and give it over 5 minutes
Give it IV push only if the client is on a continuous cardiac monitor
Potassium given by IV push can cause fatal cardiac arrest; it must be diluted and infused by pump per policy.
q1seucvd: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client taking oral potassium chloride liquid?
Dilute it in juice or water and take it with food
Take it on an empty stomach with no other fluids
Take it at bedtime with a salt substitute for taste
Mix it with an antacid to prevent stomach upset
Liquid potassium irritates the GI tract; dilute it and take it with or after meals.
q19zdnce: Four clients have an order for oral potassium chloride. Which one should the nurse ask about before giving the dose?
The client on spironolactone with a potassium of 5.2 mEq/L
The client on furosemide today with a potassium of 3.2 mEq/L
The client with vomiting and a potassium of 3.0 mEq/L
The client on a thiazide with a potassium of 3.4 mEq/L

Spironolactone is potassium-sparing, so a supplement on top of it pushes an already high level toward dangerous hyperkalemia. The other three are losing potassium, which is why the supplement is ordered.
qf86ga9: A client is ordered IV furosemide 80 mg. Over how long should the nurse plan to give it, and why?
About 20 minutes, because a fast push can damage hearing
About 10 seconds, because a fast push works better
About 4 hours, because the drug irritates the vein
Over 2 minutes, because a slower rate reduces urine output
The usual limit is 4 mg per minute, so 80 mg runs over about 20 minutes. Rapid IV administration causes tinnitus and hearing loss, and the risk rises with aminoglycosides or kidney impairment.
q1l81ho2: Which statement by a client taking furosemide indicates the need for more teaching?
I will take my water pill right before I go to bed.
I will weigh myself every morning before breakfast.
I will get up slowly when I stand from the chair.
I will eat foods like bananas and oranges each day.
Loop diuretics are taken in the morning to avoid nighttime urination and lost sleep.
q15ko4ap: A client receiving furosemide should report which finding to the nurse immediately?
Needing to urinate more in the morning
Muscle cramps and weakness may signal hypokalemia.
q1cxlpdu: A client with diabetes is started on hydrochlorothiazide. The nurse should reinforce closer monitoring of:
Blood glucose, because thiazides can raise it
Blood glucose, because thiazides can lower it sharply
Hearing, because thiazides often cause deafness
Urine color, because thiazides turn urine orange
Thiazides can cause hyperglycemia, hypokalemia, and increased uric acid.
q1ypolmv: A client taking spironolactone asks about using a salt substitute. The nurse should advise the client to:
Avoid salt substitutes, because most contain potassium
Use salt substitutes freely, because they contain no sodium
Use salt substitutes only with meals to protect the stomach
Use salt substitutes to replace lost potassium
Spironolactone is potassium-sparing; potassium-based salt substitutes can cause hyperkalemia.
q1btl7pc: A client taking lisinopril reports a persistent dry, tickling cough. The nurse should:
Report it, because it is a common ACE inhibitor effect
Tell the client it means a lung infection is starting
Advise the client to stop the drug right away at home
Tell the client to double the dose to control it
ACE inhibitors cause a dry cough from bradykinin buildup; the provider may switch to an ARB.
qqhr110: A client who started lisinopril three days ago has swelling of the lips and tongue, with no hives and no wheeze. Which feature points to drug-induced angioedema rather than an allergic reaction?
Swelling that came on within minutes
Swelling with a widespread red rash
Swelling that improves with an antihistamine

ACE inhibitor angioedema comes from bradykinin rather than histamine, so it causes deep non-itchy swelling with no urticaria and responds poorly to antihistamines. It can appear days to months after starting.
qz8v320: A client took the first dose of lisinopril this morning. When is the blood pressure most likely to fall the furthest?
Within about 1 to 6 hours after the dose
About 3 days after the first dose is given
Only after two weeks of daily therapy
Within about five minutes of swallowing it

Oral lisinopril starts working in about an hour and peaks around 6 hours, so first-dose hypotension shows up the same day. The drop is largest in clients who are volume depleted or already on a diuretic.
q1c24nau: A client taking enalapril tells the nurse she has just learned she is pregnant. The nurse should:
Notify the provider, because ACE inhibitors can harm the fetus
Tell her to keep taking it, because it is safe in pregnancy
Tell her to take it every other day until delivery
Tell her to stop it and take an herbal remedy until she delivers
ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in pregnancy because of fetal kidney toxicity.
q1m5pq3k: Which lab value is most important to monitor for a client taking losartan?
ARBs can cause hyperkalemia, especially with kidney impairment or potassium supplements.
q1ot0g5f: A client is switched from metoprolol tartrate twice daily to metoprolol succinate once daily. What should the nurse reinforce about the new tablet?
Swallow it whole or split it only on the score line
Chew it so that it starts working more quickly
Dissolve it in water before each of the morning doses
Take it only on days when the pulse is above 80
Metoprolol succinate is an extended-release tablet, so chewing or crushing it releases the whole day of drug at once. Scored succinate tablets may be split in half but not crushed.
qpu5mea: Which statement by a client taking metoprolol indicates that teaching was effective?
I will not stop this medicine suddenly.
I will stop the pills if my pulse goes up.
I will take an extra pill if I feel dizzy.
I can skip doses on days I feel fine.
Abruptly stopping beta blockers can cause rebound tachycardia, hypertension, and angina.
q17ld0fg: A client with diabetes takes atenolol. The nurse reinforces that this drug may:
Hide the fast heartbeat that warns of low blood sugar
Cause blood glucose to rise sharply after meals
Cause the client to feel very thirsty at night
Beta blockers can mask tachycardia and tremor from hypoglycemia; sweating usually remains.
quuzvnc: The nurse reviews the history of a client with a new order for propranolol. Which condition should the nurse report before giving the drug?
Nonselective beta blockers can cause bronchospasm in clients with asthma.
qfxrema: A client starting carvedilol should be taught to:
Rise slowly from lying or sitting
Take it on an empty stomach only
Stop it if the ankles swell at all
Avoid all dairy products while on it
Carvedilol can cause orthostatic hypotension; it is taken with food.
qnu434x: A client on amlodipine 10 mg has ankle edema. Which finding tells the nurse this is the drug rather than fluid overload?
Clear lungs and no weight gain
A 6 pound gain over four days

Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers dilate arterioles and raise capillary pressure in the legs, so fluid leaks locally without any rise in total body fluid. Overload brings weight gain, crackles and neck vein distention.
q1jso2kn: The nurse should help a client taking verapamil prevent which common side effect?
Verapamil commonly causes constipation; encourage fluids and fiber.
q1jsr4ia: A client has trouble swallowing tablets. Which of these ordered drugs may the nurse crush?

Immediate-release tablets such as plain lisinopril can be crushed. Crushing an extended-release nifedipine tablet delivers a whole day of drug at once and can cause severe hypotension and reflex tachycardia.
qhiy56a: A client who has taken clonidine twice daily for a year ran out of the prescription two days ago. Which finding should the nurse expect and report?
Blood pressure 190/110 with headache and agitation
Blood pressure 92/58 with lightheadedness on standing
A heart rate of 48 with a very dry mouth
Drowsiness with pinpoint pupils and nausea

Stopping a central alpha-2 agonist abruptly releases a surge of catecholamines, so pressure and heart rate rebound above baseline within 18 to 36 hours. Drowsiness, dry mouth and bradycardia are effects of taking the drug.
qttfsai: Which statement by a client shows correct use of sublingual nitroglycerin?
If one tablet does not help in 5 minutes, I will call 911.
I will take all three of the tablets at once for severe pain.
I will swallow the tablet with a full glass of water.
I will wait 30 minutes before taking a second tablet.
Pain unrelieved 5 minutes after the first dose may be an infarction rather than angina, so emergency care is called; up to three doses may be taken 5 minutes apart while help is on the way.
q1e3g1tq: How should the nurse teach a client to store sublingual nitroglycerin tablets?
In the original dark glass bottle, tightly capped
In a weekly plastic pill organizer with the other pills
In the refrigerator next to the milk
In a shirt pocket close to the body
Light, heat, moisture, and air reduce potency; keep tablets in the original amber glass container.
qe12hp: A client using a nitroglycerin transdermal patch asks why it is removed at bedtime. The nurse explains that:
A patch-free period helps prevent tolerance to the drug
The patch can cause nightmares if worn while sleeping
Nitroglycerin only works while the client is awake
The skin absorbs too much of the drug at night
A daily nitrate-free interval of 10 to 12 hours prevents tolerance.
qkqhy8m: A client who uses nitroglycerin asks if he can take sildenafil. The nurse reinforces that the combination can cause:
A rapid rise in blood glucose levels
Loss of the effect of both drugs
PDE-5 inhibitors with nitrates can cause profound hypotension.
q1dml7fe: A client starting isosorbide mononitrate reports a headache. The nurse should explain that:
Headache is common and often eases with time
Headache means the drug must be stopped now
Headache is a sign of a stroke from the drug
Headache means the dose is too low to work
Vasodilation causes headache; acetaminophen may be used if approved.
q19dki6r: A client on atorvastatin reports aching weakness in both thighs. Which lab should the nurse expect the provider to order?
Creatine kinase leaks from injured muscle and is the test that separates ordinary aches from statin myopathy. Levels many times the upper limit, especially with dark urine, point to rhabdomyolysis.
q17y0b2v: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client taking simvastatin?
Take it in the evening and avoid grapefruit juice
Take it in the morning with a glass of grapefruit juice
Take it only on days when you eat fatty foods
Take it with an antacid to protect the stomach
Cholesterol synthesis peaks at night; grapefruit raises simvastatin levels and myopathy risk.
q9qcnza: A client takes warfarin for atrial fibrillation. Which INR result should the nurse report as outside the usual goal?
The usual target for atrial fibrillation is an INR of 2 to 3. An INR of 1.3 leaves the client unprotected against stroke, which is as much of a problem as a high INR.
q1at1xan: Which statement by a client taking warfarin indicates that teaching was effective?
I will keep the amount of green leafy vegetables I eat about the same.
I will stop eating all green vegetables for as long as I take this drug.
I can take ibuprofen for my headaches while on this drug.
I will use a straight razor so I do not cut myself.
Consistent vitamin K intake keeps the INR stable; NSAIDs increase bleeding risk.
q14ysv45: A client on warfarin has an elevated INR and minor bleeding. The nurse anticipates an order for which antidote?
Vitamin K reverses warfarin; protamine reverses heparin.
qurv3yv: When giving heparin subcutaneously, the nurse should:
Not aspirate and not massage the site afterward
Aspirate first and massage the site for one minute
Use the deltoid muscle with a 1-inch needle
Rub the site briskly to speed absorption
Aspirating and massaging increase bruising and hematoma formation.
q1ot2ucj: A client receiving heparin shows signs of serious bleeding. Which antidote should the nurse expect?
q1bp5jlc: A client on heparin for five days has a platelet count that fell from 240,000 to 90,000. What is the main danger of this reaction?
A severe drop in blood pressure

Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is an antibody reaction that activates the remaining platelets, so despite the low count the risk is arterial and venous thrombosis. It appears 5 to 10 days after heparin is started.
qzohc0c: When giving enoxaparin from a prefilled syringe, the nurse should:
Leave the air bubble in and inject into the abdomen
Expel the air bubble and inject into the deltoid
Aspirate before injecting to check for blood
Massage the site well after injecting the dose
The air bubble ensures the full dose is given; inject into the abdomen at least 2 inches from the umbilicus without aspirating or rubbing.
qnwrw82: A client receiving enoxaparin after hip surgery should report which finding?
Mild soreness at the injection site
A small bruise at the injection site
Tarry stools suggest GI bleeding. Small bruises at injection sites are common.
qk01d2b: Which statement by a client taking apixaban indicates a need for more teaching?
I will stop it a few days before my dental work on my own.
I will tell my dentist that I take a blood thinner.
I will use a soft toothbrush and an electric razor.
I will report pink urine or bleeding gums right away.
Stopping anticoagulants without provider direction increases clot and stroke risk.
qbl1m3i: A client taking clopidogrel is scheduled for elective surgery. The nurse should:
Make sure the surgeon knows the client takes clopidogrel
Tell the client to double the dose the day before surgery
Tell the client to take it with aspirin on the morning of surgery
Give it with vitamin K to prevent bleeding in surgery
Antiplatelet therapy is usually held about 5 to 7 days before elective surgery per the provider.
q1kyo27i: A parent asks if aspirin can be given to a 10-year-old with chickenpox and fever. The nurse should explain that:
Aspirin should be avoided because of the risk of Reye syndrome
Aspirin is the preferred fever reducer for chickenpox
Aspirin is safe if it is given with milk or food
Aspirin is safe if the child is over 40 pounds
Aspirin in children and teens with viral illness is linked to Reye syndrome.
qwzx4nc: A client who takes high-dose aspirin for arthritis reports ringing in the ears. The nurse recognizes this as a sign of:
Tinnitus is an early sign of aspirin toxicity.
q1lnwtk2: The nurse gives insulin lispro at 0730. When should the client's breakfast be served?
Rapid-acting insulin starts working in about 15 minutes; give it with or just before the meal.
qw68bnu: The nurse gives regular insulin subcutaneously at 0700. The client is most at risk for hypoglycemia at about:
Regular insulin peaks about 2 to 4 hours after an SQ dose.
qe2l6jy: The nurse gives NPH insulin at 0800. The nurse should watch most closely for hypoglycemia:
In the afternoon, about 4 to 12 hours later
At no particular time, because NPH has no peak
NPH is intermediate-acting with a peak around 4 to 12 hours.
qq3eq69: Before drawing up NPH insulin from a vial, the nurse should:
Gently roll the vial between the hands
Shake the vial hard for 30 seconds
Warm the vial in the microwave briefly
Check that the insulin is completely clear
NPH is a cloudy suspension; roll gently to mix without making bubbles.
qesurmh: When mixing regular and NPH insulin in one syringe, the nurse should:
Draw up the clear regular insulin first
Draw up the cloudy NPH insulin first
Draw them up in either order
Shake both vials before drawing up
Clear before cloudy keeps NPH from contaminating the regular insulin vial.
q115kd6h: Which instruction about insulin glargine is correct?
Do not mix it with any other insulin in a syringe
Mix it with regular insulin to reduce the number of injections
Shake it well until it turns cloudy before use
Give it only when the blood glucose is above 300
Glargine is a clear long-acting basal insulin that should not be mixed.
q1d3q9g: How should a client store an opened insulin aspart pen?
At room temperature and discard it after 28 days
In the freezer between doses to keep it fresh
In the glove box of the car for easy access
In the refrigerator and use it for one year
Opened insulin aspart pens are kept at room temperature and discarded after 28 days.
q1c0oywk: A client with diabetes is shaky and sweaty with a fingerstick glucose of 58 mg/dL. The client is alert and can swallow. The nurse should first:
Give the scheduled insulin dose with breakfast
Have the client lie down and recheck in an hour
Call the provider for an order for IV dextrose
Treat conscious hypoglycemia with 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate such as 4 oz of juice, then recheck in 15 minutes.
q1bif622: Which statement by a client about insulin injections indicates that teaching was effective?
I will rotate sites within the same body area.
I will inject in the exact same spot each time.
I will rub the site hard after each injection.
I will inject through my clothes to save time.
Rotating within one area prevents lipohypertrophy and keeps absorption consistent.
q1mkpkpg: A client taking metformin who has an eGFR of 25 mL/min/1.73 m2 is scheduled for a CT scan with iodinated contrast. The nurse anticipates that metformin will be:
Held at the time of the test and for 48 hours after
Given with extra water right before the dye is given
Doubled the day after the test to prevent high glucose
Continued without change on the day of the scan

For clients with an eGFR below 30 or acute kidney injury, metformin is held at the time of contrast and for 48 hours afterward, and kidney function is rechecked before restarting. Clients with stable, normal kidney function usually do not need to stop metformin; follow facility policy.
qt9trh7: A client new to metformin reports nausea and loose stools. The nurse should suggest:
GI upset is common early in therapy; taking metformin with food reduces it. Persistent symptoms should be reported.
qjh1is0: The nurse reinforces teaching for a client taking glipizide. Which side effect is most important to recognize?
Sulfonylureas stimulate insulin release and can cause hypoglycemia, especially with skipped meals.
q1w7q5h9: Which client history should the nurse report before the first dose of semaglutide?
Family history of medullary thyroid cancer
Personal history of a broken wrist
GLP-1 agonists are contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.
qi2jbgr: A family member is taught to give glucagon to an unconscious client with diabetes. After giving it, the family member should:
Turn the client onto the side
Give the client water by mouth
Give a second dose right away
Lay the client flat on the back
Glucagon often causes vomiting; side-lying prevents aspiration. Give oral carbohydrate once the client is awake.
qe4wamy: Which instruction about levothyroxine should the nurse reinforce?
Take it on an empty stomach 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast
Take it with your breakfast and your daily calcium and iron supplements
Take it at bedtime with a glass of milk and a snack
Take it only on days when you feel tired or cold
Food, calcium, and iron reduce absorption; take it at the same time daily with water.
qwyjthz: A client taking levothyroxine reports a racing heart, nervousness, and trouble sleeping. These findings suggest that:
The dose may be too high
The dose may be too low
The client is in an expected adjustment phase
The client is allergic to the tablet dye
Signs of hyperthyroidism suggest excess dosing and should be reported.
q152fypl: A client taking methimazole calls about a fever of 101.5 F and a sore throat. Which test does the nurse expect to be ordered first?
A white cell count with differential
A thyroid stimulating hormone level now
A throat culture for strep only
A liver panel and bilirubin level
Methimazole can cause agranulocytosis, so the neutrophil count is what decides whether this is an ordinary sore throat or a drug reaction requiring the drug to be stopped and the infection treated.
qf2vsi: A client taking prednisone for several weeks asks if he can stop when he feels better. The nurse explains:
The dose must be tapered as ordered by the provider
He can stop as soon as his symptoms are gone
He should stop if his blood sugar goes up
He can stop and restart it as he needs it
Sudden withdrawal after long-term use can cause adrenal insufficiency.
ql56tkk: A client with diabetes starts prednisone. The nurse should expect:
Corticosteroids raise blood glucose; insulin needs may increase.
qpc9yyn: After using a fluticasone inhaler, the client should:
Rinse the mouth with water and spit
Swallow a glass of milk right away
Hold the breath for two full minutes
Use the inhaler again right away
Rinsing reduces the risk of oral thrush and hoarseness.
q1s9d8qm: A client is ordered albuterol and fluticasone inhalers at the same time. The nurse should instruct the client to use:
Albuterol first, then wait before using fluticasone
Fluticasone first, then wait before using albuterol
Both at the same time, mixed in one spacer
Only one of them on any single day
The bronchodilator opens the airways so that the steroid can reach deeper into the lungs.
q1yg10vm: A client reports feeling shaky with a fast heartbeat after using albuterol. The nurse recognizes this as:
A common side effect of the drug
A sign that the dose was too small
A sign that the inhaler is empty
Beta-2 agonists commonly cause tremor and tachycardia.
q1kax8il: Which client action shows correct use of a metered-dose inhaler without a spacer?
Breathes out fully, then inhales slowly while pressing the canister
Inhales quickly and deeply, then presses the canister afterward
Presses the canister twice, then takes one quick shallow breath
Breathes in through the nose while pressing down on the canister
After exhaling, press the canister at the start of a slow, deep breath and hold the breath for about 10 seconds.
qlksayq: Which statement indicates that a client understands teaching about tiotropium?
I use it once a day to keep my airways open.
I use it when I suddenly cannot breathe.
I swallow the capsule with a glass of water.
I use it only when my asthma flares up badly.
Tiotropium is a long-acting maintenance bronchodilator, not a rescue drug; capsules are inhaled, not swallowed.
qajpj34: A client asks if salmeterol can be used during a sudden asthma attack. The nurse's best response is:
No, it is a long-acting maintenance drug, not a rescue inhaler
Yes, it works within seconds and is the best choice for a sudden attack
Yes, but only if the client uses two puffs at once
No, it should only be used with a nebulizer
Salmeterol is a long-acting beta agonist; a short-acting drug such as albuterol is used for rescue.
qyi2vg7: The nurse reinforces that the family of a child taking montelukast should report:
Changes in mood, behavior, or sleep
Increased appetite and thirst at dinnertime
Montelukast has a boxed warning for neuropsychiatric events.
q3avs2l: A client taking amoxicillin for strep throat feels better after 3 days. Which statement indicates the need for more teaching?
I will save the rest of the pills for next time.
I will take every pill until the bottle is empty.
I will call if I get a rash or trouble breathing.
I will call if I have many watery stools a day.
Stopping antibiotics early promotes resistance and relapse.
q6gah04: Before giving the first dose of amoxicillin, which question is most important for the nurse to ask?
Have you ever had a reaction to penicillin?
Have you eaten anything in the last hour?
Do you have trouble swallowing large pills?
Have you had a flu shot this year?
Amoxicillin is a penicillin; a penicillin allergy can cause anaphylaxis.
q9gcc6w: A client on clindamycin has had many watery stools and tests positive for C. difficile. Which order should the nurse question?
An order for loperamide to slow the stools
An order for oral vancomycin given by mouth
An order to use contact precautions
An order for IV fluids with potassium
Slowing the bowel keeps the toxin in contact with the colon and raises the risk of ileus and toxic megacolon. Oral vancomycin, contact precautions and fluid replacement are the expected orders.
qsb89gj: A client takes ciprofloxacin, calcium carbonate, ferrous sulfate and levothyroxine. How should the nurse schedule the ciprofloxacin?
At least 2 hours before the calcium and iron
At the same time as the calcium and iron
With a large glass of milk at each dose
Only after an antacid to protect the stomach lining
Calcium, iron and other metal ions bind fluoroquinolones in the gut and can cut absorption enough to cause treatment failure, so doses are separated by about 2 hours before or 6 hours after.
q1su769b: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client taking doxycycline?
Use sunscreen and stay upright after each dose
Take it with milk to protect the stomach lining
Take it lying down at bedtime with little water
Take it with an antacid to prevent heartburn
Doxycycline causes photosensitivity and esophageal ulceration; dairy and antacids reduce absorption.
q5mkuz5: Which statement by a client taking metronidazole indicates understanding of the teaching?
I will not drink any alcohol while taking this.
I will take this pill with a glass of wine.
I can drink beer once I finish half the pills.
I should avoid all dairy products while on this.
Alcohol can cause a disulfiram-like reaction; avoid it during therapy and for at least 3 days after.
qg3nadq: A client taking nitrofurantoin for a UTI reports dark brown urine. The nurse should explain that:
This is a harmless, expected color change
This means the infection has spread to the kidney
This is a sign of liver damage, so stop the drug
This means the client is very dehydrated
Nitrofurantoin can turn urine rust-yellow to brown. Report cough, chest pain, or numbness.
q1ryfs4q: How should the nurse teach a client to take nitrofurantoin?
With food or milk to reduce stomach upset
On an empty stomach with an antacid
Only at bedtime with very little water
Only on days with urinary burning
Food improves absorption and reduces GI upset.
q1wy3u72: A client on gentamicin reports ringing in the ears and feels unsteady when walking. Which statement about this effect is correct?
Hearing and balance damage is often permanent
It clears within a day of the last dose
It is prevented by giving the dose along with food
It is a sign that the dose is too low
Aminoglycosides accumulate in the hair cells of the inner ear and destroy them, so hearing and balance loss may not recover, while kidney injury from the same drugs usually does.
q73lfkg: A client on gentamicin has a rising serum creatinine and decreasing urine output. The nurse recognizes possible:
Aminoglycosides are toxic to the kidneys; monitor creatinine, BUN, and urine output.
q18v1yqw: A trough level is ordered for a client receiving gentamicin. When should the blood be drawn?
Just before the next scheduled dose
Right after the dose finishes infusing
One hour after the dose is started
At any time on the same day
The trough is the lowest level, drawn just before the next dose.
q1w5ovch: A client flushes bright red over the face and chest 10 minutes into a vancomycin infusion. What explains this reaction?
A direct release of histamine from a fast infusion
An antibody reaction to a previous exposure
A sudden fall in platelets caused by the drug
An irritant effect on the lining of the vein being used

Vancomycin flushing reaction is a rate-related, non-immune release of histamine from mast cells, so it is managed by slowing the infusion to at least 60 minutes per gram rather than by labeling the client allergic.
q1vfl5g: How should the nurse teach a client to use nystatin oral suspension for thrush?
Swish it in the mouth, then swallow it
Swallow it quickly with a glass of milk
Spit it out right after it is measured
Mix it in juice and drink it with meals
Holding the suspension in the mouth provides the contact time needed to treat oral candidiasis.
q10pu3r3: A client asks how soon oseltamivir should be started for the flu. The nurse explains it works best when started:
After a fever lasts more than a week
When the cough begins to improve
Oseltamivir is most effective when started early; early treatment shortens the illness.
q9dt4df: Which instruction about ferrous sulfate tablets should the nurse reinforce?
Take it with orange juice and expect dark stools
Take it with milk and expect light gray stools
Take it with antacids to prevent stomach upset
Take it with tea and report any black stools
Vitamin C improves absorption; dark green-black stools are expected.
q1xa8ehk: A child is prescribed liquid ferrous sulfate. The nurse teaches the parent to:
Give it through a straw and brush the teeth afterward
Mix it into a full bottle of formula
Give it with a glass of milk to mask the taste
Give it only when the child is not eating
Liquid iron can stain the teeth.
qq7r85e: Which statement by a client taking alendronate indicates that teaching was effective?
I will sit or stand upright for 30 minutes after I take it.
I will take it at bedtime so I can lie down right after.
I will take it with my breakfast and morning coffee.
I will take it with a glass of milk for the calcium.
Alendronate is taken with a full glass of plain water on an empty stomach, and the client stays upright for 30 minutes to prevent esophagitis.
qc4ey4t: A client takes calcium carbonate and levothyroxine. The nurse should instruct the client to:
Take them at least 4 hours apart
Take them together to save time
Take them both with a glass of milk
Take the calcium first, then the levothyroxine right after
Calcium binds levothyroxine and lowers its absorption.
q1q9e425: Magnesium hydroxide should be used cautiously in a client with:
Impaired kidneys cannot excrete magnesium, leading to toxicity.
qafhch1: A client starting oxycodone for pain is also prescribed docusate. The nurse explains that docusate is given to:
Soften stools and prevent opioid constipation
Increase the pain relief provided by the oxycodone
Prevent nausea from the opioid medication
Reduce the risk of respiratory depression
Opioids cause constipation; stool softeners and stimulant laxatives are given preventively.
quup7px: A client asks how sennosides work. The nurse explains that sennosides:
Stimulate the bowel to move stool along
Draw water into the stool by osmosis only
Coat the bowel to slow down diarrhea
Neutralize stomach acid to stop heartburn
Senna is a stimulant laxative; it may cause cramping.
q1g92hrk: The provider orders metoprolol tartrate 25 mg PO. Scored 50 mg tablets are available. How many tablets should the nurse give?
25 mg divided by 50 mg per tablet equals 0.5 tablet.
qtpduhc: Amoxicillin 375 mg PO is ordered. The suspension is 250 mg per 5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
375 mg divided by 250 mg, times 5 mL, equals 7.5 mL.
q1b78d9b: Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg SQ every 12 hours is ordered for a client who weighs 80 kg. What is each dose?
1 mg times 80 kg equals 80 mg per dose.
qkq3yfw: Heparin 5,000 units SQ is ordered. The vial contains 10,000 units per mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
5,000 units divided by 10,000 units per mL equals 0.5 mL.
qomr7wb: Digoxin 0.125 mg PO is ordered. The tablets on hand are 0.25 mg. How many tablets should the nurse give?
0.125 mg divided by 0.25 mg equals 0.5 tablet. Count the apical pulse first.
qhvsoa7: Levothyroxine 0.1 mg is ordered. The available tablets are 50 mcg. How many tablets should the nurse give?
0.1 mg equals 100 mcg; 100 divided by 50 equals 2 tablets.
q10kqbks: A child weighing 16 kg is ordered acetaminophen 15 mg/kg PO. The liquid is 160 mg per 5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
15 mg times 16 kg equals 240 mg; 240 divided by 160, times 5 mL, equals 7.5 mL.
qieemv0: A client on a stable lithium dose now has a level of 1.9 mEq/L and a coarse tremor. Which recent change best explains the rise?
Starting a daily multivitamin with iron
Adding a second and third cup of coffee each morning

Thiazides make the kidney reabsorb lithium along with sodium, which raises the level above the usual maintenance range of 0.6 to 1.2 mEq/L. NSAIDs and ACE inhibitors do the same; acetaminophen does not.
qmkna1s: Which statement by a client taking lithium indicates teaching was effective?
I will keep my salt intake steady and drink plenty of fluids.
I will cut all salt out of my diet to stay well.
I will drink very little water to avoid swelling.
I will take extra pills whenever I exercise outside in hot weather.
Low sodium intake or dehydration raises lithium levels; 2 to 3 L of fluid daily is commonly recommended.
q11o7cnl: A client taking phenytoin has a level of 28 mcg/mL and is unsteady with nystagmus. The nurse recognizes these findings as:
Signs of a new ear infection
The usual total phenytoin range is 10 to 20 mcg/mL.
q4ji4jv: Which teaching should the nurse reinforce for a client taking phenytoin long term?
Brush and floss well and see a dentist regularly
Expect the urine to turn bright orange
Avoid all foods that contain vitamin K, such as spinach
Take it only when a seizure begins, then stop again
Gingival hyperplasia is common; good oral hygiene helps reduce it.
qnp8pd3: A client taking carbamazepine should report which symptom right away?
Fever, sore throat, or a blistering rash
Mild drowsiness during the first week
Slight dizziness when first starting it
Carbamazepine can cause blood dyscrasias and Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
qv6kb1t: A woman of childbearing age is starting valproic acid. The nurse reinforces that she should:
Use reliable birth control, since it can cause birth defects
Stop taking it on her own as soon as she misses a period
Take extra iron daily to protect any future pregnancy from harm
Avoid all exercise while on this medication
Valproate is a major teratogen (neural tube defects); pregnancy plans must be discussed with the provider.
qwlysnl: A client taking levetiracetam should be taught to report:
New mood changes, irritability, or depression
Mild tiredness during the first few weeks of treatment
A slightly increased appetite at meals
Occasional mild headaches in the morning
Levetiracetam can cause behavior changes and suicidal thoughts.
q1t9rnks: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for an older adult taking gabapentin?
Rise slowly and use caution; it can cause dizziness
Take it with antacids to improve how well it is absorbed
Stop it abruptly if the pain goes away
Drink alcohol only in small amounts with it
Gabapentin causes dizziness and sedation that raise fall risk; antacids reduce absorption, and it is tapered to stop.
q1wumjl2: A client taking sertraline and tramadol becomes agitated, sweaty, and feverish, with muscle twitching. The nurse suspects:
Combining serotonergic drugs can cause serotonin syndrome; report it immediately.
qacd6xe: A teenager is starting fluoxetine for depression. The nurse reinforces that the family should watch for:
New or worse thoughts of suicide
Mild weight gain in the first week
Antidepressants carry a boxed warning for suicidality in children and young adults.
q1baanx3: A client taking an MAO inhibitor, such as high-dose selegiline, should avoid which food?
Tyramine-rich foods such as aged cheese and cured meats can cause hypertensive crisis with MAOIs.
q1xhefde: An older adult taking amitriptyline is at increased risk for:
Diarrhea, excess saliva, and small pupils
High blood glucose and frequent thirst
Tricyclics are strongly anticholinergic and are on the Beers list for older adults.
q1p083rc: An 82-year-old client asks for diphenhydramine to help with sleep. The nurse recognizes that this drug may cause:
Confusion and urinary retention in older adults
Diarrhea and increased saliva in older adults
Improved memory and alertness the next day
Its anticholinergic effects place it on the Beers list for older adults.
qxgte8p: Which side effect should the nurse expect in a client taking oxybutynin?
Anticholinergic effects are common; older adults are also at risk for confusion.
q3uv4i2: A client taking haloperidol develops neck stiffness and upward deviation of the eyes. The nurse recognizes this as:
A seizure from low blood sugar
An allergic reaction to the dye
A normal sign of improving psychosis
Dystonia is an extrapyramidal effect; report promptly, as diphenhydramine or benztropine may be ordered.
q1208035: A client taking risperidone develops a high fever, severe muscle rigidity, and confusion. The nurse should suspect:
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) is a medical emergency; report it immediately.
qr7vl9i: The nurse should reinforce monitoring of which values for a client taking olanzapine long term?
Bone density and serum calcium levels
Second-generation antipsychotics can cause weight gain and metabolic syndrome.
qks2e9: A client on clozapine has an absolute neutrophil count of 900 per microliter. What does the nurse expect to happen?
The drug is held and the count is rechecked
The dose is doubled in order to finish the course
The count is rechecked in three months
The drug is continued with a fever check
Clozapine causes severe neutropenia, so counts are monitored on a set schedule. An ANC under 1000 per microliter means the drug is interrupted, and below 500 it is usually stopped for good.
qw34mgi: A client receiving lorazepam is very drowsy with a respiratory rate of 8. The nurse anticipates which reversal agent?
Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepine sedation; support the airway first.
q109jcuq: Which statement by a client taking alprazolam indicates a need for more teaching?
A glass of wine at night will help it work better.
I will not drive until I know how it affects me.
I will not stop this drug suddenly on my own.
I will tell my provider if I feel very sleepy during the day.
Alcohol adds to CNS and respiratory depression.
q5dmamg: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client taking zolpidem?
Take it just before bed if 7 to 8 hours of sleep are possible
Take it after dinner and then finish the evening chores
Take it with a large meal to make it work faster
Take it in the morning so it will prevent any daytime drowsiness
Complex sleep behaviors and next-day impairment can occur; food delays onset.
q138w4ea: Which client history should the nurse report before giving bupropion?
Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated with bulimia or anorexia.
qrw0akn: A male client taking trazodone should report which side effect immediately?
A painful erection lasting more than 4 hours
A dry mouth during the day
Mild dizziness when standing up quickly from bed
q11rgqa: The nurse should check which vital sign before giving donepezil to an older adult?
Heart rate, because it can cause bradycardia
Temperature, because it often causes fever
Oxygen saturation, because it often lowers it
Respiratory rate, because it causes apnea
Cholinesterase inhibitors increase vagal tone and can cause bradycardia and syncope.
q1g05aj4: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client taking carbidopa-levodopa?
Avoid high-protein meals at the time of doses
Take it with a high-protein meal each time
Expect the urine to turn bright blue or green
Stop it suddenly if dizziness occurs
Protein competes with levodopa for absorption; urine or sweat may darken. The drug should never be stopped abruptly.
q178w9k7: Which change in a client receiving scheduled morphine appears earliest and warns of respiratory depression?
Increasing sedation and difficulty staying awake
A respiratory rate that has fallen to 8
A drop in the oxygen saturation down to 88 percent
Sedation comes before respiratory depression, which is why a sedation scale is checked with every opioid dose. By the time the rate is 8 or the saturation has fallen, the problem is already advanced.
q9drwl7: After naloxone is given for an opioid overdose, the nurse should monitor closely because:
Naloxone may wear off before the opioid does
Naloxone causes long periods of deep sleep
Naloxone causes the blood glucose to drop fast
Naloxone often causes a severe allergic rash
Respiratory depression can return; repeat doses may be needed.
q12cfgm4: Which teaching is most important for a client going home on oxycodone?
Always take it on an empty stomach
Drink very little fluid with each dose
Take an extra dose if pain is moderate
Combining CNS depressants increases the risk of respiratory depression.
qzfo5x4: A client takes hydrocodone-acetaminophen and asks about adding over-the-counter acetaminophen (Tylenol) for a headache. The nurse explains that:
Total acetaminophen from all sources must stay under the daily limit
Tylenol is safe as often as needed, because it is a completely different drug
Tylenol will reverse the effects of the hydrocodone
Tylenol should be taken with alcohol for best effect
Combination products contain acetaminophen; adults generally should not exceed 4 g daily, and a limit of 3 g is often advised.
quapmcm: A client using a fentanyl transdermal patch should be taught to:
Avoid heating pads and hot tubs over the patch
Cut the patch in half when a lower dose is needed
Apply a heating pad to speed up pain relief
Throw used patches in the open trash can
Heat increases absorption and can cause overdose; fold used patches sticky sides together and dispose per instructions.
q1upoid4: Which client history should the nurse report before giving tramadol?
q13wxeam: A toddler swallowed a large amount of acetaminophen. The nurse anticipates which antidote?
Acetylcysteine protects the liver after acetaminophen overdose.
q1hbdg8m: A client with osteoarthritis takes lisinopril, furosemide and warfarin. Why does the nurse question a standing order for ibuprofen?
It raises bleeding risk and can worsen kidney function
It makes the furosemide work too strongly
It blocks the absorption of both the lisinopril and the warfarin
It raises the blood level of the warfarin

NSAIDs block the prostaglandins that maintain renal blood flow, so with an ACE inhibitor and a diuretic this is a well-known cause of acute kidney injury. Ibuprofen also impairs platelets on top of warfarin.
qn50kf9: Celecoxib should be questioned in a client with an allergy to:
q1928z7s: A client taking methadone is at risk for which cardiac problem that may need ECG monitoring?
Methadone prolongs the QT interval and can cause torsades de pointes.
qhoqz2: When should the nurse give a once-daily dose of omeprazole?
With the evening meal and a snack
At bedtime with a glass of milk
Proton pump inhibitors work best before the first meal.
q1pj16qa: A client takes sucralfate and several other oral drugs. The nurse should:
Give sucralfate on an empty stomach; space other drugs 2 hours apart
Give all of the drugs together with sucralfate at breakfast
Mix sucralfate with an antacid and give it along with the other drugs
Give sucralfate only after meals with the other drugs
Sucralfate binds other drugs; give it 1 hour before meals and separate it from other drugs.
q1hld9s8: An older adult on famotidine has become confused. Which value best explains why the drug is involved?
A hemoglobin of 11.8 g per deciliter
A serum sodium level of 139 mEq/L
Famotidine is cleared by the kidney, so with a clearance under about 50 mL/min the drug accumulates and crosses into the brain and causes confusion. The dose is reduced or the interval lengthened.
qw3v23f: Before giving ondansetron, which client history should the nurse report?
Ondansetron can prolong the QT interval.
q1na2qkq: A client taking metoclopramide develops lip smacking and tongue thrusting. The nurse should:
Report it; it may be tardive dyskinesia
Give the next dose early to stop it
Document it as a sign of anxiety
Offer gum to chew and continue the drug as ordered
Metoclopramide has a boxed warning for tardive dyskinesia, which may be irreversible.
qkbjhxg: Promethazine should not be given to:
A child under 2 years of age
Promethazine can cause fatal respiratory depression in children under 2.
q145rg0x: A client with bloody diarrhea and fever asks for loperamide. The nurse should:
Report the symptoms before giving any antidiarrheal
Give it right away to stop the diarrhea quickly
Give double the dose because the stools are bloody
Give it with a laxative to balance the effect
Antidiarrheals may worsen infectious diarrhea such as C. difficile infection.
q1fzqy5z: Which instruction about bisacodyl tablets is correct?
Swallow them whole and avoid milk or antacids within 1 hour
Chew them well before swallowing for faster bowel relief
Take them with a glass of milk to protect the stomach
Crush the tablets and mix them into applesauce or pudding
The enteric coating prevents stomach irritation; milk and antacids can dissolve it too early.
qfgj64s: A client with cirrhosis is taking lactulose. Which finding shows the drug is working?
Two to three soft stools daily and clearer thinking
No bowel movement for three days and less confusion
Hard stools once a week and better appetite
Darker yellow skin and more sleepiness each day
Lactulose lowers ammonia by trapping it in the bowel and causing soft stools.
q189bu93: How should the nurse teach a client to take polyethylene glycol powder for constipation?
Dissolve it in 4 to 8 ounces of a beverage
Swallow the dry powder, then drink a glass of water
Sprinkle it on food without any liquid
Mix it with a tablespoon of water only
The usual 17 g dose is dissolved in 4 to 8 ounces of liquid.
q1wpb711: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client taking allopurinol?
Drink plenty of fluids and report any skin rash
Limit fluids to less than 1 liter a day
Take it only during an acute gout attack, then stop
Take it with aspirin for better results
Fluids help prevent kidney stones; a rash may precede a severe reaction.
qjxn60n: A client starting colchicine for a gout flare asks how much to take. The nurse reinforces that the dose:
Stops when diarrhea or vomiting begins
Continues until the joint pain is gone
Is doubled on the first day of the flare
Is taken every two hours until relief

Diarrhea and vomiting are the signal that the cumulative colchicine dose has been reached, and going past that point causes marrow suppression and neuropathy. Flare dosing is 1.2 mg, then 0.6 mg an hour later.
q19nwgj: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client taking tamsulosin?
Rise slowly, especially after the first dose
Take it on an empty stomach at bedtime only
Expect the urine to turn reddish-orange
Avoid all dairy products while on it
Orthostatic hypotension can occur; it is taken 30 minutes after the same meal each day.
q1jvouo3: The pregnant wife of a client taking finasteride asks about the drug. The nurse reinforces that she should:
Not handle crushed or broken tablets
Take one tablet each day for her hair
Avoid sitting in the same room as him
Store the tablets in the refrigerator
Finasteride can harm a male fetus if absorbed.
q1vczty4: A client taking empagliflozin should be taught to report:
Genital itching, painful urination, or burning
Increased appetite and gradual weight gain over time
Mild constipation and bloating after meals
SGLT2 inhibitors increase genital yeast and urinary infections; also report signs of ketoacidosis.
q100c9qt: Which finding should the nurse report for a client taking pioglitazone?
Weight gain of 2 kg in 3 days with ankle swelling
Fasting glucose of 112 mg/dL in the morning
Mild hunger before meals during the day and evening
Pioglitazone causes fluid retention and can worsen heart failure.
q46z7e: A client taking acarbose and glipizide has hypoglycemia. The nurse should give:
Acarbose blocks breakdown of sucrose and complex carbohydrates, so glucose is needed.
quarc6t: A client asks why insulin detemir is not mixed with rapid-acting insulin in the same syringe. The nurse explains:
Mixing can change how each insulin works
It turns cloudy and loses all its effect
It must be mixed only with NPH insulin
It can be mixed if both are cold
Long-acting insulins such as detemir and glargine are not mixed with other insulins.
qjp59wl: A client takes sitagliptin alone for type 2 diabetes. What should the nurse teach about low blood sugar on this drug?
It is uncommon unless another diabetes drug is added
It happens most mornings and needs a bedtime snack
It is prevented by taking the dose with a large full meal
It is the most common side effect of this drug
DPP-4 inhibitors prolong incretin hormones that act only while glucose is rising, so they rarely cause hypoglycemia alone. The risk appears when they are combined with a sulfonylurea or insulin.
qjqh7rh: A parent is learning to use an epinephrine auto-injector on a child. Which part of the technique does the nurse reinforce?
Hold it against the outer thigh for about 3 seconds
Rub the thigh briskly for a minute afterward
Aim for the fleshy part of the upper arm
Give it only through bare skin and not through clothing

The device needs a few seconds of contact for the full dose to leave the spring-loaded syringe. It goes into the anterolateral thigh and works through clothing, which is why it can be used right away.
q7hx83v: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client taking amiodarone long term?
Use sunscreen; report any new cough or shortness of breath
Drink grapefruit juice daily to improve the drug's absorption
Expect a new cough as a harmless side effect
Stop the drug if the skin looks bluish-gray
Amiodarone can cause pulmonary toxicity, photosensitivity, and thyroid and liver problems.
qbixf24: Which statement by a client taking rivaroxaban indicates the need for more teaching?
I can take naproxen when my back hurts.
I will take it with my evening meal.
I will tell my dentist about this drug.
I will report red or black stools.
NSAIDs raise bleeding risk; the 15 and 20 mg doses are taken with food.
q114h2rj: How should a client store and take dabigatran capsules?
Keep them in the original bottle and swallow them whole
Open the capsules and sprinkle the beads on soft food
Move them to a weekly pill organizer to keep track of doses
Chew the capsules for faster absorption
Opening capsules increases absorption and bleeding; moisture degrades the drug.
q1ae63j: A client taking valsartan reports lightheadedness when getting out of bed. The nurse should teach the client to:
Sit at the edge of the bed before standing
Get up quickly to raise the blood pressure
Skip doses on days with dizziness
Take the dose with a high-salt snack
Orthostatic hypotension is reduced by changing positions slowly.
q1afyab1: Which lab value should the nurse report for a client taking ramipril?
q1595skp: A client taking desmopressin reports headache, nausea, and confusion. The nurse suspects:
q1ra4dcn: A client with chronic alcohol use is ordered thiamine and IV dextrose. The nurse understands that thiamine is usually given:
Before or with glucose to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy
Only after the dextrose infusion has been completely finished
Only if the client has a seizure
Only after the client eats a full meal
Glucose without thiamine can precipitate Wernicke encephalopathy.
q11qoeoe: A client taking patiromer also takes other oral medications. The nurse should:
Separate other oral drugs from patiromer by at least 3 hours
Give all the drugs together with patiromer
Mix the other drugs into the patiromer suspension before giving it
Give patiromer only at night on an empty stomach
Patiromer binds other drugs in the gut.
qr016b5: Before giving epoetin alfa, the nurse should check:
Blood glucose level and urine ketones
Epoetin raises blood pressure, and a high hemoglobin increases clot risk.
q876a49: A transplant client taking tacrolimus should be taught to:
Avoid grapefruit and take doses at the same times daily
Stop it after feeling well for a month
Double the dose after missing one
Take each dose with grapefruit juice to improve absorption
Grapefruit raises tacrolimus levels; consistent timing keeps levels steady.
q19oe3h3: Which statement by a client taking mycophenolate indicates a need for more teaching?
I do not need birth control while on this drug.
I will avoid people who are sick when I can.
I will report fever or sore throat quickly.
I will keep all of my scheduled blood test appointments.
Mycophenolate causes birth defects and requires effective contraception.
q1l3ayjl: A client taking baclofen asks about stopping it. The nurse explains:
It must be tapered, as sudden stopping can cause seizures
It can be stopped at any time without any withdrawal problems
It should be stopped if drowsiness occurs
It should be held before each meal
Abrupt withdrawal can cause seizures and hallucinations.
q1usas3g: An older adult taking cyclobenzaprine should be monitored most closely for:
Increased appetite and thirst at night
Cyclobenzaprine is sedating and anticholinergic and is on the Beers list.
q1wjyksq: A client has a lidocaine 5% patch ordered for back pain. The nurse should:
Apply it for up to 12 hours, then remove it for 12 hours
Leave it on for 3 full days before changing it
Apply it over broken skin for faster relief
Use a heating pad over the patch to improve its numbing effect
The usual schedule is 12 hours on and 12 hours off on intact skin.
qf4swu3: An older adult taking levofloxacin and prednisone is at increased risk for:
Age over 60 and corticosteroids increase fluoroquinolone tendon rupture risk.
q12x7hez: A client taking trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole should be taught to:
Drink plenty of fluids and report any rash
Limit fluids to avoid frequent urination
Take it with antacids to prevent nausea
Stop it as soon as the burning with urination stops
Fluids prevent crystalluria; a rash can signal Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
qs1n400: Furosemide 40 mg PO is ordered. The oral solution is 10 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
40 mg divided by 10 mg per mL equals 4 mL.
q1dulu4m: A client is to receive 6 units of regular insulin and 14 units of NPH insulin mixed in one syringe. What total dose will be in the syringe?
6 plus 14 equals 20 units; draw up the clear regular insulin first.
q6myh9z: Potassium chloride oral solution 40 mEq is ordered. The solution is 20 mEq per 15 mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
40 mEq divided by 20 mEq, times 15 mL, equals 30 mL. Dilute before giving.
qiw545: Morphine 4 mg SQ is ordered. The vial is 10 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
4 mg divided by 10 mg per mL equals 0.4 mL.
q18o720b: Before giving any medication, the nurse identifies the client using:
Two identifiers, such as full name and date of birth
The room and bed numbers posted on the door
The name on the chart hanging at the bedside
A question asking whether the client is the right person
Two identifiers are required; a room number is never an identifier.
qckdndw: A client asks the nurse to crush an extended-release tablet because it is hard to swallow. The nurse should:
