Do not crush it; ask the provider or pharmacist about another form
Crush it and mix it with a small amount of applesauce
Crush it and dissolve it in warm water before giving it to the client
Cut it in half and have the client take both halves
Crushing extended-release, enteric-coated, or sublingual products alters release and can cause toxicity or loss of effect.
q1d2nufp: To measure a liquid medication in a medicine cup, the nurse should read the dose:
At eye level at the bottom of the meniscus
Looking down at the top of the meniscus
While holding the cup up toward the light
At the highest point the liquid touches the cup
Set the cup on a flat surface and read at eye level at the lowest point of the curve.
qziuarc: A parent plans to give a child's liquid medicine with a kitchen teaspoon. The nurse should recommend:
An oral dosing syringe or marked dosing cup
A larger soup spoon for more accurate dosing
Pouring the dose into the child's bottle
Mixing the dose into a full cup of juice
Household spoons vary in size and cause dosing errors.
qh1dkgf: The nurse discovers that she gave a client the wrong medication. After checking the client, the nurse should:
Notify the RN or provider and file an incident report per policy
Document the error in the client's chart in the form of an incident report
Wait to see whether the client develops any side effects
Tell no one if the client shows no signs of a problem
Client safety comes first, followed by notification and reporting; the incident report is not mentioned in the client's chart.
qz8up0q: A client refuses a scheduled medication. The nurse should first:
Ask the client about the reason for refusing
Hide the medication in the client's food
Tell the client the provider will be upset if it is not taken
Leave the pill at the bedside for later
Explore the reason, reinforce teaching, then document and report the refusal. Clients have the right to refuse.
qg49wi1: Before giving a rectal suppository to an adult, the nurse should position the client:
On the left side with the upper knee bent
On the right side with both legs straight
Flat on the back with the knees raised
Sitting upright on the toilet or commode
The left Sims position follows the natural curve of the rectum and sigmoid colon.
q15bgs5b: When applying a new transdermal medication patch, the nurse should:
Remove the old patch; apply the new one to a clean, hairless site
Apply the new patch on top of the old one
Shave the site closely and apply a layer of lotion before the patch
Apply the new patch to the exact same site each time
Remove old patches to prevent overdose, and rotate sites to prevent irritation.
q1bpvm3w: Prednisone 60 mg PO is ordered. Tablets on hand are 20 mg. How many tablets should the nurse give?
60 mg divided by 20 mg per tablet equals 3 tablets.
q187wrbe: A child weighs 22 lb. Ibuprofen 10 mg/kg PO is ordered. The suspension is 100 mg per 5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
22 lb divided by 2.2 equals 10 kg; 10 mg times 10 kg equals 100 mg, which is 5 mL.
q13dai4c: Cephalexin 500 mg PO is ordered. Capsules on hand are 250 mg. How many capsules should the nurse give?
500 mg divided by 250 mg equals 2 capsules.
qispuib: Ondansetron 8 mg PO is ordered. Orally disintegrating tablets on hand are 4 mg. How many tablets should the nurse give?
8 mg divided by 4 mg equals 2 tablets; place them on the tongue to dissolve.
q141xfrz: Hydromorphone 1 mg SQ is ordered. The vial is 2 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
1 mg divided by 2 mg per mL equals 0.5 mL.
qmfteir: Lithium carbonate 600 mg PO is ordered. Capsules on hand are 300 mg. How many capsules should the nurse give?
600 mg divided by 300 mg equals 2 capsules.
q138b1j2: Guaifenesin 200 mg PO is ordered. The syrup is 100 mg per 5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
200 mg divided by 100 mg, times 5 mL, equals 10 mL.
qji946u: Warfarin 7.5 mg PO is ordered. Scored tablets on hand are 5 mg. How many tablets should the nurse give?
7.5 mg divided by 5 mg equals 1.5 tablets.
q1mm08pw: Insulin glargine 0.2 units/kg SQ daily is ordered for a client who weighs 90 kg. How many units should the client receive?
q1bn7rle: A 15 kg child is ordered amoxicillin 40 mg/kg/day PO divided every 12 hours. How many mg should the child receive per dose?
40 mg times 15 kg equals 600 mg per day; divided into 2 doses, this equals 300 mg per dose.
q1vgmprz: A client weighs 154 lb. What is the client's weight in kilograms?
qwyimau: While preparing medications, the nurse drops a tablet on the floor. The nurse should:
Discard it per policy and obtain a new dose
Wipe it off and give it to the client
Put it back in the stock bottle
Give it only if the floor was recently cleaned
A contaminated dose is discarded per policy; controlled substances need a witnessed waste.
qpy172m: When instilling eye drops, the nurse should:
Drop the medication into the lower conjunctival sac
Drop the medication directly onto the center of the cornea
Touch the dropper tip to the eyelid to steady it
Have the client blink hard right after the drop
Afterward, gentle pressure on the inner corner of the eye limits systemic absorption.
q1i8ugt2: To give ear drops to a 2-year-old, the nurse should pull the pinna:
In children under 3, pulling the pinna down and back straightens the ear canal.
q1ajnl06: When giving an IM injection using the Z-track method, the nurse should:
Pull the skin aside, inject, and release it after removing the needle
Massage the site firmly after injecting
Inject the drug into the subcutaneous fat layer of the abdomen instead
Use the same needle that was used to draw up the drug
Z-track seals the drug in the muscle and prevents leakage into the subcutaneous tissue.
q1ae10uh: Which site is preferred for an IM injection in most adults?
The ventrogluteal site is away from major nerves and blood vessels.
q1190fvw: A pregnant client asks which over-the-counter drug is generally preferred for a mild headache. The nurse reinforces that it is usually:
NSAIDs are generally avoided in pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks.
qohfvls: A nurse is titrating a continuous heparin infusion by protocol. Which result shows the infusion is in the usual therapeutic range?

Heparin is titrated to an aPTT about 1.5 to 2.5 times control, roughly 60 to 90 seconds in most labs. The INR tracks warfarin rather than heparin, and a normal platelet count says nothing about whether the dose is therapeutic.
q1w0ujgv: Heparin 25,000 units in 250 mL D5W is ordered to infuse at 1,000 units/hr. At what rate should the nurse set the pump?
25,000 units / 250 mL = 100 units/mL; 1,000 units/hr divided by 100 units/mL = 10 mL/hr.
q15l8t0f: A heparin protocol calls for 18 units/kg/hr for a client weighing 80 kg. The bag contains 25,000 units in 500 mL. What rate should the nurse program?
q1274ndh: A heparin bolus of 80 units/kg is ordered for a client who weighs 80 kg. The vial contains 5,000 units/mL. How many mL should the nurse draw up?
80 units x 80 kg = 6,400 units; 6,400 divided by 5,000 units/mL = 1.28 mL.
q1yu4af4: The nurse prepares protamine sulfate for a client with a heparin overdose. Which administration technique is correct?
Give it slowly IV, no faster than 5 mg per minute
Give it rapidly IV push so it binds heparin quickly
Add it to the running heparin bag so the two drugs neutralize
Give it deep IM in the ventrogluteal site to avoid hypotension
Rapid protamine can cause severe hypotension, bradycardia, and anaphylactoid reactions; it is given slowly IV.
q1ogi9q7: The nurse teaches a client to self-inject enoxaparin at home. Which statement indicates that the client understands the teaching?
I will leave the air bubble in the prefilled syringe.
I will rub the site well afterward to spread the drug.
I will inject it into my thigh muscle at a 90-degree angle.
I will pull back on the plunger to check for blood first.
The air bubble is left in to keep all the drug in the tissue; rubbing and aspirating increase bruising.
qqxglec: A client receiving enoxaparin for 7 days has new lab results. Which finding should the nurse report immediately?
aPTT of 34 seconds compared with 31 seconds at baseline
Hemoglobin of 13.2 g/dL, unchanged from admission
A platelet drop of more than 50% suggests heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, which needs prompt evaluation.
q72jj45: A client received enoxaparin and had an epidural catheter removed earlier today. Which finding requires immediate action?
New numbness and weakness in both legs
Mild soreness at the former catheter site
A small bruise at the abdominal injection site
Pain rated 3 out of 10 on the incision
Neuraxial anesthesia with low-molecular-weight heparin can cause a spinal or epidural hematoma; new neurologic deficits are an emergency.
q1k9z9lo: A client is started on warfarin while the heparin infusion continues. Why is heparin kept running for about five more days?
Warfarin needs days to deplete circulating clotting factors
Warfarin cannot be absorbed until all heparin is fully cleared
Heparin raises the INR so the warfarin dose can be set
Heparin protects the stomach from warfarin irritation

Warfarin blocks new synthesis of factors II, VII, IX and X, but factor II already in the blood has a half-life near 60 hours, so full effect takes about 5 days. The INR can look therapeutic from loss of factor VII before the client is truly anticoagulated.
qwhjbhe: A client on warfarin has an intracranial hemorrhage and an INR of 4.5. Which treatment should the nurse prepare to give?
Four-factor PCC plus IV vitamin K
Protamine sulfate IV and hold the next dose
Oral vitamin K alone, then recheck the INR in 24 hours
Idarucizumab 5 g IV with a platelet transfusion
Life-threatening warfarin bleeding is reversed rapidly with prothrombin complex concentrate plus IV vitamin K for sustained effect.
q4kkfhy: Which statement by a client taking warfarin indicates a need for further teaching?
I can take ibuprofen when my arthritis flares up.
I will keep my intake of green leafy vegetables about the same.
I will use a soft toothbrush and an electric razor.
I will tell my dentist that I take a blood thinner.
NSAIDs such as ibuprofen increase bleeding risk with warfarin and should be avoided.
q1beeuql: The nurse is preparing IV phytonadione for a client with a high INR. Which action is correct?
Dilute it and infuse slowly while watching for anaphylaxis
Give it undiluted by rapid IV push over 30 seconds
Mix it into the client's heparin infusion bag
Give it with protamine to speed the reversal
IV vitamin K can cause severe anaphylactoid reactions, so it is diluted and infused slowly.
qgz5dhe: A client taking dabigatran has a life-threatening GI bleed. Which reversal agent should the nurse expect to give?
Idarucizumab is a monoclonal antibody fragment that specifically binds and reverses dabigatran.
q1b93h3j: Which statement by a client starting apixaban shows correct understanding?
I will not need routine INR blood tests.
I can stop it a day before dental work on my own.
If I miss a dose I will take two doses the next time.
I should add a daily aspirin for extra clot protection.
Apixaban does not require INR monitoring; stopping abruptly, doubling doses, or adding aspirin increase the risk of clotting or bleeding.
qx4ny1x: A client is prescribed rivaroxaban 20 mg daily for atrial fibrillation. What should the nurse include in teaching?
Take it with your evening meal
Take it on an empty stomach at bedtime
Have your INR checked weekly for the first month
Eat the same amount of vitamin K every day
The 15 mg and 20 mg doses are taken with food, usually the evening meal, for proper absorption.
q3dmute: A client in DKA has a glucose of 540 mg/dL and a potassium of 3.1 mEq/L. Which order should the nurse implement first?
Regular insulin infusion at 0.1 units/kg/hr right away
Sodium bicarbonate 50 mEq IV push for acidosis
Insulin drives potassium into cells; starting it with a potassium below 3.3 mEq/L can cause fatal dysrhythmias.
q19v1boi: A client with DKA on an insulin infusion now has a glucose of 240 mg/dL, but the anion gap is still open. What should the nurse anticipate?
Add dextrose to the IV fluids and continue insulin
Stop the insulin infusion and switch to sliding scale
Increase the insulin rate to close the gap faster
Give 50% dextrose IV push and hold the insulin
Insulin is continued until the gap closes; dextrose is added to prevent hypoglycemia.
qvraq9l: An insulin infusion of 100 units of regular insulin in 100 mL NS is ordered at 0.1 units/kg/hr for a 70 kg client. What rate should the nurse set?
0.1 x 70 = 7 units/hr; the concentration is 1 unit/mL, so 7 mL/hr.
qa4wc9i: Which insulin can the nurse give as a continuous IV infusion?
Regular insulin is the standard IV insulin; long-acting and cloudy insulins are never given IV.
q1noxmcq: A client's fingerstick glucose is 52 mg/dL. The client is alert and able to swallow. What should the nurse do first?
Give glucagon 1 mg IM in the thigh
Start D50 IV push through the hand vein
Provide a full meal tray with a protein snack
An alert client who can swallow gets 15 g of simple carbohydrate, then a recheck in 15 minutes.
qjcd08i: A client with diabetes is unresponsive with a glucose of 38 mg/dL and has no IV access. Which action is best?
Give glucagon 1 mg IM and turn the client to the side
Place glucose gel in the cheek and recheck in 15 minutes
Give regular insulin subcutaneously and recheck in an hour
Start an IV and wait for a repeat glucose before treating
Glucagon works without IV access; vomiting is common, so the client is placed on the side.
q19fvif1: The nurse is giving 50% dextrose IV for severe hypoglycemia. Which action is most important?
Confirm a patent, free-flowing IV before pushing
Give it IM if the IV site looks slightly puffy
Push it through the smallest available hand vein
Mix it with regular insulin in the same syringe
D50 is hypertonic and a vesicant; extravasation can cause tissue necrosis.
q5vmmyz: A client with hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state has a glucose of 960 mg/dL and dry mucous membranes. What is the priority intervention?
Give regular insulin 20 units IV push
Start oral fluids at 120 mL per hour
Give sodium bicarbonate for the acidosis
Severe dehydration is the main problem in HHS; isotonic fluid replacement comes first.
q1jwfvb0: An order reads potassium chloride 40 mEq in 100 mL NS over 1 hour through a peripheral IV. What should the nurse do?
Clarify the order because the rate is unsafe
Give it as ordered on an infusion pump
Run it over 30 minutes to finish it sooner
Give it as ordered but check the site every hour
Peripheral potassium is usually limited to about 10 mEq/hr; 40 mEq/hr is unsafe without central access and cardiac monitoring.
qsa4psf: Before starting IV potassium chloride, which assessment is most important?
Urine output of at least 30 mL/hr
Bowel sounds in all four quadrants
Potassium is excreted by the kidneys; giving it with poor urine output can cause hyperkalemia.
q150by29: Potassium chloride 20 mEq in 100 mL is ordered to infuse over 2 hours. At what rate should the nurse set the pump?
100 mL over 2 hours = 50 mL/hr, which delivers 10 mEq/hr.
qccv0h3: Which instruction should the nurse give a client taking oral potassium chloride tablets?
Take it with a full glass of water after meals
Take it on an empty stomach first thing in the morning
Crush the extended-release tablet into pudding
Take it with a salt substitute to boost the effect
Oral potassium irritates the GI tract; taking it with fluid and food reduces ulceration.
q13xna8w: A client with preeclampsia is receiving IV magnesium sulfate. Which finding requires immediate action?
Blood pressure 146/94 mm Hg and mild headache
Patellar reflexes 2+ and urine output 50 mL/hr
Facial flushing and a feeling of warmth
Absent reflexes and respiratory depression signal magnesium toxicity.
q1eyceou: A client on a magnesium sulfate infusion becomes lethargic with a respiratory rate of 8/min. After stopping the infusion, which drug should the nurse prepare?
Calcium gluconate 1 g IV given slowly
Calcium gluconate antagonizes magnesium at the neuromuscular junction.
qlsp5d4: Which finding in a client receiving magnesium sulfate increases the risk of toxicity?
Urine output of 80 mL over 4 hours
Magnesium is cleared by the kidneys; output under 30 mL/hr allows it to accumulate.
q16xwqnm: A 4 g magnesium sulfate loading dose is ordered over 20 minutes. The bag contains 40 g in 1,000 mL. At what rate should the nurse set the pump?
40 g/1,000 mL = 0.04 g/mL; 4 g = 100 mL; 100 mL over 20 minutes = 300 mL/hr.
qca8dp6: After the loading dose, magnesium sulfate is ordered at 2 g/hr. The bag is 40 g in 1,000 mL. What rate should the nurse program?
q1t30bed: The nurse is monitoring an oxytocin induction. Which contraction pattern meets the definition of tachysystole?
More than 5 contractions in 10 minutes over 30 minutes
Contractions lasting 70 seconds with full relaxation between
A 20-minute stretch with no contractions recorded at all

Tachysystole is more than 5 contractions in 10 minutes averaged over a 30-minute window, and it is the reason oxytocin is titrated down or stopped. Contractions every 3 minutes is only 3 to 4 per 10 minutes, the usual goal in active labor.
qtgn5gu: A postpartum client has received high-dose oxytocin for 12 hours. She reports headache and confusion, and urine output has dropped. Which laboratory value should the nurse check?
Oxytocin has an antidiuretic effect and can cause water intoxication with hyponatremia.
q26773k: A client is receiving terbutaline for preterm labor. Which finding should cause the nurse to hold the next dose?
Terbutaline is a beta-agonist; maternal tachycardia over about 120/min warrants holding it.
qu1j57s: Which statement by a client in preterm labor shows understanding of betamethasone?
This shot helps my baby's lungs mature before birth.
This shot will stop my contractions within an hour.
This medicine prevents my baby from getting an infection.
This shot lowers my blood pressure during labor.
Antenatal corticosteroids speed fetal lung maturity and reduce respiratory distress syndrome.
qng3d9y: Methylergonovine 0.2 mg IM is ordered for postpartum hemorrhage. Which charted finding should the nurse question before giving it?
A blood pressure of 162/98 mm Hg
An estimated blood loss of 900 mL

Methylergonovine is an ergot vasoconstrictor, so it is avoided in hypertension and preeclampsia because of stroke and severe hypertension. Asthma is the limit on carboprost, not on this drug, and anemia with heavy blood loss is the reason it was ordered.
q1gmpxp9: A postpartum client with hemorrhage has a history of asthma. Which uterotonic order should the nurse question?
Carboprost is a prostaglandin F2-alpha that can cause bronchospasm and is avoided in asthma.
qiqkyrf: A client has a dinoprostone vaginal insert for cervical ripening and now has contractions every 90 seconds. What should the nurse do first?
Start an oxytocin infusion at 2 milliunits/min
Give a second insert to finish ripening
Have the client walk to promote dilation
Tachysystole with dinoprostone is managed by removing the insert.
q5oidz7: A peripheral norepinephrine infusion has infiltrated and the hand is pale, cool, and mottled. Which drug is infiltrated into the site to limit tissue loss?

Phentolamine is an alpha blocker, so it reverses the intense alpha-mediated vasoconstriction causing the ischemia. Hyaluronidase disperses other extravasations but does not relieve vasospasm, and protamine and calcium reverse heparin and calcium channel blockers.
q1c7g6fk: Norepinephrine 4 mg in 250 mL is ordered at 8 mcg/min. What rate should the nurse program?
4 mg/250 mL = 16 mcg/mL; 8 mcg/min divided by 16 mcg/mL = 0.5 mL/min; 0.5 mL/min x 60 = 30 mL/hr.
q1dony7s: Dopamine 400 mg in 250 mL is ordered at 5 mcg/kg/min for an 80 kg client. What rate should the nurse set?
qsf4o34: Dobutamine 500 mg in 250 mL is ordered at 10 mcg/kg/min for a 60 kg client. What rate should the nurse set?
q1c5r9km: A client with cardiogenic shock is started on dobutamine. Which finding best shows the drug is working?
Urine output rises from 15 to 45 mL/hr
Lung crackles extend higher on the posterior chest
Skin becomes cooler and more mottled at the knees
Dobutamine increases contractility and cardiac output, which improves kidney perfusion.
qvz1see: Vasopressin 20 units in 100 mL is ordered at 0.03 units/min for septic shock. At what rate should the nurse set the pump?
20 units/100 mL = 0.2 units/mL; 0.03 x 60 = 1.8 units/hr; 1.8 divided by 0.2 = 9 mL/hr.
qx24fja: After an IV phenylephrine bolus for hypotension, which finding should the nurse expect and monitor?
Phenylephrine is a pure alpha-agonist; the rise in BP can trigger a reflex drop in heart rate.
q1ui7srj: A client has anaphylaxis after an IV antibiotic. Which epinephrine order should the nurse anticipate first?
0.5 mg of 1 mg/mL solution IM in the lateral thigh
1 mg of 0.1 mg/mL solution by rapid IV push
0.5 mg of 1 mg/mL solution subcutaneously in the arm
0.1 mg of 1 mg/mL solution IV push undiluted
IM epinephrine 1 mg/mL (0.3 to 0.5 mg) in the thigh is first-line for anaphylaxis; the cardiac arrest dose is not used.
qznu7ld: Adenosine 6 mg is ordered for a client with stable SVT. Which technique is correct?
Rapid IV push followed by a 20 mL saline flush
Slow IV push over 2 minutes into a hand vein
Dilute in 50 mL and infuse over 10 minutes
Give IM in the deltoid and repeat in 5 minutes
Adenosine has a half-life of seconds, so it must reach the heart quickly via rapid push and flush.
q14i3i33: Right after adenosine, the monitor shows a 4-second pause and the client reports chest heaviness and flushing. What should the nurse do?
Continue monitoring; these effects are expected and brief
Start chest compressions and call a code
Give atropine 1 mg IV push right away
Give a second dose of adenosine immediately
Transient asystole, flushing, and chest pressure are expected and resolve within seconds.
q1o0xb6h: A client taking oral amiodarone for 6 months reports a new dry cough and shortness of breath. What should the nurse do?
Report it as possible pulmonary toxicity
Tell the client it is a common cold symptom
Advise doubling fluids and using a humidifier
Hold the drug for 2 days and then restart it
Pulmonary fibrosis is a serious amiodarone toxicity and requires prompt evaluation.
q1pp3pbn: A client on warfarin is started on amiodarone. Which effect should the nurse anticipate?
Amiodarone inhibits warfarin metabolism and raises the INR; the warfarin dose often must be reduced.
q19b30r1: A client in atrial fibrillation with RVR is ordered a diltiazem infusion. Which finding requires the nurse to hold the infusion?
Diltiazem lowers BP; hypotension is an indication to stop and notify the provider.
qt22tzu: Diltiazem 125 mg in 125 mL is ordered at 10 mg/hr. At what rate should the nurse set the pump?
125 mg/125 mL = 1 mg/mL, so 10 mg/hr = 10 mL/hr.
q1atvd1c: Which serum digoxin level falls within the usual therapeutic range for an adult treated for heart failure?

The target for heart failure is about 0.5 to 0.9 ng/mL, and levels above 2.0 ng/mL are associated with toxicity. The window is narrow, which is why hypokalemia and falling renal function matter so much with this drug.
q2uta9x: A client taking digoxin and furosemide reports nausea and seeing yellow halos. Which lab result is most important for the nurse to check?
Hypokalemia from loop diuretics increases digoxin toxicity.
qrsh71s: After a client receives digoxin immune Fab for toxicity, which finding should the nurse monitor closely?
As digoxin is bound and the Na-K pump recovers, potassium shifts back into cells and can drop.
q1a26wug: An infant is ordered digoxin 0.04 mg PO. The elixir contains 50 mcg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
0.04 mg = 40 mcg; 40 divided by 50 mcg/mL = 0.8 mL.
qtcdl8c: Which action is correct when giving a nitroprusside infusion?
Cover the bag with an opaque sleeve
Infuse it by gravity without a pump
Mix it in a bag with dobutamine
Give it as a bolus before each titration
Nitroprusside breaks down in light; it is protected and given on a pump with arterial BP monitoring.
qgpuf1k: A client has been on nitroprusside for 3 days. Which finding suggests cyanide toxicity?
Cyanide blocks cellular oxygen use, causing lactic acidosis, confusion, and hemodynamic instability.
q706t3r: A client with chest pain took tadalafil about 30 hours ago. How does this change the plan for sublingual nitroglycerin?
Nitrates are avoided for 48 hours after tadalafil
Nitrates are safe once 12 hours have fully passed
Tadalafil has no meaningful interaction with nitrates
Nitrates may be given at half the usual dose

Tadalafil is the long-acting PDE-5 inhibitor, so nitrates are held 48 hours, while sildenafil and vardenafil require 24 hours. Both drug classes act on the nitric oxide pathway, and together they cause profound hypotension.
qio9xew: A client is taught to use sublingual nitroglycerin at home. Which statement shows correct understanding?
I can take one tablet every 5 minutes for up to three doses
I can take three tablets at once for faster relief
I should wait 15 minutes between tablets so my pressure holds
I should take one tablet and then drive myself to the hospital

Up to three doses 5 minutes apart is the standard home regimen, with 911 called if pain persists after the first dose. Taking the tablets together or driving oneself both risk syncope from the abrupt fall in blood pressure.
q9yl2s1: A client using a nitroglycerin transdermal patch asks why it must be removed at night. What is the best response?
A daily patch-free period helps prevent tolerance
It keeps your blood sugar from dropping overnight
It stops the patch from causing nightmares
Your heart does not need oxygen while you sleep
A nitrate-free interval of 10 to 12 hours prevents tolerance to nitrates.
q1vdsc45: After receiving furosemide 120 mg IV push, a client reports ringing in the ears. What does the nurse suspect?
An expected sign that the diuretic is working
An allergic reaction to sulfa components
Hyperkalemia from the large single dose
High-dose IV furosemide given too fast can cause ototoxicity; rates are generally no faster than 4 mg/min.
qcchxvy: Two clients receive diuretics for heart failure. Which pairing of drug and expected potassium change is correct?
Furosemide lowers potassium and spironolactone raises it
Furosemide raises potassium and spironolactone lowers it
Both furosemide and spironolactone lower potassium
Neither drug changes potassium when renal function is normal

Furosemide blocks the sodium-potassium-2-chloride transporter in the loop, so potassium is lost in the urine. Spironolactone blocks aldosterone in the distal tubule and spares potassium, which is why hyperkalemia is its major risk.
q10vl9v6: Which finding best shows IV furosemide is effective for a client with heart failure?
Fewer crackles and a 1.5 kg weight loss
Blood pressure rising from 110 to 140 systolic
Reduced fluid overload is shown by weight loss and improved lung sounds.
q1qk3u3n: A client taking lisinopril is started on spironolactone. Which instruction is most important?
Avoid salt substitutes that contain potassium
Increase your intake of bananas and oranges
Take a potassium supplement each morning
Expect your potassium level to fall
Both drugs raise potassium; potassium salt substitutes can cause dangerous hyperkalemia.
qqgf8ni: A client who started lisinopril 3 days ago has a swollen tongue and lips and a hoarse voice. What is the priority action?
Assess the airway and call the rapid response team
Give the next lisinopril dose with diphenhydramine
Apply ice packs to the lips and recheck in 1 hour
Document the finding and notify the provider in the morning
Angioedema can obstruct the airway; airway protection comes first and the ACE inhibitor is stopped.
qgrulpr: A client taking lisinopril reports a persistent dry cough. Which change should the nurse anticipate?
Switching to an angiotensin receptor blocker
Adding a cough suppressant and continuing lisinopril
Doubling the lisinopril dose at bedtime
Switching to a different ACE inhibitor
ACE inhibitors raise bradykinin, causing cough; ARBs do not affect bradykinin.
q1gkcdwm: Which statement by a woman taking losartan requires follow-up by the nurse?
We are planning to get pregnant in a few months.
I check my blood pressure at home every morning.
I stand up slowly when I get out of bed.
ARBs and ACE inhibitors cause fetal harm; pregnancy plans require a medication change.
q77pqyq: Which medication order should the nurse question for a client with asthma?
Nonselective beta blockers block beta-2 receptors in the lungs and can trigger bronchospasm.
q1a9veat: A client with type 1 diabetes is starting metoprolol. Which statement shows understanding?
My shakiness and racing heart may not warn me of low sugar.
Metoprolol will lower my blood sugar so I need less insulin.
I should stop insulin on days I take metoprolol.
I need to eat extra sugar with every metoprolol dose.
Beta blockers mask adrenergic signs of hypoglycemia such as tremor and tachycardia; sweating may still occur.
q793szj: After IV labetalol for severe hypertension, which action is most important before the client gets up?
Labetalol has alpha-blocking effects that cause orthostatic hypotension and fall risk.
ql2gwfa: When should the nurse draw a vancomycin trough level?
Within 30 minutes before the next dose
Exactly 1 hour after the infusion ends
Any time during the day shift

A trough reflects the lowest level and is drawn just before the next dose, usually before the fourth dose. Many hospitals now dose vancomycin by AUC monitoring instead of troughs alone, so follow facility protocol.
q13ql7te: Ten minutes into a vancomycin infusion a client has flushing of the face and neck with a stable blood pressure. What explains this reaction?
Direct mast cell histamine release from the infusion rate
An IgE-mediated allergy that bars vancomycin for his life
Bacterial endotoxin released as organisms are killed
Vasodilation caused by the sodium in the diluent

Vancomycin infusion reaction is a direct, non-immune mast cell release tied to how fast the drug is given, so it can be resumed over at least 60 minutes after an antihistamine. Because it is not IgE-mediated it is not a true allergy.
qtv9r9u: Gentamicin is infused over 30 minutes. When should the nurse draw the peak level?
The peak for an IV aminoglycoside is drawn about 30 minutes after a 30-minute infusion is complete.
qcyl5ho: A client has received gentamicin for 6 days. Which finding is most important to report?
Temperature down from 38.9 to 37.2 C (102-99 F)
White blood cell count down to 9,000/mm3
Aminoglycosides are nephrotoxic; a rising creatinine requires dose adjustment or a different drug.
q152jhw1: A client says penicillin gave him a flat itchy rash as a child, with no swelling or trouble breathing. Amoxicillin-clavulanate is ordered. What does this history mean?
A rash alone is low-risk and the drug is often given
Any penicillin history rules out every beta-lactam antibiotic
The clavulanate component removes the risk of a reaction
A test dose will confirm whether he can tolerate the drug

A childhood maculopapular rash without urticaria, angioedema or airway involvement is a low-risk label, and most such clients tolerate penicillins; documented anaphylaxis is what bars the class. Clavulanate is a beta-lactamase inhibitor and does not change allergy risk.
qz44ggk: A client with a creatinine clearance of 22 mL/min is ordered ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily and cefepime 2 g IV every 8 hours. Which order should the nurse question?
The cefepime, which requires a renal dose adjustment
The ceftriaxone, which requires a renal dose adjustment
Both orders, since neither drug is used in renal failure
Neither order, since cephalosporins are cleared by the liver

Ceftriaxone is largely eliminated in bile, so its dose is not routinely adjusted for renal function. Cefepime is renally cleared, and at this clearance it accumulates and causes encephalopathy and myoclonus; most other cephalosporins also need adjustment.
q1wwwc89: A client takes ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO twice daily along with calcium carbonate, a multivitamin with iron, and a stool softener. How should the nurse schedule them?
Give the ciprofloxacin 2 hours before the calcium and iron
Give all of the medications together with a full glass of milk
Crush the ciprofloxacin and mix it in applesauce with the iron
Give the ciprofloxacin with the antacid to protect the stomach

Divalent and trivalent cations such as calcium, iron, magnesium and zinc chelate fluoroquinolones in the gut and can cut absorption by more than half. The usual spacing is 2 hours before or 6 hours after the cation.
q13xjoib: A client on clindamycin for 8 days has had 6 watery stools today. Which result would confirm the suspected cause?
Stool positive for Clostridioides difficile toxin
Stool culture growing only normal gut flora organisms
A white blood cell count of 9,000/mm3
A stool sample negative for occult blood

Clindamycin strips anaerobic gut flora and carries one of the highest risks of C. difficile colitis, which is diagnosed by stool toxin or toxin-gene testing. A normal white count and a negative occult blood test do not rule it out.
qcbhxg3: Which statement indicates that the client understands teaching about metronidazole?
I will avoid alcohol during treatment and for 3 days after.
I can have a glass of wine with dinner once in a while.
I will take it on an empty stomach with milk.
I will stop it once the diarrhea starts to improve.
Metronidazole with alcohol causes a disulfiram-like reaction.
q1whrtht: A client who takes valproic acid for seizures is started on meropenem. What should the nurse anticipate?
A large drop in the valproic acid level
A rise in valproic acid to toxic levels
No interaction between the two drugs
Carbapenems sharply lower valproic acid levels and can lead to breakthrough seizures.
qtnkq6l: A client on a morphine PCA is difficult to arouse, has pinpoint pupils, and a respiratory rate of 7/min. What is the nurse's first action?
Stop the PCA and prepare naloxone
Lower the PCA dose and recheck in 1 hour
Raise the head of bed and apply oxygen
Notify the provider and document findings
Opioid-induced respiratory depression requires stopping the opioid and reversing it with naloxone while supporting breathing.
q1h6gvud: A family member is seen pressing the PCA button while the client sleeps. What should the nurse do?
Explain that only the client should press it
Thank them for helping control the pain
Ask them to press it only every 2 hours
Increase the lockout interval to be safe
PCA by proxy bypasses the built-in safety of sedation (a sedated client cannot press the button) and can cause overdose and respiratory depression.
q1s2adr6: A client's respirations improved after naloxone for opioid overdose. Which is the priority ongoing assessment?
Watch for hypoglycemia over the next hour
Watch for a rash at the IV site
Naloxone's duration is shorter than many opioids, so sedation and respiratory depression can return.
quqz7in: Hydromorphone 0.5 mg IV is ordered. The vial contains 2 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
qx8rh5o: A client with a fentanyl transdermal patch now has a fever of 39.4°C. What is the nurse's primary concern?
Decreased drug absorption and increased pain
Loss of patch adhesion and detachment
Conversion of fentanyl to an inactive form
Heat increases skin blood flow and fentanyl absorption, raising the risk of respiratory depression.
q1o3fpoh: A client on methadone maintenance is admitted. Which finding requires the nurse to notify the provider before the next dose?
Constipation for the past 2 days despite docusate
Pupils 3 mm and reactive to light
Methadone prolongs the QT interval and can cause torsades de pointes.
qmww3u9: Which instruction should the nurse give a client discharged on scheduled oxycodone?
Take a stool softener and a stimulant laxative daily
Take it with a glass of wine to help you relax
Stop taking it abruptly once the pain is gone
Drive as usual once the first dose takes effect
Opioid-induced constipation does not resolve over time, so a bowel regimen is started along with the opioid.
qhj5e1q: A client taking sertraline is prescribed tramadol. Which findings should the nurse teach the client to report?
Drowsiness and dry mouth during the first few days
Tramadol combined with an SSRI can cause serotonin syndrome; tramadol also lowers the seizure threshold.
q3jq838: Flumazenil is ordered for a client oversedated with lorazepam who has taken benzodiazepines daily for 10 years. What is the nurse's primary concern?
Flumazenil can trigger abrupt benzodiazepine withdrawal and seizures in clients who use benzodiazepines chronically.
qrj6wip: During moderate sedation with midazolam and fentanyl, which finding requires immediate intervention?
EtCO2 rising from 38 to 58 mm Hg with an RR of 6/min
Responding to voice and following commands
SpO2 of 96% on 2 L via nasal cannula
A rising end-tidal CO2 with a low respiratory rate indicates hypoventilation, often before SpO2 falls.
q18r5at9: Which action is correct when maintaining a propofol infusion?
Change the tubing and bottle every 12 hours
Mix it with the client's antibiotic infusion
Keep an opened vial at the bedside for 24 hours
Use it as the client's only pain medication
Propofol is a lipid emulsion that supports bacterial growth, so strict aseptic technique and hang-time limits apply.
qirlfbc: A ventilated client on propofol is grimacing and has a heart rate of 118/min after turning. What should the nurse do?
Assess for pain and give the ordered analgesic
Increase the propofol because it relieves pain
Document it as an expected response to turning
Give a paralytic to stop the grimacing
Propofol has no analgesic properties, so pain must be treated separately.
q1ewz09q: A client is sedated on a dexmedetomidine infusion in the ICU. How does this drug differ from a propofol or midazolam infusion?
It sedates with little respiratory depression
It raises both the heart rate and blood pressure
It gives deep sedation with full amnesia
It can be reversed with flumazenil

Dexmedetomidine is a central alpha-2 agonist, so clients stay rousable and keep their respiratory drive, which is why it is used during ventilator weaning. Its hallmark adverse effects are bradycardia and hypotension, and flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines instead.
qsh2igy: A client sedated with ketamine in the ED is emerging from sedation, appears frightened, and is hallucinating. What should the nurse do?
Reduce stimulation and prepare a benzodiazepine
Turn on bright lights and speak loudly to reorient the client
Give a second full dose of ketamine by IV push
Restrain all four limbs and leave the room
Emergence reactions are managed with a calm, quiet environment and, if needed, a benzodiazepine.
q1wivxpd: After rapid sequence intubation with etomidate, a client with sepsis remains hypotensive. Which effect of etomidate may be contributing?
Etomidate inhibits cortisol synthesis, which may worsen hypotension in septic shock.
q15grcxc: For which client should the nurse question an order for succinylcholine for intubation?
A client with a potassium level of 6.1 after a crush injury
A client with pneumonia and a potassium level of 4.0
A client with an overdose and a normal potassium level
A client with an acute asthma attack and normal labs
Succinylcholine raises serum potassium and can cause cardiac arrest in clients with hyperkalemia or with crush or burn injuries after the first day.
q1ojk2wd: Shortly after receiving succinylcholine, a surgical client develops jaw rigidity, a sharp rise in EtCO2, and tachycardia. What should the nurse anticipate?
Stopping triggering agents and giving dantrolene
Giving more succinylcholine to relieve the rigidity
Giving acetaminophen and using cooling blankets only
Giving naloxone to reverse the sedation
These are early signs of malignant hyperthermia; dantrolene is the antidote.
q29q84p: A client is intubated and receiving a continuous rocuronium infusion. What is the nurse's priority?
Checking for intact cough and gag reflexes
Keeping the client NPO because of aspiration risk
Paralytics provide no sedation or analgesia; a paralyzed client must be sedated to prevent awareness.
q1krp33: Which teaching is essential for a female client who received sugammadex at the end of surgery?
Use a backup birth control method for 7 days
Avoid dairy products and leafy greens for 48 hours
Expect your urine to turn orange for a day
Take your birth control pill twice tomorrow
Sugammadex binds progestogens and reduces hormonal contraceptive effectiveness, similar to a missed dose.
q15iykt: A train-of-four test is performed on a client receiving vecuronium. Which result typically reflects the target level of blockade?
One or two twitches usually reflect adequate blockade without excessive paralysis.
qekkj10: Neostigmine is given to reverse neuromuscular blockade. Why is glycopyrrolate given with it?
Neostigmine also increases acetylcholine at muscarinic sites; an anticholinergic prevents bradycardia and excess secretions.
qwawv02: Which action is correct when giving IV phenytoin?
Dilute in normal saline; give no faster than 50 mg/min
Mix in D5W and infuse as fast as the client tolerates
Give it IM in the deltoid if the IV is not patent
Dilute it in lactated Ringer's and push over 1 minute
Phenytoin precipitates in dextrose solutions and causes hypotension and dysrhythmias if given too fast.
qfwsf52: A client with a serum albumin of 2.1 g/dL has a total phenytoin level reported as 9 mcg/mL. Why may this level be misleading?
Low albumin lowers the total while free drug is therapeutic
Low albumin raises the total level and hides a low free level
Phenytoin is not protein bound, so albumin has no effect
Phenytoin levels are only valid when drawn after a meal

Phenytoin is about 90 percent albumin bound and only the free fraction is active. With low albumin, less drug is carried in the bound pool, so the total reads low while the free level may be in range; the quoted 10 to 20 mcg/mL range assumes normal albumin.
qoi0f4g: Which statement by a client taking long-term phenytoin indicates correct understanding?
"I will brush and floss carefully every day."
"I can switch brands whenever one is cheaper."
"I can stop it once I have been seizure-free for a month."
"I will take an antacid with each dose."
Gingival hyperplasia is common; switching brands or stopping abruptly can change drug levels or cause seizures.
qpxi2ym: What is an advantage of fosphenytoin over IV phenytoin?
It can be infused faster with less tissue injury
It never requires blood level monitoring
It can be mixed with any IV fluid in the line
It cannot cause hypotension or dysrhythmias
Fosphenytoin is water-soluble, causes less purple glove syndrome, and can be infused at up to 150 mg PE/min.
q24so0p: Which report from a client taking levetiracetam should the nurse follow up on?
"I have been feeling angry and hopeless."
"I feel a little sleepy in the afternoon."
"I have had a slight headache this week."
"I am a bit dizzy when I first stand up."
Levetiracetam can cause irritability, depression, and suicidal thoughts.
q931wo1: A client taking valproic acid reports severe abdominal pain radiating to the back and vomiting. What does the nurse suspect?
Valproic acid carries boxed warnings for pancreatitis and hepatotoxicity.
q1q1ej6u: Which finding in a client taking carbamazepine should the nurse report immediately?
Fever, sore throat, and a blistering rash
Mild drowsiness during the first week
Mild nausea when a dose is taken on an empty stomach
Carbamazepine can cause agranulocytosis and Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
q1pbkrqr: A client starts lamotrigine on a schedule that raises the dose slowly over about 6 weeks. What is the reason for the slow titration?
It lowers the risk of Stevens-Johnson syndrome
It lets the kidneys adapt to clearing the drug
It prevents withdrawal seizures between doses
It allows a blood level to be checked each week

The risk of serious rash, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, rises with rapid dose escalation, so the manufacturer's schedule takes about 6 weeks to reach maintenance. Adding valproate roughly doubles lamotrigine levels, so the starting dose is halved.
qyfgr0f: A client on maintenance lithium has a level of 1.6 mEq/L. Which finding fits this level?
A fine tremor present since the first week
Seizures and a decreased level of consciousness
Polyuria and thirst since the drug was started

Maintenance levels run about 0.6 to 1.2 mEq/L, and 1.5 to 2.0 mEq/L brings coarse tremor, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea. A fine tremor and polyuria occur at therapeutic levels, while seizures and stupor appear above roughly 2.5 mEq/L.
q1e4zth4: Which statement by a client taking lithium indicates a need for further teaching?
"I am going to start a low-salt diet."
"I will drink about 2 to 3 liters of fluid daily."
"I will have my blood level checked as ordered."
"I will call if I have vomiting or diarrhea."
Low sodium intake causes lithium retention and toxicity.
q1rocq8j: A client taking lithium has several new orders. Which order should the nurse question?
NSAIDs decrease lithium clearance and raise lithium levels.
q1j56tob: A client taking clozapine reports a sore throat and a fever of 38.6°C. What should the nurse do first?
Check the most recent absolute neutrophil count
Give acetaminophen and recheck the temperature in 4 hours
Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia; signs of infection require an urgent ANC.
qh9bq6z: A client on haloperidol has a temperature of 104 F, lead-pipe rigidity, and a creatine kinase of 4,200 units/L. Which syndrome do these findings fit?

Neuroleptic malignant syndrome brings fever, lead-pipe rigidity, autonomic instability and a high creatine kinase from muscle breakdown, and it builds over days. Serotonin syndrome instead causes hyperreflexia, clonus and diarrhea and appears within hours.
q1hsj06e: A client given haloperidol develops sudden twisting of the neck and upward rolling of the eyes. Which order should the nurse anticipate?
Acute dystonia is treated with an anticholinergic such as diphenhydramine or benztropine.
q1gl1eo1: Which monitoring is most important for a client taking olanzapine long-term?
Hearing tests and eye exams every 6 months
Second-generation antipsychotics such as olanzapine cause weight gain, diabetes, and dyslipidemia.
q1gas36w: An 80-year-old client is started on quetiapine. Which instruction is most important for the nurse to give?
Rise slowly from a lying or sitting position
Expect reddish-orange urine for a few days
Quetiapine causes orthostatic hypotension and sedation, which increase the risk of falls in older adults.
qo7eegw: Which instruction should the nurse give about ziprasidone?
Take it on an empty stomach
Ziprasidone absorption roughly doubles with food; the drug also prolongs the QT interval.
q1xtqf0r: A client recently started on sertraline along with another serotonergic drug has agitation, diaphoresis, hyperreflexia, and leg clonus. What does the nurse suspect?
Clonus and hyperreflexia point to serotonin syndrome; NMS causes lead-pipe rigidity and slowed reflexes.
qbmvlsd: Which statement by a client starting fluoxetine indicates a need for further teaching?
"I can stop it as soon as I feel better."
"It may take several weeks to feel the full effect."
"I will report any thoughts of hurting myself."
"I will take it in the morning if it keeps me awake."
Antidepressants should not be stopped abruptly, and their full effect takes several weeks.
q18ofq0m: A client taking phenelzine ate aged cheese and salami and now has a severe occipital headache and a BP of 210/120 mm Hg. What does the nurse suspect?
MAOIs taken with tyramine-rich foods can cause a hypertensive crisis.
qw34qvv: A client taking fluoxetine is to be switched to an MAOI. What should the nurse anticipate?
A washout period of about 5 weeks
Starting the MAOI the next morning
Taking both drugs together for 1 week
Because of fluoxetine's long half-life, about 5 weeks must pass before an MAOI is started to prevent serotonin syndrome.
q157zntq: For which client should the nurse question an order for bupropion?
A client trying to quit smoking
A client taking an SSRI who has low sexual desire
Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in clients with eating disorders or seizure disorders.
qit3j2h: Which adverse effect of trazodone should the nurse teach a male client to report immediately?
An erection lasting more than 4 hours
Mild dizziness when standing up quickly
Priapism is a rare but serious emergency with trazodone.
q6j042: Which parameter should the nurse monitor in a client taking high doses of venlafaxine?
Venlafaxine can cause sustained, dose-related hypertension.
q37b58v: Which order should the nurse question for an 84-year-old client?
Diphenhydramine 50 mg at bedtime for sleep
Acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours for pain
Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime for sleep
Polyethylene glycol 17 g daily for constipation
Diphenhydramine is on the Beers list because of anticholinergic effects such as confusion, falls, and urinary retention.
q1ra0r7l: A newly admitted 82-year-old client takes glyburide. Why should the nurse discuss this drug with the provider?
It raises the risk of lactic acidosis
It often causes severe weight loss
Glyburide is on the Beers list because of prolonged hypoglycemia in older adults.
qg46bm: An 88-year-old client asks for temazepam for sleep. Which risk should the nurse discuss with the provider?
In older adults, benzodiazepines increase the risk of falls, fractures, and delirium.
q16o1uqi: Which statement indicates that the client understands teaching about zolpidem?
"I will take it right before bed when I can sleep 7 to 8 hours."
"I will take it with a glass of wine to help it work."
"I can drive to work 2 hours after taking it."
"I will take an extra tablet if I wake up at 3 AM."
Zolpidem can cause next-day impairment and complex sleep behaviors; it is taken only at bedtime.
q3bc6mr: A client has taken prednisone 40 mg daily for 4 months and asks why the dose is being stepped down over weeks. What is the best response?
Your adrenal glands need time to make cortisol again
The drug must clear slowly to protect your kidneys
Stopping quickly would make your blood sugar drop fast
A slow taper keeps the medicine from upsetting you

Daily steroids suppress the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis after about 2 to 3 weeks, so an abrupt stop can cause adrenal crisis with hypotension, weakness and hypoglycemia. The taper gives endogenous cortisol production time to recover.
q1yn6cgh: A client on long-term prednisone has been NPO for 2 days and is now confused with a BP of 78/40 mm Hg. Which drug should the nurse anticipate?
Missed steroid doses can cause adrenal crisis, which is treated with IV hydrocortisone and fluids.
qi8saxd: A client without diabetes is receiving high-dose IV methylprednisolone. Which finding is most important to monitor?
Corticosteroids cause hyperglycemia that may require insulin coverage.
q2qmy49: A client on high-dose dexamethasone for cerebral edema is also started on pantoprazole. What is the reason for the second drug?
Steroids raise the risk of gastric ulceration and bleeding
Pantoprazole improves the absorption of dexamethasone tablets
Pantoprazole prevents the steroid from raising glucose
Steroids cause reflux by relaxing the lower esophagus

Glucocorticoids reduce mucosal prostaglandins and impair healing, so ulcer and GI bleeding risk rises, particularly at high dose or alongside an NSAID. Acid suppression is added for that reason, not to change absorption or glucose.
qlfd4zf: Which instruction should the nurse give a client taking levothyroxine?
Take it on an empty stomach 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast
Take it with your calcium and iron to improve absorption
Take it at bedtime with a full meal and milk
Skip doses on days you feel full of energy
Food, calcium, and iron reduce levothyroxine absorption.
q14esjsn: An older adult with coronary artery disease recently started levothyroxine. Which finding requires immediate action?
Chest pain and a heart rate of 118/min
Mild fatigue and feeling cold in the first week
Weight loss of 0.5 kg in a month
Levothyroxine increases cardiac oxygen demand and can trigger angina or dysrhythmias.
qbk9vwf: Which finding should the nurse teach a client taking propylthiouracil to report immediately?
Dark urine and yellowing of the skin
Mild itching of the arms without a rash
Feeling warm in a hot room
A metallic taste in the mouth
PTU carries a boxed warning for severe liver injury.
q1pawb97: A client taking methimazole develops a sore throat and fever. Which lab should the nurse expect to be ordered?
q1v70hne: A client in thyroid storm has orders for propylthiouracil and an iodine solution. Which sequence is correct?
Give PTU at least 1 hour before the iodine
Give the iodine first, then PTU 1 hour later
Give both at the same time to speed recovery
Give the iodine only, and hold PTU until stable
The thionamide is given first so that the iodine cannot be used to synthesize new thyroid hormone.
qgzz8zn: A client receiving desmopressin reports a headache and nausea and has new confusion. Which laboratory value is most important to check?
Desmopressin causes water retention and dilutional hyponatremia.
qkxvxtq: A client with bleeding esophageal varices is on an octreotide infusion. Which finding best indicates that it is effective?
Stable hemoglobin and no further hematemesis
Blood glucose falling below 70 mg/dL during the infusion
Octreotide reduces portal blood flow and bleeding from varices.
q7n2yvf: Two clients react during a transfusion. Which finding points to an acute hemolytic reaction rather than a febrile nonhemolytic one?
Flank pain with dark red-brown urine
A temperature rise of 1.5 C with chills
Mild headache during the first 20 minutes
Hives on the chest that fade with an antihistamine

An acute hemolytic reaction is ABO incompatibility: free hemoglobin from lysed cells reaches the urine and causes flank pain and renal failure. Fever with chills alone is the far more common febrile reaction from donor leukocyte cytokines, and hives suggest a mild allergic reaction.
q1wsj5ur: After stopping a transfusion for a suspected reaction, which solution should the nurse use to keep the vein open?
Lactated Ringer's through the blood tubing
0.9% sodium chloride through the blood tubing
New tubing prevents infusion of more blood; normal saline is the only IV fluid compatible with blood products.
q1qz0b6c: A client develops dyspnea and bilateral infiltrates an hour into a transfusion. Which finding separates circulatory overload from acute lung injury?
A rising blood pressure with distended neck veins
A temperature of 38.5 C with shaking chills
An oxygen saturation that falls below 90 percent on air
Crackles heard through both lung fields

Circulatory overload is a volume problem, so venous and arterial pressures rise and the client improves with a diuretic. Transfusion-related acute lung injury is capillary leak with a normal or low blood pressure, and hypoxemia with crackles occurs in both.
q1cbuhjz: Which task can the RN delegate to unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) during a blood transfusion?
Taking vital signs at intervals set by the RN
Checking the blood unit with another nurse
Assessing the client for a transfusion reaction
Starting the transfusion after the first 15 minutes
UAP may take vital signs; verification, assessment, and administration remain with licensed nurses.
qbmxdac: A client receiving chemotherapy has a WBC of 2,000/mm3 with 25% segmented neutrophils and 5% bands. What is the absolute neutrophil count?
qgjhjia: A client receiving filgrastim reports several symptoms. Which one requires immediate follow-up?
Left upper abdominal pain radiating to the shoulder
Aching bones in the lower back and hips
Mild redness at the subcutaneous injection site
A low-grade headache relieved by acetaminophen
Left upper quadrant or shoulder pain may signal splenic rupture; bone pain is expected.
q5rmkdz: What should the nurse wear when hanging an IV chemotherapy drug?
Two pairs of chemotherapy gloves and a disposable gown
One pair of sterile gloves and a cloth gown
A surgical mask and one pair of exam gloves
A face shield and no gloves, for a better grip
Hazardous drug handling requires double chemotherapy-tested gloves and an impermeable gown.
q1vib20t: A vesicant chemotherapy drug has extravasated at a peripheral IV site. Which step comes before the catheter is removed?
Aspirate residual drug back through the catheter
Flush the catheter with 10 mL of normal saline
Infuse warm saline to dilute the drug in the tissue
Inject lidocaine around the site to relieve pain

The catheter stays in place so residual drug can be aspirated and any antidote given along the same path; flushing or diluting drives more vesicant into the tissue. Cold is applied for most vesicants, with heat reserved for the vinca alkaloids.
q1t8hlke: A client with neutropenia has a new temperature of 38.4°C. Which action is the priority?
Draw blood cultures and start antibiotics within 1 hour
Recheck the temperature in 4 hours before acting
Give acetaminophen and encourage fluids only
Wait for the ANC result before starting antibiotics
Neutropenic fever is an emergency; empiric antibiotics such as cefepime are started within 60 minutes, after cultures are drawn.
qoi0emp: A client with chronic kidney disease is due for epoetin alfa. Which finding should cause the nurse to hold the dose?
Hemoglobin of 12.4 g/dL and BP of 168/100
Hemoglobin of 9.2 g/dL and BP of 128/78
Ferritin level within the normal range
Epoetin is held when hemoglobin exceeds the target or hypertension is uncontrolled because of the risk of thrombosis.
q15i7tgj: Which instruction should the nurse give a client taking oral ferrous sulfate?
Take it with orange juice and expect dark stools
Take it with milk to protect your stomach
Take it at the same time as your antacid
Stop taking it if your stools become dark
Vitamin C enhances iron absorption; dark green or black stools are expected.
qksb7ve: A kidney transplant client taking tacrolimus asks what to avoid. Which item raises the tacrolimus level enough to risk toxicity?

Grapefruit juice inhibits intestinal CYP3A4, the enzyme that metabolizes tacrolimus, so blood levels can climb sharply and bring tremor, nephrotoxicity and hyperglycemia. Levels are followed with trough samples drawn just before a dose.
q1bk5k0n: Which statement indicates that a transplant client understands teaching about cyclosporine?
"I will have my blood drawn before my morning dose."
"I will drink grapefruit juice with each dose."
"I can skip doses if I feel well."
"I will have my level drawn 2 hours after my dose."
Trough levels are drawn before the dose; grapefruit increases cyclosporine levels.
q12thxg8: Which teaching is most important for a female client of childbearing age taking mycophenolate?
Use two reliable methods of birth control
Take it with a high-fat meal to improve absorption
Expect your urine to turn orange
Mycophenolate can cause pregnancy loss and birth defects.
q1n5zhrg: A client taking azathioprine is prescribed allopurinol for gout. Why should the nurse clarify the order?
No interaction exists, so the order is safe to give
Allopurinol blocks azathioprine breakdown, which can cause severe bone marrow suppression.
qnnsu4b: A client ingested a large amount of acetaminophen 6 hours ago and has no symptoms. What should the nurse anticipate?
Starting acetylcysteine without waiting for symptoms
Giving naloxone and observing for 2 hours
Waiting for liver enzymes to rise before treating
Acetylcysteine is most effective when started within 8 hours; early overdose is often asymptomatic.
q1bx4jus: A client takes oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 mg, 2 tablets every 4 hours (6 doses daily), plus an additional 1,000 mg of acetaminophen daily. What is the client's total daily acetaminophen intake?
4,900 mg, which exceeds the usual maximum
3,900 mg, which is within the usual maximum
1,950 mg, which is within the usual maximum
2,950 mg, which is within the usual maximum
650 mg x 6 = 3,900 mg plus 1,000 mg = 4,900 mg; the usual adult maximum is 4 g per day.
qrv5mly: Amoxicillin 40 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours is ordered for a child weighing 22 lb. The suspension is 250 mg/5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give per dose?
22 lb = 10 kg; 400 mg/day divided by 2 = 200 mg per dose; 200 divided by 50 mg/mL = 4 mL.
q13jn60u: Acetaminophen 15 mg/kg is ordered for a child weighing 18 kg. The liquid is 160 mg/5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
15 x 18 = 270 mg; 160 mg/5 mL = 32 mg/mL; 270 divided by 32 = 8.4 mL.
q4gr292: A 20-kg child is prescribed cefazolin 500 mg IV every 8 hours. The reference range is 25 to 50 mg/kg/day. What should the nurse do?
Clarify the order because the dose exceeds the range
Give it because the dose is within the range
Give it because the dose is below the range
Give half the dose and document the reason
500 x 3 = 1,500 mg/day; 1,500 divided by 20 kg = 75 mg/kg/day, above the stated range.
q1rv16el: Ibuprofen 10 mg/kg is ordered for a child weighing 15 kg. The suspension is 100 mg/5 mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
10 x 15 = 150 mg; 100 mg/5 mL = 20 mg/mL; 150 divided by 20 = 7.5 mL.
q4cee1l: Gentamicin 2.5 mg/kg IV every 8 hours is ordered for a 12 kg child. The vial contains 10 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give per dose?
2.5 x 12 = 30 mg; 30 divided by 10 mg/mL = 3 mL.
q560osp: Before giving IV ondansetron, the nurse reviews the ECG. Which finding should the nurse report?
Ondansetron prolongs the QT interval and can cause torsades de pointes.
q1hscnqg: A client has taken metoclopramide for diabetic gastroparesis for 3 months. Why does the provider plan to stop it?
Use beyond 12 weeks raises the risk of tardive dyskinesia
The drug loses its effect on gastric emptying after 4 weeks
Long-term use turns the urine a reddish-orange color
Prolonged use risks a tyramine reaction with aged cheese

The boxed warning limits treatment to 12 weeks, because the risk of tardive dyskinesia, which may be irreversible, rises with cumulative dose and duration. Involuntary tongue, lip and facial movements are the findings to report.
q1ky2b3u: The nurse is to give promethazine IV. Which action is correct?
Dilute it and give it slowly into a large vein
Push it rapidly through a small hand vein
Give it intra-arterially for a faster effect
Mix it with the client's potassium infusion
Promethazine can cause severe tissue injury and gangrene; deep IM injection is preferred, and IV doses must be diluted and given slowly.
q4y1g8j: A client has taken pantoprazole daily for several years. Which lab should the nurse monitor?
Long-term PPI use can cause hypomagnesemia and increases the risk of fractures and C. difficile infection.
qfn5x5i: Lorazepam 4 mg IV is ordered for a client in status epilepticus. The vial contains 2 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
q1ghyz8v: A client taking aripiprazole paces constantly and says, "I just cannot sit still." Which adverse effect does the nurse recognize?
Akathisia is an extrapyramidal effect characterized by motor restlessness and an urge to keep moving.
q11fdnth: Which medication task is most appropriate for the RN to assign to an LPN?
Giving oral metoprolol to a client with stable vital signs
Giving IV push metoprolol to a client in rapid atrial fibrillation
Providing initial teaching to a client newly started on metoprolol
Assessing a client whose heart rate fell to 44/min after metoprolol
LPNs may give routine oral medications to stable clients; care of unstable clients, initial teaching, and complex assessments remain with the RN.
q7ty30v: Which task related to insulin can the RN delegate to unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP)?
Checking a fingerstick glucose and reporting the result
Deciding the sliding-scale dose based on the reading
Teaching the client how to draw up mixed insulin
Assessing a client who is shaky and sweaty at lunch
UAP may perform routine fingerstick glucose checks; dosing decisions, teaching, and assessment are RN responsibilities.
qpvx8yr: The nurse receives report on four medical-surgical clients. Which client should the nurse see first?
A client on a heparin drip who just passed a black, tarry stool
A client on warfarin with an INR of 2.5 who wants to walk
A client awaiting a vancomycin trough to be drawn at 0900
A client with mild nausea who received ondansetron 30 minutes ago
Melena in a client on heparin suggests active GI bleeding and needs immediate assessment.
q1awx6f6: Which client on the labor unit should the nurse see first?
A client on magnesium sulfate with a respiratory rate of 10/min
A client on oxytocin with contractions every 3 minutes and a normal FHR
A client who received betamethasone and asks about the second dose
A client who is 4 cm dilated and requesting an epidural
Respiratory depression in a client receiving magnesium suggests toxicity and is the most life-threatening finding.
q1am0v4d: During an alteplase infusion for acute ischemic stroke, the client reports a sudden, severe headache and vomits. What is the nurse's first action?
Give ondansetron and continue the infusion
Give acetaminophen and recheck in 30 minutes
Slow the rate by half and call the provider
Sudden headache and vomiting suggest intracranial hemorrhage; the infusion is stopped and an emergency CT scan is obtained.
q1rty7ga: A client with an acute ischemic stroke is a candidate for alteplase. Which finding must be corrected before the drug is started?
BP must be below 185/110 mm Hg before alteplase is given and maintained below 180/105 mm Hg afterward.
q1bpcvut: After a client receives tenecteplase, which nursing action is most important during the next 24 hours?
Avoiding IM injections and unnecessary needle sticks
Giving the next enoxaparin dose deep IM in the thigh
Encouraging the client to floss and shave with a razor
Removing pressure dressings early to check the sites
Fibrinolytics greatly increase bleeding risk, so invasive procedures and punctures are minimized.
q1hs9jzy: A trauma client with major bleeding has an order for tranexamic acid. Which timing principle should guide the nurse?
It works best when given within 3 hours of injury
It must be given only after a full 12 hours
It is given only after bleeding has stopped
It works only after a platelet transfusion
Tranexamic acid reduces deaths from bleeding when given early; the benefit declines after 3 hours.
q1f6tmds: A client taking clopidogrel is scheduled for elective surgery. What should the nurse expect?
The drug is usually stopped about 5 days before surgery
The drug is continued, with an extra dose the morning of surgery
The drug is switched to a double dose for 3 days
The drug is stopped only the night before surgery
Clopidogrel irreversibly affects platelets, so it is usually held about 5 days before elective surgery.
qrnn8by: A client with salicylate toxicity has an order for a sodium bicarbonate infusion. What is the purpose of this infusion?
To alkalinize the urine and speed salicylate excretion
To bind salicylate in the stomach and stop absorption
To reverse the bleeding effects of aspirin
To raise the potassium level before dialysis
Alkaline urine traps salicylate in the urine and speeds its elimination.
qfmtij6: The nurse receives report on four clients on a cardiac unit. Which client should the nurse see first?
A client on lisinopril with new swelling of the lips
A client on furosemide whose potassium is 3.6 mEq/L
A client on metoprolol with a heart rate of 62/min
A client on atorvastatin reporting mild muscle aches
Lip swelling suggests angioedema, which can progress rapidly to airway obstruction.
qyg124k: A client is discharged on ticagrelor and aspirin after stent placement. Which daily aspirin dose should the nurse reinforce?
Aspirin doses above 100 mg per day reduce the effectiveness of ticagrelor.
q1v7461h: For which client should the nurse question an order for prasugrel?
A client with a history of stroke
A client with a recent coronary stent
Prasugrel is contraindicated after stroke or TIA because of intracranial bleeding risk.
q1qve29i: Which statement by a client taking atorvastatin requires follow-up?
"My legs are sore, and my urine looks dark."
"I take it at the same time every day."
"I get my liver labs done as scheduled."
Muscle pain with dark urine may signal rhabdomyolysis.
qg48pri: Which instruction should the nurse give a client taking simvastatin?
Take it in the evening and avoid grapefruit juice
Take it in the morning with a large glass of grapefruit juice
Stop it on days when you eat a low-fat meal
Take it only when you eat high-cholesterol foods
Simvastatin works best when taken in the evening; grapefruit raises drug levels and the risk of myopathy.
q1iad9h8: At which estimated GFR is metformin contraindicated rather than continued with monitoring?

Metformin is contraindicated below an eGFR of 30, is not newly started between 30 and 45, and is continued with caution between 45 and 60. The drug is cleared unchanged by the kidney, so accumulation raises the risk of lactic acidosis.
q1i65sru: The nurse is mixing regular and NPH insulin in one syringe. Which action is correct?
Draw up the regular insulin first
Draw up the NPH insulin first
Shake the NPH vial vigorously before drawing it up
Inject air into the regular vial first
Drawing up clear before cloudy prevents NPH from contaminating the regular insulin vial.
q17wtj7l: Which statement indicates that a client understands teaching about insulin glargine?
"I will not mix it with other insulins."
"I will take it only when my sugar is high."
"I will mix it with my lispro to save a shot."
"I need to shake the pen until it looks cloudy."
Glargine is clear, long-acting, given once daily, and never mixed with other insulins.
qctkwo0: Insulin lispro is due at 0730, and breakfast trays usually arrive at 0800. What should the nurse do?
Give it when the meal tray is in the room
Give it 1 hour after the meal is eaten
Give it IM to slow its onset
Rapid-acting insulin begins working within 15 minutes, so it is given when food is available.
qv8umsh: An insulin infusion of 50 units in 250 mL of NS is running at 15 mL/hr. How many units per hour is the client receiving?
q19w6dg4: For which client should the nurse question an order for semaglutide?
A client with a family history of medullary thyroid cancer
A client with type 2 diabetes and obesity who wants to lose weight
A client who also takes metformin twice a day
A client with high blood pressure on lisinopril
GLP-1 agonists carry a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors.
qnqwuoz: A client taking empagliflozin has nausea, abdominal pain, a glucose of 190 mg/dL, and an arterial pH of 7.18. What does the nurse suspect?
An expected side effect of the drug
SGLT2 inhibitors can cause DKA with only mildly elevated glucose.
q7npndh: Which finding in a client taking pioglitazone should the nurse report?
Weight gain of 3 kg in a week with ankle edema
Morning fasting blood glucose of 118 mg/dL
Thiazolidinediones cause fluid retention and can worsen heart failure.
q1shu5ve: When should the nurse teach the client to take immediate-release glipizide?
Only when blood glucose is over 300
After the largest meal of the day
Glipizide stimulates insulin release and is taken before a meal to match food intake.
q1eb4too: A client has a potassium level of 7.0 mEq/L and peaked T waves. Which drug should the nurse expect to give first?
Calcium stabilizes the cardiac membrane immediately; other drugs lower potassium more slowly.
q15mhn0n: A client with hyperkalemia receives regular insulin 10 units IV with 25 g of dextrose. What should the nurse monitor most closely?
Insulin shifts potassium into cells; hypoglycemia can occur for several hours afterward.
q1kmf5u6: Which instruction should the nurse give a client taking patiromer?
Separate it from other oral drugs by 3 hours
Take it with your other pills to save time
Take it only when your heart races
Mix it into hot coffee before drinking it
Patiromer binds other oral drugs in the gut, so doses must be separated.
qib8mng: Calcium chloride IV is ordered for a client in cardiac arrest. Which access is preferred?
A central line or a large, secure vein
A small hand vein with a 24-gauge catheter
Deep IM injection in the vastus lateralis
Subcutaneous injection in the lower abdomen
Calcium chloride is highly irritating and causes tissue necrosis if it extravasates.
ql7nwy9: Calcium chloride and sodium bicarbonate are both ordered through the same IV line. What should the nurse do?
Flush the line well between the two drugs
Draw both into one syringe and push them together
Give them simultaneously through a Y-site
Mix both into one 100 mL bag of D5W
Calcium and bicarbonate form a calcium carbonate precipitate in the line.
q1ryjohq: A client uses albuterol and a fluticasone inhaler. Which statement indicates understanding?
"I will use the albuterol first, then wait before using the steroid."
"I will use the steroid inhaler first, then the albuterol right away."
"I will use the steroid inhaler only when I am short of breath."
"I will use albuterol every hour to prevent all attacks."
The bronchodilator opens the airways so the inhaled steroid can reach deeper.
q1wl9ix0: Which instruction should the nurse give a client using a fluticasone inhaler?
Rinse your mouth after each use
Use it during an acute asthma attack
Use it only on days you feel wheezy
Swallow some water before each puff
Rinsing removes steroid residue and helps prevent oral thrush.
qqe9duz: Which statement by a client with asthma about salmeterol indicates a need for further teaching?
"I will use it when an asthma attack starts."
"I will use it with my inhaled steroid every day."
"I will use it twice daily, about 12 hours apart."
"I will keep my rescue inhaler with me."
Salmeterol is a long-acting bronchodilator and is not used for acute attacks.
qol6kwo: Which adverse effect should the nurse teach the family of a client taking montelukast to report?
Mood changes, nightmares, or suicidal thoughts
A slight cough when outside in cold air
Thirst after meals for a few days
Montelukast has a boxed warning for neuropsychiatric events.
qqrfutz: Which condition in a client's history should prompt the nurse to clarify an order for tiotropium?
Anticholinergics can worsen narrow-angle glaucoma and urinary retention.
qyn143q: A child with croup improves after racemic epinephrine. What should the nurse plan?
Observe for 2 to 4 hours for the return of stridor
Discharge home within 15 minutes of the treatment
Give a dose of IM epinephrine before discharge
Repeat the treatment every hour overnight
Racemic epinephrine wears off within 2 hours, so rebound stridor may occur.
q1q14qc0: Which nursing action is most important while a client is receiving IV acyclovir?
Restrict fluids to 1 liter per day
Give the dose by rapid IV push
Hold all doses if a fever develops
Acyclovir can crystallize in the renal tubules; hydration and slow infusion protect renal function.
q1nwy3jh: A client receiving amphotericin B develops fever, chills, and rigors 1 hour into the infusion. Which plan should the nurse anticipate for the next dose?
Give the dose by rapid IV push over 2 minutes
Stop the drug permanently and switch to an oral agent
Mix it in normal saline to prevent the reaction
Infusion reactions are common and are reduced by premedication; potassium, magnesium, and creatinine should also be monitored.
qhg4368: A client on warfarin is started on trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Which lab value should the nurse anticipate monitoring closely?
TMP-SMX inhibits warfarin metabolism and can greatly raise the INR.
qlh6ral: Which statement by a client taking nitrofurantoin indicates understanding?
"I should take it on an empty stomach."
"I can stop taking it once the burning stops."
Nitrofurantoin can turn urine brown; it is taken with food, and the full course is completed as prescribed.
q110fkxy: Which instruction should the nurse give a client taking doxycycline?
Stay upright for 30 minutes after each dose
Take it at bedtime with a glass of milk
Lie down after each dose to prevent nausea
Use a tanning bed to prevent sunburn
Doxycycline can cause esophageal ulceration and photosensitivity.
q1ltqg87: Two clients with a creatinine clearance near 20 mL/min receive antibiotics. Which adverse effect belongs to cefepime rather than to vancomycin?
Flushing of the face and neck during infusion

Cefepime is renally cleared and accumulates in the central nervous system, where it antagonizes GABA-A receptors and causes encephalopathy, myoclonus and nonconvulsive seizures. Nephrotoxicity, infusion flushing and ototoxicity are the vancomycin effects.
qwtujo1: A client is receiving both vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam. Which lab should the nurse monitor most closely?
This combination increases the risk of acute kidney injury.
qdihgo0: A client with influenza symptoms asks about oseltamivir. What should the nurse explain?
It works best if started within 48 hours of symptom onset
It works best if started after a week of symptoms
It replaces the need for a yearly flu vaccine
It kills the bacteria that cause influenza
Influenza antivirals are most effective when started early.
q2ryfgx: A client with alcohol use disorder is admitted with confusion and a blood glucose of 42 mg/dL. Which approach should the nurse anticipate?
IV glucose now, with IV thiamine given alongside it
IV glucose now, with thiamine held until tomorrow
IV lorazepam first, before any glucose is given
Oral folic acid first, before any glucose is given

Hypoglycemia must be treated immediately, so glucose is not delayed. Thiamine is given with or just before the glucose because a glucose load in a thiamine-deficient client can precipitate or worsen Wernicke encephalopathy.
qrmrn5g: Which finding best indicates that lactulose is effective for a client with hepatic encephalopathy?
The client is oriented and has 2 to 3 soft stools daily
The client has 8 watery stools a day and low potassium
The client's serum ammonia level is higher than yesterday
The client is drowsier and has new asterixis
Lactulose lowers ammonia; the goal is improved mental status with soft stools.
q1xu6iaa: A client who drank antifreeze is admitted. Which drug should the nurse prepare?
Fomepizole blocks alcohol dehydrogenase, preventing the formation of toxic ethylene glycol metabolites.
qjafx00: For which ingestion would the nurse expect activated charcoal to be ineffective?
Charcoal does not bind metals, lithium, iron, alcohols, or caustics.
qxood16: A client received hydroxocobalamin for cyanide poisoning. Which finding should the nurse expect?
Hydroxocobalamin is red and temporarily discolors the skin and urine.
q9cyudc: A client with organophosphate poisoning is receiving repeated atropine doses. Which finding indicates an adequate effect?
Atropine is titrated to drying of airway secretions, not to pupil size.
qjdatss: A client has symptomatic bradycardia with a heart rate of 38/min and hypotension. Which atropine dose should the nurse anticipate?
1 mg IV push, repeated every 3 to 5 minutes
0.1 mg IV push, repeated every 30 minutes
5 mg IV push, given once only
Current guidelines recommend 1 mg IV every 3 to 5 minutes, up to a total of 3 mg.
q1apdcu3: After a nerve block with bupivacaine, a client reports a metallic taste and perioral numbness and becomes agitated. What does the nurse suspect?
An expected effect of the nerve block
