An allergic reaction to latex gloves
Local anesthetic systemic toxicity can progress to seizures and cardiac arrest; lipid emulsion is the treatment.
q1g00h92: A client is receiving IV procainamide. Which finding requires the nurse to stop the infusion?
Procainamide is stopped for QRS widening of more than 50%, hypotension, or suppression of the arrhythmia.
q1l6bw98: A client is starting dofetilide for atrial fibrillation. What should the nurse expect?
Hospital admission with ECG monitoring for 3 days
Starting at home with a weekly ECG check
An outpatient start with no monitoring
Taking it only when palpitations occur
Dofetilide can cause torsades de pointes, so it is started in a monitored setting with QTc and creatinine clearance checks.
q1fpsx: Which finding in a client taking verapamil should the nurse report?
Mild constipation on the second day
Verapamil slows AV conduction and can cause symptomatic bradycardia.
qlz5aud: Which finding is the priority concern in a client receiving a milrinone infusion?
Mild headache after the infusion starts
A modest drop in central venous pressure
Milrinone is an inotrope and vasodilator that can cause hypotension and dysrhythmias.
q1yheolo: For which client should the nurse question an order for clevidipine?
A client with soy and egg allergies
A client with hypertension after surgery
A client with a history of asthma
Clevidipine is a lipid emulsion that contains soy and egg products.
q1bqx0x6: Nicardipine 25 mg in 250 mL is ordered at 5 mg/hr. At what rate should the nurse set the infusion pump?
25 mg/250 mL = 0.1 mg/mL; 5 divided by 0.1 = 50 mL/hr.
qonqueo: After IV hydralazine is given for severe hypertension in pregnancy, which finding should the nurse anticipate and monitor?
Hydralazine dilates arterioles, causing a reflex increase in heart rate.
qeraraw: Esmolol 2,500 mg in 250 mL is ordered at 50 mcg/kg/min for an 80 kg client. At what rate should the nurse set the infusion pump?
50 x 80 = 4,000 mcg/min = 4 mg/min x 60 = 240 mg/hr; 2,500/250 = 10 mg/mL; 240 divided by 10 = 24 mL/hr.
qpabcmk: Propofol 10 mg/mL is ordered at 30 mcg/kg/min for a 70 kg client. At what rate should the nurse set the infusion pump?
30 x 70 = 2,100 mcg/min = 2.1 mg/min x 60 = 126 mg/hr; 126 divided by 10 = 12.6 mL/hr.
qgr9n0o: Dexmedetomidine 400 mcg in 100 mL is ordered at 0.6 mcg/kg/hr for a 90 kg client. At what rate should the nurse set the infusion pump?
0.6 x 90 = 54 mcg/hr; 400/100 = 4 mcg/mL; 54 divided by 4 = 13.5 mL/hr.
q1i3h1lb: A fentanyl infusion of 2,500 mcg in 250 mL is ordered at 75 mcg/hr. At what rate should the nurse set the infusion pump?
q13ts21x: Nitroglycerin 50 mg in 250 mL is ordered at 20 mcg/min. At what rate should the nurse set the infusion pump?
50 mg/250 mL = 200 mcg/mL; 20 mcg/min x 60 = 1,200 mcg/hr divided by 200 = 6 mL/hr.
qwy0cmx: Amiodarone 900 mg in 500 mL is ordered at 1 mg/min. At what rate should the nurse set the infusion pump?
900/500 = 1.8 mg/mL; 1 mg/min = 60 mg/hr; 60 divided by 1.8 = 33.3 mL/hr.
q37qpuf: Vancomycin 1 g in 250 mL is to infuse over 2 hours by gravity using tubing with a drop factor of 15 gtt/mL. What drip rate should the nurse set?
250 mL divided by 120 min x 15 gtt/mL = 31.25, rounded to 31 gtt/min.
qxwhe6p: Ceftriaxone 750 mg IV is ordered. After reconstitution, the vial contains 100 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse draw up?
q1jb4eg4: Enoxaparin 1 mg/kg subcutaneously every 12 hours is ordered for a client weighing 82 kg. The syringe contains 100 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
1 mg x 82 kg = 82 mg; 82 divided by 100 mg/mL = 0.82 mL.
q1d5l0z: Morphine 4 mg IV is ordered. The vial contains 10 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
q199gfx0: Furosemide 40 mg IV push is ordered. The vial contains 10 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
40 mg divided by 10 mg/mL = 4 mL; it is pushed slowly over 1 to 2 minutes.
q107aj0b: Levothyroxine 0.075 mg PO is ordered. The tablets are 25 mcg each. How many tablets should the nurse give?
q1ff2gy1: Potassium chloride 40 mEq PO is ordered. The liquid contains 20 mEq per 15 mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
40 mEq divided by 20 mEq = 2; 2 x 15 mL = 30 mL.
q1kd15jf: A loading dose of phenytoin 20 mg/kg is ordered for a 70 kg adult. At the maximum adult rate of 50 mg/min, what is the shortest safe infusion time?
20 x 70 = 1,400 mg; 1,400 divided by 50 mg/min = 28 minutes.
q1mshn1q: The nurse receives report on four clients on a psychiatric unit. Which client should the nurse see first?
A client on clozapine with a fever and sore throat
A client on lithium with a level of 0.9 mEq/L and mild thirst
A client on sertraline who reports trouble falling asleep
A client on haloperidol who asks for a snack
Fever and sore throat with clozapine may signal severe neutropenia and life-threatening infection.
qdpp2sy: Which medication task is appropriate for the RN to assign to an LPN?
Reinforcing warfarin diet teaching provided by the RN
Assessing a client on warfarin who has new confusion
Planning discharge teaching for a new warfarin user
Deciding whether to hold warfarin based on today's INR
LPNs can reinforce teaching; initial teaching, assessment of new changes, and clinical decisions belong to the RN.
qk2i1hq: Which instruction should the RN give to unlicensed assistive personnel (UAP) caring for a client receiving IV furosemide?
Measure and record all urine output this shift
Decide whether to give the next dose based on output
Assess the client's lung sounds every 4 hours
Check the potassium result and adjust the diet
UAP can measure intake and output; assessment and medication decisions remain with the nurse.
q1xcd3p9: Four clients are receiving antibiotics. Which client should the nurse see first?
A client on vancomycin with wheezing and throat tightness
A client on vancomycin with a trough due at 0600
A client on cephalexin with mild nausea after breakfast
A client on amoxicillin who asks for an extra pillow
Wheezing and throat tightness suggest anaphylaxis, which threatens the airway.
qxamynd: Which client should the nurse assess first?
A client on a morphine PCA with a sedation score of 3 and an RR of 9/min
A client on oxycodone reporting pain of 5 out of 10 before a dose
A client on hydrocodone asking when the next dose is due
A client on morphine who has had constipation for 2 days
Increasing sedation and a low respiratory rate precede opioid-induced respiratory arrest.
q1fan8u1: Four clients are receiving potassium replacement. Which client should the nurse see first?
A client receiving IV potassium chloride with new burning and swelling at the site
A client on oral potassium who asks for juice to take it with
A client whose potassium is now 4.0 mEq/L after two rounds of replacement
A client due for a potassium level recheck at 1000
Potassium infiltration can cause tissue damage; the infusion must be stopped immediately.
q1ultwsj: Four clients with diabetes are on the nurse's assignment. Which client should the nurse see first?
A client who received lispro 20 minutes ago and refuses breakfast
A client on glargine with a fasting glucose of 132 mg/dL
A client on metformin asking about tonight's dinner
A client on NPH who needs foot care teaching today
Rapid-acting insulin without food will soon cause hypoglycemia.
qu704on: Which task can the RN assign to an LPN on a postpartum unit?
Giving scheduled oral ibuprofen to a stable client
Titrating the oxytocin infusion for a client with heavy bleeding
Assessing a client on magnesium sulfate with new blurred vision
Providing initial teaching about methylergonovine side effects
LPNs give routine oral medications to stable clients; titration and assessment of unstable clients remain with the RN.
q15cb5t4: Before giving metoprolol succinate 50 mg PO to a client with heart failure, which assessment is most important?
Bowel sounds in all four quadrants
Pupil size and reaction to light
Skin turgor over the sternum and forearms
Beta blockers slow the heart rate and lower blood pressure; check both before each dose and hold the dose according to the ordered parameters.
q1puujvt: Before the morning dose of levothyroxine, the nurse should first confirm that:
The client has not yet eaten breakfast
The client has already taken the morning calcium dose
The client has had a glass of milk or juice
The client's bedtime glucose was normal
Levothyroxine is taken on an empty stomach 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast and at least 4 hours apart from calcium or iron.
q176j85y: Which result is most important to review before giving spironolactone to a client with heart failure?
Number of bowel movements since yesterday
Spironolactone is potassium-sparing; hyperkalemia is its major risk, so check potassium and renal function before giving.
q1c9utwm: Before giving metformin to a client admitted with vomiting and dehydration, which data should the nurse review?
Recent TSH and free T4 levels
Recent serum amylase and lipase levels
Metformin is cleared by the kidneys; dehydration and a low eGFR raise the risk of lactic acidosis.
q6hmn03: Before and after albuterol is given by nebulizer, which assessment best shows the drug's effect?
Breath sounds and work of breathing
Blood glucose and level of consciousness
Albuterol is a bronchodilator; assess lung sounds, respiratory effort, SpO2, and heart rate before and after the treatment.
q1cxt7ig: Before giving insulin lispro with a meal, the nurse should first check:
The fingerstick glucose and that the meal tray is present
The serum sodium and that the client is sitting upright
The blood pressure and that the client has voided
The temperature and that the IV line is patent
Rapid-acting insulin starts working in about 15 minutes; confirm the glucose and that food is available before giving it.
q2a7ps: Before giving the evening dose of warfarin, which assessment is most important?
Today's INR result and any signs of bleeding
Today's potassium result and any muscle cramps
Today's glucose result and any shakiness
Today's sodium result and any new ankle swelling
The INR guides warfarin dosing; the nurse also assesses for bleeding before each dose.
qsu7kka: A client with gout is prescribed hydrochlorothiazide. Which data should the nurse review before the first dose?
Recent uric acid level and gout flares
Recent amylase level and alcohol use
Recent vitamin B12 level and diet
Recent TSH level and weight changes
Thiazides raise uric acid levels and can trigger gout attacks.
q1lpms1q: Before starting oral amiodarone, which baseline studies should the nurse confirm have been done?
Thyroid, liver, and pulmonary function tests
Serum amylase, lipase, and a lipid panel
Complete blood count and blood cultures
Amiodarone can cause thyroid disease, liver injury, and pulmonary toxicity; baselines are needed along with an ECG and eye exam.
qrjc222: Before giving diltiazem 20 mg IV push for atrial fibrillation with RVR, which assessment is most important?
Blood pressure and the ECG rhythm
Temperature and white blood cell count
Pupil response and level of consciousness
IV diltiazem can cause hypotension, bradycardia, and heart block; check BP and confirm the rhythm on a continuous monitor.
qm4of6c: Before starting a weight-based heparin infusion, which baseline data should the nurse verify?
Current weight, aPTT or anti-Xa, platelets, and hemoglobin
Current weight, serum sodium, potassium, chloride, and glucose levels
Height, lipid panel, and liver enzymes
Temperature, blood cultures, and white blood cell count
Dosing depends on an accurate weight; baseline coagulation tests and a CBC with platelets are needed to monitor bleeding and HIT.
q8r04nc: A client with hypomagnesemia is to receive IV magnesium sulfate. Which assessment should the nurse perform before and during the infusion?
Deep tendon reflexes, respirations, and urine output
Pupil size, bowel sounds, and skin turgor
Capillary glucose, temperature, and pain score
Peripheral pulses, edema, and daily weight
Loss of deep tendon reflexes is an early sign of magnesium toxicity; monitor respirations and urine output because magnesium is renally excreted.
qcgipmy: Before starting an IV nitroglycerin infusion for unstable angina, which question is most important to ask the client?
Have you taken sildenafil or tadalafil in the past 48 hours?
Have you had any recent changes in your bowel habits?
Do you have an allergy to shellfish or iodine dye?
Have you ever had a reaction to latex gloves or IV tubing in the past?
Nitrates with PDE-5 inhibitors can cause severe, refractory hypotension (avoid within 24 hours of sildenafil and 48 hours of tadalafil).
qolu80: Before giving insulin glargine to a client who is NPO for surgery, the nurse should first:
Check the glucose and clarify the dose with the provider
Hold the dose entirely until the client is able to eat again
Give the dose mixed with a rapid-acting insulin
Give double the dose to cover the stress of surgery
Basal insulin is usually continued, often at a reduced dose, when NPO; check glucose and confirm the dose rather than omitting it.
q1xag0wr: Before increasing the theophylline dose for a client with poorly controlled asthma, which data should the nurse review?
Serum theophylline level and heart rate
Serum potassium level and urine output
Serum calcium level and bone density
Theophylline has a narrow therapeutic range (about 5 to 15 mcg/mL); toxicity causes tachycardia, dysrhythmias, and seizures.
q1n1959i: Four clients are due for oral digoxin. Which apical pulse, counted for a full minute, meets the usual parameter to hold the dose in an adult?

The standard adult parameter is to hold digoxin and report an apical pulse below 60 beats per minute, because digoxin slows conduction through the AV node. A fast rate is not a reason to hold it, since digoxin is given to slow the rate.
q150kjiu: A client takes metoprolol and amlodipine each morning. The pulse is 48 beats per minute and the blood pressure is 128/76 mm Hg. Which action fits these findings?
Hold the metoprolol and report the pulse, and give the amlodipine
Hold both drugs, because each one slows the heart rate
Give both drugs, because the blood pressure is acceptable
Hold the amlodipine and report the pulse, and give the metoprolol

Metoprolol is the drug that slows the heart rate, so a pulse of 48 is the reason to hold it and report. Amlodipine is a dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that dilates arteries without slowing the AV node, and it may raise the rate slightly.
qwn0y3w: A client on lisinopril is also ordered spironolactone and a potassium-containing salt substitute. The morning potassium is 5.4 mEq/L. What should the nurse report?
That three sources are all raising potassium at once
That lisinopril itself has no effect on potassium
That the salt substitute will actually lower the potassium
That spironolactone offsets the lisinopril effect

ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone, spironolactone blocks aldosterone at the tubule, and salt substitutes are potassium chloride, so all three push potassium up. Normal potassium is 3.5 to 5.0 mEq/L, and this combination is a common cause of hyperkalemia.
qogn2y4: A client takes glipizide before breakfast and metformin with dinner. At 1100 the client is shaky and diaphoretic with a glucose of 54 mg/dL. Which drug best explains this?
Glipizide, because it makes the pancreas release insulin
Metformin, because it blocks glucose absorption from food
Both equally, since each one lowers glucose the same way
Neither one, since oral agents do not cause low glucose

Sulfonylureas such as glipizide stimulate insulin secretion whether or not the client has eaten, so they do cause hypoglycemia. Metformin lowers hepatic glucose output and improves insulin sensitivity, and it rarely causes hypoglycemia used alone.
qprywhx: A client started on amlodipine 10 mg daily 3 weeks ago now has pitting edema of both ankles, clear lung sounds, and no weight gain. What should the nurse report?
Ankle edema that is a known dose-related effect
Ankle edema that shows the client is in fluid overload
Ankle edema that means the dose must be doubled
Ankle edema unrelated to any of the medications

Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers dilate arterioles more than veins, so fluid is driven into the tissue at the ankles. The edema is dose-related rather than volume overload, which is why the clear lungs and stable weight matter here.
qm6jitq: Three clients take diuretics: one furosemide, one hydrochlorothiazide, and one spironolactone. Which client is most likely to have a high potassium?

Spironolactone blocks aldosterone in the distal tubule, so sodium is lost while potassium is retained, and hyperkalemia is its main risk. Furosemide and hydrochlorothiazide both deliver more sodium to the potassium-secreting segment and cause potassium loss.
q4v8030: A client has received enoxaparin for 6 days. Which platelet result should the nurse report before giving the next dose?
A drop from 240,000 to 95,000 per mm3
A drop from 310,000 to 265,000 per mm3
A rise from 180,000 to 220,000 per mm3
A steady value of 155,000 per mm3

Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is suspected when the platelet count falls by more than 50 percent, usually 5 to 10 days after starting, and it causes clotting rather than bleeding. A count near 150,000 or a small fluctuation does not fit that pattern.
qkzc3f4: A client on a heparin infusion per protocol has an anti-Xa level above the target range and no bleeding. The nurse should:
Follow the protocol to hold or reduce the infusion and recheck
Continue the infusion unchanged and recheck the level in 24 hours
Increase the rate as directed by the protocol
Give protamine and stop the heparin permanently
Heparin protocols direct a brief hold and a rate decrease for supratherapeutic levels, then a repeat level.
quit1va: A client with digoxin toxicity has a level of 4.2 ng/mL, a potassium of 6.1 mEq/L, and a ventricular rate of 36 with hypotension. Which treatment should the nurse prepare?

Digoxin immune Fab is indicated for life-threatening dysrhythmias or hyperkalemia from toxicity, because it binds digoxin and the complex is excreted. IV calcium is avoided in digoxin toxicity, since it can worsen myocardial calcium overload.
qf6a2on: An IV amiodarone infusion is being prepared. Which aspect of the preparation is specific to this drug?
It is diluted in D5W and given through an in-line filter
It is diluted in normal saline and shielded from the light
It is given undiluted by rapid IV push over 1 minute
It is mixed with heparin to keep the line patent

Amiodarone is incompatible with sodium chloride and is diluted in D5W, and its polysorbate 80 diluent leaches plasticizer and can form precipitate, so an in-line filter is used. It also causes phlebitis, so a central line is preferred beyond a few hours.
q1dtxxoa: A client with a potassium of 2.8 mEq/L has 40 mEq of potassium chloride ordered IV. Which rate is within the usual limit for a peripheral line?
10 mEq per hour by infusion pump
40 mEq per hour by infusion pump
20 mEq per hour by slow IV push

The usual peripheral limit is 10 mEq per hour, with up to 20 mEq per hour through a central line on continuous cardiac monitoring. Potassium is not given by IV push, because a bolus can cause cardiac arrest.
qpgor96: A client in DKA on an IV insulin infusion now has a glucose of 220 mg/dL, and the anion gap is still elevated. What should the nurse anticipate?
Adding dextrose to the IV fluid and continuing the insulin
Stopping the insulin now that the glucose is near normal
Switching to subcutaneous glargine now and stopping the drip
Doubling the insulin rate to close the gap faster

The insulin drip continues until the anion gap closes and the ketosis clears, so dextrose is added once glucose falls to about 200 to 250 mg/dL to prevent hypoglycemia. Stopping insulin early lets ketone production resume.
q1gpeehv: A client with severe hypertension and a history of asthma needs an IV antihypertensive. Which ordered drug should the nurse question?
Labetalol, because it also blocks beta-2 receptors
Hydralazine, because it is a direct vasodilator
Nicardipine, because it is a calcium channel blocker
Metoprolol, because it is cardioselective at low doses

Labetalol blocks beta-1, beta-2 and alpha-1 receptors, and the beta-2 blockade can trigger bronchospasm in asthma. Hydralazine and nicardipine are vasodilators with no bronchial effect, and metoprolol is relatively beta-1 selective at usual doses.
q1wuklsj: A client on apixaban is bleeding after a fall, and the provider asks the nurse about reversal. Which agent reverses a factor Xa inhibitor?

Andexanet alfa is a decoy factor Xa molecule that binds apixaban and rivaroxaban. Protamine reverses heparin, idarucizumab reverses dabigatran, and vitamin K reverses warfarin by restoring clotting factor synthesis over hours.
q1rodxug: A client with an inferior MI and right ventricular involvement has chest pain, and nitroglycerin is ordered. Why is this client at particular risk?
The right ventricle depends on preload, which nitrates reduce
Nitroglycerin raises myocardial oxygen demand in inferior MI
Nitroglycerin causes reflex bradycardia in right ventricular MI
Nitroglycerin is cleared more slowly when the right side fails

A failing right ventricle cannot generate output without adequate filling, and nitrates are venodilators that drop preload, so the blood pressure can fall sharply. Fluid, not a nitrate, is the first support for right ventricular MI hypotension.
q1p9mrfm: A client taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation asks what INR the provider is aiming for. The usual target range is:
For most indications, including atrial fibrillation and VTE, the target INR is 2.0 to 3.0.
qvzuu9z: Which lab value should be checked periodically in a client on long-term metformin?
Long-term metformin reduces vitamin B12 absorption; B12 and renal function are monitored.
q15119rn: Which lab test best shows how well a client's diabetes has been controlled over the past 2 to 3 months?
The A1c reflects average glucose over about 3 months.
q1tvicls: Which lab result is used most often to adjust a client's levothyroxine dose?
TSH is the main test for adjusting thyroid replacement in primary hypothyroidism.
qeyevgp: A client has taken hydrochlorothiazide for 6 months. Which lab changes are most likely from the drug?
Low calcium and low uric acid
Thiazides can cause hypokalemia, hyponatremia, hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia, and hypercalcemia.
qvdppdk: A client takes oral potassium chloride with furosemide. Which potassium level is within the normal range?
Normal serum potassium is about 3.5 to 5.0 mEq/L.
qcrb59x: When should blood be drawn for a routine digoxin level in a client on daily oral dosing?
Just before the next dose, at least 6 hours after the last
Thirty minutes after the morning dose, when the level is highest
Any time of day, since timing does not matter
Right after breakfast, before any fluids are given
Digoxin levels are drawn at least 6 to 8 hours after a dose, usually right before the next one, after distribution is complete.
q1lc5de1: A client taking clopidogrel and aspirin after a stent has a CBC drawn. Which result is most important to report?
Hemoglobin that fell from 13.2 to 9.8 g/dL
A significant hemoglobin drop on dual antiplatelet therapy suggests bleeding.
q1ur08tp: A client on a heparin infusion titrated by aPTT has an aPTT of 72 seconds with a control of 30 seconds. The nurse interprets this result as:
Below the range, requiring a bolus
Too high, requiring the infusion to be stopped
A therapeutic aPTT is about 1.5 to 2.5 times the control (roughly 45 to 75 seconds here).
q1xg6fdj: A client receiving IV furosemide twice daily for heart failure should have which labs monitored most closely?
Loop diuretics cause losses of potassium, sodium, and magnesium and can impair renal function.
qe93ctf: A client taking empagliflozin is admitted with nausea and malaise. The glucose is 160 mg/dL. Which labs are most important to check?
Hemoglobin A1c and a lipid panel
SGLT2 inhibitors can cause euglycemic DKA, with ketoacidosis despite a near-normal glucose.
q19ir9cj: A client on long-term amiodarone has new fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance. Which lab should the nurse anticipate?
Amiodarone contains iodine and can cause hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism.
qmd5f0h: Which result should the nurse report immediately for a client receiving an IV magnesium infusion?
Magnesium of 5.2 mg/dL with weak reflexes
Magnesium of 2.0 mg/dL with normal reflexes
Magnesium of 1.9 mg/dL with mild nausea
Magnesium of 2.3 mg/dL with warm, flushed skin
Normal magnesium is about 1.7 to 2.2 mg/dL; a high level with decreased reflexes signals toxicity.
qhktwww: A client receiving IV potassium replacement also has a low magnesium. Why should magnesium also be corrected?
Low magnesium makes low potassium hard to correct
Magnesium blocks the absorption of IV potassium
Low magnesium causes falsely high potassium results
Magnesium and potassium cannot be given on the same day
Hypomagnesemia increases renal potassium loss, so hypokalemia is refractory until magnesium is replaced.
q3fsjig: A client with renal impairment is receiving treatment-dose enoxaparin. Which lab test may be ordered to monitor its effect?
Enoxaparin does not reliably change the aPTT or INR; anti-Xa levels are used in renal impairment, obesity, and pregnancy.
q1a6tliz: A client with heart failure is starting carvedilol. Which vital sign finding is most important to report after the first doses?
Dizziness with a standing BP of 82/50
A resting pulse that decreases from 88 to 72/min
Carvedilol blocks alpha-1 receptors and often causes orthostatic hypotension when started or increased.
q1ip3mty: After a client takes sublingual nitroglycerin for chest pain, which vital sign should the nurse check before a second tablet?
Nitroglycerin causes vasodilation and hypotension; hold further doses for a systolic BP below 90 mm Hg.
qxnluzg: A client stopped taking clonidine 2 days ago because of dry mouth. Which vital sign finding should the nurse expect?
Low blood pressure and slow pulse
Abrupt clonidine withdrawal causes rebound hypertension; it must be tapered.
q19qvs5j: A child receives albuterol by nebulizer. Which vital sign change is an expected side effect?
Beta-2 agonists commonly cause tachycardia and tremor.
q1hn6fjd: An older adult with heart disease is starting levothyroxine. Which vital sign is most important to monitor as the dose is increased?
Thyroid replacement raises cardiac workload and can cause tachycardia, angina, and atrial fibrillation in older adults.
q12pvnq0: A client on long-term prednisone should have which vital sign monitored regularly?
Apical pulse for a full minute
Corticosteroids cause sodium and fluid retention, which can raise blood pressure.
qeij26o: A client takes the first dose of lisinopril at home. Which instruction about vital signs should the nurse reinforce?
Check BP and rise slowly because of first-dose dizziness
Check pulse and skip the dose if it is above 80
Check temperature daily for the first week
Check breathing rate before each dose and skip it if fast
ACE inhibitors can cause first-dose hypotension; rise slowly and monitor BP.
q1ks8ccn: A client receives verapamil 5 mg IV push for SVT. Which vital sign should the nurse monitor most closely during and after the push?
Blood pressure, because of the risk of hypotension
Temperature, because of the risk of fever
Respiratory rate, because of the risk of apnea
Oxygen saturation, because of the risk of bronchospasm
IV verapamil causes vasodilation and can produce significant hypotension and bradycardia.
q1kubnmr: Metoprolol 5 mg IV is ordered for a client with an acute MI. Which monitoring is required during administration?
Continuous ECG with BP and heart rate checks
Peak flow readings before and after each dose
IV beta blockers can cause bradycardia, heart block, and hypotension; monitor ECG, HR, and BP.
q1u2v6di: During an IV amiodarone loading infusion, which vital sign change is most common and requires monitoring?
Hypotension is the most common adverse effect of IV amiodarone, along with bradycardia.
q1catomj: A client receiving IV aminophylline has a heart rate of 132/min and new restlessness. The nurse suspects:
An allergic reaction to the diluent
Aminophylline is converted to theophylline; tachycardia, restlessness, and vomiting are early signs of toxicity.
qu07f7z: A client receiving IV digoxin loading doses for atrial fibrillation should have which vital sign monitored closely?
Digoxin slows AV conduction; monitor apical rate and rhythm for bradycardia and heart block.
q1m0rw28: A client on a heparin infusion now has a heart rate of 118/min and a BP of 92/58 mm Hg, up from 76/min and down from 128/78 mm Hg, respectively. The nurse suspects:
Rising heart rate with falling BP in an anticoagulated client suggests hemorrhage.
q1dqc0w5: A client with a hypertensive emergency is started on a nicardipine infusion. How much should the mean arterial pressure generally be lowered in the first hour?
Lowering BP too fast can cause cerebral, renal, or coronary ischemia; reduce MAP by no more than 25 percent in the first hour.
q8dtb2o: A client has had continuous albuterol nebulization for 2 hours. Which findings are the expected drug effect rather than worsening asthma?
Heart rate 118, fine tremor, potassium 3.2 mEq/L
Heart rate 118, rising carbon dioxide, drowsiness
Heart rate 56, no wheezing audible, cyanosis
Heart rate 118, single-word answers, accessory muscle use

Beta-2 stimulation causes tachycardia, tremor, and a shift of potassium into cells that lowers the serum level. A rising carbon dioxide with drowsiness, a silent chest, or single-word dyspnea point to respiratory failure instead of a side effect.
q8w5v8t: A client taking oral amiodarone reports blue-gray discoloration of the facial skin and sunburns easily. The nurse recognizes this as:
A known skin effect of amiodarone
A sign of low thyroid hormone
Amiodarone causes photosensitivity and blue-gray skin discoloration; teach sun protection.
q1fajk8c: A male client taking spironolactone reports tender, enlarged breasts. The nurse recognizes this as:
An expected effect that means the drug is working
Spironolactone has antiandrogen effects that cause gynecomastia; eplerenone is an alternative.
q10ssfsm: A client taking glimepiride skipped lunch and is now sweaty, shaky, and confused. The nurse suspects:
Sulfonylureas cause hypoglycemia, especially with missed meals.
qhjo4hj: Which adverse effect of metformin is rare but life-threatening?
Lactic acidosis is rare but serious; risk rises with renal impairment, hypoxia, and contrast dye.
q12kl6be: A client using an inhaled corticosteroid has white patches on the tongue and inner cheeks. The nurse recognizes this as:
A vitamin deficiency from the drug
Inhaled corticosteroids can cause thrush; rinsing the mouth and using a spacer lower the risk.
q1y30ptt: A client starting dapagliflozin should be monitored for which common adverse effect?
SGLT2 inhibitors increase glucose in the urine, which promotes genital fungal infections and UTIs.
q11ra1ee: A client taking semaglutide has severe abdominal pain radiating to the back, along with vomiting. The nurse suspects:
GLP-1 agonists are linked to pancreatitis; severe pain radiating to the back must be reported.
q1rq5di4: A client taking apixaban reports black, tarry stools. The nurse recognizes this as:
An expected effect of iron in the drug
A sign of a stomach virus
Melena suggests upper GI bleeding, a serious adverse effect of anticoagulants.
qe6f0k5: A client on day 6 of heparin therapy has a new painful, cool, pale leg, and the platelet count has dropped 60 percent. The nurse suspects:
An expected heparin effect on platelets
A heparin allergy limited to the skin
Compartment syndrome from an infiltrated IV in that leg
HIT typically appears 5 to 10 days into therapy and causes paradoxical arterial and venous clots.
q7vsi6j: A client receiving IV potassium chloride through a peripheral line reports burning at the site. The nurse recognizes this as:
Vein irritation that requires checking the site and rate
An expected sensation that can be ignored if the IV still flushes
A sign that the potassium level is too low
Potassium irritates veins; assess for infiltration and phlebitis and slow the rate or dilute per policy.
qguzptr: A client receiving an IV insulin infusion for DKA develops muscle weakness and flat T waves. The nurse suspects:
Insulin shifts potassium into cells; flat T waves and weakness indicate hypokalemia.
qs2yyua: Which dysrhythmias are most associated with digoxin toxicity?
Premature ventricular contractions and AV block
Rapid atrial fibrillation with a wide QRS only
Torsades de pointes from QT prolongation
Digoxin toxicity causes PVCs, bigeminy, AV block, and atrial tachycardia with block.
q9a9trk: A client receiving high-dose IV methylprednisolone should be monitored for which adverse effect?
Corticosteroids raise blood glucose, even in clients without diabetes.
q1lfmu40: A client who started warfarin 4 days ago without a heparin bridge has painful purple areas on the thighs and breasts. The nurse suspects:
Expected bruising from a therapeutic INR
Warfarin skin necrosis occurs early in therapy, often in fatty areas, and is linked to protein C deficiency.
q7q2rr9: A client receiving IV levothyroxine for myxedema coma develops chest pain and a heart rate of 128/min. The nurse suspects:
Myocardial ischemia from rapid thyroid replacement
Worsening myxedema from inadequate thyroid dosing
Thyroid hormone increases myocardial oxygen demand and can trigger ischemia and dysrhythmias.
qc72ih9: A client taking warfarin asks about diet. Which teaching is correct?
Keep vitamin K intake consistent from day to day
Avoid all green vegetables while taking warfarin
Eat extra spinach daily to protect the liver
Take warfarin with grapefruit juice for best absorption
Sudden changes in vitamin K intake change the INR; keep intake steady rather than avoiding vitamin K.
q1cw8d82: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client going home on digoxin?
Take your pulse before each dose and report a rate under 60
Take a double dose the following day whenever you miss a dose
Take the dose with an antacid to prevent nausea
Stop the drug if your ankles swell
Clients check their pulse before each dose and never double a missed dose.
q12iwfz7: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client starting empagliflozin?
Drink fluids and practice good genital hygiene
Limit fluids to 1 liter per day to prevent swelling
Take it at bedtime to prevent hypoglycemia at night
Expect to gain several pounds in the first month
SGLT2 inhibitors cause osmotic diuresis and genital infections; stay hydrated and keep the area clean.
qwtidgl: A client is starting weekly dulaglutide injections. Which teaching is correct?
Inject once a week on the same day, with or without food
Inject it only on days when the blood glucose is above 250
Mix it in one syringe with insulin glargine
Dulaglutide is a once-weekly GLP-1 agonist given the same day each week regardless of meals.
q1b8foxf: A client asks if the fluticasone inhaler can be used to stop an asthma attack. The nurse explains that it:
Prevents inflammation and does not give quick relief
Opens airways within minutes during an attack
Should be used only when wheezing starts
Works best when taken just before exercise
Inhaled corticosteroids are daily controller drugs; a short-acting beta agonist is used for attacks.
q89f5su: A client taking prednisone once daily should be taught to:
Take it in the morning with food
Take it at bedtime on an empty stomach
Stop it right away if mood changes occur
Double the dose on days when feeling well
Morning dosing mimics the natural cortisol rhythm, and food reduces GI irritation.
q1jrk7h9: A client taking clopidogrel after a coronary stent asks whether he can stop it because he feels fine. The nurse explains that:
Stopping early raises the risk of a clot in the stent
It can be stopped once the chest pain is gone
It can be stopped if he takes aspirin twice a day
It needs to be taken only for the first week
Stopping antiplatelet therapy early after a stent can cause stent thrombosis and MI.
q1o0x42c: A client asks why IV heparin is being continued after warfarin was started. The nurse explains that:
Warfarin takes several days to reach full effect
Warfarin works only when heparin is also present
Heparin prevents the stomach upset from warfarin
Heparin reverses warfarin if bleeding occurs
Warfarin takes days to deplete clotting factors, so heparin overlaps until the INR is therapeutic.
q6e0pzz: A client taking warfarin is started on oral amiodarone. Which teaching point is most important at discharge?
Expect more frequent INR checks and a lower warfarin dose
Expect the INR to fall, so the warfarin dose will be raised
Stop the warfarin while taking the amiodarone
Take the two drugs at least 4 hours apart in the day

Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 and other pathways, so warfarin levels and the INR rise over the following weeks and the warfarin dose is often cut by 30 to 50 percent. Spacing the doses does not help, since the interaction happens in the liver.
q15f24ox: A client using an insulin pump with insulin aspart asks what to do if the pump stops working. The nurse teaches the client to:
Inject rapid-acting insulin and check glucose and ketones
Wait until the pump company replaces it and skip insulin meanwhile
Drink juice every hour until the pump is fixed
Take an extra dose of metformin until it works
Pumps deliver only rapid-acting insulin, so DKA can develop within hours of an interruption.
qwsfb5t: A client taking theophylline asks about caffeine and smoking. The nurse teaches that:
Caffeine adds side effects and smoking changes drug levels
Caffeine and smoking have no effect on theophylline
Coffee should be used to increase the drug's effect
Smoking more cigarettes will reduce theophylline side effects
Caffeine adds stimulant effects; smoking induces metabolism, and quitting can raise theophylline levels.
q6nq5fh: A client with adrenal insufficiency takes hydrocortisone. Which sick-day teaching is correct?
Increase the dose as directed and seek care if vomiting occurs
Stop taking the drug until the illness has passed and appetite returns
Take the dose only when symptoms appear
Cut the dose in half whenever you have a fever or chills
Illness raises cortisol needs; stress dosing prevents adrenal crisis, and vomiting requires injectable steroid or emergency care.
qpedjx6: A client going home after an MI has sublingual nitroglycerin. Which instruction about chest pain is correct?
Call 911 if pain is not better 5 minutes after one tablet
Take up to 5 tablets 1 minute apart and call if the pain continues
Call the provider in the morning if pain lasts overnight
Wait 15 minutes between each of 3 tablets
Current guidance is to call 911 if chest pain is unimproved or worse 5 minutes after the first dose.
q8jcchc: A client newly diagnosed with type 1 diabetes is discharged on glargine and lispro. Which statement indicates understanding of sick-day management?
"I will keep taking my glargine even if I cannot eat."
"I will skip all of my insulin when I am vomiting."
"I will stop checking my glucose until I feel better."
"I will only check ketones once a week when sick."
Basal insulin is continued during illness to prevent DKA; glucose and ketones are checked more often.
q1z01ocv: A client is discharged on furosemide 40 mg twice daily. Which teaching is best?
Take the second dose by midafternoon and weigh daily
Take both doses at bedtime to rest the kidneys
Limit potassium-rich foods while taking the drug
Report weight gain only if it exceeds 10 pounds
Early dosing prevents nocturia; daily weights detect fluid gain (report 2 to 3 lb in a day or 5 lb in a week).
qkas7mg: A client taking digoxin is started on furosemide. The nurse should monitor for:
Reduced digoxin effect from high potassium
High blood glucose from the combination
Loop diuretics lower potassium and magnesium, which increases digoxin toxicity.
q16sxukp: A client taking warfarin asks about taking ibuprofen for back pain. The nurse explains that:
NSAIDs increase the risk of bleeding with warfarin
The combination is safe if taken with food
NSAIDs impair platelets and irritate the GI tract, raising bleeding risk with warfarin.
qg6st3s: A client takes levothyroxine and ferrous sulfate. The nurse should reinforce:
Take them at least 4 hours apart
Take them together to improve absorption
Take them together with a glass of milk
Take the iron first, then levothyroxine 10 minutes later
Iron binds levothyroxine and reduces its absorption.
q1opgo9k: A client on losartan takes ibuprofen daily for arthritis. The nurse should report concern for:
Reduced kidney function and higher potassium
Low blood sugar and gradual weight gain
Increased bleeding from the gums when brushing
NSAIDs with ARBs or ACE inhibitors can cause acute kidney injury and hyperkalemia and blunt BP control.
qhqbetr: A client taking oral diltiazem is also prescribed metoprolol. The nurse should monitor for:
Both drugs slow AV conduction; together they can cause bradycardia and heart block.
q1jk1415: A client taking clopidogrel asks about taking omeprazole for heartburn. The nurse explains that:
Omeprazole may reduce clopidogrel's antiplatelet effect
Omeprazole will greatly increase clopidogrel's bleeding risk
The two drugs must be taken at the same time
Omeprazole is the preferred acid reducer with clopidogrel
Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, which activates clopidogrel; pantoprazole is often preferred.
q10zalqy: A client taking glyburide asks about drinking alcohol. The nurse explains that alcohol can:
Raise blood glucose and cause ketoacidosis
Cause the drug to be excreted more quickly
Alcohol increases the risk of severe, sometimes delayed, hypoglycemia with sulfonylureas. A disulfiram-like flushing reaction is classically linked to chlorpropamide and is uncommon with glyburide.
qnn3lz2: A client using albuterol is prescribed propranolol for migraines. The nurse recognizes that:
Propranolol may block albuterol and cause bronchospasm
The combination makes albuterol twice as effective
The two drugs have no known interaction
Nonselective beta blockers block beta-2 receptors, opposing albuterol and risking bronchospasm.
q1n8au5m: A client taking digoxin is started on IV amiodarone. The nurse anticipates:
A reduction in the digoxin dose
An increase in the digoxin dose
No change in the digoxin dose
Switching digoxin to the IV route
Amiodarone raises digoxin levels; the digoxin dose is usually cut by about half.
qx6win9: A client on warfarin is started on trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a UTI. The nurse should anticipate:
Closer INR checks due to bleeding risk
Lower INR values needing a higher dose
No change, since antibiotics do not affect INR
A switch from warfarin to aspirin
TMP-SMX inhibits warfarin metabolism and can sharply raise the INR.
q13cqd61: A client taking theophylline is started on ciprofloxacin. The nurse should monitor for:
Theophylline toxicity, such as tachycardia and seizures
Subtherapeutic theophylline levels with worsening wheezing
Ciprofloxacin inhibits theophylline metabolism and can cause toxicity.
q8j6j6n: A client receiving IV potassium chloride also takes lisinopril and spironolactone. The nurse should:
Expect lower potassium from the combination
Give the potassium faster to finish sooner
Hold lisinopril because it lowers potassium
ACE inhibitors and potassium-sparing diuretics both raise potassium.
q11c2pzs: A client receiving enoxaparin is also prescribed ketorolac for pain. The nurse should:
Question the order due to increased bleeding risk
Give both, since they act on different organs
Give ketorolac only if the platelet count is low
Separate the doses by 1 hour to prevent interaction
Ketorolac impairs platelet function and adds to the bleeding risk of anticoagulants.
q1ipn4b7: A client on a diltiazem infusion is ordered IV metoprolol for rate control. The nurse should:
Clarify the order due to risk of severe bradycardia
Give both at once for a faster effect on the AV node
Give metoprolol only if the BP is above 160
Give metoprolol IM instead of IV
IV calcium channel blockers and IV beta blockers together can cause profound bradycardia, heart block, and hypotension.
q1w86n05: A client taking apixaban is prescribed rifampin. The nurse recognizes that rifampin may:
Lower apixaban levels and raise clot risk
Raise apixaban levels and cause bleeding
Have no effect on apixaban levels
Turn apixaban into a toxic compound
Rifampin strongly induces CYP3A4 and P-gp, lowering apixaban levels; the combination is avoided.
q2ttwox: A client on metformin is scheduled for a cardiac catheterization with IV contrast tomorrow. Which information should the nurse pass on to the provider?
The most recent creatinine and eGFR results
The most recent hemoglobin A1c result
The client's usual breakfast time at home
The client's weight at the last clinic visit

Metformin is cleared unchanged by the kidney, and contrast can reduce renal function, so the drug may accumulate and raise the risk of lactic acidosis. Renal function decides whether metformin is held, so creatinine and eGFR are the values to report.
q19ns2hs: Which finding in a client taking spironolactone should the nurse report?
Muscle weakness and an irregular pulse
Mild thirst after taking the dose
A weight loss of 1 pound since yesterday
Weakness and an irregular pulse suggest hyperkalemia.
q1ksgif0: Which finding in a client taking warfarin should be reported right away?
A small bruise after bumping a table
Slight gum bleeding after flossing that stops quickly
An INR of 2.4 on today's lab report
Hematuria and unexplained bruising suggest excess anticoagulation.
q8m724j: A client taking prednisone has a temperature of 100.4 F and a sore throat. The nurse should:
Report it, since steroids can mask infection
Give an extra prednisone dose for stress
Steroids suppress immunity and blunt fever, so even a low-grade fever may indicate a significant infection; steroids are never stopped abruptly.
q18wuztu: A client takes insulin glargine at bedtime and has woken at 0300 sweating and shaky for three nights, with fasting glucose near 190 mg/dL. What should the nurse report?
Nighttime hypoglycemia with rebound morning highs
A glargine dose that is clearly too low at night
An expected pattern needing no change in the dose
A need for a bedtime snack and a recheck in a month

Glargine has a flat profile lasting about 24 hours, so an excessive bedtime dose can cause overnight hypoglycemia followed by counterregulatory hormone release and a high fasting value. Raising the dose for that high reading would deepen the 0300 lows.
qefnd5b: Which finding in a client taking hydrochlorothiazide should the nurse report?
Leg cramps and a potassium of 3.0 mEq/L
Increased urination after the morning dose
A blood pressure of 128/80 mm Hg
Thiazides cause hypokalemia, which shows up as muscle cramps and weakness.
q17js1pw: A client with type 2 diabetes is started on metoprolol. Which change in hypoglycemia symptoms should the nurse teach the client to report?
Low glucose may cause sweating without a fast heart rate
Low glucose will no longer cause any symptoms at all
Low glucose will now cause slow, deep breathing instead
Low glucose will cause facial flushing instead of pallor

Beta blockers blunt the adrenergic warning signs of hypoglycemia such as tachycardia, palpitations and tremor, while sweating is cholinergic and persists. Clients check glucose more often because the early warning is reduced, not erased.
q1272srn: IV regular insulin with dextrose is given for a potassium of 6.8 mEq/L. Thirty minutes later the potassium is 5.6 mEq/L. What should the nurse report about this result?
Potassium is shifted into cells and will rebound
The potassium is now permanently corrected
The insulin dose was too low and should be repeated
The first specimen was probably hemolyzed

Insulin drives potassium into the cells, which lowers the serum level for about 4 to 6 hours but removes no potassium from the body. Unless a binder, a loop diuretic or dialysis removes it, the level rebounds, so repeat levels are followed.
q1he7d5h: Which ECG change in a client receiving amiodarone should be reported?
A QTc that increased to 540 milliseconds
A heart rate of 68/min in sinus rhythm
Amiodarone prolongs the QT interval; a QTc above 500 ms raises the risk of torsades de pointes.
qbiyxu4: One client takes furosemide and another takes hydrochlorothiazide, and both have abnormal labs. Which finding should the nurse attribute to the thiazide?

Thiazides increase calcium reabsorption in the distal tubule and can cause hypercalcemia, which is why they are used for calcium kidney stones. Loop diuretics do the opposite and increase urinary calcium loss, while both drugs waste potassium and magnesium.
q18cnwy0: A client on warfarin has a sudden severe headache and new slurred speech. The nurse should first:
Give acetaminophen and recheck in 1 hour
Hold tonight's warfarin dose and document
Dim the lights and encourage the client to rest
Sudden headache and neurologic deficits suggest intracranial hemorrhage, an emergency.
q18osy19: A client's potassium is 7.2 mEq/L with widened QRS complexes on the monitor. Which ordered drug stabilizes the myocardium first?

Calcium does not lower the potassium level, but within minutes it raises the threshold potential and restores the gap between threshold and resting membrane potential, protecting against arrest. Insulin and bicarbonate shift potassium into cells, and a binder removes it over hours.
q5f6701: Which serum theophylline level falls within the usual therapeutic range for an adult with asthma?

The usual range is about 5 to 15 mcg/mL. Nausea, vomiting and tremor begin above 20 mcg/mL, and seizures and dysrhythmias appear above roughly 35 mcg/mL, which is one reason the drug has largely been replaced by inhaled therapy.
q1mvhq0n: A client taking empagliflozin is scheduled for elective surgery. How far in advance is this drug usually stopped?
On the morning of surgery only

SGLT2 inhibitors cause euglycemic ketoacidosis during fasting and surgical stress, so the labeling calls for stopping them 3 days beforehand, or 4 days for ertugliflozin. Glucose can look normal while ketones climb, which is why the diagnosis is missed.
q10aj8tm: A client admitted with heart failure takes lisinopril, and the creatinine has risen from 1.0 to 2.1 mg/dL in 2 days. The nurse should:
Notify the provider before giving the next dose
Give the dose and encourage more fluids
Give the dose because creatinine is not a concern
Hold all doses and restart next week
A doubling of creatinine suggests acute kidney injury; ACE inhibitors may need to be held or adjusted.
qdmfth5: Before giving oral morphine for pain, which assessment is most important for the nurse to complete?
Respiratory rate, depth, and level of sedation
Bowel sounds in all four quadrants of the abdomen
Pupil response to light in both eyes
Capillary refill in the fingers and toes
Opioids cause dose-related respiratory depression, and increasing sedation usually comes before it.
q1nei4fm: Before giving an as-needed dose of oxycodone, the nurse should first assess:
The pain rating and the time of the last opioid dose
The client's preferred brand of pain medicine
Whether the client has eaten in the past hour
The client's urine color and specific gravity
Assess pain and confirm the dosing interval to prevent stacking doses, then reassess after the dose.
q12u4y5k: A client has taken oral haloperidol for several months. Which tool should the nurse use to screen for tardive dyskinesia?
The Glasgow Coma Scale for level of consciousness
The Braden Scale for pressure injury risk
The Morse Fall Scale for gait and balance
The AIMS is used at baseline and regularly to detect tardive dyskinesia from antipsychotics.
qwtfnzd: Before giving the first IM dose of ceftriaxone, which question is most important for the nurse to ask?
Have you ever reacted to penicillin or a cephalosporin?
Have you received any vaccines or shots in the past month?
Do you have any trouble swallowing large tablets?
Have you eaten any dairy products earlier today?
Cross-reactivity is low, but a history of severe beta-lactam reactions such as anaphylaxis must be reported before the drug is given.
qk4ea2f: Before giving acetaminophen 650 mg PO for a fever, the nurse should check the medication record for:
Other ordered products that contain acetaminophen
The last time the client received an antibiotic dose
Whether the client has a documented latex allergy
The client's most recent fingerstick glucose reading
Combination products such as oxycodone-acetaminophen add to the daily total and raise the risk of liver injury.
q1w1yjq2: Before applying a client's first fentanyl transdermal patch, the nurse should confirm that the client:
Is opioid tolerant and already takes opioids daily
Has not eaten for at least 4 hours before it is applied
Has a temperature above 38 C (100.4 F) to improve absorption
Has never taken any opioid medication in the past
Fentanyl patches are only for opioid-tolerant clients; use in opioid-naive clients can cause fatal respiratory depression.
qs54cm0: Before starting oral metronidazole, the nurse should ask the client about:
Recent intake of leafy green vegetables
Daily use of sunscreen when outdoors
Alcohol with metronidazole can cause a disulfiram-like reaction; avoid it during therapy and for 3 days after.
qs5rg1j: Before giving promethazine IM to an older adult, which assessment is most important?
Level of alertness and fall risk
Skin turgor on the back of the forearm
Color and moisture of the oral mucosa
Promethazine is highly sedating and anticholinergic, so older adults are at high risk for confusion and falls.
q1cd9uas: A client has a new hydromorphone PCA. During the first 24 hours, which assessment is the priority?
Number of button presses compared with doses delivered
Pain score at rest and with movement every 4 hours
Bowel sounds and passage of flatus each shift
Opioid-induced respiratory depression is most likely in the first 24 hours, and sedation precedes it.
q15rviv2: Before increasing a magnesium sulfate infusion for a client with preeclampsia, which assessment is essential?
Deep tendon reflexes, respirations, and urine output
Fetal movement count and fundal height measurement
Cervical dilation and status of the membranes
Blood glucose and skin turgor on the sternum
Loss of reflexes, respirations under 12, and low urine output suggest magnesium toxicity.
q1temgtz: Before a client's first dose of IV gentamicin, which baseline assessment should the nurse document?
Hearing, balance, and any ringing in the ears
Visual acuity and color perception in both eyes
Sense of smell and taste on the tongue
Skin color and capillary refill in the toes
Aminoglycosides are ototoxic; a baseline helps the nurse detect early changes in hearing or balance.
q9ug3l6: Before starting a norepinephrine infusion, the nurse should verify:
A patent central line or a large, well-functioning IV
That the client has received a dose of furosemide
That the client has been kept NPO for at least 8 hours
That the indwelling urinary catheter is clamped
Extravasation can cause tissue necrosis, so a central line is preferred and IV patency is checked often.
qxytlwc: Before starting an oxytocin infusion for labor induction, which assessment is most important?
A reassuring fetal heart rate tracing and fetal presentation
The client's current pain score and her plans for an epidural
Maternal blood type and Rh factor results
The time of the client's last meal or snack
Oxytocin should not be started with a nonreassuring fetal tracing, malpresentation, or other contraindication to labor.
q1qy06n4: Before giving IV phenytoin through a peripheral line, the nurse should assess:
Site patency and that only normal saline is in the line
The client's blood glucose level and urine ketone results
The time the client last ate a full meal
Phenytoin precipitates in dextrose and is very irritating to veins; use a patent large vein with normal saline only.
qzjvxwt: A client in preterm labor is ordered betamethasone. Which information should the nurse confirm before giving it?
Gestational age, since it promotes fetal lung maturity
Rh status, since it is given only to Rh-negative clients
Cervical length, since it is given to stop cervical change
Fetal sex, since it works best in male infants
Antenatal corticosteroids are generally given between 24 and 34 weeks to reduce neonatal respiratory distress; they do not stop labor.
qr2uxya: Four clients on the unit are each due for a scheduled dose of oral morphine. Which finding is the reason to hold the dose and call the provider?
Drifts off to sleep mid-sentence, respiratory rate 11
Rates the pain 8 out of 10 and is restless in the bed
Has pupils of 2 mm that are equal and briskly reactive
Has not had a bowel movement since the last two doses

Rising sedation is the finding that precedes opioid respiratory depression, so a client who cannot stay awake to talk is held. Small pupils and constipation are expected opioid effects, and uncontrolled pain is a reason to give the dose.
q9cerq2: A client has been taking nitrofurantoin for a UTI for 5 days. Which finding should the nurse report to the provider the same day?
A new dry cough with fever and breathlessness
Urine that has turned a dark brown color today
Mild nausea that settles when taken with food
A headache on the first two days of therapy

Nitrofurantoin can cause an acute pulmonary reaction with cough, fever and dyspnea that resolves when the drug is stopped. Brown urine, nausea with food and an early headache are expected and harmless.
q1olutgh: A client with cirrhosis takes lactulose for encephalopathy. Which finding suggests the dose needs to be reduced rather than raised?
Seven watery stools today with a potassium of 3.0
Confusion that is a little worse than yesterday morning
Two soft stools today with a serum ammonia of 70 mcg/dL
A flapping tremor of the hands when the wrists are extended
Lactulose is titrated to 2 to 3 soft stools a day; more than that causes hypokalemia and dehydration. Worsening confusion and asterixis point the other way, toward needing more drug.
q1swe44o: A client took no clozapine for 3 days while away from home and asks to restart the usual 400 mg dose tonight. The nurse should expect the provider to:
Restart it at a low dose and retitrate upward
Give the usual 400 mg dose with a snack tonight
Give a double dose tonight to catch back up
Stop clozapine and start a different antipsychotic

After more than 48 hours off clozapine, tolerance to its hypotensive and sedating effects is lost, so the label calls for retitration from 12.5 mg. Resuming the full dose risks collapse and respiratory arrest.
q1eqvu6w: A client has received ketorolac for pain since admission. Today is hospital day 6 and another dose is ordered. The nurse should:
Question the order, since the usual limit is 5 days
Give the dose, since the pain score is still 7 of 10
Give the dose with food to protect the stomach lining
Give half the dose and reassess the pain in an hour
Combined ketorolac therapy by all routes is limited to 5 days, because the risk of GI bleeding and acute kidney injury climbs with duration. Food does not remove that risk.
qw9c4nt: Four clients have acetaminophen 650 mg every 6 hours PRN ordered. For which client should the nurse ask the provider about a lower daily maximum?
A client with cirrhosis who drinks alcohol daily
A client who weighs 58 kg and is 70 years old
A client taking warfarin daily for atrial fibrillation
A client with stage 3 chronic kidney disease

Acetaminophen is cleared by the liver, so cirrhosis and chronic alcohol use are the usual reasons the ceiling drops from 4,000 mg toward about 2,000 mg a day. Weight, warfarin and kidney disease do not change the hepatic limit.
qyfn9as: A 24-year-old woman taking valproic acid for seizures says she has stopped her birth control because she wants to get pregnant. The nurse should:
Report it to the provider before the next refill
Reassure her that valproate is safe in pregnancy
Tell her to take folic acid and continue the dose
Tell her to stop the valproate on her own today

Valproate carries a boxed warning for neural tube defects and reduced IQ in exposed infants, so the regimen is reviewed before conception. Stopping an antiseizure drug without a plan risks status epilepticus.
q1yrot52: A client on IV vancomycin for MRSA has a trough of 28 mcg/mL. Which other result most raises the concern for nephrotoxicity?
Creatinine that rose from 0.9 to 1.8 mg/dL
A white blood cell count that fell to 9,000
A temperature that fell to 37.2 C (99 F)
A blood culture that is now showing no growth

Vancomycin nephrotoxicity is judged by the creatinine trend alongside the level, and the usual trough target is 10 to 20 mcg/mL. Falling fever, white count and cultures show the infection responding, not kidney injury.
q1dwt47q: A client is on gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV once daily. Which pair of results would lead the nurse to expect the provider to lengthen the dosing interval?
A trough of 2.4 mcg/mL with a creatinine of 1.9
A peak of 18 mcg/mL with a creatinine of 0.8 mg/dL
A trough of 0.4 mcg/mL with a creatinine of 0.7 mg/dL
A peak of 6 mcg/mL with a creatinine of 1.0 mg/dL

On extended-interval dosing the trough should fall below about 1 mcg/mL so the kidney and inner ear get a drug-free period, and a trough of 2.4 with a rising creatinine means the drug is accumulating.
qsybhdt: A nitroglycerin infusion is titrated for chest pain with an order to hold for a systolic BP under 90 mm Hg. Which findings call for reducing the rate?
BP 86/52 with pain eased to 2 out of 10
BP 104/64 with pain unchanged at 7 out of 10
BP 128/78 with a throbbing headache after 10 minutes
BP 112/70 with a heart rate that rose from 70 to 88

The drip is titrated to pain relief within the ordered pressure limits, and a systolic of 86 is below the hold parameter even though the pain is better. Headache and a mild rise in heart rate come with vasodilation.
q1ks8vlc: During an oxytocin infusion, contractions occur every 90 seconds, last 100 seconds, and late decelerations appear. The nurse should first:
Increase the oxytocin rate per protocol
Place the client flat on her back
Call the provider and wait for orders
Tachysystole with a nonreassuring tracing requires stopping oxytocin, then lateral positioning and IV fluids.
q1rjd0f3: As the serum level climbs in a client on a magnesium sulfate infusion, which finding appears first?
A respiratory rate under 12 per minute
Cardiac arrest with a widened QRS complex
Slurred speech with new double vision
Deep tendon reflexes disappear at about 8 to 10 mg/dL, before respiratory depression near 12 and cardiac arrest above 25, which is why reflexes are checked hourly during the infusion.
q1krx5z3: An 84-year-old with dementia is agitated at night, and the family asks for scheduled haloperidol to keep her calm. The nurse should:
Discuss the boxed warning for increased deaths with the team
Start the haloperidol nightly and watch the heart rate closely
Agree, since haloperidol is approved for dementia agitation
Suggest nightly diphenhydramine as the safer choice instead

Antipsychotics carry a boxed warning for increased mortality in older adults with dementia-related psychosis and are not approved for that use, so nondrug measures come first. Diphenhydramine is anticholinergic and worsens delirium.
q1g4pman: Preterm labor has been controlled with subcutaneous terbutaline for 2 days, and an order arrives for oral terbutaline at home. The nurse should:
Question it, since prolonged terbutaline is not used
Teach the client to take her pulse before each dose
Teach the client to hold a dose if contractions start
Arrange a home infusion pump to continue the drug

Terbutaline carries a boxed warning against tocolysis beyond 48 to 72 hours and against oral or home pump use, because of maternal cardiac events and death. Short-term injectable use is its only accepted role.
qy2j64: A client in alcohol withdrawal has cirrhosis with an albumin of 2.1 and an INR of 1.8. Why is lorazepam preferred over chlordiazepoxide here?
It is conjugated and has no active metabolites
It has a longer half-life, so fewer doses are needed
It can be given orally, while the other drug cannot
It does not depress respiration at any usual dose
Lorazepam, oxazepam and temazepam are cleared by glucuronidation rather than hepatic oxidation, so they do not accumulate in liver failure the way chlordiazepoxide and diazepam do.
qxwxxeh: Before giving nitrofurantoin to an older adult with a UTI, which lab result is most important to review?
Nitrofurantoin is generally avoided with a creatinine clearance under 30 mL/min because of reduced efficacy and increased toxicity.
q7e2kkn: Before a client's clozapine is refilled, which lab result must the nurse check?
Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia, so the ANC is monitored on a set schedule.
qg63d3y: A client taking lithium has a level of 0.9 mEq/L drawn 12 hours after the last dose. The nurse interprets this as:
Too low to have any effect on mood
Invalid because it was drawn too late
The label maintenance target is 0.8 to 1.0 mEq/L, measured about 12 hours after the last dose.
q1eg5rdj: A client taking valproic acid long term should have which labs checked periodically?
Liver function tests and platelet count
Serum amylase and random urine glucose only
Thyroid panel and vitamin D level
Valproate can cause hepatotoxicity and thrombocytopenia.
qvpurx9: A client taking phenytoin has a low serum albumin. Which lab best reflects the amount of active drug?
A total phenytoin level by itself
Phenytoin is highly protein bound, so low albumin raises the active free fraction even when the total level looks normal.
ql9yadx: Which lab result is most important for dosing levetiracetam in an older adult?
Levetiracetam is cleared by the kidneys, so doses are reduced when kidney function is low.
q1w55uwu: For a client receiving lactulose for hepatic encephalopathy, which lab results should the nurse monitor?
Lactulose lowers ammonia, and frequent stools can cause hypokalemia.
q1tklugf: An older adult started sertraline 3 weeks ago and is now confused and has a headache. Which laboratory value is most important?
SSRIs can cause SIADH and hyponatremia, especially in older adults.
qikz16c: When should the nurse plan to draw a vancomycin trough level?
Within 30 minutes before the next scheduled dose
Immediately after the infusion has been completed
One hour after the infusion has been completed
At any time of day, as long as it is drawn daily
A trough reflects the lowest level and is drawn just before the next dose. Many hospitals now dose vancomycin by AUC monitoring instead of troughs alone, so follow facility protocol.
qtdv5nc: A client receiving gentamicin once daily has a rising creatinine. Which additional lab result is most important to review?
An elevated trough indicates accumulation and higher risk of nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity.
qke3wsv: A client on magnesium sulfate for seizure prevention has a serum magnesium of 6 mg/dL. The nurse interprets this as:
Too low to prevent eclamptic seizures
Critically high, with respiratory arrest likely
A level requiring calcium gluconate now
The therapeutic range for seizure prevention is about 4 to 7 mg/dL; reflexes are lost near 8 to 10.
qi99w3o: Before a client receives a dose of IV cyclophosphamide, which lab results should the nurse review?
CBC with neutrophil and platelet counts
Lipid panel and fasting blood glucose
Thyroid panel and vitamin D level
Urine drug screen and alcohol level
Bone marrow suppression is dose-limiting, so counts are checked before each cycle.
q3isa0g: Before giving IV haloperidol to a client with delirium, which lab values should the nurse review?
Low potassium or magnesium increases the risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes.
qog8xnv: A client received high-dose IV methotrexate. Which lab result guides how long leucovorin rescue continues?
Leucovorin continues until methotrexate levels fall below a safe threshold; creatinine is also followed.
qkx0th7: A client with diabetes is receiving IV levofloxacin. Which laboratory value should the nurse monitor closely?
Blood glucose, for both highs and lows
Serum lithium, for signs of drug toxicity
Fluoroquinolones can cause serious hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, especially in clients with diabetes.
qtf275k: An older adult recently started quetiapine. Which vital sign check is most important before getting the client up?
Apical pulse for one full minute
Quetiapine blocks alpha receptors and commonly causes orthostatic hypotension and falls.
q1e0fpqe: A client received hydromorphone 2 mg PO 1 hour ago. Which vital sign finding is most concerning?
Heart rate of 64 per minute while resting
A respiratory rate under 10 suggests opioid-induced respiratory depression.
qwyvunf: Before giving oral methylergonovine to a postpartum client, which vital sign must the nurse check?
Methylergonovine causes vasoconstriction and can cause severe hypertension; it is held for elevated BP.
q10t7ml7: Which vital sign change should the nurse report in a client starting clozapine?
A resting heart rate of 124/min with fever
A heart rate of 96/min right after walking the hall
A temperature of 37 C (98.6 F) taken orally in the evening
A respiratory rate of 16/min while sitting in bed
Persistent tachycardia with fever may signal myocarditis, a serious early clozapine reaction.
q1we2hs: A client starting phenelzine reports dizziness when getting out of bed. The nurse should check:
Orthostatic hypotension is a common adverse effect of MAO inhibitors.
q7mqczc: For a client receiving oxycodone, which findings best indicate opioid-induced respiratory depression?
Increasing sedation with a respiratory rate of 8
Pain score of 7 with a heart rate of 100
Mild itching on the face with a respiratory rate of 18
Nausea with a blood pressure of 140/88 mm Hg
Respiratory depression is shown by slow, shallow breathing, usually preceded by increasing sedation.
q16mrp09: An older adult received lorazepam 1 mg PO at bedtime. Which finding at 0200 requires action?
Respiratory rate of 8 with shallow breathing
Heart rate of 62 while the client is sleeping
Blood pressure of 118/70 mm Hg on the left arm
Benzodiazepines can depress respirations, especially in older adults.
q1oldx3j: A client with septic shock is on a norepinephrine infusion. Which target is commonly used when titrating it?
Mean arterial pressure of 65 mm Hg or higher
Systolic blood pressure above 180 mm Hg
Heart rate kept below 50 beats per minute
Diastolic blood pressure below 40 mm Hg
Sepsis guidelines recommend an initial MAP goal of 65 mm Hg.
q8rhrem: A client on dopamine at 10 mcg/kg/min develops a heart rate of 138 and new PVCs. The nurse should:
Reduce the rate per protocol and notify the provider
Increase the rate to improve cardiac output
Give a normal saline bolus and continue the current rate
Stop all IV fluids to prevent fluid overload
Dopamine causes dose-related tachycardia and dysrhythmias.
qc8o6nj: When titrating a nitroglycerin infusion for chest pain, the nurse should monitor:
Chest pain level and BP every 5 to 15 minutes
Respiratory rate only, with BP every 4 hours
Temperature, with BP checked once a shift
Urine output, with BP checked every 2 hours
The drip is titrated to pain relief while BP is checked often, because hypotension is common.
q1ihnnxb: Which maternal finding should the nurse monitor most closely after a dose of terbutaline SQ?
Heart rate, reporting a rate over 120 per minute
Temperature, reporting a value above 37.2 C (99 F)
Respiratory rate, reporting a rate below 20
Blood pressure, reporting a systolic over 110
Beta-agonists cause tachycardia, palpitations, and chest pain; a maternal heart rate over 120 is usually reported.
q72xxif: During IV fentanyl for procedural sedation, which monitoring finding gives the earliest sign of hypoventilation?
Rising end-tidal carbon dioxide on capnography
Falling blood pressure on the automatic cuff
Slowing heart rate shown on the cardiac monitor
Rising temperature on the skin probe
Capnography detects hypoventilation before oxygen saturation falls.
qgrusov: While infusing IV phenytoin, which vital signs should the nurse monitor most closely?
Rapid IV phenytoin can cause hypotension and dysrhythmias; adults should receive no more than 50 mg/min.
q1fw5f8e: A client received naloxone for respiratory depression from IV hydromorphone. Which finding 45 minutes later is most concerning?
Respiratory rate dropping to 10 with drowsiness
Heart rate of 96 with mild sweating and anxiety
Blood pressure of 138/84 mm Hg in the right arm
Pain score rising from 2 to 5 on a 10-point scale
Naloxone can wear off before the opioid, so respiratory depression may return.
q1qgd6ra: A client on norepinephrine has a MAP of 92 mm Hg. The ordered goal is a MAP of at least 65 mm Hg. The nurse should:
Titrate the infusion down per protocol
Increase the infusion to keep the MAP high
Stop the infusion abruptly and recheck
Keep the same rate and recheck in 4 hours
Vasopressors are titrated to the lowest dose that maintains the goal to limit ischemia and dysrhythmias.
qq2hkx7: A client taking oral haloperidol has a shuffling gait, a masklike face, and a fine resting tremor. The nurse recognizes:
These are extrapyramidal symptoms that mimic Parkinson disease and are often treated with benztropine.
q1ows7fc: Which adverse effects are most common with ondansetron?
Hearing loss and ringing in the ears
Headache and constipation are the most commonly reported adverse effects of ondansetron.
q19lxz47: A client taking metronidazole reports a metallic taste. The nurse explains that this is:
A common side effect of the drug
A sign of severe liver damage
A sign the infection is getting worse
A metallic taste is common with metronidazole and is not dangerous.
q1x2o0uw: A client taking ciprofloxacin reports new burning, tingling, and numbness in both feet. The nurse recognizes possible:
Peripheral neuropathy, which can be permanent
Poor circulation in the feet from mild dehydration
A normal reaction that fades within days
Low blood sugar from a skipped meal
Fluoroquinolones carry a boxed warning for peripheral neuropathy, which may be irreversible.
q59wy72: An older adult given lorazepam becomes agitated, restless, and combative. The nurse recognizes:
Older adults may have paradoxical excitation rather than sedation from benzodiazepines.
qvdwkfl: A client who received ceftriaxone for a week now has 6 watery, foul-smelling stools a day. The nurse suspects:
An expected effect of the antibiotic
A new allergy to the hospital diet
Broad-spectrum antibiotics raise the risk of C. difficile diarrhea.
qinmo6m: Which adverse effect of oxycodone usually does not lessen with continued use?
Tolerance develops to most opioid effects but not to constipation, so a bowel regimen is needed.
qe1f6yz: A client starting lithium reports a mild hand tremor, thirst, and frequent urination. The nurse recognizes these as:
Common early side effects to monitor
Signs of severe toxicity needing dialysis
Signs of an allergic reaction to lithium
Symptoms showing the lithium is not working
Fine tremor, thirst, and polyuria are common at therapeutic levels; coarse tremor and GI upset suggest toxicity.
qj67udf: During a vancomycin infusion, a client develops flushing and a red rash on the face, neck, and upper chest. The nurse recognizes:
An infusion reaction, often caused by a fast rate
An expected effect that needs no action
This histamine-related reaction is managed by stopping or slowing the infusion and giving an antihistamine.
qorwkgl: The nurse notes blanching and coolness around the peripheral IV site of a norepinephrine infusion. After stopping the infusion, the nurse anticipates giving:
Phentolamine, an alpha blocker, is infiltrated locally to reverse vasoconstriction and limit necrosis.
q1ebhv8j: After many hours of high-dose oxytocin, a client has headache, confusion, and low urine output. The nurse suspects:
Water intoxication from its antidiuretic effect
Postpartum preeclampsia from rising blood pressure
Oxytocin has an antidiuretic effect that can cause water intoxication and hyponatremia.
q1kdthd5: After IV promethazine, a client reports severe burning at the IV site and the hand is pale. The nurse suspects:
Tissue injury from extravasation or arterial injection
A normal sensation with this medication
A mild allergy treated with oral diphenhydramine
Simple phlebitis that will resolve on its own with warm soaks
Promethazine is a vesicant with a boxed warning for severe tissue injury and gangrene.
qaiby98: A client receiving cisplatin should be monitored most closely for which adverse effects?
Hyperglycemia and excess hair growth on the face
Constipation and a mild skin rash
Cisplatin is nephrotoxic and ototoxic; vigorous hydration is used to protect the kidneys.
q1uyreo3: Shortly after IV morphine, a client has itching and mild flushing but normal breathing and blood pressure. The nurse recognizes:
Histamine release, a common nonallergic effect
A true allergy that requires epinephrine
Anaphylaxis requiring a rapid response call
Opioid withdrawal from too low a dose of morphine
Morphine releases histamine; itching and flushing alone do not indicate a true allergy.
qf6p1de: After IV phenytoin through a hand vein, the hand becomes swollen, painful, and bluish purple. The nurse suspects:
Purple glove syndrome is a soft-tissue injury from IV phenytoin, more likely with small veins.
q51coh5: A family member is learning to use naloxone nasal spray. Which statement shows understanding?
I will call 911, give the spray, and repeat it if there is no response
I only need to call 911 if the first spray does not work
I should wait 10 minutes to see if he wakes up on his own before calling
I should give the spray only if he is having a seizure
Call for help, give naloxone, and repeat every 2 to 3 minutes if needed, since it may wear off before the opioid.
q1thwx5y: Which instruction should the nurse reinforce for a client taking nitrofurantoin?
Take it with food; urine may turn dark yellow or brown
Take it on an empty stomach along with an antacid
Stop taking it once the burning with urination ends
Avoid all dairy products for the entire course
Food improves absorption and reduces GI upset, brown urine is harmless, and the full course should be finished.
q10hod40: A client starting escitalopram for depression asks when it will help. The nurse explains:
Improvement often takes 2 to 6 weeks of daily use
Mood usually improves within 1 to 2 days of the first dose
It only works if taken on days when feeling depressed
It works fastest when taken with alcohol at night
SSRIs take several weeks for full effect and must be taken daily.
qyejyrh: A client taking phenelzine plans to eat at a restaurant. Which menu choice is safest?
Fresh grilled chicken with steamed rice
Salami sandwich with a soy sauce dip
Draft beer with smoked sausage links
Aged, cured, and fermented foods and tap beers are high in tyramine and can cause hypertensive crisis.
q198a9de: Which instruction about leftover hydromorphone tablets is correct?
Store them locked up and use a drug take-back program
Keep them in a pill organizer on the counter for easy access
Share extra tablets with family members who have pain
Leave them in the medicine cabinet for future injuries
