q153atnz: A 28-year-old man given IM haloperidol develops a temperature of 40.5 C (104.9 F), lead-pipe rigidity, labile blood pressure and a CK of 18,000 U/L. Besides stopping haloperidol, which drug acting as a dopamine agonist can treat this?
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome results from D2 blockade; treatment includes supportive care, dantrolene and the D2 agonist bromocriptine.
q155i93: A 26-year-old man with schizophrenia gains 12 kg and develops hypertriglyceridemia and hyperglycemia within 6 months of starting a new drug. Which antipsychotic is most likely?
Olanzapine and clozapine carry the highest risk of weight gain and metabolic syndrome; aripiprazole and ziprasidone carry the least.
q9dlwkh: A 32-year-old woman is brought in after an amitriptyline overdose. She is tachycardic and hypotensive, and her QRS duration is 140 ms. Which treatment is first line, and why?
Sodium bicarbonate to overcome sodium channel blockade
Physostigmine to reverse its anticholinergic toxicity
Flumazenil to reverse its CNS depression
Bicarbonate adds sodium and alkalinizes the blood, overcoming TCA fast sodium channel blockade; physostigmine is avoided because of seizures and asystole.
qfmfgjp: A 20-year-old woman with bulimia nervosa wants medication to help her quit smoking. Which drug is contraindicated for her, and why?
Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold, and patients with bulimia or anorexia have a higher seizure risk from electrolyte disturbances.
qsmog74: A 35-year-old woman with generalized anxiety disorder wants a nonsedating drug with no risk of dependence and starts buspirone. What is its mechanism and onset?
GABA-A modulation; works within an hour
Alpha-2 agonism; works within an hour
Buspirone is a 5-HT1A partial agonist without sedation or dependence. Some benefit may appear in 1-2 weeks, but the full anxiolytic effect often takes 4-6 weeks.
q17dacvc: A 50-year-old man with severe alcohol withdrawal is given phenobarbital. How does its action at the GABA-A receptor differ from that of benzodiazepines?
Increases duration of chloride channel opening
Increases frequency of chloride channel opening
Opens glycine-gated chloride channels in the cord
Barbiturates prolong channel opening and can open it directly at high doses; benzodiazepines increase opening frequency.
q1t1moak: A 30-year-old man has a phenytoin level of 15 mcg/mL. His dose is raised by 20 percent, and the level rises to 35 mcg/mL with nystagmus and ataxia. Which pharmacokinetic concept explains this?
Saturation of metabolism causing zero-order kinetics
Autoinduction of its own hepatic metabolism
Displacement from albumin by a second drug
Phenytoin metabolism saturates in the therapeutic range, so small dose increases cause disproportionate rises in level.
qsz73by: A 7-year-old girl has brief staring spells many times a day, and EEG shows 3-Hz spike-and-wave discharges. What is the mechanism of the first-line drug?
Ethosuximide blocks T-type calcium channels in thalamic neurons and treats absence seizures only.
q1fsbae2: A 30-year-old woman taking valproate has lamotrigine added at the usual starting dose and develops a widespread blistering rash with mucosal involvement. Why did valproate increase her risk?
Valproate displaces lamotrigine from its receptors
Valproate inhibits UGT-mediated lamotrigine clearance, roughly doubling levels; the lamotrigine dose and titration must be reduced to lower SJS risk.
qkzxel6: A 68-year-old man with Parkinson disease takes levodopa combined with carbidopa. What does carbidopa contribute?
Carbidopa does not cross the blood-brain barrier and blocks peripheral conversion of levodopa to dopamine, lowering nausea and increasing CNS delivery.
q4rao9n: A 35-year-old man who uses heroin daily takes his first dose of buprenorphine 4 hours after his last heroin use. He soon develops yawning, diarrhea, piloerection and agitation. What explains this?
Partial agonist displacing a full agonist
Full agonist with very high receptor affinity
Antagonist with weak kappa agonist activity
Partial agonist with a very short half-life
Buprenorphine binds mu receptors with high affinity but low intrinsic activity, displacing heroin and precipitating withdrawal.
qygctdc: A 30-year-old man with 40 percent burns sustained 10 days ago receives succinylcholine for intubation and develops peaked T waves followed by cardiac arrest. What explains this reaction?
Decreased plasma cholinesterase from liver injury
Direct inhibition of cardiac sodium-potassium ATPase
Burns, crush injury and denervation upregulate extrajunctional receptors, so depolarization releases large amounts of potassium.
q1fwck7o: During sevoflurane anesthesia, a 22-year-old man develops rising end-tidal CO2, masseter rigidity, tachycardia and a temperature of 40 C (104 F). What is the mechanism of the drug used to treat this?
Antagonizes nicotinic receptors at the endplate
Malignant hyperthermia stems from RYR1 mutations; dantrolene blocks calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
qshurmh: After induction with rocuronium, a 48-year-old woman cannot be intubated or ventilated, and the neuromuscular block must be reversed immediately. How does the reversal drug act?
Competes with acetylcholine at nicotinic receptors
Sugammadex is a modified cyclodextrin that binds rocuronium and vecuronium, reversing even deep block without muscarinic effects.
qd15qbv: A 40-year-old woman receives a single IV bolus of propofol for a short procedure and is awake within 10 minutes. What mainly explains her rapid awakening?
Redistribution from brain to muscle and fat
Rapid hepatic metabolism to inactive products
Rapid renal excretion of the unchanged drug
Hydrolysis by plasma esterases in the blood
Lipid-soluble induction agents end their effect mainly by redistribution out of the brain, not by elimination.
q12qv2pe: A 25-year-old trauma patient in hemorrhagic shock is induced with a drug that maintains blood pressure and airway reflexes. On waking he has vivid hallucinations. What is the drug's mechanism?
Ketamine is a dissociative NMDA antagonist that increases sympathetic tone and causes emergence reactions.
qbdj0ee: A 72-year-old man with septic shock is intubated after induction with a hemodynamically neutral agent. The next day he has refractory hypotension, and cortisol levels are low. Which enzyme did the induction agent inhibit?
Etomidate inhibits adrenal 11-beta hydroxylase, suppressing cortisol synthesis even after a single dose.
q12vimxt: A 30-year-old man who often inhales whipped-cream chargers develops paresthesias, gait ataxia and loss of vibration sense; MRI shows dorsal column changes. What is the mechanism?
Oxidation of cobalamin inactivating methionine synthase
Direct demyelination by nitrous oxide metabolites
Inhibition of dihydrofolate reductase in neurons
Nitrous oxide oxidizes the cobalt in B12, inactivating methionine synthase and causing subacute combined degeneration.
q17xzg6: A 19-year-old woman ingests 20 g of acetaminophen, and her 4-hour level is above the treatment line. By which mechanism does the antidote prevent liver injury?
Inhibits CYP2E1 to block NAPQI formation
Binds acetaminophen in the gut lumen
NAC is a glutathione precursor and sulfhydryl donor that conjugates the toxic metabolite NAPQI.
qg58st7: A 45-year-old man is found intoxicated with an anion gap metabolic acidosis, a high osmolal gap and calcium oxalate crystals in his urine. What is the mechanism of the preferred antidote?
Chelation of oxalate in renal tubules
Fomepizole blocks ADH, preventing conversion of ethylene glycol to toxic glycolic and oxalic acids.
qtp0gwj: A 2-year-old boy ate his mother's prenatal vitamins. He has hematemesis, metabolic acidosis and radiopaque tablets on an abdominal radiograph. Which antidote is indicated?
Deferoxamine chelates free iron; the complex is renally excreted and can turn urine reddish.
qhyzn8l: A 40-year-old man is rescued from a house fire. He has a lactate of 12 mmol/L, hypotension and a high venous oxygen saturation. What is the mechanism of the preferred antidote?
Donates sulfur for the rhodanese reaction
Hydroxocobalamin binds cyanide directly; nitrites induce methemoglobin and thiosulfate supplies sulfur to rhodanese.
q3h93yh: After a benzocaine throat spray for endoscopy, a 50-year-old woman is cyanotic with chocolate-brown blood and an SpO2 of 85 percent despite oxygen. How does the antidote work?
Acts as a cofactor that reduces methemoglobin
Chelates the ferric iron within hemoglobin
Increases oxygen dissolved in the plasma
Methylene blue is reduced by NADPH-methemoglobin reductase to leukomethylene blue, which reduces ferric iron back to ferrous; it is ineffective in G6PD deficiency.
q1pbw9of: After an aspirin overdose, a 35-year-old woman has tinnitus, vomiting, and a mixed respiratory alkalosis and anion gap acidosis. She is given sodium bicarbonate. What is its main purpose?
Ion trapping of salicylate in alkaline urine
Neutralizing salicylic acid in the stomach
Inhibiting salicylate absorption in the gut
Alkalinization ionizes salicylate, trapping it in urine and keeping it out of the brain.
q4zpbb1: A 50-year-old man overdoses on propranolol and has bradycardia and hypotension that do not respond to atropine. Glucagon is given. Why can glucagon help?
Raises cardiac cAMP independent of beta receptors
Glucagon receptors on cardiac myocytes activate Gs and adenylyl cyclase, bypassing the blocked beta receptor.
q1pibfl9: A 60-year-old man started on ticagrelor after an acute coronary syndrome reports new mild dyspnea. How does ticagrelor differ from clopidogrel?
Reversibly binds P2Y12 and needs no activation
Irreversibly binds P2Y12 after CYP2C19 activation
Blocks GP IIb/IIIa and needs no hepatic activation
Inhibits platelet PDE3 and needs CYP3A4 activation
Ticagrelor is a direct reversible P2Y12 antagonist; dyspnea may relate to increased adenosine levels.
q1q5aip8: A 79-year-old woman taking apixaban for atrial fibrillation presents with a large intracerebral hemorrhage. In the US today, what is used to reverse this anticoagulant?
Protamine sulfate by slow IV push
Andexanet alfa, the decoy factor Xa, was withdrawn from the US market in 2025, so 4-factor PCC is used for factor Xa inhibitor bleeding; idarucizumab reverses only dabigatran.
q1o9lg5y: A 58-year-old man taking sildenafil for erectile dysfunction reports a transient blue tint to his vision. What mechanism explains this effect?
Blockade of muscarinic receptors in retinal cones
Toxic accumulation of the drug in the macula
Sildenafil inhibits PDE5 but also partly inhibits PDE6 in photoreceptors, causing blue-tinged vision.
q1b185rh: A 58-year-old man has 40 minutes of crushing substernal chest pain. BP is 148/90 mm Hg and pulse 92/min. ECG shows 3-mm ST elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. He has no drug allergies. While the cath lab is activated, which medication should be given immediately?
Enteric-coated aspirin 81 mg swallowed whole with water
Intravenous metoprolol 5 mg every 5 minutes for 3 doses
Oral warfarin 10 mg as a loading dose
Chewed non-enteric-coated aspirin gives rapid platelet inhibition and lowers mortality in STEMI. Routine IV beta blockade is not recommended early, and warfarin has no acute role.
q8rkybu: A 64-year-old man has an inferior STEMI. BP is 86/54 mm Hg, pulse 58/min, jugular veins are distended, and lungs are clear. Right-sided leads show ST elevation in V4R. Which medication should be avoided?
Right ventricular infarction is preload dependent; nitrates and other venodilators can cause profound hypotension. Treat with IV fluids.
qua1fyw: A 61-year-old woman with NSTEMI undergoes PCI with a drug-eluting stent. She has no bleeding history and no prior stroke. Which antiplatelet regimen is most appropriate at discharge?
Aspirin plus clopidogrel for 1 month only
After ACS with stent placement, DAPT with aspirin plus a potent P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor or prasugrel) for 12 months is recommended when bleeding risk is acceptable.
q1w5jgwq: A 72-year-old man with a transient ischemic attack 2 years ago presents with NSTEMI and is taken for PCI. Which P2Y12 inhibitor is contraindicated in this patient?
Prasugrel is contraindicated with prior stroke or TIA because of net harm from intracranial bleeding; it is also generally avoided at age 75 or older.
q12as0z: A 52-year-old man is recovering from an anterior STEMI treated with PCI. Fasting LDL cholesterol is 128 mg/dL. He has never taken lipid-lowering therapy. Which is the most appropriate lipid therapy?
Diet and exercise alone for 3 months, then recheck
All patients with clinical ASCVD up to age 75 should receive high-intensity statin therapy such as atorvastatin 40 to 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20 to 40 mg.
q1e3rva5: A 60-year-old man with an MI 1 year ago and type 2 diabetes takes atorvastatin 80 mg daily with good adherence. LDL cholesterol is 88 mg/dL. Which is the most appropriate next step?
Add fish oil 1 g daily and recheck in a year
In very high-risk ASCVD with LDL 70 mg/dL or higher on maximal statin, adding ezetimibe is a reasonable first step; niacin and high-dose simvastatin are not recommended.
qz6vtq6: A 57-year-old woman with prior MI and peripheral artery disease takes atorvastatin 80 mg and ezetimibe 10 mg daily. LDL cholesterol remains 96 mg/dL. Which is the most appropriate addition?
Colestipol plus extended-release niacin twice daily
Omega-3 fatty acid 1 g once daily
A PCSK9 monoclonal antibody is reasonable for very high-risk ASCVD with LDL 70 mg/dL or higher despite maximal statin plus ezetimibe; it lowers LDL about 60 percent and reduces events.
q16g4i9e: A 66-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes is discharged after an anterior MI. Echocardiogram shows an ejection fraction of 38 percent. BP is 128/78 mm Hg and creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL. Which medication is most appropriate to add for long-term mortality reduction?
An ACE inhibitor such as lisinopril
A nondihydropyridine calcium channel blocker such as diltiazem
ACE inhibitors reduce remodeling and mortality after MI, particularly with reduced EF, diabetes, or anterior infarction. Nondihydropyridine CCBs are harmful with reduced EF.
q1hxxlbu: A 63-year-old man has HFrEF with an ejection fraction of 30 percent and NYHA class II symptoms on lisinopril 20 mg, carvedilol, and furosemide. BP is 118/72 mm Hg and potassium is 4.3 mEq/L. His physician plans to switch him to an ARNI. Which is the correct approach?
Stop lisinopril, wait 36 hours, then start sacubitril-valsartan
Start sacubitril-valsartan today and continue lisinopril
Stop lisinopril and start sacubitril-valsartan the same evening
Halve the lisinopril dose and add sacubitril-valsartan
A 36-hour washout after the last ACE inhibitor dose is required before starting sacubitril-valsartan to avoid angioedema from combined neprilysin and ACE inhibition.
qqphxb: A 70-year-old woman with HFrEF is switched to sacubitril-valsartan after an appropriate ACE inhibitor washout. Which adverse effect is most common after starting this drug?
Hypotension is the most common adverse effect of sacubitril-valsartan. It causes less cough than ACE inhibitors and tends to raise, not lower, potassium.
qxxa8zg: A 59-year-old man with HFrEF (EF 28 percent) and NYHA class II symptoms takes sacubitril-valsartan, carvedilol, and dapagliflozin. BP is 112/70 mm Hg, potassium is 4.2 mEq/L, and eGFR is 55 mL/min. Which medication should be added next?
A mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist is one of the four pillars of HFrEF therapy and is indicated when eGFR is above 30 mL/min and potassium is below 5.0 mEq/L.
q8nq18s: A 66-year-old man with HFrEF has taken spironolactone for 8 months and now has painful bilateral breast enlargement. Potassium is 4.6 mEq/L. Which is the most appropriate change?
Replace spironolactone with hydrochlorothiazide and potassium
Eplerenone is a selective MRA without antiandrogenic effects, so it preserves the mortality benefit while avoiding gynecomastia.
q187pa2v: A 68-year-old woman without diabetes has HFrEF (EF 32 percent) and persistent NYHA class II symptoms on sacubitril-valsartan, metoprolol succinate, and spironolactone. eGFR is 45 mL/min. Which medication will most likely reduce her risk of HF hospitalization and death?
SGLT2 inhibitors reduce cardiovascular death and HF hospitalization in HFrEF regardless of diabetes status. Pioglitazone and verapamil worsen heart failure.
q9gyt07: A 55-year-old man is newly diagnosed with HFrEF (EF 25 percent). He is euvolemic on furosemide and an ARNI. Pulse is 88/min and BP is 124/76 mm Hg. Which beta blocker has proven mortality benefit and is most appropriate?
Only carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, and bisoprolol have shown mortality benefit in HFrEF; start at a low dose once the patient is euvolemic.
q11bgwr7: A 62-year-old Black man with HFrEF (EF 30 percent) remains NYHA class III despite optimal doses of sacubitril-valsartan, carvedilol, spironolactone, and empagliflozin. BP is 128/80 mm Hg. Which addition is most likely to improve survival?
In self-identified Black patients with persistent NYHA class III to IV symptoms on optimal GDMT, adding hydralazine plus isosorbide dinitrate reduces mortality (A-HeFT).
q1edkns0: A 74-year-old woman with known HFrEF has 1 week of orthopnea and leg swelling. BP is 146/88 mm Hg and SpO2 is 90 percent on room air. She has crackles to the mid-lung fields and 3+ pitting edema. Creatinine is 1.3 mg/dL. Which is the best initial treatment?
Patients with acute decompensated HF who are congested but warm and well perfused need IV loop diuretics; inotropes are reserved for low-output states.
qxxf7rd: A 57-year-old man with HFrEF (EF 30 percent) on maximally tolerated metoprolol succinate, sacubitril-valsartan, spironolactone, and dapagliflozin is in sinus rhythm with a resting heart rate of 80/min. Which medication would further reduce HF hospitalization?
Ivabradine is indicated in symptomatic HFrEF with EF 35 percent or less, sinus rhythm, and resting heart rate 70/min or higher despite a maximally tolerated beta blocker.
qzo1ljf: A 76-year-old woman has dyspnea on exertion and edema. Echocardiogram shows an EF of 60 percent with diastolic dysfunction, and BNP is elevated. After diuresis she remains NYHA class II. Which medication is most likely to reduce HF hospitalization?
SGLT2 inhibitors have a class 2a recommendation in HFpEF because they reduce HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death.
q1hgywg4: A 67-year-old woman has palpitations for 6 hours. ECG shows atrial fibrillation at 142/min. BP is 132/80 mm Hg. Echocardiogram 1 year ago showed normal EF. Which is the most appropriate initial pharmacotherapy?
Oral flecainide without an AV nodal blocker
Intravenous procainamide followed by oral quinidine
In stable AF with rapid ventricular response and preserved EF, IV diltiazem or a beta blocker is first-line for rate control. Adenosine does not treat AF.
q10vetfy: A 71-year-old man with HFrEF (EF 20 percent) has atrial fibrillation at 150/min. BP is 98/64 mm Hg and he is mentating normally with mild dyspnea. Which medication is most appropriate for acute rate control?
Nondihydropyridine CCBs are avoided in decompensated HFrEF. IV amiodarone or digoxin can control rate when blood pressure is borderline.
q17nd45l: A 69-year-old man with atrial fibrillation at 168/min becomes confused. BP is 72/40 mm Hg and he is diaphoretic. Which is the most appropriate next step?
Intravenous diltiazem bolus followed by infusion
Hemodynamically unstable AF requires immediate synchronized cardioversion; rate-slowing drugs worsen hypotension.
qo3o63: A 68-year-old woman with hypertension has newly diagnosed nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. Creatinine clearance is 70 mL/min and she has no bleeding history. Which is the most appropriate stroke prevention therapy?
No antithrombotic therapy at this time
CHA2DS2-VASc is 3 (female, age 65 to 74, hypertension). Oral anticoagulation is indicated, and a DOAC is preferred over warfarin for nonvalvular AF.
q1aeb26w: A 54-year-old woman with rheumatic heart disease has moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis and new atrial fibrillation. Which anticoagulant is most appropriate?
Warfarin with a target INR of 2 to 3
DOACs are not recommended in AF with moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis or mechanical valves; warfarin remains the anticoagulant of choice.
ql72ufp: A 45-year-old man has an episode of atrial fibrillation that converted spontaneously. He has no hypertension, diabetes, heart failure, vascular disease, or prior stroke. Which is the most appropriate long-term antithrombotic therapy?
Warfarin with a target INR of 2 to 3 for one year
With a CHA2DS2-VASc score of 0 in a man, neither anticoagulation nor aspirin is recommended for stroke prevention.
qpw2go9: A 38-year-old woman with no structural heart disease has infrequent symptomatic paroxysmal atrial fibrillation lasting a few hours. Echocardiogram and stress test are normal. She wants a pill-in-the-pocket strategy. Which regimen is most appropriate?
Flecainide taken with a beta blocker or nondihydropyridine CCB
Amiodarone 400 mg taken at the onset of each episode
Digoxin 0.25 mg taken at symptom onset
Flecainide alone without any AV nodal blocking agent
Class IC agents are safe without structural or ischemic heart disease; an AV nodal blocker is co-administered to prevent 1:1 conduction of atrial flutter.
q1777x51: A 70-year-old man has taken amiodarone for 2 years for atrial fibrillation. He now reports fatigue, cold intolerance, and weight gain. Which laboratory abnormality is most likely?
Elevated TSH with low free T4
Low TSH with elevated free T3
Amiodarone is iodine-rich and commonly causes hypothyroidism; TSH and LFTs should be monitored every 6 months, with a baseline chest x-ray and PFTs.
qbjr6bq: A 66-year-old man with persistent AF and an EF of 30 percent is selected for rhythm control with dofetilide. Creatinine clearance is 65 mL/min and baseline QTc is 430 ms. Which is required when starting this drug?
Inpatient initiation with continuous ECG monitoring for 3 days
Outpatient start with a single follow-up ECG at 3 months
Baseline pulmonary function tests and chest x-ray
Monthly liver function testing for the first 6 months
Dofetilide can cause torsades de pointes, so it must be started in the hospital with creatinine clearance-based dosing and QTc monitoring.
q1fmzyes: A 78-year-old man taking dabigatran for atrial fibrillation is brought in after a fall with an acute subdural hematoma. His last dose was 3 hours ago. Which is the most appropriate reversal agent?
Idarucizumab is a monoclonal antibody fragment that specifically binds and reverses dabigatran within minutes.
qnc663s: A 74-year-old woman taking apixaban for atrial fibrillation presents with a large intracerebral hemorrhage. Her last dose was 4 hours ago. Which is the most appropriate reversal therapy?
Fresh frozen plasma with vitamin K and platelets
With andexanet alfa withdrawn from the US market in 2025, factor Xa inhibitor-associated life-threatening bleeding is treated with 4-factor PCC. Idarucizumab reverses only dabigatran.
q19rbb2y: A man on warfarin is given oral vitamin K 2.5 mg for an INR of 11.2 without bleeding. Four hours later the INR is still 7.4. Why?
New clotting factors must be synthesized by the liver
Oral vitamin K is destroyed by gastric acid
Vitamin K acts only on factor VIII and von Willebrand factor
Warfarin blocks the vitamin K receptor on the platelet

Vitamin K restores the reduced cofactor needed for gamma-carboxylation, but the INR falls only as the liver makes new factors II, VII, IX and X; oral vitamin K takes about 24 hours for full effect. That lag is why 4-factor PCC is used when correction is needed in minutes.
quuea6j: A 77-year-old woman on warfarin presents with sudden headache and left hemiparesis. CT shows an intraparenchymal hemorrhage. INR is 3.4. Which is the most appropriate immediate therapy?
4-factor PCC plus intravenous vitamin K 10 mg
Oral vitamin K 5 mg and hold warfarin
Warfarin-associated major bleeding is reversed with 4-factor PCC for rapid correction plus IV vitamin K to sustain it.
q125o95s: A 64-year-old man receiving an IV unfractionated heparin infusion for PE develops brisk hematemesis. aPTT is 140 seconds. After stopping the infusion, which agent is most appropriate?
Tranexamic acid alone without other reversal
Protamine binds heparin and fully reverses unfractionated heparin (and partially reverses LMWH).
qgu1y6f: A 66-year-old man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis has received heparin for 6 days. Platelets fall from 230,000 to 80,000/mm3 and the PF4 antibody is strongly positive. Which anticoagulant is most appropriate?
In HIT, stop all heparins and start a non-heparin anticoagulant. Argatroban is hepatically cleared, so it is preferred in renal failure; fondaparinux is renally cleared.
q16rfdpe: A 47-year-old man has a right femoral DVT 2 weeks after a long-haul flight. He has no cancer, normal renal function, and no bleeding risk. Which is the most appropriate outpatient treatment?
Apixaban 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily
Warfarin alone starting at 10 mg daily without bridging
Unfractionated heparin infusion for 5 days, then stop
CHEST guidelines prefer DOACs over warfarin for VTE without cancer. Apixaban needs no parenteral lead-in; warfarin requires heparin overlap.
qmknm7e: A 59-year-old woman has sudden dyspnea. BP is 78/46 mm Hg despite 1 L of fluid, and pulse is 128/min. CT angiography shows a saddle pulmonary embolus with RV dilation. She has no bleeding contraindications. Which is the most appropriate next step?
Place an IVC filter and observe
Subcutaneous enoxaparin and admit to telemetry
Massive (high-risk) PE with sustained hypotension warrants systemic thrombolysis unless contraindicated, in addition to heparin.
q1c7fmnh: A 29-year-old woman at 20 weeks gestation has a left iliofemoral DVT confirmed by ultrasound. Which is the most appropriate anticoagulant?
Warfarin titrated to an INR of 2 to 3
LMWH is the anticoagulant of choice in pregnancy because it does not cross the placenta; warfarin is teratogenic and DOACs are not recommended.
q1kxknzn: A 34-year-old woman has her second unprovoked DVT. Testing shows lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, and anti-beta2-glycoprotein I antibodies on two occasions. Which long-term anticoagulant is preferred?
Warfarin with a target INR of 2 to 3
In antiphospholipid syndrome, especially triple-positive disease, DOACs have higher rates of thrombosis than warfarin; warfarin is preferred.
q12j2ijc: A 55-year-old man develops a calf-to-popliteal DVT 3 weeks after knee replacement surgery. Rivaroxaban is started. He has no other risk factors. What is the recommended duration of anticoagulation?
A first VTE provoked by a major transient risk factor such as surgery is treated for 3 months; extended therapy is for unprovoked or persistent risk factors.
q1czskbf: A 50-year-old Black man has BP readings of 152/96 mm Hg and 154/98 mm Hg at two visits. He has no diabetes, no CKD, and no albuminuria. Which is the most appropriate initial antihypertensive?
In Black adults without CKD or HF, a thiazide diuretic or calcium channel blocker is preferred initial therapy because they lower BP more effectively than ACE inhibitors.
qs3kcge: A 56-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes has a BP of 146/90 mm Hg on repeated measurements. Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio is 420 mg/g and eGFR is 70 mL/min. Which antihypertensive is most appropriate?
With diabetes and albuminuria, an ACE inhibitor or ARB is first-line because it slows progression of kidney disease.
qj15erq: A 61-year-old man started lisinopril 3 months ago for hypertension and has developed a persistent dry cough. Lung exam and chest x-ray are normal. Which is the most appropriate change?
ACE inhibitor cough is bradykinin mediated; ARBs do not raise bradykinin and are an appropriate substitute.
qyjky0u: A 62-year-old man has tearing chest pain radiating to the back. BP is 190/110 mm Hg in the right arm and 150/90 mm Hg in the left; pulse is 104/min. CT shows a type B aortic dissection. Which is the most appropriate initial medication?
In aortic dissection, give an IV beta blocker first to reduce heart rate and shear stress, then add a vasodilator if needed, targeting SBP near 120 mm Hg.
q83ijfz: A 55-year-old man presents with headache, confusion, and papilledema. BP is 236/138 mm Hg. CT head shows no hemorrhage. Which is the most appropriate goal of pharmacotherapy in the first hour?
Lower mean arterial pressure by no more than 25 percent with IV nicardipine
Lower blood pressure to below 120/80 mm Hg with IV nitroprusside
Give oral lisinopril and recheck BP in 24 hours
In hypertensive emergency without dissection or eclampsia, reduce MAP by no more than 25 percent in the first hour, then toward 160/100 mm Hg over the next 2 to 6 hours.
q5haguw: A 31-year-old woman with chronic hypertension taking lisinopril has a positive pregnancy test at 7 weeks. BP is 138/88 mm Hg. Which is the most appropriate management?
Stop lisinopril and start hydrochlorothiazide plus spironolactone
ACE inhibitors and ARBs are fetotoxic; labetalol and nifedipine are preferred antihypertensives in pregnancy.
qrqv5ti: A 27-year-old woman at 35 weeks gestation has a BP of 168/112 mm Hg on two readings 15 minutes apart. She has a headache. She has no asthma. Which is the most appropriate antihypertensive?
Severe-range BP in pregnancy (160/110 or higher) should be treated within 30 to 60 minutes with IV labetalol, IV hydralazine, or immediate-release oral nifedipine.
q9oxldk: A 44-year-old woman has resistant hypertension and a potassium level of 3.1 mEq/L. Plasma aldosterone-to-renin ratio is elevated, and adrenal CT shows bilateral hyperplasia. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
Bilateral adrenal hyperplasia is treated medically with a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist; surgery is for unilateral aldosterone-producing adenoma.
qah6o22: A 55-year-old woman has type 2 diabetes and hypertension and smokes cigarettes. LDL cholesterol is 124 mg/dL. She has no known ASCVD. Which is the most appropriate lipid-lowering therapy?
Adults aged 40 to 75 years with diabetes and additional ASCVD risk factors should receive high-intensity statin therapy.
q1mdwyxp: A 48-year-old man has fasting triglycerides of 1,250 mg/dL. He had acute pancreatitis 1 year ago. He already follows a low-fat diet and has stopped alcohol. Which medication is most appropriate to reduce his immediate risk?
Triglycerides above 1,000 mg/dL carry a risk of pancreatitis; fibrates are first-line. Bile acid sequestrants can raise triglycerides.
qp6ml03: A 67-year-old man taking simvastatin 40 mg was started on clarithromycin 5 days ago for pneumonia. He now has diffuse muscle pain and dark urine. CK is 18,000 U/L. Which medication should be discontinued first?
Clarithromycin is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor that raises simvastatin levels, causing rhabdomyolysis; the statin must be stopped.
q1xmrak5: A 49-year-old man has a hemoglobin A1c of 7.6 percent on two occasions. BMI is 31 kg/m2, eGFR is 90 mL/min, and he has no ASCVD, heart failure, or CKD. Which is the most appropriate initial pharmacotherapy?
Metformin plus lifestyle changes is first-line for type 2 diabetes without compelling indications for other agents.
q1ak7dtu: A 62-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes had an MI 2 years ago. She takes metformin 1,000 mg twice daily. A1c is 7.9 percent, BMI 34 kg/m2, and eGFR 80 mL/min. Which addition is most appropriate?
With established ASCVD, ADA recommends a GLP-1 receptor agonist or SGLT2 inhibitor with proven cardiovascular benefit independent of A1c; GLP-1 RAs also promote weight loss.
q75sb3: A 66-year-old man with type 2 diabetes has an eGFR of 40 mL/min and a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 600 mg/g on maximal lisinopril. A1c is 7.4 percent on metformin. Which addition best slows kidney disease progression?
SGLT2 inhibitors are recommended in diabetic CKD with an eGFR of 20 mL/min or higher to reduce CKD progression and cardiovascular events.
q237z8g: A woman on metformin with an eGFR of 26 mL/min presents with a lactate of 8.4 mmol/L. Which action of metformin best explains the lactate?
It inhibits hepatic gluconeogenesis from lactate
It uncouples oxidative phosphorylation in muscle
It blocks renal tubular secretion of hydrogen ion
It is converted directly into lactate in the gut wall

Metformin inhibits mitochondrial complex I and hepatic gluconeogenesis, so lactate is no longer consumed through the Cori cycle. The drug is cleared unchanged by tubular secretion via OCT2 and MATE, so an eGFR under 30 lets levels and lactate rise.
qedhv9o: A 45-year-old man has polyuria, polydipsia, and a 7-kg weight loss. Glucose is 380 mg/dL and A1c is 12.1 percent. Urine ketones are trace positive, pH is normal, and the anion gap is normal. Which is the most appropriate initial therapy?
Basal insulin such as glargine in addition to metformin
Acarbose with each meal plus a low-carbohydrate diet
Lifestyle changes alone and recheck A1c in 3 months
Symptomatic catabolic hyperglycemia or A1c above 10 percent calls for early insulin therapy.
q11l22u5: A 58-year-old woman started semaglutide 3 months ago. She now has severe epigastric pain radiating to the back and vomiting. Lipase is 900 U/L. Which is the most appropriate action regarding this medication?
Continue semaglutide at a lower dose
Hold semaglutide for 1 week, then resume
GLP-1 receptor agonists are associated with acute pancreatitis; stop the drug and do not restart a GLP-1 RA if pancreatitis is confirmed.
qqcherl: A 54-year-old man with type 2 diabetes on metformin and empagliflozin has nausea and vomiting after 2 days of poor oral intake. Glucose is 210 mg/dL, pH 7.18, bicarbonate 12 mEq/L, and anion gap 22. Serum beta-hydroxybutyrate is high. What is the most likely cause?
Euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis from the SGLT2 inhibitor
Starvation ketosis that needs no treatment
SGLT2 inhibitors can cause DKA with near-normal glucose, especially with illness, fasting, or surgery; hold the drug and treat as DKA with insulin and dextrose.
q1xj6orj: An 81-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and eGFR 35 mL/min is found confused. Fingerstick glucose is 38 mg/dL. Her medications include glyburide, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. After glucose correction, which medication change is most appropriate?
Glyburide has active renally cleared metabolites and causes prolonged hypoglycemia in older adults and CKD; it should be avoided (Beers criteria).
q7jrpm4: A 50-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes and BMI 39 kg/m2 takes metformin. A1c is 8.2 percent. She wants a medication that maximizes both glucose lowering and weight loss. She has no personal or family history of thyroid cancer. Which is most appropriate?
Dual GIP and GLP-1 agonist therapy with tirzepatide provides very high glucose-lowering efficacy and the greatest weight loss among diabetes agents.
q1cazvfl: A 60-year-old man with type 2 diabetes takes metformin and insulin glargine 20 units at bedtime. Fasting glucose readings over the past week are 170 to 190 mg/dL with no hypoglycemia. Which is the most appropriate adjustment?
Increase glargine by 2 units every 3 days until fasting glucose is at goal
Add prandial insulin lispro with every meal right away
Decrease glargine to 16 units at bedtime
Switch glargine to NPH insulin twice daily at the same dose
Basal insulin is titrated to fasting glucose (goal 80 to 130 mg/dL) by about 2 units every 3 days when there is no hypoglycemia.
qbfr921: A 19-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes has vomiting and abdominal pain. Glucose is 520 mg/dL, pH 7.12, bicarbonate 9 mEq/L, potassium 4.8 mEq/L, and serum ketones are high. BP is 94/58 mm Hg. Which is the best initial step?
Fluid resuscitation with isotonic saline is the first step in DKA; insulin follows once potassium is known to be at least 3.3 mEq/L.
qey50wz: A 24-year-old man in DKA has glucose 460 mg/dL, pH 7.10, and serum potassium 3.0 mEq/L. He has received 1 L of normal saline. Which is the most appropriate next step?
Give IV potassium and delay insulin until potassium is at least 3.3 mEq/L
Start an insulin infusion at 0.14 units/kg/h immediately
Give an IV insulin bolus and recheck potassium in 4 hours
Insulin drives potassium into cells and can cause fatal hypokalemia; hold insulin and replace potassium when it is below 3.3 mEq/L.
q2qn2h6: A 22-year-old woman with DKA is on an IV regular insulin infusion. Her glucose falls to 220 mg/dL, but the anion gap is still 18. Which is the most appropriate adjustment?
Add dextrose to the IV fluids and continue the insulin infusion
Stop the insulin infusion and switch to oral fluids
Stop insulin and give subcutaneous glargine only
Double the insulin infusion rate and stop IV fluids
Insulin must continue until the anion gap closes; dextrose is added when glucose falls to about 200 to 250 mg/dL to prevent hypoglycemia.
q1fz60cz: A 78-year-old nursing home resident is lethargic. Glucose is 980 mg/dL, serum osmolality 352 mOsm/kg, bicarbonate 22 mEq/L, and ketones are negative. BP is 92/50 mm Hg. Which is the most appropriate initial therapy?
Intravenous 0.9 percent saline at about 1 L per hour
Intravenous insulin bolus before any fluids
Oral water and subcutaneous insulin glargine
HHS is driven by profound volume depletion; aggressive isotonic fluid is the first priority, followed by insulin.
q5uwad2: A 34-year-old woman has weight loss, tremor, and a diffuse goiter with proptosis. TSH is suppressed and free T4 is elevated. TSH receptor antibodies are positive. Pulse is 112/min. She is not pregnant. Which is the most appropriate initial pharmacotherapy?
Methimazole is the preferred thionamide outside the first trimester; a beta blocker controls adrenergic symptoms.
q1hm6m9y: A 28-year-old woman at 8 weeks gestation has Graves disease with free T4 twice the upper limit of normal. Which is the most appropriate antithyroid medication?
PTU is preferred in the first trimester because methimazole is associated with embryopathy; switch to methimazole in the second trimester.
q1j7rji5: A 42-year-old woman with Graves disease has a fever of 40 C (104 F), agitation, vomiting, and atrial fibrillation at 160/min after an appendectomy. Propranolol has been started. Regarding iodine therapy, which sequence is correct?
Give propylthiouracil, then give iodine at least 1 hour later
Give iodine immediately, then propylthiouracil 1 hour later
Give iodine alone and avoid thionamides
Give radioactive iodine as soon as she is stable
In thyroid storm, a thionamide must be given before iodine so that iodine is not used as substrate for new hormone synthesis. Steroids are also given.
qs4rq3t: A woman with Graves disease in her first trimester needs a thionamide. Which fact guides the choice between methimazole and propylthiouracil?
Methimazole is linked to aplasia cutis and choanal atresia
Methimazole causes more hepatocellular failure than PTU does
Methimazole crosses the placenta far less than PTU does
Methimazole also blocks peripheral T4 to T3 conversion

Methimazole embryopathy, including aplasia cutis and choanal or esophageal atresia, follows first-trimester exposure, so PTU is preferred then despite its own risk of fulminant hepatic failure. PTU, not methimazole, is the one that blocks peripheral deiodination.
q1pmfykn: A 78-year-old man with stable coronary artery disease has fatigue and constipation. TSH is 24 mU/L and free T4 is low. Which is the most appropriate initial therapy?
Levothyroxine 1.6 mcg/kg daily as a full dose
Older patients and those with CAD start levothyroxine at a low dose to avoid precipitating angina or arrhythmia.
q8hg3va: A 30-year-old woman with Hashimoto thyroiditis on levothyroxine 100 mcg daily has a positive home pregnancy test. TSH was normal 2 months ago. Which is the most appropriate step?
Increase levothyroxine by about 30 percent now
Continue the same dose until the second trimester
Stop levothyroxine for the first trimester
Thyroid hormone needs rise early in pregnancy; increase the dose by about 2 extra tablets weekly (about 30 percent) and check TSH every 4 weeks.
qcxdjqn: A 65-year-old woman on a stable levothyroxine dose now has a TSH of 9.8 mU/L. Three months ago she began taking calcium carbonate and ferrous sulfate with her levothyroxine every morning. Which is the most appropriate step?
Separate levothyroxine from calcium and iron by at least 4 hours
Double the levothyroxine dose and keep timing the same
Add liothyronine to her morning regimen
Stop levothyroxine and recheck TSH in 6 weeks
Calcium, iron, and PPIs reduce levothyroxine absorption; take levothyroxine on an empty stomach separated from these products.
qnxgtjm: A 35-year-old woman with known Addison disease has vomiting and diarrhea. BP is 72/40 mm Hg, sodium 126 mEq/L, potassium 5.9 mEq/L, and glucose 58 mg/dL. Which is the most appropriate immediate therapy?
Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV plus normal saline with dextrose
Dexamethasone 1 mg orally and recheck cortisol in the morning
Norepinephrine infusion before any steroid is given
Adrenal crisis needs immediate high-dose IV hydrocortisone (which also provides mineralocorticoid activity) plus fluids and dextrose; never delay steroids for testing.
q1tht5oe: A 40-year-old man is newly diagnosed with primary adrenal insufficiency. He has salt craving, hyperkalemia, and orthostatic hypotension. Which maintenance regimen is most appropriate?
Primary adrenal insufficiency lacks both cortisol and aldosterone, so glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement are needed.
qscv47g: A 16-year-old girl has asthma symptoms twice a month with no nighttime awakenings and normal spirometry between episodes. Which reliever regimen is preferred by current GINA recommendations?
As-needed albuterol alone for symptom relief
Daily salmeterol alone with as-needed albuterol
GINA Track 1 prefers as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol for mild asthma because it reduces severe exacerbations compared with SABA-only therapy.
qged5un: A 28-year-old woman with asthma uses low-dose budesonide-formoterol as maintenance and reliever therapy. She still has symptoms most days and woke at night twice last week. Inhaler technique and adherence are good. Which is the most appropriate step?
Increase to medium-dose budesonide-formoterol maintenance and reliever
Add a long-acting beta agonist alone as a separate inhaler
Stop the inhaled steroid and start daily montelukast instead
Start a 30-day course of oral prednisone at 40 mg daily
Step up within the ICS-formoterol track to medium-dose maintenance-and-reliever therapy after confirming technique and adherence.
q1fiei6a: A 25-year-old woman with a severe asthma exacerbation has received three back-to-back albuterol-ipratropium nebulizers and IV methylprednisolone. She still speaks in words only, and peak flow is 30 percent of predicted. Which is the most appropriate next medication?
IV magnesium sulfate is recommended for severe exacerbations not responding to initial bronchodilators and steroids.
q8wbjse: A 34-year-old man has severe allergic asthma with 3 prednisone bursts in the past year despite high-dose ICS-LABA and good technique. Total IgE is 420 IU/mL with sensitization to dust mite. Which add-on therapy is most appropriate?
Anti-IgE therapy is indicated for severe allergic asthma with elevated IgE uncontrolled on step 4 to 5 therapy.
q1enq0jt: Montelukast is added for a boy with asthma and allergic rhinitis. Which receptor action produces its effect?
Blockade of the cysteinyl leukotriene type 1 receptor
Inhibition of 5-lipoxygenase in the leukotriene pathway
Blockade of thromboxane A2 receptors on bronchial muscle
Inhibition of phosphodiesterase 4 inside airway cells

Montelukast is a competitive antagonist at the CysLT1 receptor, blocking the bronchoconstriction, mucus secretion and eosinophil recruitment driven by LTD4. Zileuton is the 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor and roflumilast the PDE4 inhibitor, so each acts at a different point.
q35moqf: A 66-year-old man with COPD (FEV1 55 percent predicted) has an mMRC dyspnea score of 2 and no exacerbations in the past year. Blood eosinophils are 120/microL. Which is the most appropriate maintenance therapy?
LAMA plus LABA such as tiotropium-olodaterol
Inhaled corticosteroid alone such as fluticasone
Albuterol as needed only, with pulmonary rehab
Daily low-dose oral prednisone plus albuterol
GOLD recommends LABA plus LAMA for symptomatic patients (group B); ICS monotherapy is not recommended in COPD.
qil3z47: A 70-year-old woman with COPD on LAMA plus LABA has had 2 exacerbations requiring prednisone in the past year. Blood eosinophils are 380/microL. Which is the most appropriate change?
Add an inhaled corticosteroid to make triple therapy
Stop the LAMA and continue the LABA alone
Add daily low-dose oral prednisone long term
Switch to as-needed albuterol only for symptoms
GOLD recommends escalating to LABA, LAMA, and ICS for exacerbations when eosinophils are 100/microL or higher, with the strongest benefit at 300/microL or higher.
qkvjni3: A 68-year-old man with COPD has 3 days of worsening dyspnea, increased sputum volume, and green sputum. SpO2 is 91 percent and he is not in respiratory distress. In addition to bronchodilators and an antibiotic, which is the most appropriate therapy?
Prednisone 60 mg daily tapered over 6 weeks
A short course of prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days is as effective as longer courses for COPD exacerbations and has less toxicity.
q55iyaz: A 32-year-old man has 3 days of fever, productive cough, and right lower lobe consolidation. He has no comorbidities and has not taken antibiotics recently. Pulse is 96/min and SpO2 96 percent. Which is the most appropriate outpatient antibiotic?
ATS/IDSA recommends high-dose amoxicillin (or doxycycline or a macrolide where resistance is low) for healthy outpatients with CAP.
q6dd79c: A 64-year-old woman with COPD and type 2 diabetes has CAP. She is stable for outpatient treatment and has no recent antibiotic use. Which is the most appropriate regimen?
Outpatients with comorbidities receive a beta-lactam plus a macrolide or doxycycline, or monotherapy with a respiratory fluoroquinolone.
q1hk9e0t: A 70-year-old man is admitted to a medical ward with CAP. He is not in the ICU, has no MRSA or Pseudomonas risk factors, and has no drug allergies. Which is the most appropriate empiric therapy?
Non-severe inpatient CAP is treated with a beta-lactam plus a macrolide, or a respiratory fluoroquinolone alone.
q1ro1o3t: A 58-year-old man with prior MRSA pneumonia is admitted to the ICU with severe CAP requiring norepinephrine. Which is the most appropriate empiric regimen?
Severe CAP with prior respiratory MRSA isolation warrants empiric MRSA coverage with vancomycin or linezolid added to standard therapy.
q13irmxt: A 55-year-old woman with a history of anaphylaxis to penicillin is admitted to a medical ward with CAP. Which is the most appropriate empiric therapy?
A respiratory fluoroquinolone covers typical and atypical pathogens and avoids beta-lactams in severe penicillin allergy.
q1sr53lp: A 26-year-old nonpregnant woman has 2 days of dysuria and frequency without fever or flank pain. Urinalysis shows pyuria and nitrites. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
IDSA first-line options for uncomplicated cystitis are nitrofurantoin for 5 days (Macrobid label: 7 days), TMP-SMX for 3 days (if resistance is low), or a single dose of fosfomycin.
q1moy4i3: A 30-year-old woman has a fever of 38.6 C (101.5 F), flank pain, and costovertebral tenderness. She is tolerating oral intake and is not pregnant. Local fluoroquinolone resistance is below 10 percent. Which is the most appropriate outpatient treatment?
Nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin do not achieve adequate renal tissue levels; oral fluoroquinolones for 7 days are first-line for pyelonephritis.
qz0rxex: A 24-year-old woman at 26 weeks gestation has fever, rigors, and right flank pain. Urinalysis shows pyuria and bacteriuria. Which is the most appropriate management?
Admit and give IV gentamicin plus doxycycline
Pyelonephritis in pregnancy is treated as an inpatient with IV beta-lactam therapy; fluoroquinolones and tetracyclines are avoided.
q1oh4gmx: A 25-year-old woman at 12 weeks gestation has a urine culture with more than 100,000 CFU/mL of E. coli. She has no symptoms. The organism is susceptible to all tested agents. Which is the most appropriate management?
No treatment because she is asymptomatic
Asymptomatic bacteriuria in pregnancy is treated to prevent pyelonephritis; beta-lactams are preferred in the first trimester.
q2r0iuf: A 22-year-old college student has fever, headache, neck stiffness, and a petechial rash. CSF shows neutrophilic pleocytosis and low glucose. Which is the most appropriate empiric regimen?
Empiric adult bacterial meningitis coverage is vancomycin plus a third-generation cephalosporin, with dexamethasone given before or with the first dose.
q13ie0lw: A 68-year-old man has fever, confusion, and nuchal rigidity. CSF shows 1,800 WBC/mm3 with neutrophils and low glucose. Which is the most appropriate empiric antibiotic regimen?
Adults older than 50 need ampicillin added for Listeria monocytogenes coverage, along with dexamethasone.
qd87hbm: A 35-year-old man with suspected pneumococcal meningitis is about to receive vancomycin and ceftriaxone. When should dexamethasone be given?
Shortly before or with the first antibiotic dose
Only after CSF culture confirms pneumococcus
Only if the patient develops seizures
Dexamethasone reduces mortality and hearing loss in pneumococcal meningitis when given before or with the first antibiotic dose.
qi1xu93: A 45-year-old man has a 2-day history of a spreading, warm, erythematous area on the lower leg without purulence or abscess. He is afebrile with normal vital signs. Which is the most appropriate antibiotic?
Nonpurulent cellulitis is usually streptococcal; oral beta-lactams such as cephalexin are first-line. TMP-SMX alone covers streptococci poorly.
q1pnz3n7: A 28-year-old man has a 4-cm fluctuant abscess on the thigh with surrounding erythema and a temperature of 38.3 C (100.9 F). Incision and drainage is performed. Which antibiotic is most appropriate?
Purulent infections with systemic signs warrant drainage plus MRSA coverage such as TMP-SMX or doxycycline.
q8bqcq4: A 52-year-old man with diabetes has rapidly spreading thigh erythema, severe pain out of proportion to exam, crepitus, and BP 84/50 mm Hg. Along with emergency surgical debridement, which regimen is most appropriate?
Cephalexin plus oral doxycycline twice daily
Penicillin G alone at high intravenous doses
Nafcillin alone, then oral dicloxacillin step-down
Necrotizing soft tissue infection requires broad coverage including MRSA and gram-negatives, plus clindamycin to suppress toxin production.
qyfkznj: A 50-year-old woman receiving IV vancomycin over 20 minutes develops flushing and an erythematous rash on the face, neck, and upper trunk. BP is 118/76 mm Hg and there is no wheezing or angioedema. Which is the most appropriate management?
Slow the infusion rate and give an antihistamine
Stop vancomycin permanently and record an allergy
Switch to cefazolin plus clindamycin indefinitely
Vancomycin infusion reaction is non-IgE histamine release from rapid infusion; infuse over at least 60 minutes and premedicate with an antihistamine.
q14vywkf: A 63-year-old man has MRSA pneumonia confirmed by sputum culture. Which antibiotic should not be used for this infection?
Daptomycin is inactivated by pulmonary surfactant and is not used for pneumonia, although it is effective for MRSA bacteremia and endocarditis.
qval795: A 23-year-old man has urethral discharge and dysuria. NAAT is positive for Neisseria gonorrhoeae and negative for Chlamydia. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
CDC recommends a single 500-mg IM ceftriaxone dose for uncomplicated gonorrhea (1 g if 150 kg or more); add doxycycline only if chlamydia is not excluded.
q1rjmjn3: A 20-year-old nonpregnant woman has a positive NAAT for Chlamydia trachomatis on routine screening. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days
Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days
CDC now prefers doxycycline for 7 days over single-dose azithromycin for chlamydia in nonpregnant patients.
qi9689n: A 29-year-old woman has 6 weeks of depressed mood, anhedonia, early morning awakening, poor concentration, and excessive guilt. She has no suicidal ideation, no history of mania, and no medical illness. PHQ-9 score is 17 and she prefers medication. Which is the most appropriate initial pharmacotherapy?
Amitriptyline 75 mg at bedtime, titrated over 2 weeks

An SSRI such as sertraline is first-line for moderate major depression because of efficacy, tolerability, and safety in overdose. TCAs are more toxic in overdose, and benzodiazepines do not treat depression.
qlx47i6: A 44-year-old man with bipolar I disorder has been stable on lithium for 5 years. He now has coarse tremor, ataxia, vomiting, and confusion. Lithium level is 2.4 mEq/L (previously 0.8). Two weeks ago a new antihypertensive was started. Which medication most likely precipitated this?

Thiazides increase proximal tubular sodium and lithium reabsorption and can raise lithium levels 25 percent or more. ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and NSAIDs also raise levels; calcium channel blockers and alpha blockers do not meaningfully affect levels.
q4i0dfm: A man has been on clozapine for 5 weeks. Which laboratory result requires the drug to be interrupted under its REMS program?
Absolute neutrophil count of 900 per microliter
White blood cell count of 6,200 per microliter
Absolute eosinophil count of 720 cells per microliter

Clozapine is interrupted when the ANC falls below 1,000 per microliter, and the ANC rather than the total WBC is the monitored value, weekly for the first 6 months. The eosinophil and platelet values shown here are not treatment-limiting.
q1y9jf0b: A man on IV haloperidol has fever, rigidity and a CK of 18,000 U/L. Which additional finding would instead point to serotonin syndrome?
Inducible ankle clonus with brisk reflexes
Lead-pipe rigidity of the arms and legs
Diaphoresis with a labile blood pressure reading
A temperature above 40 C with confusion

Clonus and hyperreflexia are characteristic of serotonin syndrome and are absent in neuroleptic malignant syndrome, where rigidity is lead-pipe and reflexes are normal or reduced. Fever, diaphoresis and autonomic instability occur in both, so they do not separate them.
q1dz4a8u: A 40-year-old woman taking sertraline was started on tramadol for back pain. She now has agitation, a temperature of 39.0 C (102.2 F), diaphoresis, diarrhea, mydriasis, hyperreflexia, and inducible clonus most prominent in the legs. Both drugs are stopped and IV benzodiazepines are given, but symptoms persist. Which medication is indicated next?

Serotonin syndrome features clonus and hyperreflexia. After stopping serotonergic drugs and giving benzodiazepines, cyproheptadine, a 5-HT2A antagonist, is used. Bromocriptine worsens serotonin toxicity, and dantrolene is for NMS or malignant hyperthermia.
q1h49sxu: A 34-year-old woman with schizophrenia well controlled on olanzapine 20 mg daily has gained 14 kg in 9 months. Fasting glucose is 118 mg/dL and triglycerides are 290 mg/dL. Which antipsychotic is the best alternative to minimize metabolic risk?

Aripiprazole, ziprasidone, and lurasidone have the lowest metabolic liability. Clozapine and olanzapine carry the highest risk, and quetiapine and low-potency typicals also cause substantial weight gain.
qee9bvo: A 22-year-old woman with bulimia nervosa (self-induced vomiting until 1 year ago) wants help quitting her 1-pack-per-day smoking habit. Which smoking cessation medication is contraindicated?
Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in seizure disorders and in bulimia or anorexia nervosa, in which electrolyte disturbances further increase seizure risk.
q1d3x0x7: A 56-year-old man with decompensated alcoholic cirrhosis (ascites, INR 2.0, albumin 2.4 g/dL) is admitted. Thirty hours after his last drink he has tremor, diaphoresis, pulse 118/min, BP 162/96 mm Hg, and visual hallucinations. CIWA-Ar score is 22. Which is the most appropriate medication?

Benzodiazepines are first-line for alcohol withdrawal. In severe liver disease, agents metabolized only by glucuronidation without active metabolites (lorazepam, oxazepam) are preferred over long-acting chlordiazepoxide or diazepam.
q13k5nvz: A 48-year-old man with alcohol use disorder has completed detoxification and wants medication to help maintain abstinence. He has decompensated cirrhosis with bilirubin 3.1 mg/dL and an elevated INR. Creatinine is 0.8 mg/dL. Which is the most appropriate medication?
Acamprosate is renally cleared without hepatic metabolism, making it suitable in advanced liver disease. Naltrexone is avoided in acute hepatitis or liver failure, and disulfiram is hepatotoxic.
q10xq25u: A 4-year-old boy has had hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention at home and in preschool for 9 months, causing significant impairment. Hearing, vision, and development are otherwise normal. Which is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
For preschool children ages 4 to 5, the AAP recommends evidence-based parent training in behavior management first; methylphenidate may be considered if behavioral therapy is insufficient.
q11zcpq2: A 17-year-old girl has morning myoclonic jerks and had one generalized tonic-clonic seizure after a sleepless night. EEG shows 4- to 6-Hz generalized polyspike-and-wave discharges. Which is the most appropriate initial medication?

Juvenile myoclonic epilepsy responds to broad-spectrum agents. Valproate is effective but is avoided in people who may become pregnant because of neural tube defects and lower offspring IQ. Carbamazepine and phenytoin can worsen myoclonic seizures.
q1c0aqib: A 61-year-old woman has taken haloperidol for 8 years for stable schizophrenia. She has developed involuntary lip smacking, tongue protrusion, and choreiform finger movements. Which medication is most appropriate to treat this movement disorder?
Tardive dyskinesia is treated with a VMAT2 inhibitor such as valbenazine or deutetrabenazine. Anticholinergics such as benztropine do not help and may worsen TD.
q13ha1l3: A 32-year-old veteran has PTSD with intrusive memories, nightmares, hypervigilance, and avoidance. He is starting trauma-focused psychotherapy and asks about medication. Which medication should be avoided for PTSD?
Guidelines recommend against benzodiazepines in PTSD because they may worsen outcomes and impede extinction learning. Sertraline, paroxetine, and venlafaxine are recommended pharmacotherapies.
q1ik3syx: An 84-year-old man becomes acutely confused 2 days after hip fracture surgery. His attention fluctuates and is worse at night. He picks at the sheets but is not a danger to himself or staff. Infection and metabolic causes are being addressed. Which is the most appropriate initial management?
Reorientation, sleep promotion, mobilization, and family presence
Lorazepam 1 mg IV at night as needed
Scheduled oral haloperidol 2 mg every 6 hours for the rest of the stay
Diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime for sleep

Delirium is managed by treating underlying causes and using multicomponent nonpharmacologic measures. Antipsychotics are reserved for severe distress or danger, and benzodiazepines and anticholinergics worsen delirium.
qxs2659: An older woman taking nightly diphenhydramine has urinary retention, constipation and worsening memory. Which receptor action explains these?
Antagonism at central histamine H1 receptors
Antagonism at peripheral alpha-1 adrenergic receptors

First-generation antihistamines are nonselective and block muscarinic receptors, producing retention, constipation, dry mouth and cognitive impairment, which is why they sit on the Beers list. H1 blockade in the brain explains the sedation but not the anticholinergic findings.
qilk0y2: An 82-year-old man with Alzheimer disease on donepezil has urge urinary incontinence. Oxybutynin was started 3 weeks ago and his confusion has worsened. Which is the best alternative for his bladder symptoms?
Antimuscarinics worsen cognition and oppose cholinesterase inhibitors. A beta-3 agonist such as mirabegron treats overactive bladder without anticholinergic effects.
q2618gf: A 34-year-old man is having a generalized tonic-clonic seizure that began 12 minutes ago. He has received IV lorazepam 4 mg twice without cessation. Glucose is 104 mg/dL and the airway is supported. Which is the most appropriate next medication?
A third dose of IV lorazepam 4 mg
Oral phenytoin 1 g loading dose by nasogastric tube

After benzodiazepines fail, a second-line IV agent is given: levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, or valproate, which had similar efficacy in ESETT. Further benzodiazepine doses add respiratory risk without benefit.
q6iqxu9: A 7-year-old girl has many brief staring spells daily, lasting about 10 seconds with eyelid fluttering and no postictal confusion. Hyperventilation provokes an episode. EEG shows 3-Hz generalized spike-and-wave discharges. Which is the most appropriate initial medication?
Ethosuximide is first-line for childhood absence epilepsy, with better tolerability than valproate. Carbamazepine, phenytoin, and gabapentin can worsen absence seizures.
q14ibsaa: A 32-year-old man of Han Chinese ancestry has brief electric-shock pains in the right cheek triggered by chewing and brushing his teeth. Exam and MRI are normal. Carbamazepine is planned. Which test should be performed before starting it?
HLA-B*1502, common in people of Asian ancestry, strongly predicts carbamazepine-induced SJS and TEN. HLA-B*5701 predicts abacavir hypersensitivity and TPMT guides thiopurine dosing.
q18fv24j: A 54-year-old woman with migraine without aura had an MI with a coronary stent placed 1 year ago. She asks for an acute treatment for her migraine attacks. Which medication should be avoided?
Triptans cause vasoconstriction and are contraindicated in coronary artery disease, stroke, and uncontrolled hypertension. Gepants such as ubrogepant do not vasoconstrict and are an option.
q9zad30: A 28-year-old woman has migraine with 7 headache days per month despite trigger avoidance. She has moderate persistent asthma and a BMI of 33 kg/m2. She uses a levonorgestrel IUD. Which is the most appropriate preventive medication?

Topiramate is an effective migraine preventive that tends to cause weight loss. Propranolol is avoided in asthma, amitriptyline and valproate cause weight gain, and valproate is teratogenic. Topiramate also needs reliable contraception.
q1hraj6: A 30-year-old woman with generalized myasthenia gravis on pyridostigmine has dysuria and frequency without fever. Urinalysis shows pyuria. Which antibiotic should be avoided?
Fluoroquinolones carry a boxed warning for exacerbating myasthenia gravis. Aminoglycosides, macrolides, and magnesium also impair neuromuscular transmission.
qlsawr0: A 63-year-old woman has a minor ischemic stroke (NIHSS 2) and is not a thrombolysis candidate. ECG and telemetry show sinus rhythm. Which antithrombotic regimen is most appropriate?
Aspirin plus clopidogrel for 21 days, then single antiplatelet
Aspirin plus clopidogrel continued indefinitely for secondary prevention
Warfarin with an INR goal of 2 to 3

Short-term DAPT started within 24 hours reduces recurrent stroke after minor stroke or high-risk TIA (CHANCE, POINT). Prolonged DAPT increases bleeding without added benefit, and anticoagulation is not indicated without AF.
q1awpdtn: A 79-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease started donepezil 6 weeks ago. She has now had two episodes of syncope. Pulse is 44/min and ECG shows sinus bradycardia. Which is the most likely mechanism?
Increased vagal tone from cholinesterase inhibition
Orthostatic hypotension from alpha-1 adrenergic blockade
QT prolongation with torsades de pointes
Cholinesterase inhibitors increase acetylcholine at cardiac muscarinic receptors, causing bradycardia, heart block, and syncope. They should be used cautiously with conduction disease.
q16xjhxa: A 74-year-old man with Parkinson disease has distressing visual hallucinations. Anticholinergics and amantadine have been stopped and levodopa reduced as far as tolerated. Which antipsychotic is most appropriate?

Parkinson disease psychosis is treated with quetiapine, clozapine, or pimavanserin, which have minimal D2 blockade in the nigrostriatal pathway. Haloperidol, risperidone, and olanzapine worsen motor symptoms.
q1mz05d4: A 55-year-old woman has an urge to move her legs in the evening, relieved by walking, that disrupts sleep. Exam is normal. Serum ferritin is 32 ng/mL and transferrin saturation is 18 percent. Which is the most appropriate initial treatment?
Iron is recommended in restless legs syndrome when ferritin is 75 ng/mL or lower or TSAT is below 20 percent. Dopamine agonists and levodopa cause augmentation, and antihistamines worsen symptoms.
qnwhmh0: A 46-year-old man with heavy alcohol use is brought in confused. He has horizontal nystagmus, bilateral lateral rectus weakness, and a wide-based gait. Fingerstick glucose is 82 mg/dL. Which is the most appropriate next step?
Intravenous 50 percent dextrose followed by oral thiamine
Wernicke encephalopathy requires high-dose IV thiamine immediately, given before or with glucose. Oral thiamine is poorly absorbed in alcohol use disorder and inadequate for acute treatment.
q8nqncm: A 3-year-old boy has 2 days of ear pain and fever of 39.2 C (102.6 F). The right tympanic membrane is bulging and erythematous. He has not received antibiotics in the past month and has no drug allergies. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
Azithromycin 10 mg/kg on day 1, then 5 mg/kg daily

High-dose amoxicillin is first-line for acute otitis media in the absence of recent amoxicillin use, concurrent conjunctivitis, or penicillin allergy. Severe symptoms such as fever of 39 C (102.2 F) or higher warrant immediate antibiotics.
q1pgyxe5: A 10-year-old girl has fever, sore throat, tonsillar exudates, and tender anterior cervical nodes. Rapid strep test is positive. She had anaphylaxis to amoxicillin at age 5. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
With immediate-type penicillin allergy, IDSA recommends clindamycin, azithromycin, or clarithromycin. First-generation cephalosporins are acceptable only for non-anaphylactic allergy.
q1spqji1: A 4-month-old girl has 3 days of rhinorrhea, cough, and wheeze. Respiratory rate is 52/min, SpO2 is 93 percent on room air, and she is feeding adequately. Which is the most appropriate management?
Oral prednisolone 1 mg/kg daily for 5 days
Nebulized hypertonic saline and oral azithromycin in the clinic
AAP guidelines recommend supportive care for bronchiolitis. Albuterol, epinephrine, glucocorticoids, and antibiotics are not routinely recommended; oxygen is given if SpO2 stays below 90 percent.
q15t4d59: A 3-year-old boy has had fever for 6 days with bilateral nonexudative conjunctivitis, cracked red lips, a polymorphous rash, cervical lymphadenopathy, and swollen hands. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
Aspirin alone with echocardiography in 6 weeks
Kawasaki disease is treated with IVIG 2 g/kg plus aspirin within 10 days of fever onset to reduce coronary artery aneurysms. Ibuprofen antagonizes aspirin's antiplatelet effect.
q8813jp: A 12-day-old girl has a temperature of 38.4 C (101.1 F) and is feeding less than usual. CSF shows pleocytosis and Gram stain is pending. Which is the most appropriate empiric antibiotic regimen?

Febrile neonates need coverage for GBS, E. coli, and Listeria. Ampicillin plus ceftazidime or cefepime is used when meningitis is suspected. Ceftriaxone is avoided in neonates because it displaces bilirubin and precipitates with calcium.
q41z7cv: A 3-year-old boy living in an older home has a venous blood lead level of 52 mcg/dL on repeat testing. He is asymptomatic with a normal neurologic exam. Which is the most appropriate management besides removing the lead source?
Intramuscular dimercaprol plus calcium disodium EDTA
Repeat lead level in 3 months without chelation
Oral succimer is used for lead levels of 45 to 69 mcg/dL. Levels of 70 or higher or encephalopathy require hospitalization with dimercaprol plus CaNa2EDTA.
q14i472w: A 2-year-old girl ingested her mother's prenatal iron tablets 4 hours ago. She has vomiting, hematemesis, and lethargy. Serum bicarbonate is 12 mEq/L and serum iron is 620 mcg/dL. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
Severe iron poisoning with acidosis, shock, or a level above 500 mcg/dL is treated with IV deferoxamine. Activated charcoal does not bind iron.
qu1x6ev: A 31-year-old woman at 36 weeks gestation has BP 166/110 mm Hg, a severe headache, and platelets of 88,000/mm3. Antihypertensive therapy has been given and delivery is planned. Which medication should be given to prevent seizures?
Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice to prevent and treat eclamptic seizures and is superior to phenytoin and diazepam.
qimbjbp: A 27-year-old woman receiving magnesium sulfate for preeclampsia with severe features becomes drowsy. Patellar reflexes are absent and respiratory rate is 8/min. Which is the most appropriate treatment after stopping the infusion?
Magnesium toxicity causes loss of deep tendon reflexes, then respiratory depression and cardiac arrest. Calcium gluconate antagonizes magnesium at the neuromuscular junction.
q1ynnyhi: A 30-year-old woman with moderate persistent asthma has uterine atony and heavy bleeding after vaginal delivery despite uterine massage and oxytocin infusion. BP is 118/72 mm Hg. Which uterotonic is contraindicated?
Carboprost (15-methyl PGF2-alpha) causes bronchoconstriction and is contraindicated in asthma. Methylergonovine is acceptable in normotensive patients.
qy9h5np: A 33-year-old woman with preeclampsia delivered vaginally and has uterine atony with 1,000 mL of blood loss despite oxytocin. BP is 158/102 mm Hg. She has no asthma. Which uterotonic should be avoided?
Methylergonovine, an ergot alkaloid, causes vasoconstriction and is contraindicated in hypertension and preeclampsia.
qhyo59h: A 25-year-old woman at 9 weeks gestation has daily nausea with occasional vomiting. She is tolerating fluids, has no ketonuria, and dietary changes and ginger did not help. Which is the most appropriate first-line pharmacotherapy?
Intravenous metoclopramide every 6 hours at home

ACOG recommends vitamin B6 alone or with doxylamine as first-line pharmacotherapy for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy. Ondansetron and other antiemetics are later options, and steroids are for refractory hyperemesis.
qlmfgm0: A 26-year-old woman with a BMI of 36 kg/m2 had unprotected intercourse 4 days ago. She wants to avoid pregnancy and would like long-term contraception. Which is the most effective option?
Two doses of combined oral contraceptive pills 12 hours apart

The copper IUD is the most effective emergency contraception up to 5 days after intercourse, is unaffected by body weight, and provides ongoing contraception. Oral levonorgestrel loses efficacy after 72 hours and with obesity.
qbaxufw: A 29-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome and BMI 31 kg/m2 has oligomenorrhea and has been trying to conceive for 14 months. Her partner's semen analysis is normal and tubes are patent. Which is the most appropriate first-line ovulation induction agent?
Letrozole produces higher live birth rates than clomiphene in PCOS and is first-line per ACOG and ASRM. Metformin alone is less effective, and oral contraceptives prevent pregnancy.
q1nogy87: A 51-year-old woman has frequent severe hot flashes and night sweats that disrupt sleep. Her last period was 14 months ago and she has an intact uterus. She has no history of breast cancer, VTE, or cardiovascular disease. Which is the most effective treatment?
Hormone therapy is the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms. With an intact uterus, a progestogen must be added to estrogen to prevent endometrial hyperplasia and cancer.
qq23sbq: A 30-year-old woman at 30 weeks gestation has gestational diabetes. Despite 2 weeks of medical nutrition therapy, fasting glucose values are 104 to 112 mg/dL, while postprandial values are at goal. Which is the preferred pharmacotherapy?

Insulin is preferred for gestational diabetes because it does not cross the placenta. Glyburide and metformin cross the placenta, and DPP-4 inhibitors are not used in pregnancy. Bedtime NPH targets fasting hyperglycemia.
q1k9lyyf: A 23-year-old nonpregnant woman has a frothy yellow-green vaginal discharge and vulvar itching. Wet mount shows motile flagellated organisms and vaginal pH is 6.0. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
Metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days
Metronidazole 2 g orally as a single dose
Clindamycin 2 percent vaginal cream for 7 days
CDC recommends the 7-day metronidazole regimen for trichomoniasis in women because it is more effective than single-dose therapy. Sex partners should also be treated.
q1osdlqm: A 28-year-old woman at 18 weeks gestation has vulvar itching and thick white discharge. KOH prep shows pseudohyphae. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
Oral fluconazole 150 mg weekly for 6 months
Vaginal boric acid capsules for 14 days
Topical azoles for 7 days are recommended for vulvovaginal candidiasis in pregnancy. Oral fluconazole has been linked to miscarriage and birth defects.
q1mdkav1: A 25-year-old woman received benzathine penicillin G for secondary syphilis 4 hours ago. She now has fever of 38.7 C (101.7 F), myalgias, headache, and a more prominent rash. BP is 118/74 mm Hg. Which is the most appropriate management?
Intramuscular epinephrine and admission for anaphylaxis
Switch to doxycycline for penicillin allergy
Give a second dose of penicillin for treatment failure
The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction is an acute febrile response to treponemal lysis within 24 hours of treatment. It is self-limited, is not an allergy, and is treated supportively.
q18uc3lm: A 30-year-old man is newly diagnosed with HIV. CD4 count is 420 cells/mm3 and viral load is 60,000 copies/mL. HLA-B*5701 is negative, hepatitis B serologies are negative, and creatinine is normal. Which is the most appropriate approach?
Defer ART until the CD4 count falls below 350
Start efavirenz-tenofovir-emtricitabine after resistance testing returns in 4 weeks
Guidelines recommend starting ART at diagnosis regardless of CD4 count, ideally the same day. Initial regimens are based on an integrase inhibitor such as dolutegravir or bictegravir with two NRTIs.
q1t7zqqn: A 26-year-old nurse sustained a deep needlestick injury 3 hours ago from a patient with known HIV and a detectable viral load. Her baseline HIV test is pending. Which is the most appropriate management?
Start a 3-drug PEP regimen now for 28 days
Wait for the source viral load before deciding on PEP
Start PEP only if her baseline HIV test is positive
Post-exposure prophylaxis should begin as soon as possible, ideally within hours and no later than 72 hours, with a 3-drug regimen such as bictegravir-emtricitabine-tenofovir alafenamide for 28 days.
qefp6mk: A 39-year-old man with untreated HIV (CD4 60 cells/mm3) has progressive dyspnea, dry cough, and bilateral interstitial infiltrates. PaO2 is 62 mm Hg on room air. Induced sputum confirms Pneumocystis. TMP-SMX is started. Which medication should be added?
Adjunctive glucocorticoids reduce mortality in moderate to severe Pneumocystis pneumonia with PaO2 below 70 mm Hg or an A-a gradient of 35 or more, and should start within 72 hours.
q1f6s71b: A 34-year-old man with HIV (CD4 30 cells/mm3) has 2 weeks of headache and fever. CSF opening pressure is 32 cm H2O and cryptococcal antigen is positive. Which is the most appropriate induction therapy?
Amphotericin B plus immediate initiation of antiretroviral therapy

Induction for cryptococcal meningitis is liposomal amphotericin B plus flucytosine, with serial LPs for elevated pressure. ART is delayed 4 to 6 weeks to reduce fatal immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome.
qexfrsc: A 35-year-old woman from Vietnam has a positive interferon-gamma release assay during employment screening. She has no symptoms and chest x-ray is normal. HIV is negative and she takes no other medications. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
Rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol for 2 months

Rifamycin-based short regimens (4 months of rifampin, 3 months of weekly isoniazid-rifapentine, or 3 months of daily isoniazid-rifampin) are preferred for latent TB because of better completion and less hepatotoxicity.
qx5din0: A 27-year-old woman taking a combined oral contraceptive is starting rifampin for latent TB. Which is the most appropriate contraceptive advice?
Use a copper IUD or other nonhormonal method during therapy
No change, since the interaction is not clinically significant
Double the daily dose of the oral contraceptive pill
Rifampin strongly induces CYP3A4 and reduces levels of oral hormonal contraceptives and implants. A copper IUD, levonorgestrel IUD, or DMPA injection is recommended.
q1fvbutk: A 29-year-old woman at 14 weeks gestation must travel for work to rural Ghana, where chloroquine-resistant P. falciparum is widespread. Which malaria chemoprophylaxis is most appropriate?

Mefloquine is the recommended chemoprophylaxis in pregnancy for chloroquine-resistant areas. Doxycycline is contraindicated, primaquine risks hemolysis in a G6PD-deficient fetus, and chloroquine resistance is widespread in Africa.
qnouvqj: A 26-year-old man traveling in Thailand develops fever of 38.8 C (101.8 F), abdominal cramps, and bloody diarrhea. Which is the most appropriate antibiotic?
Azithromycin is preferred for dysentery and for travelers' diarrhea in Southeast Asia because of high fluoroquinolone resistance in Campylobacter. Rifaximin is not used for invasive disease.
qkpe1qc: A 45-year-old woman has 2 days of fever, headache, and confusion with an episode of olfactory hallucinations. MRI shows right temporal lobe hyperintensity and CSF has lymphocytic pleocytosis with red cells. Which is the most appropriate treatment while awaiting PCR?
Oral valacyclovir 1 g three times daily
Withhold antivirals until the HSV PCR result returns
Suspected HSV encephalitis requires empiric IV acyclovir immediately because delay increases mortality and neurologic sequelae. Oral agents do not achieve adequate CNS levels.
q1dj2wc9: A 30-year-old man from Connecticut had an expanding red rash after a camping trip and now, 3 weeks after the trip, has a left facial droop involving the forehead. Lyme serology is positive. He has no headache or meningismus. Which is the most appropriate treatment?
Lyme facial palsy without meningitis can be treated with oral doxycycline for 14 days. IV ceftriaxone is reserved for meningitis, high-grade AV block, or inability to take oral therapy.
q1a1knql: A 66-year-old woman has 8 watery stools daily after a course of clindamycin. WBC is 11,000/mm3 and creatinine is 0.9 mg/dL. Stool testing confirms C. difficile infection. This is her first episode. Which is the most appropriate treatment?

IDSA prefers fidaxomicin for an initial episode because of lower recurrence, with oral vancomycin as an acceptable alternative. Metronidazole is only an option for nonsevere disease when the others are unavailable.
qbgsux: A 58-year-old man with lung cancer will receive cisplatin-based chemotherapy. Which antiemetic regimen is most appropriate before the first cycle?
NK1 antagonist, 5-HT3 antagonist, dexamethasone, and olanzapine
