Hypoxia from a failed airway attempt
Atropine blocks vagal effects, so it is appropriate for vagally mediated bradycardia or primary AV block. Hypoxic bradycardia is treated first with oxygenation and ventilation.
qp25fa8f55: Why are lower concentrations of dextrose used for infants and young children than the concentrated form used in adults?
Concentrated solutions are hypertonic and can damage small veins
Concentrated dextrose causes seizures in children
Highly concentrated dextrose is very hypertonic and can injure small veins and tissues, so diluted forms are used in children. Lower concentrations do not work faster.
qp1d23f6ea: A child is having a prolonged seizure and no IV can be started. Which route of midazolam is commonly used?
Intranasal midazolam is absorbed quickly through the nasal mucosa and is effective for pediatric seizures without IV access. Oral and transdermal routes are not practical during a seizure.
qp79ba8c76: Why is caution needed with naloxone in a newborn whose mother has used opioids regularly during pregnancy?
It can cause abrupt, life-threatening withdrawal including seizures
It has no effect in newborns
It blocks the newborn's breathing reflex
Abrupt reversal in an opioid-dependent newborn can trigger severe withdrawal and seizures, so ventilation support is the priority. Naloxone does work in newborns.
qp9bbbbbd9: An infant has a very fast, narrow-complex rhythm. Which feature suggests SVT that may respond to adenosine rather than sinus tachycardia?
Abrupt onset with a fixed rate and absent P waves
Gradual rise in rate with fever and dehydration
Rate that varies with crying and activity
Visible P waves before every QRS complex
SVT starts and stops abruptly, has little rate variability and usually lacks visible P waves. Sinus tachycardia varies with activity, has P waves and usually has a cause such as fever.
qpe1fc6683: How does ondansetron help a child with vomiting from gastroenteritis?
It reduces vomiting so oral rehydration can succeed
It cures the underlying viral infection
It stops diarrhea by slowing the gut
By reducing vomiting, ondansetron helps children tolerate oral fluids and may avoid an IV. It does not treat the infection or replace fluids.
qp762a17a2: What should caregivers be taught when giving liquid acetaminophen to a child?
Use the measuring device supplied and dose by weight
Use a kitchen spoon for convenience
Combine it with adult cold medicines
Give extra doses if the fever persists
Kitchen spoons are inaccurate and many combination products also contain acetaminophen, so mixing them risks overdose and liver injury. The supplied device and weight-based dosing reduce errors.
qpbd7e2f47: Which child should not receive ibuprofen without provider guidance?
A child with severe vomiting and signs of dehydration
A child with a fever and earache
A child with a sprained ankle
NSAIDs reduce blood flow to the kidneys and can cause kidney injury in dehydrated children. The other children are common, appropriate uses.
qp549c1901: A child in severe asthma has diminished breath sounds and no audible wheezing after albuterol. How should this be interpreted?
Worsening obstruction with very little air movement
Full recovery from the asthma attack
An expected side effect of albuterol
A sign the child is ready for discharge
A quiet or silent chest in severe asthma means too little air is moving to produce wheezing, which is ominous. Improvement would include better air movement and less work of breathing.
qp63577e69: During transport of a patient with norepinephrine running through a peripheral IV, what is essential?
Frequent checks of the IV site for infiltration
Flushing the line hourly to keep it open
Hanging it on the same line as the antibiotic
Checking the site only at arrival

Peripheral norepinephrine is acceptable short term in a large, proximal vein, but extravasation can cause tissue necrosis, so the site must be checked often. Sharing or flushing the line risks boluses.
qpe3b74e31: Which finding suggests excessive vasoconstriction from a norepinephrine infusion?
Cold, mottled fingers and toes with poor perfusion
Warm, flushed skin and bounding pulses
Low blood pressure with a slow heart rate
Intense alpha-1 vasoconstriction can reduce blood flow to the extremities and organs, causing cool, mottled skin. Warm, flushed skin suggests vasodilation.
qp38cdda8c: Why should a norepinephrine infusion run through a dedicated line that is not flushed?
Flushing would deliver an unintended bolus and spike the blood pressure
Flushing would dilute it and make it inactive
Flushing would cause the drug to crystallize
Flushing would cause a drop in heart rate
Norepinephrine is potent and short acting, so pushing the drug remaining in the line can cause a sudden rise in blood pressure. A dedicated line prevents unplanned boluses.
qp1825eb6f: Why may a fentanyl infusion have a longer effect than expected after several days?
It is fat soluble and accumulates in tissues during prolonged infusion
It is converted into a long-acting toxic metabolite
It is excreted unchanged only by the lungs
It loses potency the longer it is infused
Fentanyl is highly lipophilic, so it builds up in fat and muscle and is slowly released, prolonging its effect. Its short duration applies to single doses.
qp9d1d9216: An intubated patient is fighting the ventilator. Why does an analgesia-first approach often start with fentanyl?
Pain often drives agitation, and treating it may reduce sedative needs
Fentanyl paralyzes the patient so they cannot fight
Fentanyl has no effect on breathing in ventilated patients
Many ventilated patients are agitated from pain, so treating pain first can reduce the need for deeper sedation. Fentanyl does not cause paralysis.
qp5b533901: Why may a patient with kidney failure remain sedated long after a midazolam infusion ends?
An active metabolite builds up when kidney function is poor
Midazolam is not removed by the liver at all
Kidney failure makes midazolam more water soluble
Midazolam converts into an opioid in kidney failure
Midazolam's active metabolite is cleared by the kidneys and accumulates in renal failure, prolonging sedation. Prolonged infusion also causes accumulation in fat.
qpd17bbbd0: What concern is linked to prolonged benzodiazepine sedation such as a midazolam infusion in critically ill patients?
Increased risk of delirium and longer time on the ventilator
Increased risk of high blood pressure
Critical care guidelines prefer non-benzodiazepine sedation where possible because benzodiazepines are associated with delirium and longer ventilation. They do not cause hypertension.
qp01a5c27b: How should the depth of sedation be assessed during a midazolam infusion?
Use a validated sedation scale such as the RASS
Rely on the heart rate alone
Assume sedation if the patient is quiet
Validated scales such as the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale give an objective measure to avoid under- or over-sedation. Heart rate and pupils are unreliable sedation markers.
qp9b3d1822: In which patient should ketamine be used with caution due to its cardiovascular effects?
A patient with severe, uncontrolled hypertension or active ischemia
A patient with septic shock and low blood pressure
A patient with asthma who needs sedation
A patient with a long bone fracture
Ketamine's sympathomimetic effects raise heart rate and blood pressure, which can worsen severe hypertension or myocardial ischemia. In hypotension or asthma these effects can be helpful.
qpb5fde404: Which effect of ketamine may require more frequent suctioning?
Ketamine increases salivary and airway secretions, which may need suctioning. It tends to relax, not tighten, bronchial smooth muscle.
qpc0680a8e: Before giving a scheduled dose of digoxin, which assessment is most important for the nurse to perform?
Count the apical pulse for one full minute
Check the radial pulse for fifteen seconds
Measure blood pressure in both arms
Auscultate bowel sounds in all four quadrants
Digoxin slows conduction through the AV node, so a full apical count is needed to detect bradycardia before giving it. A brief radial check can miss irregular beats and undercount the rate.
qpf22ec7cb: A patient taking digoxin and furosemide reports nausea, poor appetite, and yellow-green halos around lights. What does the nurse recognize?
Possible digoxin toxicity, which low potassium can worsen
Expected adjustment effects of digoxin therapy
Dehydration from drinking too much water

GI upset and visual changes are classic signs of digoxin toxicity, and loop diuretics can lower potassium, which makes toxicity more likely. These are not expected effects and should be reported along with a digoxin level and potassium.
qp9b880123: A patient is on long-term amiodarone. Which set of tests does the nurse expect to be monitored periodically?
Thyroid, liver, and lung function tests
Amylase, lipase, and uric acid levels
Hemoglobin A1c, lipase, and bone density
Creatine kinase, ammonia, and lactate levels
Amiodarone can cause thyroid dysfunction, liver injury, and pulmonary toxicity, so these organs are monitored over time. The other panels do not target its known organ toxicities.
qpa2e2515d: Before a scheduled dose of oral metoprolol, the nurse finds a heart rate well below the patient's usual rate and the patient reports dizziness. What is the priority action?
Notify the provider before giving the dose
Give the dose and recheck vital signs later
Give the dose with a full glass of water
Have the patient walk to assess tolerance
Beta blockers slow the heart rate, and symptomatic bradycardia needs provider review before more drug is given. Giving the dose and rechecking later could worsen the bradycardia.
qpeaeee13b: A patient taking lisinopril develops sudden swelling of the lips and tongue. What does the nurse recognize?
A mild contact allergy to a food

ACE inhibitors can cause angioedema at any time during therapy, and tongue or throat swelling can block the airway. It is not a first-dose blood pressure effect and needs urgent airway assessment and provider notification.
qpa9d8b239: Which laboratory value is the nurse's priority to monitor in a patient receiving furosemide?
Loop diuretics cause loss of potassium, and low potassium can trigger dangerous dysrhythmias. Furosemide tends to lower, not raise, sodium and calcium.
qp6b7847e3: A patient prescribed sublingual nitroglycerin for angina asks about other medicines. Which medicine should the nurse teach the patient to avoid combining with it?
Nitrates combined with PDE-5 inhibitors such as sildenafil can cause severe, life-threatening hypotension. Aspirin is commonly used together with nitroglycerin in coronary disease.
qp57000a69: A patient takes spironolactone and lisinopril. Which finding should the nurse report to the provider?
High serum potassium with muscle weakness
Low serum potassium with leg cramps
A mild increase in daytime urination
Mild breast tenderness that is unchanged
Spironolactone is potassium-sparing, and ACE inhibitors also raise potassium, so hyperkalemia is the key risk. Low potassium is the concern with loop and thiazide diuretics, not this combination.
qp1515aa29: A patient with atrial fibrillation and a rapid ventricular rate is receiving IV diltiazem. Which monitoring is the priority?
Continuous heart rhythm and frequent blood pressure
IV diltiazem slows AV conduction and dilates vessels, so bradycardia, heart block, and hypotension can develop quickly. Intake and output alone would miss these changes.
qpc60ac992: The nurse is preparing a patient for IV adenosine to treat SVT. Which expected effect should the nurse explain?
A few seconds of very slow heartbeat with flushing or chest pressure
Drowsiness that lasts for several hours
A sustained rise in blood pressure
Gradual slowing of the heart over a day

Adenosine is given by rapid IV push with a saline flush and briefly blocks the AV node, often causing a few seconds of very slow or absent heartbeat, flushing, or chest discomfort. Its effects last seconds, not hours.
qp8338d7a3: During a peripheral norepinephrine infusion, the nurse notes blanching, coolness, and swelling at the IV site. Which treatment should the nurse anticipate?
Phentolamine infiltrated into the affected area

Norepinephrine extravasation causes intense local vasoconstriction, and phentolamine, an alpha blocker, is infiltrated into the area to limit tissue damage. Protamine reverses heparin and has no role here.
qpf7c597d7: Which route is preferred for a continuous norepinephrine infusion whenever possible?
A small vein in the back of the hand
A central line lowers the risk of tissue injury from extravasation of this potent vasoconstrictor. Small hand veins carry the highest risk of infiltration.
qp955302eb: A patient in anaphylactic shock needs epinephrine right away and has no IV access. Which route is recommended?
Intramuscular injection into the outer thigh
Subcutaneous injection into the upper arm
Undiluted IV push through a new line
A dissolving tablet under the tongue
Intramuscular injection into the anterolateral thigh gives faster, more reliable absorption than subcutaneous injection. Undiluted IV push epinephrine can cause dangerous dysrhythmias.
qp7dddd792: A patient receiving a dopamine infusion develops a new rapid, irregular heart rhythm. How does the nurse interpret this finding?
A known adverse effect that needs prompt reporting
An expected sign that the drug is working
A sign of low blood volume only
An allergic reaction to the IV diluent
Dopamine stimulates beta-1 receptors and can cause tachydysrhythmias, which should be reported promptly. A new dysrhythmia is not a marker of therapeutic effect.
qpe4ffc3ca: Which statement best describes how dobutamine helps a patient in cardiogenic shock?
It increases heart contractility through beta-1 stimulation
It constricts arteries through alpha-1 stimulation
It blocks calcium channels in vascular muscle
It inhibits phosphodiesterase-3 in heart muscle
Dobutamine is mainly a beta-1 agonist that strengthens contraction and raises cardiac output. Phosphodiesterase-3 inhibition describes milrinone, another inotrope.
qp086c3d66: A patient receives IV phenylephrine for hypotension. Which change in vital signs should the nurse watch for as blood pressure rises?
Phenylephrine is a pure alpha-1 agonist, and the rise in blood pressure can trigger a reflex slowing of the heart. It lacks the beta effects that would cause tachycardia.
qp69cf3b6c: How does vasopressin raise blood pressure in septic shock?
It constricts blood vessels through V1 receptors
It speeds the heart through beta-1 receptors
It dilates renal arteries through dopamine receptors
It boosts contractility by inhibiting PDE-3
Vasopressin acts on V1 receptors in vascular smooth muscle, causing vasoconstriction without beta-adrenergic effects. It does not directly increase heart rate.
qpcae3c734: A patient with decompensated heart failure is started on milrinone. Which assessment is the nurse's priority?
Milrinone is an inotrope and vasodilator, so hypotension and ventricular dysrhythmias are the main risks. It does not cause respiratory depression.
qp89af2101: Which teaching is appropriate for a patient taking midodrine for orthostatic hypotension?
Take doses during daytime hours, not close to bedtime
Take the last dose at bedtime for overnight effect
Lie flat for an hour after each dose
Take each dose only while lying down
Midodrine can cause supine hypertension, so doses are taken while upright during the day and not near bedtime. Lying flat after a dose increases that risk.
qp95b8efdc: Which adverse effect is the main safety concern with droxidopa, and what does the nurse teach?
Supine hypertension; rest with the head of the bed raised
Hypoglycemia; carry a fast-acting sugar source
Bradycardia; check the pulse before standing
Droxidopa carries a boxed warning for supine hypertension, so patients sleep with the head of the bed elevated and supine blood pressure is monitored. Hypoglycemia is not a known effect.
qp3fe377d1: Which laboratory test does the nurse use to evaluate the therapeutic effect of warfarin?
Warfarin is monitored with the INR, which reflects its effect on vitamin K-dependent clotting factors. The aPTT is used for unfractionated heparin.
qpafd55ff1: Which dietary teaching is appropriate for a patient starting warfarin?
Keep intake of leafy green vegetables consistent
Eat extra leafy greens when bruising occurs
Take a vitamin K supplement every morning
Vitamin K in leafy greens counters warfarin, so a steady intake keeps the INR stable. Cutting out greens entirely is unnecessary and can make the INR swing when intake changes.
qp6a04d6b2: Several days after starting heparin, a patient's platelet count has dropped by more than half and a new clot is suspected. What does the nurse recognize?

Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is an immune reaction that lowers platelets and paradoxically causes clotting, and it must be reported right away. Dilution would not explain a large drop with new thrombosis.
qp4016924a: Which laboratory test is commonly used to monitor a continuous IV infusion of unfractionated heparin?
Unfractionated heparin is monitored with the aPTT (or an anti-Xa level by facility protocol) to keep it in the therapeutic range. The INR is used for warfarin.
qp90d34964: Which technique is correct when giving enoxaparin from a prefilled syringe?
Inject subcutaneously in the abdomen without expelling the air bubble
Inject intramuscularly into the deltoid muscle
Rub the site firmly afterward to reduce bruising
Expel the air bubble, then inject into the thigh muscle
Enoxaparin is given by deep subcutaneous injection, usually in the abdomen, and the air bubble in the prefilled syringe is not expelled. Rubbing the site increases bruising.
qpe466db52: Which statement by a patient taking apixaban shows correct understanding?
"I will report black stools or unusual bruising."
"I need weekly INR checks to adjust my dose."
"I will double my next dose if I miss one."
"I can take ibuprofen freely for pain."
Bleeding is the main risk with apixaban, so signs like black stools or easy bruising should be reported. Apixaban does not need routine INR monitoring, unlike warfarin.
qpe28fe0dd: A patient with acute ischemic stroke symptoms is being considered for alteplase. Which finding must be confirmed before it is given?
A head CT showing no bleeding in the brain
That the patient has been fasting
Alteplase dissolves clots and is contraindicated in intracranial hemorrhage, so imaging must rule out bleeding first. A lipid panel has no bearing on eligibility.
qpc463b486: While giving protamine to reverse heparin, which adverse effects should the nurse watch for?
Low blood pressure, slow heart rate, and allergic reaction
High potassium and peaked T waves
Protamine can cause hypotension, bradycardia, and anaphylaxis-like reactions, especially if given too fast. It does not cause hypertension or seizures.
qp7ffebc07: A patient with chronic kidney disease receives epoetin alfa. Which finding should the nurse report?
A rapid rise in hemoglobin or new high blood pressure
A gradual rise in reticulocyte count
Mild tenderness at the injection site
Epoetin raises the risk of hypertension, clots, and stroke, especially when hemoglobin rises quickly or too high. A rising reticulocyte count is an expected sign it is working.
qpa5b8d860: Which medicine can reduce the antiplatelet effect of clopidogrel and is generally avoided with it?
Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, the enzyme that activates clopidogrel, which can reduce its effect. Acetaminophen has no meaningful interaction with clopidogrel.
qp1ca75a36: Which patient is at the highest risk for dangerous hyperkalemia if given succinylcholine?
A patient with a severe burn injury several days ago
A patient who takes a daily multivitamin
After major burns, crush injuries, or denervation, extra receptors on muscle allow succinylcholine to release large amounts of potassium. Mild dehydration does not create this risk.
qp72a9b42b: Shortly after succinylcholine is given, the patient develops jaw rigidity, rising end-tidal carbon dioxide, and a fast heart rate. What does the nurse recognize?
Masseter rigidity with rising end-tidal CO2 and tachycardia are early signs of malignant hyperthermia, which is treated with dantrolene. Fasciculations are brief twitches, not sustained rigidity.
qp5cb77896: After intubation, a patient is receiving rocuronium. Which nursing priority applies?
Ensure adequate sedation and pain control, since it provides neither
Reduce sedation, since rocuronium causes deep sleep
Expect the patient to breathe well without support
Ask the patient to rate pain on a numeric scale
Neuromuscular blockers paralyze muscles but do not affect awareness or pain, so sedation and analgesia must be given. A paralyzed patient cannot breathe or report pain.
qpabcf3740: How does sugammadex reverse neuromuscular blockade?
It binds and encapsulates rocuronium or vecuronium
It inhibits acetylcholinesterase at the synapse
It blocks nicotinic receptors on muscle
It stimulates muscarinic receptors in the heart
Sugammadex forms a tight complex with rocuronium or vecuronium, removing it from the junction. Acetylcholinesterase inhibition is how neostigmine works.
qpece32cbb: A patient who takes oral hormonal contraceptives received sugammadex during surgery. Which teaching is appropriate?
Use a backup nonhormonal method for the next week
No change is needed; contraceptives are unaffected
Take two contraceptive pills the next day
Skip the next week of contraceptive pills
Sugammadex can bind progestogen and lower contraceptive effect, so labeling advises a backup method for seven days. It is not true that contraceptives are unaffected.
qpe3e76727: Which adverse effect is associated with etomidate used for rapid sequence intubation?
Etomidate briefly inhibits cortisol production, a concern in critically ill or septic patients. It is not a trigger for malignant hyperthermia.
qpb2e345e1: Why may ketamine be chosen for induction in a patient with low blood pressure?
It tends to maintain blood pressure and breathing drive
It lowers heart rate and blood pressure
It reliably abolishes all airway reflexes
It has a specific reversal agent
Ketamine's sympathetic stimulation usually supports blood pressure and heart rate while preserving respiratory drive. It has no specific reversal agent.
qpcef7968e: Which handling practice is important when giving propofol?
Use strict aseptic technique, since the lipid supports bacterial growth
Shake the vial and give it intramuscularly
Mix it with other drugs in the same syringe
Save an opened vial in the refrigerator for tomorrow
Propofol is a lipid emulsion that can grow bacteria, so aseptic technique and timely disposal of opened product are required. It is given IV, not intramuscularly.
qp9e730571: A patient becomes oversedated after midazolam. Which reversal agent should the nurse anticipate?
Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines such as midazolam. Naloxone reverses opioids, not benzodiazepines.
qp13b9b099: After a rapid IV push of fentanyl, ventilation becomes difficult because the chest feels stiff. What does the nurse recognize?
Rapid, large IV doses of potent opioids like fentanyl can cause chest wall rigidity that impairs ventilation. Fentanyl is not a malignant hyperthermia trigger.
qp799f71bc: Which side effects should the nurse teach a patient to expect after using albuterol?
Tremor, nervousness, and a fast heart rate
Drowsiness and a slow heart rate
Albuterol is a beta-2 agonist, and some beta stimulation causes tremor and tachycardia. Thrush and hoarseness are linked to inhaled corticosteroids.
qp60a00e77: Which teaching is appropriate for a patient using an inhaled fluticasone inhaler?
Rinse the mouth and spit after each use
Use it first for sudden wheezing
Swallow the rinse water after each use
Use it only on days with symptoms
Rinsing and spitting lowers the risk of oral thrush from inhaled corticosteroids. Fluticasone is a daily controller and does not relieve sudden wheezing.
qpb47cbc9a: Which teaching is correct about salmeterol?
It is not used to relieve a sudden asthma attack
It works within seconds for acute wheezing
It can be used alone without a controller in asthma
It may be used several times every hour as needed
Salmeterol is a long-acting beta agonist with slow onset for maintenance, not rescue. In asthma it should be paired with an inhaled corticosteroid, never used alone.
qp942ecdab: Which history should the nurse report before a patient starts tiotropium?
Tiotropium is an anticholinergic that can worsen narrow-angle glaucoma and urinary retention. Seasonal allergies are not a concern.
qpe4ec26d5: Which effect should the nurse teach patients and families to report while taking montelukast?
Mood changes, agitation, or suicidal thoughts
Montelukast has a boxed warning for serious neuropsychiatric events. Yellow-green halos are a sign of digoxin toxicity.
qpa1ba0b3a: A patient on theophylline starts ciprofloxacin and then reports nausea, restlessness, and a racing heart. What does the nurse recognize?
Possible theophylline toxicity from a drug interaction
Ciprofloxacin slows theophylline clearance, and theophylline has a narrow therapeutic range, so toxicity can follow. A theophylline level should be checked and the provider notified.
qp31154851: A patient with diabetes is started on a short course of prednisone for an asthma flare. Which change should the nurse anticipate?
Corticosteroids raise blood glucose, so closer monitoring is needed in diabetes. Prednisone tends to lower potassium and raise the white cell count.
qp09b46de4: When is oseltamivir treatment most effective for influenza?
When started within two days of symptom onset
Only after a fever has lasted a full week
After a culture confirms flu several days later
Only if pneumonia has already developed
Oseltamivir works best when started within 48 hours of symptoms, though it may still be used later for hospitalized or high-risk patients. Waiting for culture results delays benefit.
qp132f7d99: Which teaching is essential for a patient prescribed benzonatate capsules?
Swallow capsules whole without chewing or sucking
Chew the capsules for faster relief
Open the capsule and mix it in applesauce
Let the capsule dissolve under the tongue
Releasing benzonatate in the mouth numbs the throat and can cause choking or severe reactions. It should also be stored away from children, for whom accidental ingestion can be fatal.
qp01794234: Which history should the nurse report before a patient takes pseudoephedrine for congestion?
Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic decongestant that can raise blood pressure and heart rate. Seasonal allergies are a common reason it is used.
qp376f3d6e: Which IV fluid is compatible for flushing before and after IV phenytoin?
Any fluid already running in the line
Phenytoin precipitates in dextrose solutions, so the line is flushed with normal saline. It should not be mixed with other fluids or drugs.
qpe3196e51: Which teaching helps a patient manage a common long-term effect of phenytoin?
Brush and floss carefully and see a dentist regularly
Expect hair thinning and use a mild shampoo
Avoid all dairy products to protect the liver
Take it with grapefruit juice to improve absorption
Phenytoin causes gingival hyperplasia, and good oral hygiene reduces it. Phenytoin levels are also monitored by name since it has a narrow therapeutic range.
qp848b729a: Which new symptom in a patient taking carbamazepine should be reported right away?
Skin rash with blisters, fever, or mouth sores
Mild drowsiness during the first days
Mild nausea relieved by taking with food
Slight dizziness that improves with time
Carbamazepine can cause Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, which need urgent attention. Mild early drowsiness is common and usually fades.
qp99700649: Which effect should the nurse teach a patient and family to watch for with levetiracetam?
Irritability, mood changes, or thoughts of self-harm
Yellowing of the skin and eyes
Levetiracetam is linked to behavioral changes, and antiepileptics carry a warning for suicidal thoughts. Gum overgrowth is linked to phenytoin.
qp0ee66a4b: Which instruction is most important for a patient starting lamotrigine?
Report any new rash, since it may signal a serious skin reaction
Expect weight gain during the first month
Expect a fine hand tremor as it starts working
Lamotrigine has a boxed warning for serious rashes, including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, especially early in therapy. Gum overgrowth is a phenytoin effect.
qpfdf2a7a5: Which laboratory tests does the nurse expect to be monitored for a patient taking valproic acid?
Liver function tests and platelet count
Valproic acid can cause hepatotoxicity and thrombocytopenia, so liver tests and platelets are checked, along with valproic acid levels. A lithium level is unrelated.
qpa0f9789b: After IV lorazepam is given for status epilepticus, which assessment is the nurse's priority?
Benzodiazepines can depress breathing, especially after repeated doses, so airway and breathing are monitored closely. Hypertension is not a typical effect.
qp5af4af1d: Which teaching is appropriate for a patient taking carbidopa-levodopa?
Large high-protein meals may reduce how well it works
Its full effect is felt minutes after the first dose
It works best when taken with iron supplements
Dietary protein competes with levodopa for absorption and transport into the brain, so large protein loads near doses can blunt its effect. Iron also reduces levodopa absorption.
qp48f2b178: Which history is a contraindication to sumatriptan?
Triptans cause vasoconstriction and are contraindicated in coronary artery disease and uncontrolled hypertension. Seasonal allergies do not affect triptan use.
qp11f3d2e2: Which finding should the nurse report in a patient taking donepezil?
As a cholinesterase inhibitor, donepezil increases vagal tone and can cause bradycardia and syncope. Dry mouth and constipation are anticholinergic effects, the opposite of its action.
qp6da4cb30: Before giving IV morphine, which assessment is most important?
Respiratory rate and level of sedation
Respiratory depression is the most dangerous opioid effect, and increasing sedation usually comes before it. Bowel sounds matter for constipation but are not the priority.
qp282d89aa: After naloxone reverses an opioid overdose, what must the nurse continue to monitor for?
Return of respiratory depression as naloxone wears off
Naloxone often wears off before longer-acting opioids, so sedation and slow breathing can return. Repeat doses may be needed.
qp98cde102: Which teaching helps prevent accidental acetaminophen overdose?
Check cold and sleep products for hidden acetaminophen
Take it with alcohol to improve its effect
Any amount is safe because it is sold over the counter
Combine it freely with other pain relievers
Many combination products contain acetaminophen, and taking several at once can cause liver injury. Over-the-counter status does not make any amount safe.
qpc9402633: Which finding should the nurse report in a patient receiving ketorolac?
Decreased urine output or black stools
Slight warmth at the injection site
Ketorolac is a potent NSAID with boxed warnings for kidney injury and GI bleeding, and its total course is limited. Improved pain is the intended effect.
qpd2d40b3e: Which teaching is essential for a patient using a fentanyl transdermal patch?
Avoid heating pads, hot tubs, and direct heat over the patch
Cut the patch in half for a smaller effect
Apply each new patch to the same spot
Cover the patch with a heating pad at night
Heat increases fentanyl absorption from the patch and can cause a fatal overdose. Cutting the patch damages the release system.
qpd2c78d41: Why is hydromorphone considered a high-alert medicine?
It is far more potent than morphine, so mix-ups can cause overdose
It is given only by the intrathecal route
Hydromorphone is several times more potent than morphine, and look-alike names and products have led to fatal errors. Naloxone does reverse it.
qp40285cc5: Which adverse effect requires ECG monitoring in a patient taking methadone?
Methadone can prolong the QT interval and cause torsades de pointes. It does not cause hyperkalemia.
qp96c5f3b3: A patient taking warfarin asks about using ibuprofen for back pain. Which response is accurate?
It increases bleeding risk when combined with warfarin
It lowers the INR and makes warfarin weaker
It has no interaction with warfarin
It speeds up clotting and raises clot risk
NSAIDs impair platelet function and irritate the GI tract, adding to warfarin's bleeding risk. They do not make warfarin weaker.
qp9b70b098: Which adverse effects should the nurse monitor for during a dexmedetomidine infusion?
Severe hypertension and fast heart rate
Dexmedetomidine is an alpha-2 agonist that lowers sympathetic tone, so bradycardia and hypotension are its most common effects. It usually causes little respiratory depression.
qpc1ba6915: Which interaction is a concern when tramadol is given to a patient taking an SSRI?
Tramadol has serotonergic activity, and combining it with SSRIs raises the risk of serotonin syndrome and seizures. Hyperkalemia is not linked to this combination.
qp5f4b1c40: A patient taking lithium has vomiting, diarrhea, coarse hand tremor, and confusion. What does the nurse recognize?
Possible lithium toxicity needing a lithium level
Expected side effects that will pass
GI symptoms, coarse tremor, and confusion are signs of lithium toxicity, which has a narrow therapeutic range. A fine tremor can be expected, but a coarse tremor with confusion is not.
qpeb4be38f: Which teaching helps keep lithium levels stable?
Keep salt and fluid intake consistent day to day
Low sodium or dehydration causes the kidneys to retain lithium and raises levels. NSAIDs such as ibuprofen also raise lithium levels.
qpbd629a29: Which symptom should a patient taking clozapine report right away?
Fever, sore throat, or flu-like symptoms
Clozapine can cause severe neutropenia, so signs of infection need urgent evaluation with an ANC. Weight gain and drooling are common but not emergencies.
qp560271b2: A patient on haloperidol develops high fever, rigid muscles, confusion, and unstable blood pressure. What does the nurse recognize?
Fever, lead-pipe rigidity, altered mental status, and autonomic instability define neuroleptic malignant syndrome, a medical emergency. Tardive dyskinesia causes involuntary movements without fever.
qp2c957058: A young adult is starting sertraline for depression. Which monitoring is most important early in treatment?
Watch for worsening depression or suicidal thoughts
Check blood glucose before each dose
Antidepressants carry a boxed warning for increased suicidal thinking in children and young adults, especially early or after dose changes. Routine sertraline levels are not used.
qp99ae173e: Which foods should a patient taking tranylcypromine avoid?
Aged cheeses, cured meats, and tap beer
Fresh fish, pasta, and green beans
MAOIs block the breakdown of tyramine, and high-tyramine foods can trigger a hypertensive crisis. Fresh meats and fish are low in tyramine.
qpf07f4b1b: Which monitoring is most important for a patient taking olanzapine long term?
Weight, blood glucose, and lipid levels
Olanzapine commonly causes weight gain, hyperglycemia, and high lipids, so metabolic monitoring is routine. Lithium levels are unrelated.
qp983e23ee: Which teaching is correct for a buprenorphine-naloxone sublingual film?
Let the film dissolve fully under the tongue
Swallow the film whole with water
Chew the film for a faster effect
Dissolve the film in juice and drink it
The film is designed to be absorbed under the tongue, and swallowing or chewing it lowers absorption. Naloxone is included to discourage injection misuse.
qpc4fcbd25: Which teaching is essential for a patient taking disulfiram?
Avoid hidden alcohol in mouthwash, cough syrup, and sauces
Small amounts of beer are safe
Alcohol is fine once a week
Only hard liquor causes a reaction
Even small amounts of alcohol, including in mouthwash or cooking, can cause flushing, vomiting, and a racing heart. Any form of alcohol can trigger the reaction.
qpc5d981e6: Which history is a concern before a patient starts bupropion?
An eating disorder such as bulimia
Bupropion lowers the seizure threshold and is contraindicated in seizure disorders and in bulimia or anorexia nervosa. Smoking cessation is one of its uses.
qpb75664bf: Which practice is essential when giving IV potassium chloride?
Give it only as a diluted infusion on a pump, never IV push
Give it by slow IV push over a few seconds
Give it undiluted to save fluid volume
Hang it by gravity without a pump
IV push or concentrated potassium can cause fatal cardiac arrest, so it is a high-alert medicine given diluted by infusion pump. Slow push is still unsafe.
qp3d45fd17: Before starting IV potassium replacement, which assessment is most important?
Adequate urine output and kidney function
The kidneys excrete potassium, so poor urine output raises the risk of dangerous hyperkalemia. Pupil checks do not guide potassium safety.
qp5564ab14: Which teaching is correct for a patient taking patiromer?
Separate it from other oral medicines by a few hours
Take it together with all other morning pills
Take it only when potassium is very low
Mix it with hot liquids before drinking
Patiromer can bind other oral drugs, so labeling advises spacing other medicines by about three hours. It lowers, not raises, potassium.
qpcf0f15bf: Why is IV calcium gluconate given to a patient with severe hyperkalemia and ECG changes?
It stabilizes the heart muscle membrane against dysrhythmias
It shifts potassium into the cells
It removes potassium from the body
It increases potassium loss in the urine
Calcium protects the heart quickly but does not lower serum potassium. Insulin with dextrose shifts potassium into cells.
qp54fef95e: After IV regular insulin with dextrose is given for hyperkalemia, which assessment is the nurse's priority?
Blood glucose, since hypoglycemia can follow
Insulin shifts potassium into cells, and hypoglycemia is a common complication even with dextrose. Frequent glucose checks are needed.
qpf557a528: Which practice is important when preparing an IV mannitol infusion?
Inspect for crystals and use an in-line filter
Mix it with blood products in the same line
Shake vigorously to dissolve any crystals
Give it as a rapid intramuscular injection
Mannitol can form crystals, so it is inspected and given through a filter. It is not given intramuscularly.
qp4e6e73fd: A patient with a history of gout is starting hydrochlorothiazide. Which effect should the nurse watch for?
Raised uric acid that may trigger a gout flare
Thiazides reduce uric acid excretion and can provoke gout. They tend to raise glucose and calcium and lower potassium.
qp06d1470c: Which finding should the nurse report in a patient receiving desmopressin?
Low serum sodium with headache or confusion
Desmopressin causes water retention, which can lead to hyponatremia and seizures. Fluid intake is monitored and sodium checked.
qp47f16b68: A patient with heart failure is receiving a normal saline bolus. Which finding should the nurse report?
New lung crackles and shortness of breath
A rise in blood pressure toward baseline
Crackles and dyspnea suggest fluid overload, a risk with isotonic fluids in heart failure. Improved urine output is an expected response.
qpc441bd42: Which effects should the nurse watch for in an older adult taking oxybutynin?
Oxybutynin is anticholinergic, and older adults are especially prone to confusion and falls. Diarrhea and salivation are cholinergic effects, the opposite.
qp5f1d6f05: Which teaching is correct for a patient taking oral alendronate?
Take it with plain water on an empty stomach and stay upright
Take it with breakfast and coffee
Lie down afterward to prevent dizziness
Take it together with a calcium supplement
Alendronate is poorly absorbed with food or minerals and can irritate the esophagus, so it is taken with plain water and the patient remains upright. Calcium blocks its absorption.
qpab0b3807: Which symptom should a patient taking alendronate report?
New heartburn or pain when swallowing
Mild muscle aches after the first dose
Alendronate can cause esophagitis and esophageal ulcers. Heartburn or painful swallowing should be reported promptly.
qp990c72a3: Which teaching is appropriate for a patient starting allopurinol?
Drink plenty of fluids and report any skin rash
Take it only during a gout attack
Expect a rash as a normal effect
Fluids reduce kidney stone risk, and a rash can signal a severe hypersensitivity reaction such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Allopurinol prevents attacks rather than treating an acute flare.
qp8455248a: Which early symptoms may signal colchicine toxicity?
GI symptoms are often the first signs of colchicine toxicity, which is more likely with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors such as clarithromycin. Constipation is not typical.
qp627f80e2: Which symptoms should the nurse teach a patient taking febuxostat to report right away?
Chest pain, shortness of breath, or stroke symptoms
Mild joint pain early in therapy
Febuxostat has a boxed warning for increased cardiovascular death. Gout flares can occur early in therapy and are expected.
qp409b8fc3: Which lab values should be checked before an IV zoledronic acid infusion?
Zoledronic acid can harm the kidneys and lower calcium, so kidney function and calcium are checked and the patient is well hydrated. Clotting tests are unrelated.
qp387746fb: Which adverse effect is a particular concern with denosumab, especially in patients with kidney disease?
Denosumab can cause significant hypocalcemia, so calcium is checked and calcium with vitamin D is often given. Potassium is not affected.
qp5616947c: Which teaching is correct for a patient using calcitonin salmon nasal spray?
Use the same nostril every day
Tilt the head back and sniff hard
Use it only when bone pain occurs
Alternating nostrils reduces nasal irritation, a common side effect. Nasal dryness, crusting, or nosebleeds should be reported.
qp69f4f4ae: Which teaching is important for a patient taking raloxifene?
Report leg pain or swelling and avoid long periods sitting still
Expect leg swelling as a normal effect
Use it to relieve hot flashes
Take it with a high-fat meal for absorption
Raloxifene raises the risk of blood clots, so signs of DVT should be reported and prolonged immobility avoided. It can cause, not relieve, hot flashes.
qpf70d4c6b: Which screening test is needed before the first pegloticase infusion?
Pegloticase can cause hemolysis and methemoglobinemia in G6PD deficiency, so patients at risk are screened. HLA-B*5801 testing relates to allopurinol.
qp7c498f7e: Acetylcysteine is the antidote for overdose of which medicine?
Acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione, protecting the liver from acetaminophen's toxic metabolite. Aspirin overdose is treated with supportive care and bicarbonate.
qpb0bf7c7c: Which risk is greatest when flumazenil is given to a patient who uses benzodiazepines long term?
Flumazenil can trigger withdrawal seizures in patients with benzodiazepine dependence or mixed overdoses. It reverses rather than causes respiratory depression.
qp4e8070d7: After digoxin immune fab is given for toxicity, which lab change should the nurse watch for?
As digoxin is bound, potassium shifts back into cells and can drop, so potassium is monitored closely. Total digoxin levels also become unreliable afterward.
qpfe9cc08f: Which adverse reaction is a concern when phytonadione is given intravenously?
IV vitamin K carries a boxed warning for severe, sometimes fatal hypersensitivity reactions, so it is infused slowly with monitoring. Other routes are preferred when practical.
qpfe9f78b2: Which substance is not well bound by activated charcoal?
Charcoal binds poorly to metals and ions such as lithium and iron, and to alcohols. Aspirin and acetaminophen are well adsorbed.
qpb5e62a47: Fomepizole is used as an antidote for ingestion of which substance?
Fomepizole blocks alcohol dehydrogenase, preventing formation of toxic metabolites of ethylene glycol and methanol. Organophosphates are treated with atropine and pralidoxime.
qp5d8e5b7e: After hydroxocobalamin is given for cyanide poisoning, the patient's skin and urine turn red. What does the nurse recognize?
An expected effect of the antidote's red color
A sign of acute kidney failure
Hydroxocobalamin is deep red and commonly discolors skin and urine; it can also interfere with some lab tests. It does not indicate kidney failure.
qp59237f34: In organophosphate poisoning, which finding shows atropine is having the desired effect?
Drying of airway secretions and easier breathing
The goal of atropine in organophosphate poisoning is drying of bronchial secretions. Pupil size is not a reliable endpoint.
qpa39eef9b: Before methylene blue is given for methemoglobinemia, which medication history is a concern?
Use of an SSRI or other serotonergic drug
Methylene blue inhibits MAO-A and can cause serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs. G6PD deficiency is another important concern.
qpd8159355: Glucagon may be used as an antidote for which overdose?
Glucagon raises cAMP in heart cells independently of beta receptors, improving heart rate and contractility. Vomiting is common, so airway protection is monitored.
qp704463e9: During an IV vancomycin infusion, the patient develops flushing and itching of the face, neck, and upper body. What does the nurse recognize?
An infusion reaction linked to fast infusion
Expected effect of a working antibiotic
Vancomycin infusion reaction is a histamine release related to infusion speed, managed by slowing the infusion and notifying the provider. It is not true anaphylaxis or ototoxicity.
qp995eea74: Which monitoring is routine for a patient on IV vancomycin?
Vancomycin is nephrotoxic and dosed using vancomycin levels or AUC, so kidney function is followed closely. Liver toxicity is not its main concern.
qp4127cd58: Which symptom should a patient on gentamicin report?
Ringing in the ears, hearing loss, or dizziness
Aminoglycosides can cause ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity, so hearing changes and gentamicin levels are monitored. Orange urine is linked to rifampin.
qpa3ff342a: Before the first dose of IV cefazolin, which assessment is most important?
Ask about drug allergies, including penicillin reactions
Cephalosporins can cause allergic reactions, and a history of severe penicillin reaction raises concern. Allergy assessment comes before any first antibiotic dose.
qp6a575167: Which teaching is essential for a patient taking metronidazole?
Avoid alcohol during therapy and for a few days after
Take it with milk to improve absorption
Expect orange urine as a harmless effect
Use extra sun exposure to speed healing
Alcohol with metronidazole can cause a disulfiram-like reaction with flushing, nausea, and vomiting. Orange urine is caused by rifampin, not metronidazole.
qpce399336: Which symptom should a patient taking ciprofloxacin report right away?
Sudden pain or swelling at the heel or a tendon
Fluoroquinolones carry a boxed warning for tendinitis and tendon rupture, especially in older adults and those on corticosteroids. Mild nausea is common.
qp2bdf4837: Which vitamin is often given with isoniazid to prevent peripheral neuropathy?
Isoniazid depletes pyridoxine, which can cause numbness and tingling. Liver function is also monitored because of hepatotoxicity.
qp42cf406f: Which teaching is appropriate for a patient starting rifampin?
Body fluids may turn orange, and soft contact lenses can stain
Urine may turn blue-green and is a sign of toxicity
It must be taken with antacids
Rifampin harmlessly colors urine, sweat, and tears orange-red. It reduces, not strengthens, hormonal contraceptive effectiveness.
qpa0997632: Which symptom should a patient taking clindamycin report, even weeks after finishing?
Clindamycin carries a boxed warning for Clostridioides difficile infection, which can appear weeks after therapy. Frequent watery diarrhea needs evaluation.
qp877184f7: Which route is correct for penicillin G benzathine?
Penicillin G benzathine has a boxed warning that IV use can cause cardiac arrest and death. It is given only by deep IM injection.
qp38625518: Which teaching is correct for insulin glargine?
Do not mix it in the same syringe with other insulins
Draw it up together with regular insulin
Shake it until it looks cloudy
Give it only with high blood glucose
Insulin glargine is a clear, long-acting basal insulin that must not be mixed with other insulins. It is given on schedule, not only for high readings.
qp6d70845f: When is rapid-acting insulin lispro given relative to meals?
Shortly before a meal, so food follows soon after
An hour after finishing a meal
Only for high readings without food
Lispro starts working quickly, so it is given shortly before or right after eating to avoid hypoglycemia. Giving it without food raises the risk of low blood glucose.
qp3489dc8e: When drawing up regular insulin and NPH insulin in one syringe, which order is correct?
Draw up the clear regular insulin before the cloudy NPH
Draw up the cloudy NPH before the clear regular
Mix both in the vial before drawing up
Draw them in either order without difference
Drawing clear before cloudy keeps NPH from contaminating the regular insulin vial. NPH is gently rolled, not shaken, before use.
qpfcb3a629: Which upcoming event should the nurse report to the provider for a patient taking metformin?
A procedure using iodinated contrast dye
Iodinated contrast can impair kidney function and increase the risk of metformin-associated lactic acidosis, so the provider decides on timing of doses. Routine dental care does not affect metformin.
qpefbdfae1: Which adverse effect is most important to teach a patient taking glipizide?
Low blood glucose, especially if meals are skipped
Sulfonylureas stimulate insulin release and can cause hypoglycemia, especially in older adults or with missed meals. Genital yeast infections are linked to SGLT2 inhibitors.
qpd5e860a5: Which teaching is correct for a patient taking levothyroxine?
Take it on an empty stomach, apart from calcium or iron
Take it with a calcium supplement at breakfast
Take it with a large meal for absorption
Take it whenever convenient during the day
Levothyroxine absorbs best on an empty stomach, and calcium and iron bind it. Taking it with calcium reduces its effect.
qp75a58048: Which findings may indicate that a patient's levothyroxine effect is too strong?
Palpitations, heat intolerance, and weight loss
Fatigue, cold intolerance, and weight gain
Dry skin, constipation, and slow pulse
Excess thyroid hormone mimics hyperthyroidism. Fatigue, cold intolerance, and weight gain suggest the effect is too weak.
qpc82910bd: Which symptom should a patient taking methimazole report right away?
Methimazole can cause agranulocytosis, and fever or sore throat may be the first sign. A CBC is checked when these occur.
qp4db565e3: Which history is a contraindication to semaglutide?
Personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer
GLP-1 receptor agonists carry a boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors and are contraindicated with medullary thyroid cancer or MEN 2. Family history of diabetes is common in those who use it.
qp06d8c07a: After glucagon is given for severe hypoglycemia, the patient wakes and can swallow. What is the next step?
Give oral carbohydrate to prevent glucose dropping again
Give a second glucagon injection right away
Have the patient sleep without eating
Glucagon's effect is short-lived, so oral carbohydrate is given once the person can swallow safely. The patient is placed on their side beforehand because vomiting is common.
qp9ebd78a1: Which ECG change is a concern with ondansetron, especially at higher doses or with other risk factors?
Ondansetron can prolong the QT interval, increasing the risk of torsades de pointes. Electrolytes such as potassium and magnesium are corrected before use in at-risk patients.
qpb0450018: Which finding should a patient taking metoclopramide report?
Involuntary movements of the face, tongue, or limbs
Metoclopramide has a boxed warning for tardive dyskinesia, which can be irreversible. Mild drowsiness is common and less concerning.
qp136ceb5c: During IV promethazine administration, which patient complaint is the nurse's priority?
Burning or pain at the IV site
Promethazine has a boxed warning for severe tissue injury, including gangrene, from extravasation or inadvertent arterial injection. Drowsiness is expected.
qp11e6c5e7: Which outcome shows lactulose is effective for hepatic encephalopathy?
Improved mental status with soft stools
Firm stools once every few days
Lactulose traps ammonia in the colon and removes it in stool, which improves mental status. A rising ammonia level shows it is not working.
qp47c6d1dd: Which risks are associated with long-term pantoprazole use?
Low magnesium, bone fractures, and C. difficile diarrhea
High potassium, gout, and kidney stones
Hair loss, gum overgrowth, and rash
Long-term proton pump inhibitor use is linked to hypomagnesemia, fractures, and Clostridioides difficile infection. Gum overgrowth is a phenytoin effect.
qp6e65c7a4: Which teaching is correct for a patient taking sucralfate?
Take it on an empty stomach, apart from other medicines
Take it with antacids at the same time
Take it immediately after large meals
Chew it together with other pills
Sucralfate forms a protective barrier over ulcers and can bind other drugs, reducing their absorption. Antacids taken at the same time interfere with it.
qpe9a34a69: For which patient is misoprostol for NSAID ulcer prevention contraindicated?
A patient who takes daily aspirin
Misoprostol can cause uterine contractions and pregnancy loss, so it is contraindicated in pregnancy for ulcer prevention. Arthritis patients on NSAIDs are its main users.
qp214a8e5d: Which situation should be reported to the provider rather than self-treated with loperamide?
Diarrhea with fever or blood in the stool
Mild diarrhea after a new food
Loose stools for half a day
Bloody diarrhea or fever can signal an invasive infection, where slowing the gut may cause harm. Mild, short-lived diarrhea is a common use for loperamide.
qp05b46c53: Which teaching is correct for bisacodyl enteric-coated tablets?
Swallow whole, and not with milk or antacids
Crush them for a faster effect
Take them with a glass of milk
Milk, antacids, or crushing can dissolve the coating early, causing stomach irritation and cramping. The tablets work in the colon.
qp08e89ab1: Which teaching is correct for a patient taking pancrelipase capsules?
Take with every meal and snack, swallowing capsules whole
Crush the beads and mix with milk
Take only when stools become oily
Pancrelipase replaces pancreatic enzymes for digestion, so it must be taken with food. Crushing or chewing the beads destroys the protective coating.
qp1ed94194: Which findings suggest magnesium toxicity in a patient receiving IV magnesium sulfate for preeclampsia?
Absent deep tendon reflexes and slow breathing
Loss of reflexes, respiratory depression, and low urine output are signs of magnesium toxicity, along with a high magnesium level. Brisk reflexes and clonus suggest worsening preeclampsia instead.
qpb86c2ebe: Which medicine should be readily available as the antidote for magnesium sulfate toxicity?
IV calcium gluconate counters the effects of magnesium on the heart and neuromuscular junction. Naloxone reverses opioids.
qp6be0b7eb: During an oxytocin infusion for labor, which finding requires immediate action?
Contractions too frequent with a nonreassuring fetal heart rate
Contractions every few minutes with moderate variability

Uterine tachysystole with fetal heart rate changes signals reduced placental blood flow and needs immediate intervention per protocol and provider notification. Regular contractions with moderate variability are reassuring.
qpd81bb577: With prolonged oxytocin use, which complication should the nurse monitor for?
Water intoxication with low serum sodium
Oxytocin has an antidiuretic effect, and prolonged infusion with large amounts of fluid can cause water intoxication and hyponatremia. Headache, confusion, or seizures are warning signs.
qpaf356530: Which condition is a contraindication to methylergonovine for postpartum hemorrhage?
Methylergonovine causes vasoconstriction that can sharply raise blood pressure. Asthma is the key contraindication for carboprost, not methylergonovine.
qp69b20193: Which history is a concern before carboprost is given for postpartum hemorrhage?
Carboprost, a prostaglandin, can cause bronchospasm and is avoided in asthma. Hypertension is the key concern with methylergonovine.
qpf03a1bb2: Which patient is a candidate for Rho(D) immune globulin after birth?
An Rh-negative mother with an Rh-positive newborn
An Rh-positive mother with an Rh-negative newborn
An Rh-positive mother with an Rh-positive newborn
An Rh-negative mother with an Rh-negative newborn
Rho(D) immune globulin prevents an Rh-negative mother from forming antibodies after exposure to Rh-positive fetal blood. It is given within 72 hours of birth.
qpe86b20fe: Which maternal assessment is the priority when terbutaline is given?
Heart rate, since tachycardia is common

Terbutaline is a beta agonist that causes maternal tachycardia and can cause serious cardiac effects; it carries a boxed warning against prolonged use for preterm labor. It tends to raise, not lower, glucose.
qpb0229582: Why is betamethasone given to a patient in preterm labor?
To speed fetal lung maturity before birth
Antenatal corticosteroids speed fetal lung maturation and reduce neonatal respiratory distress. They do not relax the uterus.
qpe2cb6cb6: Why is erythromycin ophthalmic ointment applied to the newborn's eyes after birth?
Erythromycin eye ointment prevents gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum. It does not affect jaundice.
qp839252c0: Which teaching is correct for using an epinephrine auto-injector?
Inject into the outer thigh, then seek emergency care
Inject into the upper arm muscle, then rest
Inject into a vein for faster action
Inject only after an antihistamine fails
The auto-injector is given into the anterolateral thigh, even through clothing, and emergency care is needed because symptoms can return. Waiting for an antihistamine delays life-saving treatment.
qp91d6c157: Which effects should the nurse watch for when an older adult takes diphenhydramine?
Diphenhydramine is strongly anticholinergic and sedating, which raises the risk of confusion and falls in older adults. Diarrhea and salivation are the opposite effects.
qp9cc34601: Which teaching is most important for a patient taking oral methotrexate for rheumatoid arthritis?
It is usually taken once a week, not daily
It is taken every day with breakfast
Extra doses help during a flare
Alcohol is safe in any amount
Daily dosing errors with weekly methotrexate have caused fatal toxicity. Alcohol increases liver toxicity, and blood counts and liver tests are monitored.
qpdd573b89: Which screening is required before a patient starts adalimumab?
TNF inhibitors carry a boxed warning for serious infections, including reactivation of latent tuberculosis. Hepatitis B screening is also done.
qp16265d84: During an infliximab infusion, which findings should the nurse report?
Fever, chills, hives, or shortness of breath
Slight warmth at the IV site
Infliximab can cause infusion reactions ranging from mild to anaphylaxis. Improved stiffness is the desired effect.
qp0db3bf4f: Which monitoring is routine for a transplant patient taking cyclosporine?
Kidney function, blood pressure, and cyclosporine levels
Cyclosporine is nephrotoxic, raises blood pressure, and has a narrow therapeutic range, so cyclosporine levels guide therapy. Grapefruit juice can raise levels.
qpba4ef89c: Which adverse effects are common with tacrolimus?
Tremor, high blood glucose, and kidney injury
Low blood pressure and weight loss
Tacrolimus can cause neurotoxicity such as tremor, new-onset diabetes, and nephrotoxicity, and tacrolimus levels are monitored. Gum overgrowth and excess hair are more typical of cyclosporine.
qp6b700cd7: Which monitoring is recommended for a patient taking hydroxychloroquine long term?
Regular eye exams for retinal damage
Hydroxychloroquine can cause irreversible retinal toxicity, so baseline and periodic eye exams are recommended. Hearing loss is not a typical concern.
qpba59297f: Which teaching is essential for a patient of childbearing potential taking mycophenolate?
It can cause pregnancy loss and birth defects, so reliable contraception is needed
It only matters for male patients
Mycophenolate has a boxed warning for embryofetal toxicity and a REMS program requiring pregnancy testing and contraception. It is not safe in pregnancy.
qp0c17e55a: Which adverse effect requires monitoring of blood counts in a patient taking azathioprine?
Azathioprine can suppress the bone marrow, especially in patients with low TPMT or NUDT15 activity. CBCs are monitored regularly.
qp09083541: Which route is correct for vinblastine?
Intravenous only; it is fatal if given intrathecally
Intrathecal injection into the spinal fluid
Vinca alkaloids carry a boxed warning that intrathecal administration is fatal and must be labeled for IV use only. It is also a vesicant, so extravasation is watched for.
qp391bde87: Why is a corticosteroid premedication given before docetaxel?
To reduce fluid retention and hypersensitivity reactions
To raise the white blood cell count
Corticosteroid premedication lowers the risk and severity of fluid retention and hypersensitivity reactions with docetaxel. It does not prevent hair loss.
qp54d321f2: Which symptom should a patient taking tamoxifen report?
Abnormal vaginal bleeding or one-sided leg swelling
Tamoxifen increases the risk of uterine cancer and blood clots. Hot flashes are common and expected.
qp365c353e: Which adverse effect should a patient taking capecitabine report?
Redness, swelling, or pain on the palms and soles
Capecitabine commonly causes hand-foot syndrome, which can limit therapy if not addressed early. Diarrhea is another important effect to report.
qp4302c25a: Which finding is a key concern with ifosfamide?
Ifosfamide can cause hemorrhagic cystitis, which mesna and hydration help prevent. Neurotoxicity such as confusion is another concern.
qp7be2234b: Which symptoms should a patient receiving nivolumab report promptly?
Immune checkpoint inhibitors can cause immune-related inflammation of the colon, lungs, skin, and other organs. These effects can become serious if not treated early.
qp3513ced6: Which adverse effect of irinotecan needs prompt reporting?
Irinotecan causes early and late diarrhea that can lead to dehydration and electrolyte loss. Early cholinergic diarrhea may be treated with atropine.
qp83a3ab0e: Which teaching is appropriate for a patient receiving oxaliplatin?
Avoid cold drinks and cold objects for several days after
Use ice chips during the infusion
Drink only cold fluids that day
Apply ice packs to the hands
Oxaliplatin causes cold-triggered peripheral neuropathy and throat discomfort. Ice chips, used with some other drugs, can worsen these symptoms.
qpdac51c26: Which symptoms should a patient receiving trastuzumab deruxtecan report right away?
New cough, shortness of breath, or fever
Trastuzumab deruxtecan has a boxed warning for interstitial lung disease, which can be fatal. New respiratory symptoms need prompt evaluation.
qp9c934ea9: Which teaching is appropriate after intravesical BCG treatment?
Sit to urinate and add bleach to the toilet before flushing
Stand to urinate and flush right away
Avoid drinking any fluids that day
Hold urine for a full day
BCG is a live organism, so urine is disinfected with bleach for several hours after treatment to protect others. Sitting reduces splashing.
qp05315dc7: Which requirement applies to a patient who can become pregnant and is starting isotretinoin?
Use two forms of birth control and complete pregnancy tests
Use one form of birth control as needed
Take a pregnancy test only once at the end
Isotretinoin causes severe birth defects, and the iPLEDGE program requires two forms of contraception and regular pregnancy testing. A single test at the end is not enough.
qp8ac5d76a: Which technique reduces systemic effects of timolol eye drops?
Press on the inner corner of the eye after instilling
Blink rapidly after instilling the drops
Tilt the head forward after instilling
Rub the eye gently after instilling
Punctal occlusion limits drainage into the nose and bloodstream, reducing beta-blocker effects such as bradycardia and bronchospasm. Rubbing the eye does not help.
qpfb7d4178: Which effect should a patient using latanoprost be taught about?
Prostaglandin analogs can increase brown pigment in the iris, which may be permanent, and can lengthen eyelashes. They do not cause eyelash loss.
qp74f14275: Which allergy is a concern before applying silver sulfadiazine to a burn?
Silver sulfadiazine is a sulfonamide and can cause reactions in sulfa-allergic patients. It can also cause transient leukopenia.
qp96e094d3: Which teaching is appropriate when permethrin cream is prescribed for scabies?
Treat close contacts and wash bedding in hot water
Reapply every day for a month
No cleaning of bedding is needed
Scabies spreads by close contact, so household members are treated and bedding and clothing are washed hot. Itching may persist for weeks even after successful treatment.
qpc613d30a: Which teaching is correct for clobetasol topical cream?
Avoid the face, groin, and tight coverings
Apply it thickly under plastic wrap
Use it on the face for best results
Use it continuously for many months
Clobetasol is a very high-potency corticosteroid that can cause skin thinning and systemic absorption. Occlusion and thin-skin areas increase these risks.
qpc851bc4f: Which teaching is appropriate for a patient using topical tretinoin?
Use sunscreen and limit sun exposure
Use it with harsh scrubs for faster results
Tretinoin increases sensitivity to sunlight and commonly causes irritation at first. Harsh scrubs worsen irritation.
qp978533e0: Which teaching is correct for a lidocaine patch?
Avoid heat over the patch and fold used patches before disposal
Cover the patch with a heating pad
Apply it to broken or irritated skin
Leave used patches where pets can reach
Heat increases absorption, and used patches still contain drug that can harm children and pets. Patches are applied only to intact skin.
qp0eb9c321: Which teaching is appropriate for a patient using pilocarpine eye drops?
Use caution driving at night because vision may be dim
Expect wider pupils and light sensitivity
Use the drops only when eyes are dry
Pilocarpine constricts the pupils, which reduces light entry and can make night vision dim or blurred. Pupil dilation is caused by anticholinergic drops.
qpd6b4db0c: Which teaching is correct for prednisolone acetate eye drops?
Shake the bottle well before each use
Store the bottle in the freezer
Rinse the eye right after instilling
Share the bottle with family members
Prednisolone acetate is a suspension, so shaking ensures an even dose. Long-term use can raise eye pressure, so follow-up eye exams are needed.
qp501b2217: A client has used omeprazole daily for six years. Which nutrient deficiency is most associated with long-term proton pump inhibitor use?
Gastric acid and pepsin release protein-bound B12 from food. Long-term acid suppression lowers B12 absorption.
qp06c69091: A client on a proton pump inhibitor needs a calcium supplement. Which form is absorbed well without stomach acid?
Calcium carbonate needs acid to dissolve. Calcium citrate is absorbed well with or without food and acid.
qpab11ef7e: Which electrolyte problem carries an FDA warning for long-term proton pump inhibitor use?
Prolonged PPI use can cause low magnesium, which can lead to cramps, arrhythmias and secondary low calcium or potassium.
qp85dc84ba: Why can long-term acid suppression worsen iron status?
Acid helps convert ferric iron to the more absorbable ferrous form
Acid suppression increases urinary iron losses
Acid-suppressing drugs bind iron in the small intestine
Acid suppression blocks transferrin production in the liver
Nonheme iron absorption depends on an acidic stomach. Heme iron is less affected.
qpf1d40b6f: A client taking cholestyramine for high LDL cholesterol is at greatest risk of deficiency of which nutrients?
Fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E and K
Bile acid sequestrants bind bile acids, impairing fat and fat-soluble vitamin absorption. Folate can also be affected.
qp56513851: Which counseling point applies to bile acid sequestrants such as colestipol?
Other medicines are spaced apart in time because the resin can bind them
The resin works best mixed with grapefruit juice
The resin increases absorption of fat-soluble vitamins
The resin must be taken with a high-fat meal to work
Resins bind many drugs and nutrients in the gut. Other medicines are usually timed well before or after the resin.
qpa2b7a427: A client starting orlistat asks about vitamins. Which statement is accurate?
Fat-soluble vitamin absorption falls, so a multivitamin is advised at a separate time
Orlistat blocks starch digestion, so B vitamins are lost
Orlistat raises vitamin K absorption, which lowers INR
Orlistat increases vitamin D absorption from fatty foods
Orlistat inhibits lipase, so dietary fat and fat-soluble vitamins pass unabsorbed. A multivitamin is typically separated by at least 2 hours, often at bedtime.
qp09947e15: A client on furosemide for heart failure is at risk for loss of which electrolytes?
Loop diuretics block sodium reabsorption in the loop of Henle, increasing urinary loss of potassium, magnesium and calcium.
qp7db26897: How do thiazide diuretics differ from loop diuretics in calcium handling?
Thiazides lower urinary calcium loss, while loop diuretics raise it
Thiazides raise urinary calcium loss more than loop diuretics
Both classes retain calcium to the same degree
Neither class has any effect on urinary calcium
Thiazides increase calcium reabsorption and can cause mild hypercalcemia; loop diuretics increase calcium excretion.
qp7dc8fc59: Which timing best supports levothyroxine absorption?
On an empty stomach with water, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast
With breakfast and a glass of milk to ease stomach upset
With a high-fiber cereal to keep absorption steady
At any time, since food does not change absorption
Food, coffee, fiber, soy, calcium and iron reduce levothyroxine absorption. Consistent empty-stomach timing keeps levels stable.
qp9480b9df: A client on levothyroxine is prescribed ferrous sulfate. What is the best counseling?
Separate the two by about 4 hours, since iron lowers levothyroxine absorption
Combine them in one dose to improve absorption of both
Iron raises levothyroxine levels, so watch for tremor
No interaction exists between these two products
Iron and calcium bind levothyroxine in the gut. Separating the doses by about 4 hours limits the interaction.
qp08c3ca20: Which description matches how alendronate is taken?
First thing in the morning with plain water, staying upright at least 30 minutes before eating
With breakfast and coffee to reduce esophageal irritation
At bedtime with milk to increase calcium uptake
With orange juice to improve its absorption
Food, beverages other than water and minerals block alendronate absorption. Staying upright reduces esophageal injury.
qp7d9d6835: A client taking phenelzine asks which cheese is the greatest concern. Which is correct?
Aged cheeses are high in tyramine. Fresh, unaged cheeses are low in tyramine.
qp9ea33fd3: Eating aged salami while taking tranylcypromine can cause which reaction?
Hypertensive crisis from tyramine-driven norepinephrine release
Severe hypoglycemia from increased insulin release
Serotonin syndrome from excess dietary tryptophan
Hyperkalemia from reduced renal potassium excretion
MAOIs block tyramine breakdown. Tyramine then releases norepinephrine, causing severe headache and dangerous blood pressure elevation.
qp8278e663: How long are tyramine restrictions usually continued after an MAOI such as phenelzine is discontinued?
MAO enzyme activity takes about 2 weeks to recover after an irreversible MAOI ends.
qp45b377a6: Which antipsychotic pair carries the highest risk of weight gain and metabolic syndrome?
Olanzapine and clozapine cause the most weight gain, hyperglycemia and dyslipidemia among antipsychotics.
qpe90b2279: A client recently started olanzapine. Which labs should the RD expect to be monitored?
Fasting glucose or A1C and a lipid panel
Second-generation antipsychotics require metabolic monitoring: weight, waist, blood pressure, glucose and lipids.
qp3051e09b: Besides weight gain, which GI effect of clozapine matters most for diet planning?
Severe constipation from slowed gut motility
Clozapine slows GI motility and can cause serious constipation and ileus. Fiber, fluids and bowel habits are monitored.
qp3e35d8a1: A client takes prednisone each morning. When is hyperglycemia most often seen?
Only after the drug is tapered
Morning prednisone raises glucose mostly later in the day, so fasting glucose may look normal while afternoon values are high.
qp59bc9888: Which diet pattern is often advised with long-term prednisone therapy?
Moderate sodium restriction with adequate calcium and vitamin D
High sodium intake to prevent low blood pressure
Low-protein diet to protect the kidneys
Low-calcium diet to prevent kidney stones
Corticosteroids cause sodium and fluid retention and bone loss. Protein needs are maintained to limit muscle wasting.
qp651921b0: Long-term corticosteroids raise the risk of which nutrition-related problems?
Bone loss, muscle wasting and increased appetite
Glucocorticoids increase appetite, break down muscle protein, reduce calcium absorption and cause hypokalemia rather than hyperkalemia.
qp1dfb4d63: A client new to metformin reports nausea and diarrhea. Which counseling is appropriate?
GI effects often ease when it is taken with meals and over the first weeks
Taking it on an empty stomach reduces these effects
A high-fat meal with each dose prevents these effects
These effects mean the drug is not being absorbed
Metformin GI upset is common at the start and is reduced by taking it with food. Extended-release forms may also help.
qpd6da54e0: A client on chemotherapy reports a metallic taste when eating meat. Which suggestion is appropriate?
Plastic utensils and other proteins such as eggs, beans or dairy
Metal utensils and more red meat for iron
Eating only very hot foods to mask taste
Dysgeusia is common with chemotherapy. Plastic utensils, marinades, tart flavors and alternative proteins can improve intake.
qp37577a08: Which food choice is best for chemotherapy-related oral mucositis?
Soft, moist, bland foods served cool or at room temperature
Acidic, spicy, rough and hot foods irritate inflamed mucosa. Soft, moist, bland foods are easier to eat.
qp5b0d3337: A hospitalized client develops frequent watery diarrhea after a course of clindamycin. Which complication should be suspected and reported?
Antibiotics such as clindamycin, fluoroquinolones and cephalosporins disrupt gut flora and allow C. difficile overgrowth.
qpd39f472a: Why is Saccharomyces boulardii used with caution in critically ill or immunocompromised clients with central lines?
Risk of fungemia from the live yeast
It contains a large amount of lactose
Live probiotic yeast can enter the bloodstream, especially via central catheters, in vulnerable patients.
qpcf7037f2: A child on methylphenidate for ADHD is losing weight. Which strategy is appropriate?
A nutrient-dense breakfast before the morning dose and an evening snack
The largest meal at midday when the drug effect peaks
Limiting snacks so appetite returns at dinner
Stimulants suppress appetite during the day. Meals before the dose and after it wears off support growth.
qp577bb710: When megestrol is used for cachexia, which outcome is most typical?
Increased appetite, with weight gain mostly as fat and fluid
Lean muscle gain through anabolic effects
Faster gastric emptying and less bloating
Megestrol improves appetite and weight, but gains are mainly fat and fluid rather than lean mass.
qp8f201bf9: A client on megestrol reports one swollen, painful calf. What does this suggest?
A possible blood clot that needs prompt reporting
An expected effect of increased appetite
Normal fluid gain from better intake
A sign the drug is working well
Megestrol increases thromboembolism risk. Leg swelling or pain should be reported promptly.
qp90ad1e55: Dronabinol is FDA-approved for which nutrition-related use?
Anorexia with weight loss in AIDS
Dronabinol is approved for AIDS-related anorexia with weight loss and for chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.
qpc3fc7fa8: Insulin lispro begins to lower blood glucose within about how long?
Rapid-acting insulins start in about 15 minutes, peak in 1 to 2 hours and last 3 to 5 hours.
qp57651539: Because of its rapid onset, insulin aspart is usually given at what time relative to a meal?
About 5 to 10 minutes before the meal
Rapid-acting insulin is matched closely to meals. A delayed meal after a dose raises hypoglycemia risk.
qpd313f6dc: Regular insulin peaks about how long after a subcutaneous injection?
Regular insulin starts in 30 to 60 minutes, peaks in 2 to 4 hours and lasts 5 to 8 hours, so it is given about 30 minutes before meals.
qp4587eca2: A client injects NPH insulin at breakfast. When is hypoglycemia risk highest?
Afternoon, during its peak about 4 to 12 hours later
Right before breakfast the next day
Late night, about 18 to 24 hours later
NPH peaks 4 to 12 hours after injection. Missing lunch or an afternoon snack is a classic cause of lows.
qpbe5b43e2: Which describes the action of insulin glargine?
Relatively peakless basal action lasting about 24 hours
Rapid onset with a peak at about 1 hour
A sharp peak at 6 hours, lasting 12 hours
Glargine provides a steady basal level with no pronounced peak, so hypoglycemia risk is lower than with NPH.
qp8430b2d4: Insulin detemir is classified as which type?
Detemir is a long-acting basal analog with a relatively flat profile lasting up to 24 hours. The US brand was discontinued in 2024.
qpb1a32ab0: What is the primary action of metformin?
Lowers liver glucose production and improves insulin sensitivity
Stimulates insulin release from the pancreas
Blocks glucose reabsorption in the kidney
Slows starch digestion in the small intestine
Metformin is a biguanide. It does not stimulate insulin release, so it rarely causes hypoglycemia alone.
qpdb327f39: Long-term metformin use is linked to deficiency of which vitamin?
Metformin reduces B12 absorption in the ileum. Periodic B12 checks are recommended, especially with neuropathy or anemia.
qpdcf36d44: How does empagliflozin lower blood glucose?
Blocks kidney glucose reabsorption so glucose is lost in urine
Increases insulin release from beta cells
Inhibits starch digestion in the gut
SGLT2 inhibitors cause glucosuria, which also produces a modest calorie loss and weight loss.
qp996baf38: Which counseling point is important for a client on empagliflozin?
Adequate fluids, and watching for dehydration and genital yeast infections
Extra sodium to prevent high potassium
Expecting weight gain from fluid retention
Glucosuria causes osmotic diuresis and a sugary urinary environment, raising dehydration, genital infection and UTI risk.
