Night-time and early-morning falls from sedation and poor balance
Falls caused by low blood glucose
Falls caused by high heart rate
Sedative-hypnotics impair balance and alertness, especially when getting up at night to toilet.
qp00da3566: Which over-the-counter drug in an older adult is a Beers Criteria concern for confusion and falls?
First-generation antihistamines are strongly anticholinergic, causing confusion, urinary retention and falls in older adults.
qpc7ba107e: Xerostomia caused by medications most often results from blocking which receptors?
Salivary secretion is driven by parasympathetic muscarinic stimulation. Anticholinergic drugs block these receptors and reduce saliva flow.
qp27812864: An 80-year-old with overactive bladder reports a sticky mouth and difficulty chewing bread. Which of her medicines is the most likely contributor?
Oxybutynin is a bladder antispasmodic with strong anticholinergic effects; dry mouth is its most common side effect.
qp0004164a: Which antidepressant is known for strong anticholinergic effects such as dry mouth and constipation?
Tertiary-amine tricyclics like amitriptyline block muscarinic receptors strongly, causing xerostomia, constipation and confusion.
qp53d1ac3b: A patient takes an over-the-counter sleep aid nightly and complains of morning dry mouth. Which ingredient is the likely cause?
Diphenhydramine is a first-generation antihistamine with anticholinergic activity, causing dry mouth and next-day sedation.
qp4bf749fa: How does reduced saliva most directly affect the oral preparatory phase?
Poor bolus cohesion with prolonged chewing
Saliva moistens food and binds particles into a cohesive bolus. Without it, chewing is prolonged and the bolus falls apart, leaving residue.
qp3cfe7a8c: A patient with xerostomia has dry crumbly solids scattered in the oral cavity after the swallow. Which compensation is most commonly recommended?
Alternating bites of solid with sips of liquid
Chin tuck with every liquid swallow
Head rotation toward the weaker side
Liquid washes help moisten and clear dry solids when saliva is reduced. Moist, sauced foods also help.
qp3dea78a9: Pilocarpine improves dry mouth by which mechanism?
Stimulating muscarinic receptors on salivary glands
Coating the oral mucosa with a lubricant
Blocking histamine release in the mouth
Increasing fluid absorption from the gut
Pilocarpine is a cholinergic (muscarinic) agonist, a sialogogue that stimulates remaining salivary tissue.
qp4de6ed7b: Cevimeline is FDA-approved for dry mouth associated with which condition?
Cevimeline is a muscarinic agonist approved for dry mouth in Sjogren's syndrome.
qp47b202af: Which side effect is most commonly reported with pilocarpine tablets?
Because pilocarpine stimulates muscarinic receptors throughout the body, sweating is the most common side effect.
qpe3b3e8d9: Why might a saliva substitute help a patient when pilocarpine does not?
Substitutes lubricate even without working salivary tissue
Substitutes stimulate muscarinic receptors more strongly
Sialogogues need functioning glands to stimulate. Saliva substitutes simply coat and moisten the mouth, so they work after extensive gland damage.
qpe07add52: A child with cerebral palsy is prescribed a medicine to reduce drooling. Which drug is commonly used for this purpose?
Glycopyrrolate is an anticholinergic used to reduce chronic drooling; it can also thicken secretions and cause constipation.
qp4bea574a: A hospice patient has a patch placed behind the ear to dry secretions. Which drug is this most likely?
Transdermal scopolamine is an anticholinergic patch sometimes used to reduce secretions; it can cause dry mouth and confusion.
qp65a26633: Which oral health problem is a long-term consequence of chronic medication-induced xerostomia?
Saliva buffers acid and clears bacteria; chronic dryness raises the risk of caries and oral candidiasis.
qpab119615: The term anticholinergic burden refers to which concept?
The cumulative effect of several drugs with anticholinergic activity
The single strongest anticholinergic drug in a regimen
The length of time an anticholinergic stays in the body
The dose needed to treat anticholinergic toxicity
Several mildly anticholinergic medicines can add up to a large total effect, especially in older adults.
qpe50eb710: Which inhaled medicine for COPD commonly causes dry mouth?
Tiotropium is an inhaled long-acting muscarinic antagonist; dry mouth is its most common side effect.
qpfc80b6b8: Unlike most antipsychotics, which one commonly causes excessive salivation rather than dry mouth?
Clozapine frequently causes sialorrhea, especially at night, despite its anticholinergic properties.
qpf8793488: Shortly after receiving haloperidol, a patient has sustained tongue protrusion and difficulty swallowing. What is this most likely?
Acute dystonia appears within hours to days of starting a high-potency antipsychotic and can involve the tongue, jaw and larynx. It needs prompt medical attention.
qpdcf747a2: Tardive dyskinesia most commonly produces which oral-motor finding?
Involuntary lip smacking and tongue writhing
Fixed tongue deviation to one side
Flaccid lips with loss of tone
TD causes repetitive involuntary orofacial movements that can disrupt bolus control and the oral phase.
qp629a8c5a: Compared with acute dystonia, tardive dyskinesia typically appears when?
After months to years of exposure
Within hours of the first dose
Only after the drug is withdrawn
Within the first week of therapy
TD is a late complication of long-term dopamine blockade and may persist even after the drug changes.
qpc400d737: Which medication is FDA-approved to treat tardive dyskinesia?
Valbenazine and deutetrabenazine are VMAT2 inhibitors approved for TD. Anticholinergics like benztropine are not effective for TD.
qp0424f0be: Which GI medicine carries a boxed warning for tardive dyskinesia?
Metoclopramide blocks dopamine receptors and has a boxed warning for TD, with risk rising with long-term use.
qp21c3d2cd: Drug-induced parkinsonism from antipsychotics most often affects swallowing by causing which finding?
Reduced tongue movement and delayed swallow initiation
Dopamine blockade can produce bradykinesia and rigidity of oral and pharyngeal muscles, much like Parkinson's disease.
qp154f061a: A college student takes a pill at bedtime with a small sip of water and wakes with sharp pain when swallowing. Which drug is a classic cause?
Doxycycline is acidic and a classic cause of pill esophagitis, especially when taken lying down with little water.
qp8348d23c: Alendronate labeling directs patients to remain upright for 30 minutes after a dose mainly to lower which risk?
Bisphosphonates irritate the esophagus; staying upright with a full glass of water helps the pill clear quickly.
qp9ceba9fb: Solid potassium chloride tablets are a known cause of which swallowing-related injury?
Potassium chloride can injure the esophageal mucosa if it lodges in place, causing odynophagia or ulceration.
qpb8e06b6d: Which patient factor most increases the risk of pill esophagitis?
Taking pills lying down with little fluid
Taking pills with a full glass of water
Taking pills spaced through the day
Recumbent position and low fluid volume let pills stall in the esophagus. Upright posture and adequate fluid aid clearance.
qp8f14d69f: Odynophagia is painful swallowing, a hallmark of pill esophagitis; dysphagia is difficulty swallowing.
qp275eba62: A patient with dysphagia has trouble swallowing an extended-release tablet. What is the best SLP action?
Ask the pharmacist or prescriber about alternative forms
Cut the tablet into small pieces
Dissolve the tablet in hot water
Many extended-release or enteric-coated products cannot be crushed; the pharmacist can identify a safe alternative form.
qp60ad54fc: Two weeks after neck injections for cervical dystonia, a patient reports new trouble swallowing. What is the most likely explanation?
Spread of botulinum toxin to swallowing muscles
An allergic reaction to the injection
Dysphagia is a known effect of cervical botulinum toxin injection due to spread to nearby pharyngeal muscles; distant spread carries a boxed warning.
qp48aa1127: After laryngeal botulinum toxin for adductor spasmodic dysphonia, which early effects are commonly expected?
Breathy voice and mild thin-liquid aspiration
Strained voice with vocal fold spasm
Temporary breathiness and mild choking on thin liquids are common in the first weeks before voice improves.
qpe0c15de3: An SLP notices increasing tongue writhing in a long-term resident on an antipsychotic. What is the most appropriate action?
Report the movements to the prescriber or nursing
Advise the resident to skip doses
New or worsening involuntary movements should be reported so the team can assess for tardive dyskinesia.
qpc29a5ecb: Why do opioids increase aspiration risk?
They suppress cough and reduce alertness
Opioids depress the cough reflex and level of consciousness, reducing airway protection.
qp6127db75: Silent aspiration is defined as which finding?
Material entering below the vocal folds without cough
Residue in the valleculae after swallow
In silent aspiration, material passes below the true vocal folds with no outward sign such as cough or throat clearing.
qp358ebb54: A patient received lorazepam for agitation one hour before a scheduled bedside swallow evaluation and is drowsy. What is the best plan?
Reschedule when the patient is more alert
Proceed with thin liquids by straw
Test only solid foods to stay safe
Proceed and rate the patient as normal
Sedation lowers alertness and airway protection; results may not reflect true function. Testing when alert gives a valid picture.
qpcdc0806e: Which benzodiazepine is commonly used for procedural sedation and can cause transient swallowing impairment afterward?
Midazolam is a short-acting benzodiazepine used for procedures; residual sedation can briefly impair swallowing.
qp355ed93e: When documenting a swallow evaluation, why should recent sedating medicines be noted?
They may affect alertness and performance
They determine the diet texture by law
They change the scoring scale used
They replace the need for instrumental testing
Medication timing helps the team interpret results and plan re-evaluation.
qp72e9545c: Which pairing of drugs carries an FDA boxed warning for profound sedation and respiratory depression?
Combining opioids and benzodiazepines adds sedation and respiratory depression, raising aspiration and overdose risk.
qpbbc8db34: Antipsychotic use in older adults is associated with which pulmonary complication?
Sedation, EPS and reduced swallow function from antipsychotics raise aspiration pneumonia risk.
qp2c2c2af9: A patient took zolpidem late at night and is groggy at an early morning swallow evaluation. What is the concern?
Zolpidem can cause next-day impairment, especially in older adults and women; alertness affects swallow safety.
qp7e207bb2: Which antispasticity medicine commonly causes drowsiness and weakness that may affect swallowing?
Baclofen is a GABA-B agonist muscle relaxant; drowsiness and weakness can reduce swallow efficiency.
qpbf5b012a: The ideal time to schedule a swallow evaluation for a patient on scheduled sedating medicines is when?
When the patient is typically most alert
During the patient's usual nap time
Alertness supports airway protection and valid results; coordinate timing with nursing.
qpd990e5aa: Which effect of morphine most directly reduces the ability to clear aspirated material?
Opioids are antitussives; a weak cough cannot clear material from the airway.
qp229d386e: A resident's chart shows several sedating medicines. Which screening finding most suggests reduced airway protection?
Wet vocal quality without a spontaneous cough
Prompt cough with a strong throat clear
Complete oral clearance of the bolus
A wet voice suggests material at the laryngeal vestibule; absent cough suggests reduced sensation or response.
qpeeef3e2a: Which drug class is the reversal agent naloxone used for?
Naloxone reverses opioid effects; flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines in limited settings.
qpb73db025: Which statement about sedation and swallowing is most accurate?
Reduced alertness can impair both oral control and airway protection
Sedation affects only the esophageal phase
Sedation improves swallow timing by relaxing muscles
Sedation increases sensitivity of the cough reflex
Sedation slows oral control, delays swallow initiation and blunts protective responses.
qp094f74eb: When should an SLP alert the team about a patient's sedation before a meal?
When the patient cannot stay awake for oral intake
When the patient asks for a snack
When the patient finishes the meal quickly
When the patient talks during the meal
A patient too drowsy to stay alert is at high risk of aspiration; the team should be told so meal and medicine timing can be reviewed.
qpeb094df4: An older adult with new confusion takes diphenhydramine, oxybutynin and amitriptyline. What is the most likely contributing factor?
Anticholinergic drugs can cause confusion, memory problems and delirium in older adults; the Beers Criteria advise avoiding them.
qpf27d865e: Which reference lists medicines that are potentially inappropriate in older adults, including strong anticholinergics?
The American Geriatrics Society Beers Criteria flag drugs such as diphenhydramine and amitriptyline for older adults.
qp998a257d: A patient with asthma uses an inhaled corticosteroid and develops hoarseness. What is the most likely cause?
Inhaled steroid effect on the larynx
Inhaled corticosteroids can cause dysphonia through laryngeal muscle effects and candidiasis.
qp322bf1ef: Which practice is recommended after using an inhaled corticosteroid to reduce oral and laryngeal side effects?
Rinsing reduces drug deposited in the mouth and throat, lowering thrush and hoarseness risk. A spacer also helps.
qp46f58b05: A patient referred for chronic cough and throat clearing recently started a blood pressure medicine. Which drug is the most likely cause?
ACE inhibitors like lisinopril cause a dry, persistent cough in a notable minority of patients.
qpb45fc6f1: ACE inhibitor cough is thought to result from accumulation of which substance?
ACE also breaks down bradykinin; its buildup in the airway is linked to the dry cough.
qp8267d3ae: Pyridostigmine improves strength in myasthenia gravis by what mechanism?
Inhibiting acetylcholinesterase at the neuromuscular junction
Blocking dopamine receptors in the brain
By slowing acetylcholine breakdown, pyridostigmine increases neuromuscular transmission and muscle strength.
qp2147359f: A patient with myasthenia gravis has the best speech and swallowing about an hour after a pyridostigmine dose. How should therapy be scheduled?
Coordinate meals and sessions with peak medicine effect
Schedule sessions just before the next dose
Schedule only in the late evening
Schedule without regard to medicine timing
Pyridostigmine onset is about 30 to 60 minutes; aligning activities with peak effect supports best function.
qp48ff483a: Which speech pattern is typical of myasthenia gravis?
Hypernasality and weakness that worsen with prolonged speaking
Sudden voice breaks only on vowels
MG causes fatigable flaccid dysarthria; speech deteriorates with use and improves with rest.
qp46280740: Which side effect of pyridostigmine might an SLP observe during a swallow session?
Cholinergic effects include increased salivation, bronchial secretions, cramping and diarrhea.
qp50d56424: In Parkinson's disease, when are speech and swallowing usually best?
During the 'on' period after a levodopa dose
During the 'off' period before a dose
Only on waking in the morning
Motor function, including speech and swallowing, often improves when levodopa is working; sessions are often timed to 'on' periods.
qp771549b1: A patient with Parkinson's develops 'wearing off' before each dose. How might this appear in therapy?
Softer voice and slower swallow near the next dose
Improved loudness right before the next dose
Stuttering that appears only after meals
As levodopa wears off, hypophonia, reduced articulation and dysphagia can return; reporting the pattern helps the team.
qp0489b95f: Which hyperkinetic speech change can result from levodopa peak-dose dyskinesia?
Peak-dose dyskinesias are involuntary movements that can disrupt articulation and respiration for speech.
qp25d415c9: Which antiseizure medicine is known for word-finding difficulty and slowed thinking?
Topiramate commonly causes cognitive slowing and word-finding problems that can resemble mild aphasia.
qpa6f2e8d7: Donepezil is used to treat which condition?
Donepezil is a cholinesterase inhibitor that modestly improves cognition in Alzheimer's disease.
qp6c2dd572: Why are anticholinergic medicines concerning in a patient taking donepezil?
They oppose the drug's cholinergic effect
They prevent its absorption in the stomach
They have no interaction at all
Anticholinergics block acetylcholine while cholinesterase inhibitors increase it, working against each other and worsening cognition.
qpe21c4663: Compared with bupivacaine, lidocaine has which profile?
Lidocaine works within minutes and lasts about 1-2 hours plain. Bupivacaine is slower to set up but lasts several hours.
qpdbba53e0: A surgeon wants a local anesthetic that will give the longest postoperative pain relief after a hernia repair. Which drug is most likely requested?
Bupivacaine is a long-acting amide, commonly infiltrated at closure for prolonged pain relief.
qp475dedfb: Which local anesthetic carries the greatest risk of cardiotoxicity if absorbed into the bloodstream?
Bupivacaine binds cardiac sodium channels tightly and can cause hard-to-treat dysrhythmias and arrest.
qpe75eca07: Why is epinephrine added to a local anesthetic?
It constricts vessels, prolonging the block and reducing bleeding
It speeds the onset by dilating local vessels
It neutralizes the acidity of the anesthetic
It prevents allergic reactions to the anesthetic
Vasoconstriction slows absorption, so the drug stays at the site longer, toxicity risk drops and the field is drier.
qp844758a6: Local anesthetic with epinephrine has traditionally been avoided in which surgical site?
End-artery areas such as fingers, toes, nose, ears and penis were traditionally avoided because of concern for ischemia.
qpdff63380: Which statement about lidocaine with epinephrine compared with plain lidocaine is correct?
It lasts longer and reduces bleeding at the site
It acts faster and lasts a shorter time
It has no effect on bleeding at the site
It is safe to use for IV regional block
Epinephrine prolongs lidocaine's effect and narrows nearby vessels. Epinephrine-containing solutions are not used for Bier block.
qpa2122ef1: Which local anesthetic is used for an intravenous regional (Bier) block?
Plain lidocaine is the standard Bier block agent; bupivacaine is avoided because of cardiotoxicity, and epinephrine is not given IV this way.
qp5f59fcdf: A patient receiving local infiltration reports a metallic taste, ringing in the ears and numbness around the mouth. What do these signs suggest?
Circumoral numbness, metallic taste and tinnitus are early CNS signs of LAST. Report them to the surgeon and anesthesia right away.
qpfdc77fe6: Which finding represents severe local anesthetic systemic toxicity?
LAST can progress from CNS excitation to seizures and then cardiovascular collapse.
qpe401e489: What is the specific treatment that should be available when local anesthetic systemic toxicity is suspected?
Lipid emulsion therapy is the specific rescue for LAST, alongside airway support and seizure control.
qp9073504c: Why does the surgeon aspirate before injecting local anesthetic?
To avoid injecting into a blood vessel
To mix the drug with tissue fluid
To speed the onset of the block
To measure how much drug was used
Aspiration helps detect intravascular placement, which is a common cause of systemic toxicity.
qpe97a7e70: Two vials on the back table look identical except one reads 'with epinephrine.' What is the best way for the CST to prevent a mix-up?
Read the full label aloud and label each syringe including 'with epinephrine'
Use a different size syringe for each drug
Rely on the color of the solution to tell them apart
Draw both drugs into one syringe for the surgeon
Plain and epinephrine-containing solutions are both clear. The label on every container must state the drug, strength and whether epinephrine is present.
qp7fe23de8: Which local anesthetic is an ester with a very rapid onset and short duration?
Chloroprocaine is an ester broken down quickly by plasma cholinesterase, so it acts fast and wears off quickly.
qp19f84d4c: Which statement about liposomal bupivacaine (Exparel) is correct?
It provides infiltration analgesia lasting up to about 72 hours
It is mixed freely with lidocaine on the field
It is given intravenously for sedation
It works within seconds as an eye drop
Liposomal bupivacaine releases drug slowly over days. Other local anesthetics can trigger rapid release, so mixing is restricted per labeling.
qpc1b31d4b: Ropivacaine is often chosen over bupivacaine for nerve blocks because it:
Has less cardiotoxicity with a similar long duration
Has a much faster onset than lidocaine
Is an ester that rarely causes allergy
Ropivacaine is a long-acting amide with a better cardiac safety profile than bupivacaine.
qp4a8cd325: What is the most important safety rule for topical thrombin?
It must never be injected into a blood vessel
It must be mixed with sterile water only
It is applied only to bone surfaces
Topical thrombin can cause extensive clotting and death if it enters the circulation. It is for topical use only.
qpd205874d: How does topical thrombin promote hemostasis?
It constricts arterioles at the site
Thrombin acts on the patient's fibrinogen to form a fibrin clot at the bleeding surface.
qp775d698b: Thrombin-JMI is bovine-derived. What is a known risk of bovine thrombin?
Antibody formation that can cause bleeding problems
Bovine thrombin can trigger antibodies to clotting factors, leading to coagulopathy. Recombinant human thrombin (Recothrom) lowers this risk.
qpec8a167e: An absorbable gelatin sponge (Gelfoam) is often prepared by soaking it in:
Gelfoam can be used dry or moistened with saline or thrombin to enhance its hemostatic effect.
qp85b0456e: Why should excess absorbable gelatin sponge or oxidized cellulose be removed near the spinal cord or bony foramina?
Both swell and can compress nerves
Both cause hemolysis of nearby blood
These agents expand as they absorb fluid, which can compress nerves in closed spaces.
qp4ff0e8b6: Oxidized regenerated cellulose (Surgicel) should not be soaked with thrombin because:
It turns the thrombin into heparin
The low pH of oxidized cellulose deactivates thrombin, so it is applied dry.
qp413ff060: How should microfibrillar collagen (Avitene) be handled?
With dry gloves and dry instruments
Microfibrillar collagen sticks to wet gloves and instruments, so it is handled dry.
qp3fe3fa03: Which hemostatic agent should be kept out of cell-saver (blood salvage) suction?
Collagen fibers can pass through cell-saver filters and be reinfused, so it should not be suctioned into salvage systems.
qpdcc34c45: Which irrigation solution is most commonly used for wound and body cavity irrigation?
Normal saline is isotonic, so it does not damage cells or shift fluid significantly.
qpdf86d800: Why is sterile water avoided when large volumes may be absorbed into the bloodstream?
It is hypotonic and can cause hemolysis
It is hypertonic and causes dehydration
It is too acidic for tissue
Water entering the circulation moves into red cells and ruptures them. It is used for rinsing instruments, not for routine wound irrigation.
qp62724a0e: During a monopolar transurethral resection, why is normal saline not used as the irrigant?
It conducts electricity and disperses the current
It is hypotonic and causes hemolysis
It causes the scope lens to fog
Monopolar resection needs a non-conductive fluid such as glycine or sorbitol. Bipolar systems can use saline.
qpf5f30583: Which is a feature of lactated Ringer's as an irrigation solution?
It is isotonic and contains calcium and lactate
It is hypotonic like sterile water
It contains heparin to prevent clotting
It is non-conductive for monopolar resection
LR is a balanced isotonic solution often used for arthroscopy irrigation.
qpb3578a1e: In 2020, the FDA requested removal of bacitracin for injection from the market. Why?
Risk of kidney injury and anaphylaxis
It was replaced by a generic
FDA cited nephrotoxicity and anaphylaxis risk; facilities now often choose other irrigation antibiotics.
qp771a0097: Before antibiotic irrigation is prepared, which check is most important?
Antibiotics in irrigation can cause allergic reactions, so allergies are confirmed before preparation.
qp113de377: Why are irrigation solutions usually warmed before use?
Large volumes of cold irrigation can lower core temperature, so fluids are warmed to near body temperature.
qpbb6256a0: Tropicamide is used before cataract surgery because it:
Tropicamide is an anticholinergic mydriatic that also causes short-lived cycloplegia.
qpd238692a: How does phenylephrine eye drop differ from tropicamide?
It dilates the pupil without paralyzing focus
Phenylephrine is an alpha agonist that contracts the dilator muscle; it does not cause cycloplegia.
qpce837590: Which systemic effect should be watched for with phenylephrine eye drops?
Systemic absorption of phenylephrine can raise blood pressure, especially in sensitive patients.
qp0f03039b: Under the standard ophthalmic cap color code, mydriatic eye drops have which cap color?
Mydriatics and cycloplegics are red; miotics green; anti-infectives tan; steroids pink.
qp57c72e05: What is proparacaine used for in eye surgery?
Proparacaine drops numb the eye surface within seconds for a short time.
qpd1514d36: What is a concern with repeated use of topical anesthetic eye drops like tetracaine?
Repeated topical anesthetic use can delay healing and damage the corneal surface.
qp66650c24: Intraocular acetylcholine (Miochol-E) is given during cataract surgery to:
Acetylcholine is a miotic that constricts the pupil within seconds after lens placement.
qpd6fe8629: How does intraocular carbachol (Miostat) compare with intraocular acetylcholine?
Carbachol works over minutes and its effect can last about a day; acetylcholine acts in seconds and is short-lived.
qp51f323ae: Why is hyaluronidase added to local anesthetic for an eye block?
To help the anesthetic spread through tissue
Hyaluronidase breaks down hyaluronic acid in connective tissue, improving anesthetic spread.
qpeab8d9a3: Which serious interaction is associated with methylene blue?
Methylene blue inhibits MAO-A, so the FDA warns of serotonin syndrome with SSRIs, SNRIs and similar drugs.
qpe6e2921c: After methylene blue is given, which monitoring change may occur?
A falsely low pulse oximetry reading
Blue dye in the blood interferes with pulse oximeter light absorption.
qp2c536671: Isosulfan blue is used for which procedure?
Isosulfan blue travels through lymphatics to stain the first draining node. Anaphylaxis is a known risk.
qpd5b3a48c: Before indocyanine green (ICG) is used, which allergy should be confirmed?
ICG formulations contain sodium iodide, so iodide allergy is a caution.
qp5380fd45: Heparinized saline on a vascular case is used to:
Irrigate vessel lumens to prevent clotting
Heparinized saline keeps clots from forming in vessels and catheters during vascular work.
qp8aa55293: Which drug reverses heparin at the end of a vascular procedure?
Protamine binds heparin. Watch for hypotension and anaphylaxis, especially with fish allergy or prior protamine-insulin use.
qpa7ad3bbb: According to The Joint Commission, which containers on the sterile field must be labeled?
Every syringe, cup and basin containing medication
Only syringes handed to the surgeon
Only when more than one drug is present
All medications and solutions on and off the sterile field must be labeled, even if only one is present.
qp3d3044c9: When should a medication container on the sterile field be labeled?
Immediately when the drug is placed in it
At the end of the procedure
When the surgeon asks for it
Labeling at once prevents mix-ups between clear solutions.
qp45b47f9d: When receiving a medication from the circulator, what should be verified aloud?
Drug name, strength and expiration date
Both the circulator and scrub confirm name, strength and expiration before the drug is transferred.
qp1667ce27: How should a medication in a vial be transferred to the sterile field?
Using a sterile transfer device or sterile syringe
By the circulator reaching over the field
By pouring after removing the stopper with fingers
By the scrub touching the outside of the vial
Sterile technique is maintained during transfer; the circulator never reaches over the sterile field.
qpcba0b16d: The CST finds an unlabeled cup of clear fluid on the back table. What is the correct action?
Discard it and obtain a fresh, labeled supply
Assume it is saline and use it
An unlabeled solution can never be identified with certainty, so it is discarded.
qp781a99a6: When handing a syringe of local anesthetic to the surgeon, the CST should:
State the drug name and strength aloud
Pass it silently to avoid distraction
State only the volume in the syringe
Stating the drug and strength allows the surgeon to confirm before injecting.
qp2e3f3cb9: Why are original medication vials kept in the room until the case ends?
To allow verification if a question arises
To return them to pharmacy for credit
Original containers allow the team to recheck drug, strength and amount used.
qp8ab75902: During a scrub relief, what should happen with medications on the field?
Both scrub persons review each labeled medication together
The relief assumes labels are correct
A hand-off review prevents errors when staff change.
qpa10d8dad: Cefazolin for surgical prophylaxis should be infused within what time before incision?
Most prophylactic antibiotics, including cefazolin, should start within 60 minutes before incision so tissue levels are adequate.
qpe0448637: Why may vancomycin prophylaxis begin up to 120 minutes before incision?
It must infuse slowly to avoid a reaction
It needs time to be absorbed orally
It only works after a long delay
It must be given after induction drugs
Vancomycin is infused slowly to prevent infusion-related flushing, so it starts earlier.
qpb8cf70c1: A patient receiving vancomycin develops flushing and itching of the face and upper body. What is the likely cause?
Vancomycin infusion reaction (formerly red man syndrome) is related to infusion rate. Report it to anesthesia.
qp8594f5e5: Cefazolin is the most common surgical prophylactic antibiotic mainly because it:
Covers common skin organisms like Staphylococcus aureus
Cefazolin targets typical skin flora that cause surgical site infections.
qpd414230a: For a patient with a severe beta-lactam allergy, which antibiotic is a common prophylaxis alternative?
Clindamycin or vancomycin are common alternatives when beta-lactams must be avoided.
qp115cab90: During a long procedure, what may happen with cefazolin prophylaxis?
It is redosed at set intervals or after major blood loss
It is replaced with sterile water irrigation
It is given only after closure
It is mixed into the local anesthetic
Cefazolin is redosed for prolonged cases or significant blood loss to keep tissue levels adequate.
qpcf26b0b6: When is the patient's allergy status confirmed with the whole team before incision?
Allergies are reviewed in the time-out because they affect antibiotics, dyes and irrigation choices.
qpce432bd5: Propofol has a milky white appearance because it is formulated as which of the following?
A lipid emulsion containing soybean oil and egg lecithin
A crystalline suspension in normal saline
A colloid dissolved in hydroxyethyl starch
Propofol is an oil-in-water emulsion. Its lipid base explains the white color and the strict handling rules.
qpb444749d: Why does propofol labeling require strict aseptic technique and prompt discard of opened vials and syringes?
Its lipid emulsion supports bacterial growth
It breaks down into a toxic compound in light
It loses all potency within minutes of opening
It crystallizes when exposed to room air
Contaminated propofol has caused outbreaks of sepsis. Labeling limits how long a drawn syringe or spiked vial may be used.
qp81e9a244: Which induction agent is chosen for its hemodynamic stability but can briefly suppress adrenal cortisol production?
Etomidate inhibits 11-beta-hydroxylase in the adrenal cortex. It causes little change in blood pressure or heart rate.
qp9f6db1ff: Which feature best distinguishes ketamine from other IV induction agents?
It keeps spontaneous breathing and airway reflexes largely intact
It reliably lowers heart rate and blood pressure
It never causes dreams or emergence reactions
It markedly dries oral and airway secretions
Ketamine is a dissociative NMDA antagonist. It tends to raise heart rate and BP and increases secretions.
qp12adfb02: A hypotensive trauma patient with a history of severe asthma needs induction. Which agent's properties fit best?
Ketamine, because it bronchodilates and supports blood pressure
Propofol, because it bronchodilates and raises blood pressure
Methohexital, because it relaxes airway smooth muscle best
Midazolam, because it supports blood pressure and the airway
Ketamine's sympathomimetic effect supports blood pressure, and it relaxes bronchial smooth muscle.
qpba69854d: Why is methohexital commonly used for anesthesia during electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)?
It does not strongly raise the seizure threshold, so the therapeutic seizure is preserved
It is a benzodiazepine that reliably prevents all seizure activity
It provides strong analgesia through NMDA receptor blockade
It can be fully reversed with flumazenil after the treatment
Methohexital is a short-acting barbiturate with less anticonvulsant effect than many agents. It can cause myoclonus and hiccups.
qpb07a162c: Which volatile anesthetic is preferred for inhalational (mask) induction, especially in children?
Sevoflurane, because it is nonpungent and well tolerated
Desflurane, because it has the fastest onset of all
Isoflurane, because it is the least irritating agent
Halothane, because it is the current US standard
Sevoflurane does not irritate the airway. Desflurane and isoflurane are pungent and can cause coughing and laryngospasm.
qp6da17fea: Why does desflurane require a special heated, pressurized vaporizer?
Its boiling point is close to room temperature
It is rapidly broken down by light
It is too viscous to vaporize normally
Desflurane's high vapor pressure would give unpredictable output in a standard variable-bypass vaporizer, so it is heated and pressurized.
qp9e3de5ef: A provider uses desflurane to speed wake-up after a long case. Which property explains its rapid emergence?
Less soluble agents equilibrate and wash out quickly. Desflurane has the lowest blood-gas solubility of the modern volatiles.
qp7feef526: Which inhaled anesthetic is the most potent, meaning it has the lowest minimum alveolar concentration (MAC)?
MAC is the alveolar concentration that prevents movement to incision in half of patients. Potency order is isoflurane, sevoflurane, desflurane, then nitrous oxide.
qpa96ecfad: Why is nitrous oxide usually avoided in patients with a pneumothorax or bowel obstruction?
It enters closed air spaces faster than nitrogen leaves, expanding them
It is a potent trigger of malignant hyperthermia
It causes severe bronchospasm in damaged lungs
It stimulates bowel motility and raises gut pressure
Nitrous oxide is far more soluble in blood than nitrogen. Air-filled cavities such as the middle ear and eye gas bubbles are also affected.
qpd9b060cd: Why does the pressure gauge on a nitrous oxide E-cylinder poorly reflect how much remains?
It is stored as a liquid, so pressure stays steady until the liquid is nearly gone
The gauge reads only the oxygen mixed into the cylinder
The cylinder is filled with helium to keep pressure constant
Its pressure rises steadily as the cylinder is emptied
Liquid nitrous oxide keeps the gas above it at constant pressure. Weighing the cylinder is the reliable way to estimate contents.
qp9755c6aa: What causes diffusion hypoxia at the end of an anesthetic that used nitrous oxide?
Nitrous oxide leaving the blood floods the alveoli and dilutes oxygen
Residual opioids depress the brain's response to carbon dioxide
Carbon monoxide from dry absorbent binds hemoglobin
Leftover blockers weaken the diaphragm at extubation
Large volumes of nitrous oxide move from blood into the lungs once it is turned off. High-flow oxygen for several minutes prevents it.
qpacf519d6: Which statement about remifentanil is correct?
Blood and tissue esterases break it down, so effects fade within minutes after infusion ends
The liver clears it slowly, so effects last hours after infusion ends
The kidneys clear it, so effects are prolonged in renal failure
It accumulates in fat, so long infusions cause delayed waking
Remifentanil's context-sensitive half-time stays short regardless of infusion length. A plan for postoperative pain is needed.
qpcf1c6358: After a remifentanil infusion ends, why is clearing the IV line important?
Drug left in the line can later be flushed in, causing apnea or rigidity
The drug crystallizes in tubing and blocks the IV catheter
Remifentanil reacts with saline to form a toxic product
Residual drug in tubing loses potency and contaminates fluid
Even a small inadvertent bolus of remifentanil can cause sudden apnea and chest wall rigidity in the PACU.
qp93213b34: A rapid, large IV bolus of fentanyl can cause which effect that makes mask ventilation difficult?
Opioid-induced muscle rigidity (wooden chest) is treated by the provider, often with a neuromuscular blocker.
qpabf0ab26: Brief, visible muscle twitching right after succinylcholine is given is caused by what?
Depolarization of the motor end plate before paralysis
Histamine release from mast cells in the skin
An early sign of local anesthetic toxicity
Succinylcholine acts like acetylcholine at the nicotinic receptor, producing fasciculations and then a depolarizing block.
qp368787fe: A patient remains paralyzed for hours after a single intubating dose of succinylcholine. What is the most likely cause?
Reduced or atypical plasma cholinesterase activity
Rapid liver metabolism to an active metabolite
Accidental sugammadex given before the case
Succinylcholine is broken down by plasma (pseudo)cholinesterase. Inherited or acquired deficiency prolongs the block; supportive ventilation and sedation follow.
qp0b4e4757: Which patient is at greatest risk of life-threatening hyperkalemia from succinylcholine?
An adult with extensive burns sustained several days ago
A healthy adult having an outpatient appendectomy
An adult with well-controlled essential hypertension
A teenager with mild, intermittent asthma
Burns, crush injury, denervation and prolonged immobility upregulate receptors, so potassium release surges after the first day or two.
qpa7079b25: What does the boxed warning for succinylcholine describe?
Hyperkalemic cardiac arrest in children with undiagnosed muscle disease
Delayed liver failure after repeated use in adults
Severe hypoglycemia in children younger than two
Permanent hearing loss after rapid IV injection
Children with undiagnosed myopathies such as Duchenne muscular dystrophy can develop rhabdomyolysis and hyperkalemic arrest.
qp967c0314: How is succinylcholine normally stored on anesthesia workstations?
Refrigerated, with a limited beyond-use period once kept at room temperature
Frozen, then thawed in warm water before use
At room temperature, protected only from light
In a warming cabinet to prevent crystallization
Labeling allows a limited time at room temperature. Carts should show the date it left the refrigerator.
qp18619091: When succinylcholine is contraindicated, which nondepolarizing blocker is usually chosen for rapid sequence intubation?
Rocuronium has the fastest onset of the nondepolarizers at intubating doses, and sugammadex can reverse it.
qp898d91de: Which neuromuscular blocker is supplied as a powder that must be reconstituted before use?
Vecuronium is a lyophilized powder; the tech should know it takes extra preparation time in an emergency.
qpe9fb51b1: Why is cisatracurium often selected for patients with kidney and liver failure?
It undergoes Hofmann elimination, which does not depend on organ function
It is cleared entirely unchanged by the kidneys
It is fully reversed by sugammadex in seconds
It is metabolized only by plasma cholinesterase
Hofmann elimination is a spontaneous breakdown that depends on temperature and pH. Cisatracurium also releases little histamine.
qp1f62d158: A patient given pancuronium develops a fast heart rate. Which property explains this?
Pancuronium is a long-acting aminosteroid with vagolytic effects. It is cleared largely by the kidneys.
qpb0d2b22a: It encapsulates rocuronium in plasma, drawing it away from the neuromuscular junction
It inhibits acetylcholinesterase so more acetylcholine reaches receptors
It blocks muscarinic receptors to prevent bradycardia
It speeds up liver metabolism of rocuronium
Sugammadex is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin. It works even in deep block and needs no paired anticholinergic.
qp44371f6a: Sugammadex would be expected to reverse a block produced by which agent?
Sugammadex binds aminosteroid blockers, mainly rocuronium and vecuronium. It has no effect on benzylisoquinolines or succinylcholine.
qp4ed8296e: What should patients taking hormonal contraceptives be told after receiving sugammadex?
Contraceptive effect may be reduced, so a backup method is advised for 7 days
Their contraceptive will become stronger for the next month
Sugammadex has no known effect on hormonal contraception
Their contraceptive effect will be reduced for one day only
Sugammadex can bind progestogen, lowering exposure similar to a missed pill. Labeling advises backup contraception for 7 days.
qp058a2b8e: Why is glycopyrrolate given along with neostigmine for reversal?
To block muscarinic effects such as bradycardia and secretions
To speed the onset of neostigmine at the muscle
To encapsulate residual rocuronium in plasma
Neostigmine raises acetylcholine at both nicotinic and muscarinic sites. Glycopyrrolate's onset roughly matches neostigmine's.
qpa9445133: The train-of-four shows zero twitches near the end of surgery. Why is neostigmine unlikely to work at this point?
It can only enhance recovery that has already begun and has a ceiling effect
It is inactivated by the volatile anesthetic still in use
It reverses only depolarizing blockers like succinylcholine
It takes several hours to reach peak effect
Once acetylcholinesterase is fully inhibited, more neostigmine adds nothing. Some twitches should be present before it is used.
qpe8fd24a1: Which train-of-four ratio is generally considered adequate neuromuscular recovery before extubation?
Visual and tactile assessment cannot reliably detect fade above about 0.4, so quantitative monitors are preferred.
qp2d228dff: What does train-of-four monitoring typically show during a phase I succinylcholine block?
All four twitches reduced equally, without fade
Progressive fade from the first to the fourth twitch
Four normal twitches with absent tetanus
Fade is the hallmark of nondepolarizing (and phase II) block. Phase I depolarizing block reduces twitches evenly.
qp7dbc3a8f: Where are nerve stimulator electrodes most commonly placed for train-of-four monitoring?
Over the ulnar nerve at the wrist, watching thumb adduction
Over the median nerve, watching wrist flexion
Over the femoral nerve, watching knee extension
Over the radial nerve, watching finger extension
The adductor pollicis is the standard site. Facial sites recover sooner and may overestimate recovery.
qp97e31341: Which group of drugs can trigger malignant hyperthermia?
Sevoflurane, isoflurane, desflurane and succinylcholine are triggers. The other listed agents are considered safe.
qp9d793f1b: Which inhaled agent is considered safe for a patient who is susceptible to malignant hyperthermia?
All potent volatile agents are triggers. Nitrous oxide, propofol, opioids and nondepolarizers are not.
qp2516a131: Which is often the earliest sign of malignant hyperthermia under general anesthesia?
Unexplained rising end-tidal CO2 despite increased ventilation
Cola-colored urine in the Foley bag
Low serum potassium on the first gas
Hypermetabolism produces CO2 quickly. Hyperthermia and myoglobinuria usually come later.
qpc1846c4e: Which statement about body temperature in malignant hyperthermia is correct?
Temperature often rises after earlier signs such as rising EtCO2 and tachycardia
Fever is always the first sign and is required for diagnosis
Temperature typically falls as the crisis begins
Temperature changes are not seen in malignant hyperthermia
Waiting for fever delays recognition. Hyperthermia can then climb very quickly.
qpc30cf677: After succinylcholine, a child's jaw becomes rigid and the mouth cannot be opened. Why is this finding important?
Masseter muscle rigidity can be an early warning of malignant hyperthermia
It confirms the block is complete and intubation is ideal
It indicates local anesthetic toxicity from the IV
It is a normal effect that needs no further attention
Masseter spasm should be reported. The team watches closely for other MH signs and checks CK and urine myoglobin.
qpb840883b: How does dantrolene treat malignant hyperthermia?
It reduces calcium release from the muscle's sarcoplasmic reticulum
It blocks acetylcholine receptors at the end plate
It lowers the hypothalamic temperature set point
It binds and removes volatile anesthetic from blood
Dantrolene acts at the ryanodine receptor to stop the runaway muscle hypermetabolism.
qpdf818b29: Which diluent is used to reconstitute dantrolene?
Sterile water for injection without a bacteriostatic agent
Saline and dextrose can cause precipitation. Labeling specifies sterile water without preservatives.
qp59e58ce3: What is a practical advantage of Ryanodex compared with older dantrolene products (Dantrium, Revonto)?
It needs far less diluent and fewer vials, so it is ready faster
It is given orally, so no IV access is needed
It is a premixed bag that needs no preparation
It also reverses residual neuromuscular blockade
Older forms need many vials, each mixed with a large volume of water and shaken. Ryanodex is a concentrated suspension.
qp0921e8c5: Which drug class should not be combined with dantrolene during an MH crisis because of hyperkalemia and cardiovascular collapse?
Calcium channel blockers such as verapamil
Arrhythmias in MH are treated with standard drugs other than calcium channel blockers. Insulin with dextrose is used for hyperkalemia.
qp3a2c36f9: What is the purpose of activated charcoal filters on the anesthesia circuit in an MH event?
They rapidly lower volatile anesthetic in inspired gas
They absorb carbon dioxide in place of soda lime
They warm and humidify inspired oxygen
They filter bacteria from the expiratory limb
Filters on both limbs of the circuit remove residual vapor quickly, without waiting to swap the machine.
qp6e54c550: Preparing an anesthesia machine for a known MH-susceptible patient includes which step?
Removing or securing vaporizers, flushing per the maker, and adding charcoal filters
Filling every vaporizer to the top before the case
Keeping the old circuit to save setup time
Switching to a lower oxygen flow during the flush
A fresh circuit and CO2 absorbent are also used. Follow the machine manufacturer's MH preparation guidance.
qp6d78c3ae: Which cooling measures are used during a malignant hyperthermia crisis?
Cold IV saline and ice packs to the groin, axillae and neck
Fans alone with no other cooling
Active cooling continues until temperature approaches normal, to avoid overshooting into hypothermia.
qp2d1727e4: Which lab pattern is expected during a malignant hyperthermia crisis?
Mixed acidosis, high potassium, rising CK and myoglobin
Alkalosis, low potassium, normal CK and myoglobin
Normal blood gases, low glucose, low calcium
Isolated low sodium with a normal CK
Muscle breakdown releases potassium, CK and myoglobin. Both respiratory and metabolic acidosis develop.
qp73cf893b: After an MH episode is controlled, why is the patient monitored in the ICU for at least 24 hours?
Symptoms can recur (recrudescence) after initial control
Dantrolene causes delayed seizures in all patients
The patient cannot breathe without a ventilator
Cooling must continue for the full day
Recrudescence occurs in a meaningful share of cases, so monitoring and dantrolene continue under the team's direction.
qpf10138c5: During an MH crisis, which resource provides 24-hour expert consultation by phone?
MHAUS (Malignant Hyperthermia Association of the United States) runs the hotline and the North American MH Registry.
qpa3c7b548: Which tasks typically fall to the anesthesia technologist during an MH crisis?
Bringing the MH cart, mixing dantrolene, gathering ice and cold fluids
Choosing the dantrolene dose and pushing it
Deciding when to end the surgical procedure
Interpreting the arterial blood gas for the team
Techs also help change the circuit, place charcoal filters, set up lines and run labs, then restock the cart.
qp7a94c279: Which local anesthetic is the most cardiotoxic, with cardiac arrest that is notably hard to resuscitate?
Bupivacaine binds cardiac sodium channels tightly. Ropivacaine was developed partly to lower that risk.
qpfca06ec4: Chloroprocaine has a very short duration because it is metabolized by what?
Plasma cholinesterase, since it is an ester
The liver, since it is an amide
Ester local anesthetics are rapidly hydrolyzed in plasma. Amides have two i's in their names and rely on the liver.
qp0551cc22: A patient receiving a nerve block reports a metallic taste, ringing in the ears and numbness around the mouth. What do these suggest?
An expected sign that the block is working
A vasovagal reaction to needle placement
An allergic reaction to the skin prep
CNS symptoms often come first and can progress to seizures and cardiac collapse. Report them right away.
qp80a874a5: Which specific treatment for LAST should be in the LAST kit wherever nerve blocks are performed?
Lipid emulsion is thought to draw local anesthetic away from heart and brain and supports cardiac function.
qp50f44eba: How does ASRA guidance modify ACLS for cardiac arrest from LAST?
Smaller epinephrine doses; avoid vasopressin, beta blockers and local anesthetics
Higher epinephrine doses and early amiodarone with lidocaine
Vasopressin first, then calcium channel blockers
Standard ACLS with lidocaine for every rhythm
Lipid emulsion is given alongside high-quality CPR. Recovery may take a long time, so resuscitation is prolonged.
qped1a51cd: Why is epinephrine sometimes added to a local anesthetic for a nerve block?
To prolong the block and signal intravascular injection by raising heart rate
To lower blood pressure during the block
To reverse sedation after the block
To speed liver metabolism of the anesthetic
Vasoconstriction slows absorption. A sudden rise in heart rate during injection suggests the needle is in a vessel.
qp5d3420aa: Why does liposomal bupivacaine (Exparel) labeling warn about giving lidocaine at the same site around the same time?
Lidocaine can cause immediate release of bupivacaine from the liposomes
Lidocaine permanently inactivates the liposomal bupivacaine
Lidocaine and bupivacaine form a solid precipitate
Lidocaine shortens the block to only a few minutes
Labeling advises waiting at least 20 minutes after lidocaine before liposomal bupivacaine is given locally.
qp6d06b7d3: A patient becomes cyanotic with low pulse oximetry readings after a dental block with prilocaine. What complication should be suspected?
Prilocaine and benzocaine can oxidize hemoglobin. Methylene blue is the usual treatment.
qp0d8aae5b: An anesthetized patient has low blood pressure with a heart rate of 110. Which vasopressor fits this picture best?
Phenylephrine, a pure alpha-1 agonist that may slow the heart rate
Ephedrine, which raises both heart rate and blood pressure
Atropine, which mainly increases heart rate
Epinephrine, which strongly increases heart rate
Phenylephrine constricts vessels and can cause reflex bradycardia, which is helpful when the heart rate is high.
qpc4848723: Which vasopressor is typically chosen for hypotension with a slow heart rate, and shows tachyphylaxis with repeat doses?
Ephedrine works directly and by releasing norepinephrine, so repeated doses become less effective.
qp0830ff5a: How does atropine differ from glycopyrrolate?
Atropine crosses into the brain and can cause confusion; glycopyrrolate does not
Atropine slows the heart; glycopyrrolate speeds it up
Atropine is a cholinesterase inhibitor; glycopyrrolate is not
Atropine has no effect on secretions; glycopyrrolate does
Both are anticholinergics. Atropine is a tertiary amine; glycopyrrolate is quaternary and stays outside the CNS.
qp94124d8e: Epinephrine is stocked in more than one concentration. Which cart practice best prevents mix-ups?
Store each concentration in its own labeled spot and verify the label before handing it off
Store all concentrations together so they are easy to find
Remove the labels so the vials are not confused
Mix concentrations in one bin sorted by expiration date
Concentration errors with epinephrine are a known cause of serious harm. Separation and label checks are key safeguards.
qpf7e2adae: On ASTM color-coded anesthesia syringe labels, which color identifies neuromuscular blockers?
Induction agents are yellow, opioids blue, vasopressors violet, local anesthetics gray and anticholinergics green.
qpe8907e6b: A technologist moves refrigerated rocuronium into a room-temperature cart drawer. What should be done?
Label it with the date removed and the new beyond-use date
Nothing, since refrigeration has no effect on its shelf life
Return it to the refrigerator every night after cases
Discard it at once because it cannot be kept at room temperature
Refrigerated blockers have a shorter shelf life at room temperature, so dating is required.
qpb0eb9fa7: When restocking the cart, where should newly delivered drugs with later expiration dates be placed?
Behind existing stock so the earliest-expiring items are used first
In front of existing stock so they are used first
In a separate bin away from the drug's usual slot
Mixed randomly with older stock in the same bin
First-expiring, first-out rotation keeps expired drugs off the cart.
qpa6994599: What is the purpose of a numbered breakaway seal on an emergency or MH cart?
To show whether the cart has been opened since its last check
To keep controlled substances counted automatically
To prevent anyone from opening it during a code
To track the cart's location in the department
The seal number is recorded on the check log. A broken or changed seal means the cart needs a full check and restock.
qp2b1d0886: According to Joint Commission standards, which syringes on the anesthesia workstation must be labeled?
Any syringe of medication not given right after it is drawn up
Only syringes prepared by a pharmacist
Only syringes holding more than one drug
Labels include the drug name, strength and expiration. Unlabeled syringes are a common cause of wrong-drug errors.
qpa6dfe9e8: Why is epinephrine added to dental local anesthetic cartridges?
To slow systemic absorption and lengthen duration
To speed the onset of the nerve block
To buffer the acidic anesthetic solution
To prevent allergic reactions to the anesthetic
Vasoconstriction keeps anesthetic at the site longer, prolonging the block, lowering blood levels and toxicity risk, and improving hemostasis.
qp87fb8d9f: Which amide local anesthetic is partly metabolized in plasma because it contains an ester side chain?
Articaine's ester group is hydrolyzed by plasma esterases, giving it a short half-life even though it is classed as an amide.
qp360b4125: Prilocaine's metabolite o-toluidine can cause which adverse effect?
o-Toluidine oxidizes hemoglobin to methemoglobin, which cannot carry oxygen.
qpeb550661: A child develops gray-blue skin after heavy use of a topical anesthetic gel; pulse oximetry stays low despite oxygen. Which agent is most likely?
Benzocaine is a well-known cause of methemoglobinemia; FDA warns against its use for teething in children under 2.
qp314d4a25: Which finding is most characteristic of methemoglobinemia?
Cyanosis that does not improve with supplemental oxygen
Bright red flushing of the face and neck
Hives and wheezing soon after injection
Methemoglobin cannot carry oxygen, so cyanosis persists and blood may look chocolate-brown. Methylene blue is the treatment.
qpc97f20aa: A patient taking propranolol receives epinephrine-containing anesthetic. What reaction is the clinician watching for?
Prolonged bleeding at the injection site
Nonselective beta blockade leaves epinephrine's alpha effects unopposed, raising BP; the baroreceptor reflex slows the heart.
qp25000a2a: Compared with propranolol, why is metoprolol less likely to interact with dental epinephrine?
It is cardioselective, leaving beta-2 vasodilation intact
It is a calcium channel blocker, not a beta blocker
It speeds the hepatic breakdown of epinephrine
It blocks alpha receptors as well as beta receptors
Metoprolol mainly blocks beta-1 receptors, so beta-2 mediated vasodilation still offsets epinephrine's alpha effect.
qpf8ee61e1: Why are vasoconstrictors used cautiously in patients taking amitriptyline?
It blocks norepinephrine reuptake, exaggerating the pressor response
It inhibits liver metabolism of amide anesthetics
It lowers the seizure threshold only with esters
Tricyclics enhance adrenergic effects; levonordefrin is avoided and epinephrine is limited.
qp44d46ee3: Which local anesthetic is chosen for long procedures and postoperative pain control because of its long duration?
Bupivacaine is a long-acting amide; patients should be warned about prolonged numbness and lip biting.
qp3bf01cc3: When a vasoconstrictor should be avoided, which anesthetic works well plain because it causes only mild vasodilation?
Mepivacaine's minimal vasodilation gives useful duration without epinephrine.
qpc62afe73: Which statement about lidocaine is correct?
It is an amide metabolized mainly by the liver
It is an ester metabolized by plasma cholinesterase
It is metabolized to PABA in the plasma
It is excreted unchanged without metabolism
Lidocaine is the prototype amide; severe liver disease slows its clearance.
qp8484c4df: Which topical anesthetic is an ester and is metabolized by plasma pseudocholinesterase?
Tetracaine and benzocaine are esters; esters produce PABA, a source of allergy.
qp46c62a31: What are typically the earliest signs of local anesthetic overdose?
Circumoral numbness, tinnitus and slurred speech
CNS excitation comes first (numbness, metallic taste, ringing ears, talkativeness, twitching) before seizures and depression.
qpc5eac7a6: Minutes after an injection, a patient reports a pounding heart, tremor and anxiety that fade quickly. The most likely cause is:
A transient reaction to the epinephrine
An allergic reaction to the amide
Local anesthetic toxicity to the heart
Brief tachycardia, palpitations and tremor are typical of absorbed epinephrine and resolve as it is metabolized.
qpb845d0b7: Which practice best reduces the risk of local anesthetic toxicity?
Using a longer needle for every block
Aspiration helps avoid intravascular injection, and slow injection limits peak blood levels.
qp653bd121: Which complication has been reported more often with articaine used for inferior alveolar nerve blocks?
Prolonged paresthesia of the lip or tongue
Higher-concentration agents such as articaine have been linked to more paresthesia reports after mandibular blocks.
qpe59b4cf5: A young adult with epilepsy has firm, enlarged interdental papillae. Which medicine is most likely responsible?
Phenytoin is the classic cause of drug-induced gingival overgrowth.
qp7d68d2bf: A kidney transplant recipient has gingival enlargement. Which immunosuppressant is most associated with this?
Cyclosporine causes gingival overgrowth, which can be worse when combined with a calcium channel blocker.
qpd9a92cfe: Which antihypertensive class is linked to gingival overgrowth, with nifedipine the most cited example?
Nifedipine, amlodipine, diltiazem and verapamil can all cause gingival enlargement.
qpcaeecae2: Which factor most reduces the severity of drug-induced gingival overgrowth?
Plaque-induced inflammation worsens overgrowth; frequent recall and good home care help.
qp7b34d1bb: A patient taking oxybutynin for overactive bladder is most at risk for which oral problem?
Anticholinergic drugs reduce saliva, raising the risk of root and cervical caries and candidiasis.
qp66fca393: Why does diphenhydramine commonly cause dry mouth?
First-generation antihistamines block muscarinic receptors in salivary glands.
qp48de2698: Pilocarpine relieves dry mouth by which mechanism?
Stimulating muscarinic receptors in salivary glands
Blocking histamine receptors in the mucosa
Replacing saliva with a lubricating gel
Pilocarpine and cevimeline are cholinergic agonists; sweating and flushing are common effects.
qp00cf4567: Cevimeline is used cautiously in patients with which condition?
As a muscarinic agonist it can increase bronchial secretions and constriction; narrow-angle glaucoma is another caution.
qpd73fb8cd: Which preventive measure is most important for a patient with medication-induced xerostomia?
Daily fluoride use and frequent recall
Loss of saliva removes buffering and remineralization; fluoride, xylitol and saliva substitutes help.
qp8066fe3f: A patient taking alendronate for osteoporosis needs an extraction. Which complication is the concern?
Bisphosphonates reduce bone turnover; extractions are the most common trigger for MRONJ, though risk is low with oral osteoporosis therapy.
qp33892230: Which patient has the highest MRONJ risk?
A cancer patient receiving IV zoledronic acid
An adult taking oral alendronate briefly
A patient taking calcium and vitamin D
IV antiresorptive therapy for bone metastases or myeloma carries far higher risk than oral osteoporosis therapy.
qpcc3b909f: How does denosumab differ from bisphosphonates?
It inhibits RANKL and does not bind to bone
It binds bone mineral for many years
It is a calcium channel blocker
Denosumab is a monoclonal antibody against RANKL; its effect on bone fades over months after the last injection.
qp94bad666: MRONJ is defined in part by exposed bone in the maxillofacial region lasting longer than:
The definition also requires current or past antiresorptive or antiangiogenic therapy and no history of jaw radiation.
qp1da560f3: An asthmatic using an inhaled corticosteroid has white plaques that wipe off. Which advice helps prevent recurrence?
Rinse the mouth and spit after each inhaler use
Swallow water before each inhaler use
Use the inhaler only at bedtime
Brush the tongue with baking soda once weekly
Pseudomembranous candidiasis is common with inhaled steroids; rinsing and a spacer reduce oral deposition.
qpebda2891: Which agent is a topical antifungal used for oral candidiasis?
Nystatin suspension or clotrimazole troches treat oral candidiasis topically; fluconazole is systemic.
qp7847d90d: Intrinsic gray-brown banding of the permanent teeth suggests exposure to which drug during tooth development?
Tetracyclines bind calcium in developing teeth, so they are avoided in pregnancy and young children.
qpfba9c211: Which lab test is used to monitor warfarin?
The INR standardizes the prothrombin time; a common therapeutic range is 2-3.
qpb8411b2d: Antagonizing vitamin K-dependent clotting factor production
Warfarin reduces synthesis of factors II, VII, IX and X.
qpce58bcf5: For a patient on warfarin scheduled for scaling and root planing, what should the clinician confirm?
A recent INR, ideally within 24 hours
A current INR in the therapeutic range lets most dental care proceed with local hemostasis.
qp4588cde2: Why is INR not used to assess bleeding risk in patients taking apixaban?
It inhibits factor Xa and INR does not reliably reflect its effect
It is an antiplatelet drug measured by bleeding time
It is monitored with hemoglobin A1c
It has no effect on clotting
DOACs need no routine monitoring; the timing of the last dose matters more.
qp502b688c: Rivaroxaban belongs to which drug class?
Rivaroxaban and apixaban are oral factor Xa inhibitors.
qp8fdc9abd: Dabigatran is an oral direct thrombin inhibitor cleared largely by the kidneys.
qp153d794c: Why does a single exposure to aspirin affect platelets for about a week?
Platelets cannot make new COX-1, so the effect lasts their lifespan of about 7-10 days.
qp55681399: A patient on aspirin and clopidogrel after a recent coronary stent needs periodontal therapy. What is the best approach?
Proceed with local hemostasis and consult the cardiologist with any concerns
Tell the patient to skip clopidogrel for a week
Postpone all dental care for one year
Interrupting dual antiplatelet therapy risks stent thrombosis; bleeding is usually managed locally.
qp93c78deb: Which antibiotic is most likely to raise the INR in a patient taking warfarin?
Metronidazole inhibits warfarin metabolism (CYP2C9); fluconazole has a similar effect.
qpa1566ccb: A warfarin patient is prescribed fluconazole for oral candidiasis. What is the concern?
Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9 and can markedly increase warfarin's effect; the prescriber should be informed.
qp7f32f4d5: Which analgesic is usually preferred for a patient taking warfarin?
NSAIDs add antiplatelet effects and GI bleeding risk; acetaminophen is generally preferred.
qp0e24819d: Why is ibuprofen a concern for a patient taking apixaban?
It adds antiplatelet and GI bleeding risk
Combining NSAIDs with anticoagulants increases bleeding risk.
qp2180b8bb: Unfractionated heparin is monitored with which test?
Heparin enhances antithrombin; the aPTT reflects its effect.
qp290d3b28: Which is a local hemostatic measure after an extraction in an anticoagulated patient?
Oxidized cellulose placed in the socket
Pressure, sutures, gelatin sponge, oxidized cellulose and tranexamic acid rinses help control bleeding.
qp8c288b4a: What is the most important first step in assessing bleeding risk before treatment?
Reviewing the full medication list, including supplements
Anticoagulants, antiplatelets, NSAIDs and supplements such as ginkgo or fish oil can all affect bleeding.
qp63cbe142: According to the AHA, which patient should receive antibiotic prophylaxis before scaling?
A patient with a prosthetic heart valve
A patient with mitral valve prolapse
A patient with a coronary artery stent
Prophylaxis is reserved for highest-risk conditions: prosthetic valves, prior endocarditis, certain CHD and transplant valvulopathy.
qp75e3ed0c: Which history alone qualifies a patient for endocarditis prophylaxis?
Prior infective endocarditis places a patient in the highest-risk group.
qpa26cba8f: Which antibiotic is first-line for AHA endocarditis prophylaxis in a patient who can take oral medicine?
Amoxicillin is first-line, given as a single dose 30-60 minutes before the procedure.
qp444d9eb5: A patient with a mild rash to penicillin (no anaphylaxis) needs prophylaxis. Which is an appropriate alternative?
Cephalexin is acceptable if there is no history of anaphylaxis, angioedema or urticaria with penicillins.
qpd005b257: A patient with penicillin anaphylaxis needs prophylaxis. Which oral option fits current AHA guidance?
Azithromycin, clarithromycin or doxycycline are options; cephalosporins are avoided after anaphylaxis.
qp1b57d2d6: What did the 2021 AHA update change about clindamycin for dental prophylaxis?
It is now required with amoxicillin
Clindamycin was removed because of higher C. difficile risk and adverse effects.
qp2e6aeb50: If prophylaxis was not taken before the appointment, when may it still be given?
Up to 2 hours after the procedure
Only the day before the visit
Up to 1 week after the visit
The dose is ideally 30-60 minutes before but may be given up to 2 hours after.
qp9f57ea5e: Which dental procedure does NOT require prophylaxis in a high-risk cardiac patient?
Radiographs, anesthetic injections through noninfected tissue and adjusting appliances do not need prophylaxis.
qpa13e4586: Under ADA guidance, what is the usual recommendation for patients with prosthetic joints before dental care?
The ADA does not generally recommend prophylaxis for joint replacement; decisions may be individualized with the surgeon.
qp87327862: A patient prescribed metronidazole for necrotizing periodontal disease should be warned about which interaction?
Flushing, nausea and vomiting can occur with alcohol during and shortly after therapy.
qp50d7249c: Per ADA guidance, antibiotics are NOT indicated for which condition?
Localized pulpal and periapical conditions are treated with definitive dental care; antibiotics are for systemic involvement.
qp1f5d3be7: How does subantimicrobial-dose doxycycline help in periodontitis?
It inhibits collagenase that breaks down connective tissue
It kills all periodontal pathogens directly
It forms fluorapatite on root surfaces
At subantimicrobial levels doxycycline acts as a host modulator, reducing tissue destruction.
qp4e53bf8f: What is the most common side effect of chlorhexidine rinse?
Chlorhexidine also alters taste and increases calculus; the stain is removable by polishing.
qpd44d6572: Why is chlorhexidine rinse used separately from toothpaste?
Sodium lauryl sulfate in toothpaste inactivates it
It turns toothpaste into a gel
Chlorhexidine is cationic and binds anionic detergents; spacing use about 30 minutes apart preserves activity.
qpe32204e1: Why is acidulated phosphate fluoride avoided on patients with porcelain or composite restorations?
It can etch the restoration surface
The low pH of APF can roughen porcelain and composite; neutral sodium fluoride is used instead.
qp2f6a5327: Which is the main way topical fluoride reduces caries?
Killing all oral bacteria on contact
Fluoride enhances remineralization, makes enamel more acid-resistant and inhibits bacterial enzymes.
qpe21a99ac: A patient taking warfarin has blood drawn to check how well the medicine is working. Which test is ordered?
Warfarin lowers vitamin K-dependent clotting factors and is followed with PT reported as INR.
qp7e52fdb0: A patient on a continuous IV heparin infusion is most commonly monitored with which test?
Unfractionated heparin is followed with aPTT or an anti-Xa assay, both drawn in a light blue citrate tube.
qp36dc85ab: Which tube is used for PT/INR and aPTT?
Coagulation tests need 3.2% sodium citrate, which binds calcium so clotting can be measured in the lab.
qpae914720: Why must a light blue citrate tube be filled to the fill line?
To keep the blood-to-citrate ratio at 9 to 1
To prevent the gel barrier from failing
So the tube can be centrifuged sooner
So the lab has enough for repeat tests
Underfilling leaves extra citrate relative to blood, which falsely prolongs clotting times; underfilled coag tubes are rejected.
qpc08b7ae0: An underfilled light blue tube is sent for aPTT. What is the likely effect?
Excess citrate binds the calcium added in the test, so clotting takes longer and the result reads falsely long.
qp75d1f794: You draw a PT using a butterfly, and the light blue tube is the first tube. What should you do?
Fill the light blue tube halfway
Draw the light blue tube last
Tap the tubing to remove air
Air in the butterfly tubing would underfill the first tube, so a discard tube clears the dead space before the citrate tube.
qpbc07a69a: A patient says he takes apixaban. What should you expect after the venipuncture?
The site may bleed longer than usual
The vein will be harder to find
The sample will clot in the tube
The patient will need a fasting draw
Apixaban is an oral factor Xa inhibitor; plan for extra pressure and check the site carefully before bandaging.
qpe895a11d: When anti-Xa monitoring is ordered for a patient on subcutaneous enoxaparin, the draw is usually timed for about when?
Peak anti-Xa activity for low-molecular-weight heparin is about 4 hours after a subcutaneous dose, so timing must be documented.
qpeb87ad98: Clopidogrel affects which part of clotting at the puncture site?
Clopidogrel is a P2Y12 antiplatelet; the platelet plug forms more slowly, so the site can ooze.
qp89c60150: An outpatient takes daily aspirin. Which practice best prevents a hematoma?
Firm pressure with the arm straight until bleeding stops
Bending the arm up over the gauze
A tight bandage right after needle removal
Rubbing the site to speed clotting
Straight-arm pressure until the site is sealed prevents a hematoma; bending the elbow traps blood under the skin.
qp755cae27: A patient received alteplase for a stroke an hour ago. Why should venipunctures be kept to a minimum?
Very high risk of bleeding at puncture sites
The drug causes blood to clot in tubes
Thrombolytics dissolve clots throughout the body, so every puncture is a bleeding risk and needs prolonged pressure.
qp317c9cc6: Dabigatran is a direct thrombin inhibitor. Which coag result may it prolong?
Dabigatran blocks thrombin, so thrombin time is very sensitive to it and aPTT is often prolonged.
qpb9f1ef64: A blood sample for aPTT on a heparin patient sits at room temperature for several hours before processing. Why is that a problem?
Platelets release a factor that neutralizes heparin
The citrate evaporates from the tube
Platelet factor 4 released over time neutralizes heparin and falsely shortens the aPTT, so these samples are processed within about 1 hour.
qpab085c4e: After a draw on a patient taking warfarin, the site keeps oozing after extended pressure. What is the best action?
Keep pressure on and notify the nurse
Apply a bandage and dismiss the patient
Have the patient hold the gauze and leave
Apply a tourniquet above the site
Never leave a bleeding site unattended; continue pressure and report it so the nurse or provider can assess.
qp510c51c9: Protamine is given to reverse which anticoagulant?
Protamine binds and neutralizes heparin; vitamin K (phytonadione) is used for warfarin reversal.
qpa494f38d: A patient with a very high INR receives phytonadione. Which test will be redrawn to see if it worked?
Vitamin K restores warfarin-affected clotting factors, which is tracked with PT/INR.
qp6c46a022: The lowest drug level, drawn just before the next dose
The highest level, drawn right after the dose
A level drawn at any random time
A level drawn after the first dose only
Troughs are drawn just before a scheduled dose, usually within about 30 minutes of it.
qpa12fdb6c: Why must the phlebotomist record the exact collection time on a drug level?
The result is interpreted against the last dose time
The lab bills by collection time
Drug levels expire after one hour
It sets the order of draw
A level means nothing without timing; the same value can be fine as a peak and toxic as a trough.
qp48af2258: A vancomycin trough is ordered with the next dose due at 1000. When is the trough usually drawn?
One hour after the infusion ends
Troughs represent the lowest level, just before the next dose begins.
qp44a2f875: A gentamicin peak is ordered after a 30-minute infusion. When is it typically drawn?
About 30 minutes after the infusion ends
Six hours after the infusion ends
Aminoglycoside peaks are drawn after distribution, usually 30 minutes after a 30-minute infusion is complete.
qp7621e93f: Why are tobramycin levels monitored closely?
High levels can harm the kidneys and hearing
Low levels cause high blood sugar
The drug changes the order of draw
Aminoglycosides are nephrotoxic and ototoxic, so peaks and troughs guide safe dosing.
qpe98ca397: When is a routine digoxin level usually drawn?
At least 6 to 8 hours after the last dose
Exactly at the time of the dose
Digoxin takes hours to distribute into tissue; an early draw reads falsely high.
qpef382cfa: Which tube should NOT be used for a lithium level?
Lithium heparin contains lithium and falsely raises the result.
qp90c9b0f6: A lithium level is usually drawn about how long after the last dose?
Standard lithium levels are 12-hour post-dose levels, so dose and draw times must be recorded.
qpbb6e26e3: A patient with low albumin has a phenytoin level ordered. Which test may the provider also order?
Serum albumin in a gray tube
Phenytoin is highly protein bound; with low albumin, the total level can look normal while the active free drug is high.
qpdd30ae8e: A valproic acid level for routine monitoring is usually drawn when?
As a trough before the next dose
Routine anticonvulsant levels such as valproate are troughs, drawn before the next dose.
qp7e8bc117: Tacrolimus levels for a transplant patient are drawn in which tube?
Tacrolimus concentrates in red cells, so it is measured in whole blood from an EDTA tube, usually as a trough.
qp72e149c3: When is a routine cyclosporine level most often drawn?
Trough, just before the next dose
Cyclosporine is most often monitored with a trough whole-blood level.
qp6f6da733: The vancomycin trough is drawn 2 hours late, after the dose has started. What should you do?
Notify the nurse and document the actual time
Label it with the scheduled time
Discard the sample without telling anyone
Draw from the IV arm to save time
A level drawn during the infusion is not a trough; accurate time documentation and communication prevent wrong dosing decisions.
qp802c9eb2: Why is theophylline a drug that needs level monitoring?
It has a narrow therapeutic range
It only works when drawn fasting
Small changes in level can cause toxicity such as seizures or arrhythmias, so levels guide therapy.
qp0b24e7a2: A carbamazepine level is ordered. What information must accompany the sample?
Collection time and time of last dose
Collection time and last dose time let the provider decide whether the level is a trough and interpret it correctly.
qp2a76fd4b: Some labs ask for drug levels in a red top tube without gel. Why?
Gel separators can absorb some drugs
Gel causes the sample to clot faster
Gel adds extra drug to serum
Certain drugs can be absorbed into gel separators, lowering results, so follow the lab's tube requirements.
qp3f2365bc: Methotrexate levels after high-dose therapy are drawn at exact timed points. Why?
It changes the order of draw
It is always drawn with blood cultures
It only matters for outpatient draws
Methotrexate clearance is followed at set times after the infusion; the result decides how long rescue therapy continues.
qp76caa1b0: Which drug class does amikacin belong to, making peak and trough levels common?
Amikacin, gentamicin and tobramycin are aminoglycosides monitored for kidney and hearing toxicity.
qp91ba4b6f: A patient has an IV infusing in the left arm. Which site is preferred for a routine draw?
Above the IV in the left arm
The left hand near the IV
Drawing from the arm opposite the IV avoids dilution and contamination by the infusing fluid.
qpd3cbdc09: A glucose result is extremely high in a patient with no diabetes; the sample was drawn above a running IV. What fluid most likely contaminated it?
Dextrose-containing IV fluid in the sample falsely raises glucose; drawing above an IV is never acceptable.
qp068c4033: A sample drawn above an IV running potassium chloride will most likely show what?
The infused potassium mixes with the sample and raises the result.
